nodes.label: Georg Bühler
variants: ゲオルグ・ビューラー
ゲオルク・ビューラー
ヨハン・ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, Bühler studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (1863-1880) and held the Sanskrit chair at the University of Vienna from 1880.

nodes.id: I:Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
nodes.label: Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
variants: Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
Grundriss der Indo-arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
Grundriss der indo-arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde

nodes.label: Franz Kielhorn
variants: フランツ・キールホルン
nodes.summary: Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Deccan College (1866–1881) and the University of Göttingen, where he assumed the chair in Indology in 1881.

nodes.label: Ernst Kuhn
nodes.image: Ernst Kuhn - Aufsätze zur Kultur- und Sprachgeschichte.jpg
nodes.description: German indologist, linguist, philologist and orientalist (1846–1920)
nodes.summary: Ernst Kuhn was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg, under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Halle, Leipzig, Heidelberg, and Munich (1877–1917).

nodes.label: Lucian Scherman
nodes.summary: Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and earned his doctorate at Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He served as a professor at the University of Munich (c. 1893–1933) and headed the Museum Fünf Kontinente from 1907.

nodes.label: Ernst Windisch
variants: エルンスト・ヴィルヘルム・オスカー・ヴィンディシュ
エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.summary: Ernst Windisch worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Friedrich Zarncke, and Hermann Brockhaus, later holding chairs at Heidelberg and Strasbourg, and teaching at Leipzig from 1869.

nodes.label: Willem Caland
variants: ウィレム・カーランド
nodes.summary: Willem Caland worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Leiden University (1877) under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held posts at Utrecht University (1903–1929) and Leiden University (1913–1914).

nodes.label: Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze
nodes.image: Portrait Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze (Pesne workshop).jpg
nodes.summary: Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Indology. He served as librarian and antiquary at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1697–1739) and as librarian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1697).

nodes.label: Royal Library of Berlin
variants: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin – Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Oriental Department
Oriental Department, Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin – Preußischer Kulturbesitz

nodes.label: Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg
nodes.image: Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg monument in Tranquebar, Tamil Nadu, South India.jpg

nodes.label: August Hermann Francke
nodes.summary: August Hermann Francke (1870–1930) was a Tibetologist, linguist, and historian. Educated at Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and Humboldt University of Berlin, he later served as a Privatdozent (1922) and extraordinary professor (1925) at Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres
variants: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres
Akademie der schönen Wissenschaften zu Paris

nodes.label: Alexander Johnston
nodes.summary: Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Christian Friedrich Schwarz, at the University of Göttingen, and at Lincoln's Inn. He served on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819) and founded the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron
variants: アンクティル・デュペロン
アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン
nodes.image: David d'Angers - Portrait d'Abraham-Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron (1731-1805), orientaliste.jpg
nodes.jawiki: アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies, Anquetil-Duperron studied at the Sorbonne, Amersfoort, and under Dastur Darab. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and Institut de France.

nodes.label: Joseph Tiefenthaler
nodes.summary: Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and held the post of Rector at the Jesuit High School of Agra.

nodes.label: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed
nodes.description: Civilian of the British East India Company (1751-1830)
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was an Indologist and linguist. He was educated at Harrow School and studied at Christ Church in 1768. From approximately 1771 to 1785, he served as an official for the East India Company.

nodes.label: East India Company
variants: Court of Directors of the East-India-Company
イギリス東インド会社

nodes.label: Paulinus of St. Bartholomew
nodes.summary: Paulinus of St. Bartholomew was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University, Sapienza University of Rome, and Collegio San Pancrazio. He served in the Malabar Mission (1776–1789) and later held posts in Rome in 1800.

nodes.label: Hendrik van Rheede
nodes.dewiki: Hendrik Adriaan van Rheede tot Draakenstein

nodes.label: University of Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学
オックスフォード大學

nodes.label: Charles Wilkins
variants: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.summary: Charles Wilkins (1749–1836) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kālinātha (~1778–1785). He founded The Asiatic Society in 1784, served in the East India Company, and was librarian at the India Office Library (~1801–1836).

nodes.label: Henry Thomas Colebrooke
variants: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.jawiki: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.summary: Henry Thomas Colebrooke (1765–1837), an Indologist who studied under Citrapati, served the East India Company and Bengal Civil Service, taught Sanskrit at Fort William College, and was Director of the Royal Asiatic Society, which he co-founded.

nodes.label: William Jones
variants: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ (言語学者)
nodes.description: Anglo-Welsh philologist and scholar of ancient India (1746–1794)
nodes.summary: William Jones was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College, Oxford, and Middle Temple. He became Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in 1783 and founded the Asiatic Society in 1784.

nodes.id: I:Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
nodes.label: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
variants: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William

nodes.label: Robert Chambers
nodes.summary: Robert Chambers (1737–1803) was an Indology scholar who studied at Lincoln College, Oxford. He was Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766), Principal of New Inn Hall (1766), Chief Justice in Bengal (~1789–1798), and president of The Asiatic Society (~1797–1799).

nodes.label: John Shore
nodes.summary: John Shore was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He succeeded William Jones and served as President of The Asiatic Society from circa 1794 to 1798.

nodes.label: Fort William College
variants: College von Fort William in Kalkutta
College of Fort William in Calcutta

nodes.label: William Carey
variants: ウィリアム・ケアリー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ケアリー (宣教師)
nodes.description: English Baptist missionary and Particular Baptist minister (1761-1834)
nodes.summary: William Carey was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. He was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at Fort William College in 1801 and founded Serampore College and the Baptist Missionary Society.

nodes.label: Otto von Böhtlingk
variants: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.jawiki: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.summary: Otto von Böhtlingk was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp and Christian Lassen. He served at the Russian Academy of Sciences (director 1849–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

nodes.label: Charles Rieu
nodes.summary: Charles Rieu (1820–1902) studied at Geneva and Bonn under Christian Lassen, Georg Freytag, and Johann Gildemeister. Working in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he served at the British Museum (from 1847) and Cambridge as Adams Professor of Arabic.

nodes.label: George Thibaut
nodes.summary: Indologist George Thibaut studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as director of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, principal of Sanskrit College and University and Muir Central College, and registrar at the University of Allahabad and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Sudhākara Dvivedī
nodes.summary: Sudhākara Dvivedī, an Indologist and historian, studied under Devakṛṣṇa. He was a librarian and later professor of mathematics and astrology at Sanskrit College and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he headed the mathematics faculty from 1898 to 1905.

nodes.label: Horace Hayman Wilson
variants: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.jawiki: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.summary: Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. He served as Boden Professor of Sanscrit at the University of Oxford (1831-1860) and held posts at the East India Company and Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Monier Monier-Williams
variants: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.jawiki: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.summary: Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College (1844–1858) and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1860 to 1887, founding the Indian Institute.

nodes.label: Vans Kennedy
nodes.description: Scottish major-general of the British Army
nodes.summary: Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1846).

nodes.label: James Prinsep
variants: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.summary: James Prinsep (1799–1840) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served at the Benares Mint (~1820–1830) and Kolkata Mint (1819, 1830–1838), led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, and founded Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum.

nodes.id: P:Guillaume Le Gentil de La Galaisière
nodes.label: Guillaume Le Gentil de La Galaisière
Arthur Schopenhauer
variants: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
アルトゥール・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.jawiki: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.summary: Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena, where he earned his doctorate in 1813. His teachers included Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Boeckh, and Friedrich August Wolf, and he held a lectureship in Berlin in 1820.

nodes.label: Paul Regnaud
nodes.summary: Paul Regnaud was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1876). He subsequently held a post at the University of Lyon (~1879–1908).

nodes.label: École Pratique des Hautes Études
variants: École des Hautes Études in Paris
École pratique des Hautes Études, Paris
École Pratique des Hautes Études, PSL Research University
École des Hautes Études, Section des sciences religieuses

nodes.label: John Muir
nodes.summary: John Muir studied at East India Company College, Glasgow, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1844, and later held a post at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Johannes Klatt
nodes.summary: Johannes Klatt was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber (1868–1872) and earned a doctorate at Halle-Wittenberg (~1869–1873). He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin as staff, assistant, custodian, and librarian between 1872 and 1889.

nodes.label: Albrecht Weber
variants: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
アルブレヒト・フリードリヒ・ヴェーバー
nodes.jawiki: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Christian Lassen, Johann Gildemeister, and Adalbert Kuhn. He held teaching posts at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1848 to 1901.

nodes.label: Ignazio Guidi
nodes.summary: Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) studied at the Sapienza University of Rome, where he subsequently served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

nodes.label: Emilio Teza
nodes.description: Italian translator, indo-europeanist, romanist, orientalist and linguist
nodes.summary: Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied under Anton Boller. He held professorial chairs at the University of Bologna (1860), the University of Pisa (~1860–1886), and the University of Padua (~1886–1912).

nodes.label: Ram Mohan Roy
variants: ラーム・モーハン・ローイ
nodes.image: Portrait of Raja Ram Mohun Roy, 1833.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ラーム・モーハン・ローイ
nodes.description: Indian religious, social, and educational reformer, and humanitarian
nodes.summary: Ram Mohan Roy worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Vedanta College (1826), Brahmo Samaj (1828), and the Calcutta Unitarian Committee.

nodes.label: Alexander Hamilton
nodes.summary: Alexander Hamilton was an Indologist. He served at the East India Company College, becoming Professor of Sanskrit in 1806 and Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu Literature in 1808.

nodes.label: Louis-Mathieu Langlès
variants: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.jawiki: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.description: French academic, philologist, linguist, translator, author, librarian and orientalist
nodes.summary: Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology. He studied at the Collège de France under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He was director and Persian chair at INALCO and chief keeper at the Bibliothèque nationale.

nodes.label: Henry Pitts Forster
nodes.summary: Henry Pitts Forster (1766–1815) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1783 to 1815, worked for the East India Company, and was Master of the Calcutta Mint from 1803 to 1804.

nodes.label: Joshua Marshman
variants: ジョシュア・マーシュマン
nodes.summary: Joshua Marshman worked in Indology, sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and went on to found Serampore College in 1818.

nodes.label: Friedrich Majer
variants: フリードリヒ・マイヤー
nodes.summary: Friedrich Majer (1772–1818) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1789–1792) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1797–1803), later serving as a Privatdozent at Jena.

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried von Herder
variants: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried von Herder was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied theology at Königsberg (1761). His posts included teaching at Riga Cathedral School (1764–1769), general superintendent at Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach (1776), and director at Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar (~1776–1803).

nodes.label: Friedrich Schlegel
variants: カール・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・フォン・シュレーゲル
フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, critic and scholar, editor
nodes.summary: Friedrich Schlegel (1772–1829) worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Göttingen and Leipzig, and under Heyne, Hamilton, and Chézy. He held posts at Jena (1800), Cologne (1804), and TU Dresden (1828).

nodes.label: Bibliothèque nationale de France
variants: Bibliothèque Impériale, Département des Manuscrits Orientaux

nodes.label: August Wilhelm von Schlegel
variants: アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・シュレーゲル
アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・フォン・シュレーゲル
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, translator, critic, and writer (1767–1845)
nodes.summary: August Wilhelm von Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, and later under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Alexander Hamilton. He held professorships at the University of Jena and the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Peter von Bohlen
nodes.summary: Peter von Bohlen studied at Halle, Berlin, and Bonn, learning under Franz Bopp, Georg Freytag, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He spent his career at the University of Königsberg, becoming ordinary professor of oriental literature in 1828 and 1830.

nodes.label: Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier
nodes.summary: Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier (1741–1795) was an Indologist who studied under Ramchandra and served as a colonel in the East India Company.

nodes.label: Othmar Frank
nodes.summary: Indologist Othmar Frank studied at the universities of Paris and London. He held teaching posts at Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, Banz Abbey, and served as professor at the universities of Bamberg, Würzburg (from 1821), and Munich (from 1826).

nodes.label: University of Bamberg
variants: Indological Institute at the University of Bamberg

nodes.label: University of Paris
variants: Institute de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne

nodes.label: Franz Bopp
nodes.summary: Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Paris under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Antoine-Léonard Chézy, and at London and Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

nodes.label: University of London
variants: Institute of Germanic Studies, University of London
Institute of Germanic Studies in London University

nodes.label: Vyāsa
variants: Vyāsa, Über Philosophie, Mythologie, Literatur und Sprache der Hindu

nodes.label: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann
variants: カール・ヴィンディシュマン
nodes.summary: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the universities of Mainz and Würzburg, later holding positions at the Lyceum and Hofbibliothek in Aschaffenburg and as a professor at the University of Bonn from 1818.

nodes.label: Friedrich Windischmann
nodes.summary: Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, and others, and completed a doctorate in theology at Munich (ca. 1836), where he held an extraordinary professorship (1838–1839).

nodes.label: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy
variants: Antoine Isaac, Baron Silvestre de Sacy
アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.summary: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist, historian, and Iranian specialist. He founded the Société Asiatique, serving as its president, and was a professor of Arabic and Persian at INALCO and of Persian at the Collège de France (1806–1838).

nodes.label: Antoine-Léonard Chézy
variants: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.summary: Antoine-Léonard Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Silvestre de Sacy and Langlès. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and held the chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832.

nodes.label: Collège de France
variants: Institut des Hautes Etudes Chinoises, Collège de France
コレージュ・ド・フランス
コレジュ・ド・フランス

variants: Department of Indian and Buddhist Studies, University of Göttingen

nodes.label: Wilhelm von Humboldt
variants: Friedrich Wilhelm Christian Carl Ferdinand von Humboldt
Friedrich Wilhelm Christian Karl Ferdinand von Humboldt
ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
カール・ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.description: Prussian philosopher, government official, diplomat, and educator (1767–1835)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Viadrina, Göttingen, and Jena under scholars including Lichtenberg and Heyne. He served at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1809–1810) and as a Prussian minister (~1819).

nodes.label: Ernst Siecke
nodes.description: born:1846|died:1935|; Siecke, Ernst (Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl), 1846-; Siecke, Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl, 1846-1935

nodes.label: Alexandre Langlois
nodes.summary: Alexandre Langlois was a scholar in Indology who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He taught classes at Lycée Charlemagne (c. 1817–1835) and held posts at the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres and Académie de Paris from around 1835 to 1854.

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat
variants: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a sinologist and linguist who studied at INALCO under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as conservator at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

nodes.label: Jean-Louis Burnouf
variants: ジャン＝ルイ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Jean-Louis Burnouf studied at Lycée Saint-Louis and under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held posts at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the École Normale Supérieure, the University of Paris, and was chair of Latin eloquence at the Collège de France (1816–1844).

nodes.label: Eugène Burnouf
variants: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.jawiki: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Eugène Burnouf (1801–1852) was a French Indologist and scholar of Buddhism and Iranian studies who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held posts at the Société Asiatique and succeeded Chézy at the Collège de France (1832–1852).

nodes.label: Christian Gottlob Heyne
nodes.summary: Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar who earned a master's degree from Leipzig (1748–1752). He served at the University of Göttingen as professor from 1763 and as library director (1764–1812).

nodes.label: Christian Lassen
variants: クリスチャン・ラッセン
nodes.jawiki: クリスチャン・ラッセン (東洋学者)
nodes.summary: Christian Lassen (1800–1876) studied at Oslo, Heidelberg, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel, working in Indology and linguistics. He served as Privatdozent (1830) and professor of Old Indian language and literature (1840–1876) at Bonn.

nodes.label: Paul Deussen
variants: パウル・ヤーコプ・ドイセン
nodes.summary: Paul Deussen was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Christian Lassen at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin. He taught at RWTH Aachen University (~1876–1879), Berlin (1881–1887), and served as professor at Kiel University from 1889.

nodes.label: Otto Strauss
nodes.summary: Otto Strauss worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel (doctoral degree ~1905) under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held professorships at Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel (1920), and Breslau (1928–1935).

nodes.label: Société Asiatique
variants: フランスのアジア協会

nodes.label: Alexander von Humboldt
variants: アレクサンダー・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.image: Stieler, Joseph Karl - Alexander von Humboldt - 1843.jpg
nodes.jawiki: アレクサンダー・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.summary: Alexander von Humboldt worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at European University Viadrina, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, the University of Jena, and the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, and held a post at the University of Jena.

nodes.label: University of Königsberg
variants: ケーニヒスベルク大学

nodes.label: Theodor Goldstücker
variants: テオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.summary: Theodor Goldstücker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg and Bonn under Peter von Bohlen, Karl Rosenkranz, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He later served as professor of Sanskrit at University College London and University of London.

nodes.label: Friedrich Rückert
variants: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
ヨーハン・ミヒャエル・フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.description: German poet, translator, and professor of Oriental languages (1788–1866)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Rückert (1788–1866) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Bopp and von Hammer-Purgstall. He held posts at Jena (1811), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826), and Berlin (1841–1849).

nodes.label: Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff
nodes.summary: Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff worked in Indology and other fields after studying at Tübingen (~1793–1797). He held posts at the University of Tartu (~1803–1809), University of Würzburg (~1815–1818), and University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1818–1835).

nodes.label: Adolf Holtzmann
nodes.summary: Adolf Holtzmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin, Munich under Frank and Schmeller (~1834–1837), and Paris under Burnouf (~1839–1840), later serving as professor of German literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

nodes.label: Johann Andreas Schmeller
nodes.summary: Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) studied at the University of Munich (~1801–1803). He served at the Bavarian Cadet Corps (~1817–1826), the Bavarian State Library (from 1829), and held a professorship in Old German language and literature at the University of Munich (1828; 1846).

nodes.label: Heidelberg University
variants: Sinologisches Seminar of the University of Heidelberg
South Asia Institute of Heidelberg University

nodes.label: Salomon Lefmann
nodes.summary: Salomon Lefmann was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Münster, Berlin (PhD under Franz Bopp), Heidelberg, and Paris. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University starting in 1866, becoming an associate and later honorary professor.

nodes.label: University of Freiburg
variants: Orientalisches Seminar, Abt. Indologie, Universität Freiburg
Confucius Institute at the University of Freiburg

nodes.label: Friedrich Rosen
nodes.summary: Friedrich Rosen (1805–1837) completed doctoral studies under Franz Bopp (~1824–1826) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London from ~1828 to 1837.

nodes.label: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler
variants: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.jawiki: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, and Sacy, earning a PhD at Berlin (1826–1829). He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Breslau (1833–1847) and its rector (1862–1863).

nodes.label: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (1801–1888) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Gottfried Hermann, and Caussin de Perceval. In 1836, he was appointed to the Oriental languages chair at Leipzig.

nodes.label: Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary
nodes.summary: Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, he was appointed lecturer in oriental languages (1829) and extraordinary professor of theology (1831) at Berlin.

nodes.label: Karl Albert Agathon Benary
nodes.summary: Karl Albert Agathon Benary (1807–1860) was a linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and earned a doctorate from Halle-Wittenberg. He served as a professor at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and as a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

nodes.label: Köllnisches Gymnasium
variants: ケルン・ギムナジウム

nodes.label: Bernhard Hirzel
nodes.summary: Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp, completing studies in Zurich, Berlin, Göttingen, and Paris. He held several academic posts at the University of Zurich as reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent between 1833 and 1845.

nodes.label: Hermann Brockhaus
variants: ヘルマン・ブロックハウス
nodes.summary: Hermann Brockhaus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He became a professor at the University of Jena in 1839 and at the University of Leipzig from 1848 until 1877.

nodes.label: University of Zurich
variants: Völkerkundemuseum of the University of Zurich
Institute for Social Anthropology and Empirical Cultural Studies at the University of Zurich

nodes.label: Georg Martin Dursch
nodes.summary: Dursch specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tübingen and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy at the University of Paris (~1827-1829), later serving as a professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen beginning in 1829.

nodes.label: Friedrich von Adelung
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Adelung worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology after studying at Leipzig (1787–1790). He held honorary professorships at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809) and was director at Vienna (1824).

nodes.label: Johann Christoph Adelung
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・クリストフ・アーデルング
nodes.summary: Johann Christoph Adelung (1732–1806) was a linguist who studied at the Kloster Berge school (~1746–1752) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1752). He taught at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and served as chief librarian at Dresden (1787).

nodes.label: Colin Mackenzie
nodes.image: Colonel Colin Mackenzie and his Indian pandits by Thomas Hickey.jpg
nodes.summary: Colin Mackenzie studied at Dollar Academy and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1810 to 1815.

nodes.label: William Ward
variants: ウィリアム・ウォード
nodes.description: English pioneer Baptist missionary, author, printer and translator
nodes.summary: William Ward (1769–1823) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Ewood Hall Academy under John Fawcett (1797), served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (~1799–1823), and founded Serampore College (1818).

nodes.label: Claude-Auguste Court
nodes.summary: Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Claude-Auguste Court studied at the École polytechnique and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1813–1814). Between ~1827 and 1843, he served as an engineer officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army and Court of Ranjit Singh.

nodes.label: École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr
variants: サン・シール陸軍士官学校

nodes.label: George Turnour
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ターナー (歴史家)
nodes.summary: George Turnour was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and historian. In the Ceylon Civil Service, he served as a Member of the Supreme Council in 1818 and as Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

nodes.label: John Wilson
nodes.description: Christian missionary, orientalist, and educator in Maharashtra, India (1804-1875)
nodes.summary: John Wilson (1804–1875) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies after studying at the University of Edinburgh. He served as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and founded Wilson College, Mumbai.

nodes.label: Asiatic Society of Mumbai
variants: Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Brian Houghton Hodgson
variants: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.image: Brian Houghton Hodgson by Louisa Starr-Canziani.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.summary: Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at East India Company College and Haileybury, and served as Assistant Resident and later British Resident at the Court of Nepal (~1820–1843).

nodes.label: Bhagwanlal Indraji
nodes.summary: Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was an Honorary Member of the Royal Asiatic Society, a Fellow at the University of Mumbai, and a member of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

nodes.label: Charles Masson
nodes.description: British East India Company soldier and explorer (1800–1853)

nodes.label: Edwin Norris
nodes.summary: Edwin Norris was an Indologist, linguist, and historian. After serving as a clerk for the East India Company (1818–1837), he worked as a Foreign Office translator (1847–1866) and held several administrative and librarian roles at the Royal Asiatic Society between 1836 and 1872.

nodes.label: Edward Upham
nodes.summary: Edward Upham worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1824–1834) and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London (~1832–1834).

nodes.label: Francis Wilford
nodes.summary: Francis Wilford was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (circa 1790–1822) and secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Eugène Jacquet
nodes.summary: Eugène Jacquet (1811–1838) was an Indologist and linguist. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from around 1828 to 1832, and later under Eugène Burnouf from around 1832 to 1838.

nodes.label: Daniel Wright
nodes.description: Scottish surgeon and physician; resided in Nepal

nodes.label: William Wright
nodes.summary: William Wright (1830–1889) was a linguist who studied at St Andrews, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leiden. He held posts at University College London, Trinity College Dublin, the British Museum (1861–1870), and Cambridge as Adams Professor of Arabic (1870–1889).

nodes.label: Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern
nodes.summary: Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (1833–1917) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Utrecht, Leiden (doctorate 1855), and under Albrecht Weber, he taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1863–1865) and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).

nodes.label: Bunyiu Nanjio
nodes.summary: Bunyiu Nanjio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology who studied at Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held teaching and leadership posts at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and Bussho Kankōkai.

nodes.label: Edward Byles Cowell
variants: エドワード・バイルズ・コウェル
nodes.image: Portrait of Edward Byles Cowell by Charles Edmund Brock-1905.jpg
nodes.summary: Edward Byles Cowell, an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Iranian/Central Asian specialist, studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He held posts at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and Sanskrit College, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (1867–1903).

nodes.label: Julius Eggeling
nodes.summary: Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and as Professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

nodes.label: Robert Alexander Neil
nodes.image: R A Neil-R H Lord recto.tif
nodes.summary: Robert Alexander Neil (1852–1901) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and Peterhouse, Cambridge. He served as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge from 1884 and as a Fellow of Pembroke College, Cambridge, in 1900.

nodes.label: Sándor Kőrösi Csoma
variants: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.jawiki: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.summary: Sándor Kőrösi Csoma (1784–1842) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College, the University of Göttingen, and with traditional teachers Sangye Phuntsok and Kunga Cholek Dorje, later serving as Librarian at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Isaak Jakob Schmidt
nodes.summary: Isaak Jakob Schmidt was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctoral degree from the University of Rostock. He served at the Russian Bible Society and became a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1838–1847).

nodes.label: Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire
nodes.description: French philosopher, journalist, statesman, and possible illegitimate son of Napoleon I of France (1805-1895)
nodes.summary: Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who attended Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

nodes.id: I:Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
nodes.label: Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
variants: Académie des Sciences morales et politiques
Academy of Moral and Political Science

nodes.label: Julius Mohl
nodes.summary: Julius Mohl was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinological studies. After studying at Tübingen and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf, he held posts at Tübingen, the Société Asiatique, and the Collège de France (1847–1876).

nodes.label: Stanislas Julien
variants: エニャン＝スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.jawiki: スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.summary: Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. He held chairs at the Collège de France and INALCO, and served at the Institut de France and Bibliothèque nationale de France.

nodes.label: Robert Lenz
nodes.summary: Robert Lenz studied at the University of Tartu and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Tallinn Cathedral School, University of Breslau, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University as professor of Sanskrit (~1835–1836).

nodes.label: Gaspare Gorresio
nodes.image: Gaspare Gorresio, post 1869 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0015 B.jpg
nodes.summary: Gaspare Gorresio studied at the University of Turin and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He taught at the Military Academy of Turin, held Turin's chair in Sanskrit from 1852, and served as director of the National University Library of Turin.

nodes.label: Émile-Louis Burnouf
nodes.summary: Émile-Louis Burnouf worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and University of Paris under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor at the University of Nancy (1854–1867) and director of the École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).

nodes.label: Théodore Pavie
nodes.image: Théodore Pavie (1811–1896), Orientalist, friend of the artist MET 31523.jpg
nodes.summary: Théodore Pavie was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He succeeded Burnouf as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and later taught Hebrew at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

nodes.label: Adolphe Regnier
nodes.summary: Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, having studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at the Collège de France (1838), the École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), and served as librarian at the Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

nodes.label: Félix Nève
nodes.summary: Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist. He earned a doctorate from KU Leuven (~1834–1838) and studied under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor at KU Leuven from 1841.

nodes.label: Abel Bergaigne
variants: アベル・ベルゲーニュ
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Abel Bergaigne studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He served as répétiteur at the EPHE (~1869–1877) and as lecturer and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the Sorbonne and University of Paris.

nodes.label: Theodor Benfey
variants: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.summary: Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. and habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He spent his career there as a Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

nodes.label: Friedrich Max Müller
variants: フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
マックス・ミューラー
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
nodes.description: German-born British philologist, orientalist and indologist (1823–1900)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Max Müller (1823–1900) worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under Brockhaus, Bopp, Schelling, and Burnouf, and under Wilson. He held posts at Oxford from 1850, including professor from 1868 to 1900.

nodes.label: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud
nodes.summary: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1824, 1854, 1858) and INALCO (from 1838), and presided over the Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: Heinrich Ewald
nodes.description: German orientalist, theologian, and Biblical exegete (1803–1875)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Ewald (1803–1875) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and Thomas Christian Tychsen, later serving as professor at Göttingen and the University of Tübingen.

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
variants: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: Ernst Trumpp
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・トランプ
nodes.summary: Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Tübinger Stift under Rudolf von Roth, held a post at East India House, and served as Privatdozent at Tübingen and professor at the University of Munich (circa 1874–1885).

nodes.label: August Schleicher
variants: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.summary: August Schleicher worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald and Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, among others. He held academic posts at Bonn (1846), Charles University (1850, 1853), and Jena (1857).

nodes.label: Moritz Abraham Stern
variants: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.summary: Moritz Abraham Stern was a mathematician and linguist who studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen, completing his doctorate under Carl Friedrich Gauss. He was appointed Extraordinarius at Göttingen (1829–1884), succeeding Gauss in 1858.

nodes.label: Rudolf von Roth
variants: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.jawiki: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.summary: Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald (~1839–1843) and under Eugène Burnouf (~1843–1844). He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent from 1845 and Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

nodes.label: William Dwight Whitney
variants: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.summary: William Dwight Whitney was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Williams, Yale under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, and in Germany under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Yale from 1853 to 1894.

nodes.label: James Tod
nodes.description: 1782-1835, English officer of the British East India Company and an Oriental scholar
nodes.summary: James Tod (1782–1835) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1797–1798) and under Gyanchandra (~1812–1823). He served with the East India Company (~1798–1822) and as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).

nodes.label: Adalbert Kuhn
variants: フランツ・フェーリクス・アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.jawiki: アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.summary: Adalbert Kuhn worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (1833–1837) and served at Köllnisches Gymnasium as teacher, professor, and director (1837, 1841, 1856, 1870).

nodes.label: Andrzej Gawroński
nodes.summary: Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv and University of Leipzig. He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and Lviv (1917) and founded Rocznik Orientalistyczny, among other societies.

nodes.label: Stamford Raffles
variants: トーマス・スタンフォード・ラッフルズ
nodes.image: George Francis Joseph - Sir Thomas Stamford Bingley Raffles.jpg
nodes.jawiki: トーマス・ラッフルズ
nodes.summary: Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, linguistics, and other fields. He was employed by the East India Company from circa 1795 to 1824 and founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, serving as its president in 1826.

nodes.label: John Crawfurd
nodes.summary: John Crawfurd worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803), served as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808), and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.

nodes.label: James Fergusson
nodes.summary: James Fergusson (1808–1886) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal High School and became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1840.

nodes.label: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer
nodes.summary: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Königsberg (~1710–1716) and under Christoph Theodosius Walther. He held posts at Königsberg schools, the University of Königsberg (~1717–1725), and the Russian Academy of Sciences (1726).

nodes.label: Christoph Theodosius Walther
nodes.summary: Christoph Theodosius Walther was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied theology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1720. He later served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from circa 1725 to 1739.

nodes.label: Friedrich Bollensen
nodes.summary: Friedrich Bollensen was a linguist and Indologist who studied Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen. He served as adjunct professor at Saint Petersburg State University and Main Pedagogical Institute, and as ordinary professor of Sanskrit at Kazan State University.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Geiger
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ルートヴィヒ・ガイガー
ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Geiger was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD under Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he became professor in 1891, later serving as professor at Munich (1920–1924).

nodes.label: Friedrich von Spiegel
variants: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
フリードリヒ・（フォン・）シュピーゲル
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Spiegel specialized in Iranian and Indological studies. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Leipzig under Lassen, Brockhaus, and others, earning his doctorate at Jena (ca. 1842). He was professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1849–1891).

nodes.label: University of Leipzig
variants: Institute for Indology and Central Asian Studies, Leipzig University
ライプツィヒ大学インド学・中央アジア学研究所
Department of Indology and Central Asian Studies, University of Leipzig
Institute for the Study of Religions at Leipzig University

nodes.label: Heinrich Uhle
nodes.summary: Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig (~1865–1870) under Hermann Brockhaus. He served as a classical languages teacher at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

nodes.label: Eduard Sachau
nodes.summary: Eduard Sachau studied at Kiel under Theodor Nöldeke, Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus and Heinrich Fleischer, and Halle-Wittenberg (PhD). He worked in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies at Vienna (1869), Berlin (from 1876), and the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1887).

nodes.label: Hermann Camillo Kellner
nodes.summary: Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus around 1862–1865 and later served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau from around 1876 to 1904.

nodes.label: Kreuzschule
variants: Dresden College of the Sacred Cross

nodes.label: Richard Fritzsche
nodes.summary: Richard Fritzsche was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1870–1875). He later served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg (~1888–1913).

nodes.label: University of Marburg
variants: Philipps-Universität Marburg, FG Indologie u. Tibetologie
Philipps Universität in Marburg an der Lahn
マールブルク大学大学院

nodes.label: Niels Ludvig Westergaard
variants: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.image: Niels Ludvig Westergaard by Budtz Müller.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.summary: Niels Ludvig Westergaard worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, London, and Oxford, later serving as professor and Rektor at the University of Copenhagen.

nodes.label: Albert Hoefer
nodes.summary: Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin, where he completed his doctorate (1837) and habilitation (1838–1840). He spent his career as a professor at the University of Greifswald (~1840–1883).

nodes.label: University of Greifswald
variants: グライフスヴァルト大学

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
variants: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald (1808) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1812). He held posts at Greifswald (adjunct 1815, professor 1824–1850) and Jena (professor 1817–1824).

nodes.label: Siegfried Goldschmidt
nodes.summary: Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844-1884) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen, and Tübingen (PhD 1867) under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, becoming an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

nodes.id: I:Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society
nodes.label: Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society
Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca
variants: Anton Edmund Xavier Evarist Wollheim da Fonseca
nodes.image: PPN663949858 Bildnis von Anton Eduard Wollheim Dafonseca.jpg
nodes.summary: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from Humboldt University of Berlin around 1828–1831. He lectured there in oriental and modern occidental languages (1849–1852) and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

nodes.label: Richard Pischel
variants: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.jawiki: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.summary: Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Breslau, studying under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Kiel (1875), Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902), and Berlin (1902–1908).

nodes.label: Alfred Hillebrandt
nodes.summary: Alfred Hillebrandt worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Martin Haug. He served as professor at the University of Breslau from 1883, becoming a full professor in 1887.

nodes.label: Adalbert Bezzenberger
nodes.summary: Adalbert Bezzenberger studied at Göttingen and Munich under Theodor Benfey, working in linguistics and Indology. He served as Privatdozent at Göttingen (1874) and at the University of Königsberg as Professor of Sanskrit (1879), Prorektor (1890–1891), and Rektor (1919–1921).

nodes.label: Hermann Oldenberg
variants: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.summary: Hermann Oldenberg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889–1908), and Göttingen (1908).

nodes.label: Jacob Wackernagel
variants: ヤコブ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.jawiki: ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.summary: Jacob Wackernagel was an indologist and linguist who studied at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig under Theodor Benfey and Friedrich Nietzsche. He held professorial chairs and posts at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and Göttingen (1902–1915).

nodes.label: Leo Meyer
nodes.summary: Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey, Jacob Grimm, and Franz Bopp. He held chairs at the University of Tartu (1865–1899) and the University of Göttingen (1862–1865, 1898), teaching Georg Bühler and Leopold von Schroeder.

nodes.label: Hermann Collitz
nodes.summary: Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg under August Fick and Theodor Benfey. He held faculty posts at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928).

nodes.label: Friedrich Bechtel
nodes.summary: Friedrich Bechtel was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey and August Fick at the University of Göttingen. He taught at Göttingen and served as ordinary professor of comparative linguistics at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.

nodes.label: Berthold Delbrück
variants: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
ベルトルト・グスタフ・ゴットリープ・デルブリュック
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
nodes.description: German comparative linguist and Sanskrit scholar (1842–1922)
nodes.summary: Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, and Franz Bopp in Halle and Berlin. He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1867–1870) and the University of Jena (1870–1913).

nodes.label: University of Copenhagen
variants: University of Copenhagen, Department of Asian Studies
Institute of Oriental Studies, University of Copenhagen

nodes.label: August Leskien
variants: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.summary: August Leskien worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Kiel, Leipzig (under Georg Curtius), and Jena (under August Schleicher). He held posts at Göttingen, Jena, and served as professor at the University of Leipzig from 1870 to 1915.

nodes.label: Leopold von Schroeder
nodes.summary: Leopold von Schroeder was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer, as well as at Tübingen, Jena, and under Rudolf von Roth. He held professorships at the universities of Tartu, Innsbruck (1896), and Vienna (1899).

nodes.label: Anton Schiefner
variants: フランツ・アントン・シーフナー
nodes.summary: Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated in law at Saint Petersburg State University and Oriental studies at Humboldt University of Berlin, he was an academician at the Russian Academy of Sciences and taught at Saint Petersburg institutions.

nodes.label: Carl Cappeller
nodes.summary: Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin, Königsberg, and Leipzig (PhD ~1867-1868) under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He completed his habilitation at Jena (~1871-1872) and became a professor there in 1875.

nodes.label: Karl Rosenkranz
variants: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.summary: Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Heidelberg, studying under G. W. F. Hegel. He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1831) and the University of Königsberg (1833).

nodes.label: Raymond West
variants: レイモンド・ウェスト
nodes.summary: Raymond West was an Indologist who studied under Martin Haug. He served as a Bombay High Court judge (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (c. 1878–1886), Asiatic Society president, and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Cambridge (c. 1892–1900).

nodes.label: University of Tübingen
variants: Seminar für Indologie und Vergleichende Religionswissenschaft, Universität Tübingen

nodes.label: Tübinger Stift
variants: テュービンゲン神学校

nodes.label: Martin Haug
nodes.summary: Martin Haug was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He taught at Bonn and Deccan College before becoming Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Munich in 1868.

nodes.label: Karl Friedrich Geldner
variants: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.jawiki: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.summary: Karl Friedrich Geldner worked in Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Brockhaus, and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin (from 1890), and Marburg (1907–1921).

nodes.label: Bruno Lindner
nodes.summary: Bruno Lindner was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig and under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Privatdocent at Leipzig from 1878 to 1919.

nodes.label: Richard von Garbe
nodes.summary: Richard von Garbe was an Indologist who earned his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and habilitation at Königsberg. He was a professor at Königsberg and held the chair of Indology at Tübingen from 1895 to 1927.

nodes.label: Maurice Bloomfield
variants: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.jawiki: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Maurice Bloomfield studied at Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins (PhD), learning under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He spent his career as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

nodes.label: Julius Grill
nodes.summary: Julius Grill was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and earned a Lic. theol. at Jena. He served as professor of Old Testament exegesis at Tübingen (1888–1913).

nodes.label: Adolf Kaegi
nodes.summary: Adolf Kaegi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Zurich, Leipzig, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. From 1875 he taught at the University of Zurich, serving as full professor of Sanskrit and classical philology (1893–1914).

nodes.label: Heinrich Zimmer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Zimmer was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Strasbourg, Tübingen, and Berlin under scholars including Rudolf von Roth, Siegfried Goldschmidt, Albrecht Weber, and Ernst Windisch, and held chairs at Greifswald and Berlin.

nodes.label: Theodor Aufrecht
variants: テーオドール・アウフレヒト
nodes.summary: Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Bodleian Library and served as a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875) and the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

nodes.label: Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung
variants: Zeitschrift für Vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete des Deutschen, Griechischen und Lateinischen
Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiet der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Beiträge zur vergleichenden Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete der arischen, keltischen und slawischen Sprachen
variants: Beiträge zur Vergleichenden Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete der Arischen, Celtischen und Slawischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Beiträge zur Kunde der indogermanischen Sprachen
variants: Beiträge zur Kunde der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Wilhelm Schulze
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Schulze, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Berlin and Greifswald under Johannes Schmidt, Heinrich Zimmer, Adolf Kiessling, and Georg Kaibel. He held chairs at Marburg (1892), Göttingen (1895), and Berlin (1902–1932).

nodes.label: Johannes Schmidt
variants: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.jawiki: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.summary: Johannes Schmidt worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bonn, Jena, and under August Schleicher, Albrecht Weber, F. W. Ritschl, and Otto Jahn. He held professorships at Bonn (1868), Graz (1873–1876), and Berlin (1876).

nodes.label: Gottfried Hermann
nodes.image: Gottfried Hermann, von Carl Christian Vogel von Vogelstein.jpg
nodes.summary: Gottfried Hermann was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig and the University of Jena. He spent his career at Leipzig, serving as extraordinary professor of philosophy from 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.

nodes.label: Moriz Haupt
nodes.summary: Moriz Haupt was a German classical philologist and linguist who studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig. He was a professor at the University of Leipzig (1841–1851) and later held the chair of Roman literature at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1853.

nodes.label: Anton Westermann
nodes.summary: Anton Westermann (1806–1869) was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served as co-director there from 1830 to 1865.

nodes.label: Reinhold Klotz
nodes.summary: Reinhold Klotz was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who completed his habilitation at the University of Leipzig (1826–1831). He served on Leipzig's faculty from 1832, becoming an außerordentlicher Professor in 1849 until his death in 1870.

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling
variants: フリードリヒ・ヴィルヘルム・ヨーゼフ・フォン・シェリング
フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.image: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling, 1848 daguerreotype - cropped.jpg
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.summary: Philosopher Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling studied at the Tübinger Stift, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Berlin (1841–1845).

nodes.label: Hermann Brunnhofer
nodes.summary: Hermann Brunnhofer worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Bonn, Berlin, Zurich, and under Albrecht Weber. He held positions at Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek (1881–1888), Saint Petersburg State University (1891–1901), and the University of Bern (1901–1914).

nodes.label: Moriz Winternitz
variants: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.summary: Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and with Georg Bühler. He worked with Max Müller at Oxford, taught at Visva-Bharati University, and served as professor at the German University Prague (~1902–1934).

nodes.label: Sampurnanand Sanskrit University
variants: ベナレス大学のサンスクリット・カレッジ

nodes.label: Jean-Baptiste Biot
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝バティスト・ビオ
nodes.summary: Jean-Baptiste Biot was a French physicist and scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École des Ponts ParisTech, and École Polytechnique. He held long-term professorships at the Collège de France (1800–1862) and the Science Faculty of Paris (1809–1862).

nodes.label: Ebenezer Burgess
nodes.description: United States missionary to the Mahrattas, in western India

nodes.label: Ludwig Noiré
variants: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ
nodes.image: Plate 13 Ludwig Noiré, Photograph album of German and Austrian scientists (cropped).png
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ

nodes.label: Louis Havet
nodes.summary: Louis Havet was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1872) under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and Latin philology chair at the Collège de France (1885–1925).

nodes.label: Kenjiu Kasawara
nodes.summary: Kenjiu Kasawara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, where he was taught by Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.

nodes.label: Heinrich Wenzel
nodes.summary: Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Jena, Tübingen (PhD), and Leipzig. He studied with Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Friedrich Max Müller, and held a habilitation post at Leipzig in 1887.

nodes.label: Heinrich August Jäschke
variants: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ
nodes.summary: Heinrich August Jäschke (1817–1883) was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky in 1847 and as a missionary for the Moravian Church and Moravian Mission in Kyelang between 1856 and 1868.

nodes.label: Bruno Liebich
nodes.summary: Bruno Liebich was an Indologist who studied under Franz Kielhorn and attended the universities of Munich, Göttingen, and Breslau. He held professorships in Indology at the University of Breslau and Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Archibald Edward Gough
nodes.description: (1845-1915) British educationalist, translator, editor and academic administrator
nodes.summary: Archibald Edward Gough was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Professor of Philosophy at Presidency University, and Principal of Aliah University.

nodes.label: John Pickford
nodes.summary: John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as a Professor at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: University of Madras
variants: Centre of Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras
University of Madras, Department of Vaishnavism
University of Madras, Department of Sanskrit
Department of Sanskrit, University of Madras

nodes.label: Ralph T. H. Griffith
nodes.summary: Ralph T. H. Griffith was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford (BA ~1843-1846) under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1849) and Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1861-1876).

nodes.label: Robert Needham Cust
nodes.summary: Robert Needham Cust worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, Haileybury, and Fort William College, later serving in the Bengal Civil Service from approximately 1843 to 1867.

nodes.label: Government of India
variants: Department of Finance and Commerce, Government of India

nodes.label: Calcutta Madrasa
variants: Madrassa, il Collegio maomettano di Calcutta

nodes.label: James Sutherland Cotton
nodes.summary: James Sutherland Cotton (1847–1918) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Oxford (1867–1870), he held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge (1871–1874) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1871–1874).

nodes.label: William Wilson Hunter
variants: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.summary: William Wilson Hunter (1840–1900) worked in history and Indology. Educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887) and was vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1886).

nodes.label: Indian Institute, University of Oxford
variants: Indian Institute at the University of Oxford

nodes.label: University of Edinburgh
variants: Professur für Sanskrit und vergleichende Sprachwissenschaft an der Universität zu Edinburg

nodes.label: Adolf Kirchhoff
nodes.summary: Adolf Kirchhoff worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842–1846) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh, later serving at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium (1846) and as ordinary professor at Frederick William University Berlin (from 1865).

nodes.label: Hermann Jacobi
variants: ヘルマン・ゲオルク・ヤコービ
nodes.summary: Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber at Humboldt University of Berlin and Johann Gildemeister at the University of Bonn. He held professorships at Münster (1876–1885), Kiel (1885), and Bonn (1889–1922).

nodes.label: Jarl Charpentier
nodes.summary: Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University (PhD 1908) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Uppsala University as assistant, deputy, and full professor (1927).

nodes.label: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
variants: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.image: Young India; an interpretation and a history of the nationalist movement from within (1916) (14781987942).jpg
nodes.jawiki: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.description: Indian nationalist leader, writer and journalist (1856–1920)
nodes.summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Deccan College, Elphinstone College, and Government Law College, Mumbai, and later taught at the New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

nodes.label: Reinhold Rost
nodes.image: Reinhold Rost, Porträt mit Signatur, um 1890.jpg
nodes.summary: Reinhold Rost was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena under Johann Gustav Stickel and Johann Gildemeister. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and Head Librarian at the India Office (1869–1893).

nodes.label: Heinrich Kiepert
nodes.description: German geographer, cartographer and university professor in Berlin (1818–1899)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Kiepert (1818–1899) studied under August Boeckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann at Berlin and earned a doctorate at Jena. A geography and archaeology scholar, he held posts at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Deecke
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Deecke, who worked in linguistics and Indology, earned a doctorate from Leipzig and studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as director of the Ernestinenschule, Gymnasium Bouxwiller, and Lycée Albert-Schweitzer Mulhouse.

nodes.label: Ferdinand von Eckstein
nodes.summary: Ferdinand von Eckstein was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Friedrich Creuzer. He founded Le Catholique in 1826 and was a member of the Société Asiatique (~1823–1861).

nodes.label: Ghent University
variants: Research Centre Vergelijkende Cultuurwetenschap, Ghent University

nodes.label: Josef Schick
nodes.summary: Josef Schick was a linguist who studied at the University of Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he earned his PhD in 1889. He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich, where he was professor from 1896 to 1925.

nodes.label: Michael Viggo Fausbøll
variants: ミケール・ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.jawiki: ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.description: Danish educator, translator, orientalist and linguist (1821–1908)
nodes.summary: Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his Cand.theol. at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847) studying under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, where he later served as assistant librarian (1861) and Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

nodes.label: Emil Sieg
nodes.summary: Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and Franz Kielhorn, earning a PhD from Berlin. He held chairs at Kiel University (1909, 1918–1919) and the University of Göttingen (1920).

nodes.label: Walther Schubring
variants: ヴァルター・シュブリング
nodes.summary: Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich and completed his doctorate under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin and held the Indology chair at Hamburg (1920–1951).

nodes.label: Ernst Leumann
variants: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.summary: Ernst Leumann specialized in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Zurich, Geneva, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Leipzig, and Strasbourg. He worked on the Sanskrit-English Dictionary at Oxford and held professorships at Frauenfeld, Strasbourg, and Freiburg.

nodes.label: Luigi Suali
nodes.summary: Luigi Suali was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi. He held an academic post at the University of Pavia from circa 1907 to 1939.

nodes.label: Helmuth von Glasenapp
variants: ヘルムート・フォン・グラーゼナップ
nodes.summary: Helmuth von Glasenapp specialized in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn (PhD under Hermann Jacobi). He was a Privatdozent at Berlin and Bonn, then held chairs at Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

nodes.label: Yale University
variants: Yale University's Interdisciplinary Center for Bioethics
Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures at Yale University

nodes.label: Edward Elbridge Salisbury
nodes.summary: Edward Elbridge Salisbury was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale and in Europe under Woolsey, Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, Lassen, and Burnouf. He was Professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841–1854).

nodes.label: Charles Rockwell Lanman
nodes.image: Charles Rockwell Lanman Professor of Sanskrit Harvard.jpg
nodes.summary: Charles Rockwell Lanman (1850–1941) studied at Yale, Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Whitney, Weber, and Roth. A linguist and Indologist, he taught at Johns Hopkins (~1876–1880) and served as a professor at Harvard University from 1880 to 1926.

nodes.label: John Avery
nodes.summary: John Avery was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Amherst College, the universities of Tübingen and Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He later served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College and Bowdoin College.

nodes.label: Ernst Haas
nodes.summary: Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He worked at the British Museum (1866) and became Professor of Sanskrit at University College London in 1875.
