nodes.label: Wilhelm Pertsch
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Pertsch was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. Beginning in 1855, he held librarian posts at Forschungsbibliothek Gotha, becoming its director in 1883, and led Schloss Friedenstein from 1874.

nodes.label: Fritz Johaentgen
nodes.summary: Fritz Johaentgen studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

nodes.label: Hermann Grassmann
nodes.summary: Hermann Grassmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher and later taught at several institutions, serving for decades as a professor at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from around 1842 to 1877.

nodes.label: Alfred Ludwig
nodes.summary: Alfred Ludwig was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna and Berlin under teachers including Albrecht Weber and August Boeckh. He completed his Habilitation at Vienna before holding professorships at Charles University from 1860.

nodes.label: Friedrich Müller
variants: フリードリヒ・ミューラー
nodes.summary: Friedrich Müller (1834–1898) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Vienna, Göttingen, and Tübingen, learning under Anton Boller. He worked at the Vienna University Library and Austrian National Library, and was professor at Vienna from 1869.

nodes.label: Anton Boller
nodes.summary: Anton Boller was an Austrian linguist and Indologist. He was a corresponding member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences and served as a lecturer and professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Vienna from 1845.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Scherer
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Scherer worked in linguistics. He studied at Vienna and Berlin under Moriz Haupt, Franz Bopp, and Karl Müllenhoff. He held posts at Vienna (1864, 1868–1872), Strasbourg (1872), and Berlin (1877), and joined the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1884).

nodes.label: University of Cambridge
variants: Department of History and Philosophy of Science, University of Cambridge
Faculty of Classics in the University of Cambridge
University of Cambridge, Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies
Faculty of Oriental Studies, University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Edward Granville Browne
variants: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.summary: Edward Granville Browne was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist who studied at Cambridge under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell. He was a lecturer in Persian (1888) and Adams Professor of Arabic (1902) at Cambridge.

nodes.label: Franz Heinrich Trithen
nodes.summary: Franz Heinrich Trithen specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Frederick William University and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, later holding positions at the British Museum (around 1844–1848) and the University of Oxford (around 1848–1854).

nodes.label: Friedrich Haag
nodes.description: Swiss classical philologist, linguist and teacher (1846-1914)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Haag (1846–1914) studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, as well as at Göttingen and Berlin. He taught at Zurich, Tallinn, Schaffhausen, and Burgdorf, and was professor of classical philology at Bern from 1887 to 1906.

nodes.label: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler
nodes.summary: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Zurich under Bernhard Hirzel, Johann Caspar von Orelli, and Hermann Sauppe. He spent his career at Zurich, becoming Ordinarius for Sanskrit and comparative linguistics in 1864.

nodes.label: Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren
variants: Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren

nodes.label: Georg Curtius
variants: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: A linguist who studied at Bonn and Berlin under Lassen, Ritschl, Schlegel, and Bopp, Curtius held professorships of classical philology at Charles University (1849-1854), Kiel University (1854-1862), and the University of Leipzig (1862-1885).

nodes.label: Friedrich Zarncke
variants: フリードリヒ・ツァルンケ
nodes.summary: Friedrich Zarncke was a linguist who studied at Rostock and Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Rostock (ca. 1847–1848) and Leipzig, where he was Privatdozent (1852) and Rektor (1869–1882).

nodes.label: Walter Elliot
nodes.summary: Walter Elliot (1803–1887) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the East India Company College and the College of Fort St George, later serving as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in Madras (1837–1842).

nodes.label: Hermann Reich
nodes.description: German writer, literary scholar and classical philologist

nodes.label: Johannes Hertel
nodes.summary: Johannes Hertel was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Leipzig (1892–1897). He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898–1920) and held the chair of Indian philology at the University of Leipzig (1919–1937).

nodes.label: August Friedrich Pott
variants: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.summary: August Friedrich Pott (1802–1887) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen and under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He lectured in Berlin (1830) before serving as a professor at Halle-Wittenberg from 1833.

nodes.label: Karl Brugmann
variants: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.jawiki: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.summary: Karl Brugmann (1849–1919) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Georg Curtius at the University of Leipzig. He served as a professor at the University of Freiburg (1884) and the University of Leipzig (1887–1919).

nodes.label: Eugen Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under August Schleicher from circa 1864 to 1868 and served as a professor at the University of Jena from around 1870 to 1917.

nodes.label: Carl Gaedicke
nodes.summary: Carl Gaedicke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller, completing his PhD at the University of Jena by 1877.

nodes.label: Ferdinand de Saussure
variants: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.image: Ferdinand de Saussure by Jullien Restored.png
nodes.jawiki: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.summary: Ferdinand de Saussure was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Geneva, Berlin, EPHE, the Sorbonne, and Leipzig. He held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and University of Paris (1881–1891), and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).

nodes.label: Eduard Sievers
variants: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.jawiki: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.summary: Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Georg Curtius, August Leskien, and Friedrich Zarncke. He held professorships at the universities of Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).

nodes.label: Ernst Curtius
variants: エルンスト・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He was a professor at Göttingen (1855–1867) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1844, 1863, 1867), and directed the Altes Museum (circa 1872–1896).

nodes.label: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli
variants: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.image: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli, post 1861 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0066 B.jpg
nodes.jawiki: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.summary: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a linguist and Indologist. He founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873 and served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.

nodes.id: I:Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik
nodes.label: Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik
variants: Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik

nodes.id: I:Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
nodes.label: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
variants: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Hermann Osthoff
variants: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.summary: Hermann Osthoff was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Friedrichsgymnasium Kassel, the University of Leipzig (~1875–1877), and Heidelberg University (1877).

nodes.label: University of Geneva
variants: ジュネーブ大学文学部

nodes.label: Pietro Merlo
nodes.summary: Pietro Merlo (1850–1888) studied under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin (1867). He taught at the University of Pavia from 1877, becoming extraordinary professor in 1880 and full professor of comparative linguistics in 1885.

nodes.label: Michele Kerbaker
nodes.summary: Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin (~1853–1857) under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and was a professor at the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1910).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Bardelli
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Bardelli was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Giuseppe Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as a lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1851–1865).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Mezzofanti
nodes.jawiki: ジュゼッペ・ガスパロ・メゾファンティ
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Mezzofanti studied at the University of Bologna (~1793–1797) and later held an academic post there (~1797–1831), also teaching Giuseppe Bardelli.

nodes.label: Carlo Giussani
nodes.summary: Carlo Giussani was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) and was taught by Giuseppe Bardelli, Rudolf von Roth, and Albrecht Weber.

nodes.label: Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano
variants: Academy of Science and Letters (Italian: Accademia scientifico-letteraria) in Milan
ミラノ科学・文学アカデミー

nodes.label: Francisco García Ayuso
nodes.image: 1897-05-30, La Ilustración Española y Americana, Francisco García Ayuso (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich from circa 1868 to 1871, working under Martin Haug between 1869 and 1871.

nodes.label: Ivan Pavlovich Minaev
nodes.summary: Ivan Pavlovich Minaev worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber, later serving as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

nodes.label: Garcin de Tassy
variants: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.dewiki: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.summary: Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collège de France under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Jean Daniel Kieffer. He held the chair in Indian languages at École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1828–1878).

nodes.label: Philippe Édouard Foucaux
variants: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.jawiki: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.summary: Philippe Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) was a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, Collège de France (1857, 1870–1894), and University of Paris (c. 1862–1894).

nodes.label: Léon Feer
nodes.summary: Léon Feer (1830–1902) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Marc Quatremère and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at INALCO (from 1864), Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872, 1900).

nodes.label: Michel Bréal
nodes.summary: Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, EPHE, and Collège de France (1864–1905), founding the Société de Linguistique de Paris in 1866.

nodes.label: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel
nodes.summary: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel specialized in linguistics, studying under August Boeckh, August Friedrich Pott, and doctoral supervisor Franz Bopp. He held posts at Beheim-Schwarzbach'sche Realschule, Gymnasium Schneidemühl, and as chair of comparative philology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1872).

nodes.label: Otto Blau
nodes.summary: Otto Blau studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1848, under August Friedrich Pott (~1848–1851), and at the University of Leipzig (~1850–1852).

nodes.label: József Budenz
nodes.summary: József Budenz was a linguist who studied at the University of Marburg and under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (Promotion 1858). He served as librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and full professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

nodes.label: August Fick
variants: フリードリヒ・コンラート・アウグスト・フィック
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フィック
nodes.summary: August Fick (1833–1916) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (1852–1856). He later held professorships at the University of Göttingen (from 1876) and the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

nodes.label: Ferdinand Justi
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Justi worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Marburg, where he later served as professor and Rektor (1887–1888).

nodes.label: Ludwig Lange
nodes.summary: Ludwig Lange was a scholar in linguistics and archaeology who studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and at Leipzig. He served as professor of classical philology at Charles University, the University of Giessen, and the University of Leipzig, where he was also rector.

nodes.label: Theodor Nöldeke
nodes.jawiki: テオドール・ネルデケ
nodes.summary: Theodor Nöldeke was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, linguist, and religious studies specialist. He studied at Göttingen, Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin, later serving as professor at Kiel (1864, 1868–1872) and Strasbourg (1872–1906).

nodes.label: John Peile
nodes.summary: John Peile was an Indologist and linguist educated at Christ's College, Cambridge (circa 1856–1860) and under Theodor Benfey (circa 1869). He was a Fellow and Tutor at Christ's College, Cambridge Reader of Comparative Philology, and Newnham College president.

nodes.label: Émile Senart
variants: エミール・シャルル・マリー・スナール
nodes.summary: Senart specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Munich and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, served as professor at the Collège de France, and was president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928).

nodes.label: Ernst Osiander
nodes.summary: Ernst Osiander was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as a Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and at Tübinger Stift.

nodes.label: Carl Siegfried
nodes.summary: Carl Siegfried worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn, and under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He taught at several gymnasiums, held a Sanskrit professorship at Trinity College Dublin, and was professor at Jena (1875–1901).

nodes.label: Julius Euting
nodes.summary: Julius Euting specialized in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Ernst Heinrich Meier and Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Director of the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire (1871, 1900–1909) and professor at Strasbourg (1880).

nodes.label: Matthias von Lexer
nodes.summary: Matthias von Lexer worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Graz and Erlangen-Nuremberg, and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp, later holding posts at St. Anne's Gymnasium, Freiburg, Würzburg (1868), and Munich (1890).

nodes.label: Sophus Bugge
nodes.summary: Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a Norwegian linguist who studied in Oslo, Copenhagen, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He was appointed Professor of Comparative Philology and Old Norse at the University of Oslo in 1866 and held a post at Uppsala (1877).

nodes.label: Angelo De Gubernatis
nodes.summary: Angelo De Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).

nodes.label: Henri Gaidoz
nodes.summary: Henri Gaidoz was a linguist who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber in 1865. He taught geography and ethnography at École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and was Directeur d’études in Celtic philology at École Pratique des Hautes Études (1876).

nodes.label: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug, earning a PhD from Göttingen (1885). He held professorships at Elphinstone College and Deccan College, and was Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893-1894).

nodes.label: Heinrich Hübschmann
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hübschmann (1848–1908) studied linguistics and Iranian studies at Jena, Tübingen, Munich, and Leipzig under August Schleicher and Martin Haug. He held professorships at the University of Leipzig (1876) and the University of Strasbourg (1877).

nodes.label: Julius Jolly
nodes.summary: Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Leipzig, completing his PhD under Martin Haug. He served as Tagore Professor at Calcutta (1882–1883) and long-term professor at the University of Würzburg (1877–1920).

nodes.label: University of Florence
variants: Istituto dei Studi Superiori in Florenz
Istituto degli studii superiori in Florenz
Istituto di studi superiori di Firenze

nodes.label: Trinity College Dublin
variants: ダブリン大学トリニティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Frédéric Baudry
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist Frédéric Baudry studied under Eugène Burnouf (ca. 1845–1852). He worked as a librarian at Versailles (1849) and Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal (1859), and served as administrator of the Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885).

nodes.label: Peter Peterson
nodes.summary: Peter Peterson (1847–1899) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh under Theodor Aufrecht and at Balliol College, Oxford. He served as professor at Elphinstone College (~1873–1899) and Fellow and Registrar at the University of Mumbai (~1881–1899).

nodes.label: James Burgess
nodes.summary: James Burgess was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the universities of Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India from 1873, holding the post of Director General from 1886 to 1889.

nodes.label: Robert Caesar Childers
nodes.summary: Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College, Oxford, and under Yatramulle Dhammarama Thera. He served at the India Office and as Professor of Pali at University College London (~1872–1876).

nodes.label: Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle
nodes.summary: Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as director of Calcutta Madrasa (~1881–1899) and was Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society in 1891.

nodes.label: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
nodes.description: Philosopher, academic, writer, translator, entrepreneur, social reformer and philanthropist (1820-1891)
nodes.summary: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, later serving at Fort William College (1841–1846, 1849), Sanskrit College (1846–1849), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1851).

nodes.label: Austrian Academy of Sciences
variants: kaiserl. Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien
Institute for the Study of Ancient Culture
Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften Institut für Kultur- und Geistesgeschichte Asiens
Austrian Academy of Sciences, Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia
Imperial Academy of Sciences, Vienna (Physical Class)

nodes.label: Malabar Mission
variants: Mission an der Küste von Malabar

nodes.label: Henri Hubert
nodes.summary: Henri Hubert specialized in religious studies and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1927), and the École du Louvre (~1906–1927).

nodes.label: Marcel Mauss
nodes.summary: Marcel Mauss (1872–1950) was a French scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under Émile Durkheim and Sylvain Lévi. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1901–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1940).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Grube
variants: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.summary: Sinologist and linguist Wilhelm Grube studied at Saint Petersburg and Leipzig (PhD 1880) under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Georg von der Gabelentz. He worked at the Asiatic Museum, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1884; 1892).

nodes.label: Karl Florenz
variants: カール・フローレンツ
カール・アドルフ・フローレンツ
nodes.jawiki: カール・フローレンツ
nodes.summary: Karl Florenz specialized in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Georg von der Gabelentz, Ernst Windisch, Friedrich Max Müller, and Tetsujiro Inoue. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut, and University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: University of Tokyo
variants: 東京大学大学院印度哲学専門課程

nodes.label: Fitzedward Hall
nodes.summary: Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard, he held positions at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1850), Sanskrit College and University (1853), King's College London (1862), and the India Office (~1862–1869).

nodes.label: Arthur Berriedale Keith
nodes.summary: Arthur Berriedale Keith was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, worked for the Colonial Office (~1901–1914), and served as a professor at the University of Edinburgh from 1914 to 1944.

nodes.label: Junjirō Takakusu
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist
nodes.summary: Junjirō Takakusu was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Leipzig, and Tokyo under Friedrich Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served as professor and president at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Otto Stein
nodes.summary: Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at Charles University (Dr. phil. 1918) under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He worked at the Oriental Institute in 1929 and served as ordinary professor at Charles University from 1930 to 1939.

nodes.label: Joseph Estlin Carpenter
variants: エストリン・カーペンター
nodes.summary: Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religion who studied at University College School and the University of London. He served as President of Harris Manchester College, Oxford, and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1889–1915).

nodes.label: Robert Chalmers
nodes.description: British civil servant, and Pali and Buddhist scholar (1858-1938)
nodes.summary: Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

nodes.label: Richard Morris
nodes.summary: Richard Morris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at Battersea Training College. He served as headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888) and was Ex-President of the Philological Society (~1871–1874).

nodes.label: Edmund Hardy
nodes.summary: In Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Edmund Hardy studied at Mainz, Heidelberg (PhD under Kuno Fischer), Berlin, and Freiburg. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1885–1893), University of Fribourg (1894–1898), and University of Würzburg (~1894–1904).

nodes.label: Dines Andersen
nodes.summary: Dines Andersen was a Danish Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll. He served at Copenhagen University Library (~1883–1903) and as Professor at Copenhagen University (1903–1927).

nodes.label: W. H. D. Rouse
nodes.summary: W. H. D. Rouse (1863–1950) studied at Cheltenham College, Regent's Park College, and Christ's College, Cambridge. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Bedford School, Cheltenham, and Rugby, and was headmaster of The Perse School (1902–1928).

nodes.label: Sylvain Lévi
nodes.summary: Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Sorbonne under Abel Bergaigne and held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Collège de France.

nodes.label: Louis de La Vallée Poussin
variants: ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
L・ドゥ・ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
Louis Étienne Joseph Marie de La Vallée Poussin
Louis Étienne Joseph Marie de La Vallée-Poussin
nodes.summary: Louis de La Vallée Poussin worked in Buddhist studies and indology. He studied at Liège, KU Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden under Lévi, Kern, Harlez, Colinet, and Henry. He served as professor at Ghent University (1893–1929).

nodes.label: Godefroy de Blonay
nodes.description: Swiss linguist and member of the International Olympic Committee (1869-1937)

nodes.label: Henry Clarke Warren
nodes.summary: Henry Clarke Warren (1854–1899) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Harvard Oriental Series in 1891. He studied at Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, working under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Maurice Bloomfield, and T. W. Rhys Davids.

nodes.label: Vincent Arthur Smith
nodes.image: The Early History of India by Vincent Arthur Smith.jpg
nodes.summary: Vincent Arthur Smith was a historian and Indologist who earned a doctorate from Trinity College Dublin (~1867–1919). He served in the Bengal and Indian Civil Service (1871–1900) and later at the University of Oxford and its Indian Institute (~1910–1920).

nodes.label: Sarat Chandra Das
variants: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.image: Sarat Chandra Das, C.I.E. photo from Journey to Lhasa and Central Tibet (page 10 crop).jpg
nodes.jawiki: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.description: Indian scholar of Tibetan language and culture (1849-1917)
nodes.summary: Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Presidency University and University of Calcutta. He served as Director of Bhutia Boarding School (1874) and as Tibetan translator for the Government of Bengal (1881–1904).

nodes.label: Cecil Bendall
nodes.summary: Cecil Bendall was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and Cambridge.

nodes.label: Unrai Wogihara
nodes.summary: Unrai Wogihara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at the University of Tokyo and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Vasily Radlov
variants: ヴァシーリー・ヴァシーリエヴィチ・ラドロフ
ヴィルヘルム・ラドロフ
nodes.summary: Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Berlin and Jena under Pott, Steinthal, and Schott. He directed the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Kunstkamera (1894–1918), and founded the Russian Museum of Ethnography.

nodes.label: Alexander von Staël-Holstein
variants: Alexander Wilhelm Freiherr Staël von Holstein
nodes.summary: Alexander von Staël-Holstein worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tartu, Berlin, Harvard, and Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1909), Peking University (1918–1929), and the Sino-Indian Institute (c. 1928–1937).

nodes.label: Rudolf Seydel
nodes.summary: Rudolf Seydel was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1855–1858) and subsequently held an academic post there (~1860–1892).

nodes.label: Masaharu Anesaki
nodes.summary: Masaharu Anesaki (1873–1949) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo and Kiel under scholars including Tetsujiro Inoue, Friedrich Max Müller, and Paul Deussen, later serving as professor (from 1904) and library director at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.label: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
variants: G. A. van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.image: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga.jpg
nodes.enwiki: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.dewiki: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies scholar. After studying at Leiden University (1893–1901), he held posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

nodes.label: Richard Fick
nodes.summary: Richard Fick was an Indologist who studied at Kiel University (~1885–1888). He worked at Kiel University Library (1886–1897), the Royal Library of Berlin (1897), and served as head of the Göttingen State and University Library (1921–1932).

nodes.label: Richard Schmidt
nodes.summary: Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Privatdozent at Halle-Wittenberg, librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft, and ordinary professor at Münster (1910).

nodes.label: Helmer Smith
nodes.summary: Helmer Smith worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University and under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, Richard Pischel, and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Dozent at Lund University (1921) and professor at Uppsala University (1936–1947).

nodes.label: Louis Finot
nodes.summary: Louis Finot worked in indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École des chartes and under Sylvain Lévi. He was director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1898) and held posts at the EPHE and Collège de France.

nodes.label: Édouard Huber
nodes.summary: A scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Édouard Huber studied under Johann Baptist Schibenegg and Sylvain Lévi at the Sorbonne, Collège de France, and ENLOV. From 1901 to 1905, he was director of the China and Indochina department at EFEO.

nodes.label: Kaikyoku Watanabe
nodes.summary: Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) studied under Kaitei Hayama and Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho universities, and led Shiba High School.

nodes.label: Robert Gauthiot
nodes.summary: Robert Gauthiot worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1898–1904) and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.

nodes.label: Max Lindenau
nodes.summary: Max Lindenau studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig until 1913.

nodes.label: Ludwig Heller
nodes.summary: Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Kielhorn at Göttingen and habilitated at Greifswald. He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin (1893), the University of Greifswald (1904), and the University of Tartu (1918).

nodes.label: Theodor Zachariae
nodes.summary: Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Sauppe, Theodor Benfey, Georg Curtius, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held posts as professor at the University of Greifswald (1883) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

nodes.label: Hermann Beckh
nodes.summary: Hermann Beckh worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at the Royal Library of Berlin (1908–1916), Humboldt University (1911–1921), and the Kiel Institute for the World Economy.

nodes.label: Theodor Bloch
nodes.summary: Theodor Bloch was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch from around 1888 to 1892. He also studied under Georg Bühler from roughly 1893 to 1895 as a Specialschüler.

nodes.label: Hermann Schlagintweit
nodes.summary: Hermann Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich (~1845–1848). He later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1852 to 1854.

nodes.label: Georg Morgenstierne
variants: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.dewiki: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist who also worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Morgenstierne studied at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin, learning under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Schulze. He held professorships at the University of Gothenburg (1930-1937) and Oslo (1937-1962).

nodes.label: Sten Konow
nodes.summary: Sten Konow was a scholar of indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Oslo, Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, and Berlin. His main posts were at the Archaeological Survey of India, Hamburg, and Oslo.

nodes.label: Frederick William Thomas
nodes.summary: Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Assistant Librarian at the India Office, lectured at University College London and the University of London, and was Boden Professor at Oxford.

nodes.label: Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu
nodes.summary: Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.

nodes.label: Edward Denison Ross
variants: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.image: Edward Denison Ross by John Lavery (1856-1941).jpg
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.summary: Edward Denison Ross was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who studied at UCL and under Theodor Nöldeke at Strasbourg. He held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the National Archives of India, the British Museum, and directed SOAS (1916–1937).

nodes.label: Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan
nodes.summary: Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Krishnagar Government College, Sanskrit College, and University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das, later serving as Principal of Sanskrit College and Joint Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Ganganatha Jha
nodes.summary: Ganganatha Jha was an Indologist and philosopher. After studies at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Allahabad, he served as professor at Muir Central College (1902–1918), principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1918–1923), and vice chancellor of the University of Allahabad (1923–1932).

nodes.label: University of Munich
variants: Institute for Indology and Tibetan Studies at the LMU Munich
Institute for Sinology at LMU Munich

nodes.label: Edward Washburn Hopkins
nodes.summary: Edward Washburn Hopkins studied at Columbia and earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he taught at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1895) before serving as professor at Yale University (1895–1926).

nodes.label: Arthur Coke Burnell
nodes.summary: Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London (~1857–1860). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1860–1880) and examined Sanskrit manuscripts for the Chief Commissioner of Mysore in 1870.

nodes.label: Peter von Bradke
nodes.summary: Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth at Tartu and Tübingen, before earning degrees at Jena and Giessen. He served as an extraordinary professor at the University of Giessen from 1886 to 1896.

nodes.label: George Melville Bolling
variants: ジョージ・M・ボーリング
nodes.summary: George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Loyola University Maryland and completed his doctorate at Johns Hopkins University. He held professorships at the Catholic University of America and Ohio State University, and served as president of the Linguistic Society of America.

nodes.label: S. M. Natesa Sastri
nodes.summary: An Indologist, S. M. Natesa Sastri was educated at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. Around 1884 to 1892, he worked as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Debendranath Tagore
variants: デヴェンドラナート・タゴール

nodes.label: Rabindranath Tagore
variants: ラビンドラナート・タゴール
nodes.jawiki: ラビンドラナート・タゴール
nodes.summary: Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and other fields. He studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School (~1875–1876) and University College London (~1878–1880), and founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.

nodes.label: Arthur Anthony Macdonell
variants: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.summary: Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Tübingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He was a fellow of Balliol College and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1888/1899–1926).

nodes.label: LeRoy Carr Barret
nodes.summary: LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1894–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

nodes.label: Franklin Edgerton
variants: フランクリン・エジャトン
フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.jawiki: フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.summary: Franklin Edgerton worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cornell, Munich, Jena, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Hermann Collitz, he served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Yale University (1926–1953).

nodes.label: Bernhard Geiger
nodes.summary: Bernhard Geiger worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Leopold von Schroeder and Franz Kielhorn across several universities, later holding posts at Vienna (~1909–1938), the Iranian and Tibetan-Iranian Institutes (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

nodes.label: Willibald Kirfel
nodes.summary: Willibald Kirfel (1885–1964) was an Indologist. He earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, working there as a librarian and privatdozent (1920) before becoming full professor (1922).

nodes.label: Robert Zimmermann
nodes.summary: Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin (1908–1913). He served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and led the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Leiden University
variants: Leiden University, Department of Indo-European Comparative Linguistics (VIET)

nodes.label: Friedrich Otto Schrader
nodes.summary: Friedrich Otto Schrader (1876–1961) worked in Indology and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Strasbourg (~1899–1902), directed the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1905–1916), and became a professor at Kiel University in 1921.

nodes.label: Heinrich Lüders
variants: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.summary: Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich and Göttingen, earning his PhD under Franz Kielhorn. He held positions at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, and Kiel, and served as professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1935).

nodes.label: Edward Joseph Thomas
nodes.summary: Edward Joseph Thomas worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet (1896–1901) and studied at Cambridge (~1903–1905), later serving at Cambridge University Library and as Dean of Oriental Languages (~1910–1939).

nodes.label: Shwe Zan Aung
nodes.summary: Shwe Zan Aung (1871-1932) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. at the University of Rangoon in 1891 and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.

nodes.label: Pe Maung Tin
nodes.native: ဖေမောင်တင်
nodes.summary: Pe Maung Tin was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the universities of Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as Professor of Pali and Principal at the University of Rangoon (1912; 1937–1946).

nodes.label: Benimadhab Barua
nodes.description: Bengali Writer, Indologist, and pundit of Pali and Buddhism (1888-1948)
nodes.summary: Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at institutions including the University of Calcutta and the University of London (D.Litt.). He taught at the University of Calcutta as Lektor (1913–1914) and Professor (1918–1948).

nodes.label: Hakuju Ui
nodes.image: Recent portrait of Dr. Hakuju Ui.jpg
nodes.summary: Hakuju Ui (1882–1963) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo, as well as at Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He taught at Tohoku University, Tokyo, and Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Frank Lee Woodward
nodes.summary: Frank Lee Woodward was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Christ's Hospital and Sidney Sussex College under Caroline Rhys Davids, he served as Dekan at Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translated for the Pali Text Society (around 1914–1919).

nodes.label: Theodore Stcherbatsky
nodes.summary: Theodore Stcherbatsky was a specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. He was attested as a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences from 1927 to 1931.

nodes.label: Chimanlal Dahyabhai Dalal
nodes.description: Sanskrit scholar and librarian of the Central Library in Baroda

nodes.label: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar
nodes.summary: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta, Presidency University, and other colleges. He held posts at the universities of Calcutta, Dhaka, Chicago, and Pennsylvania, served as principal at BHU, and presided over the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: A. B. Gajendragadkar
nodes.summary: An Indology scholar, he served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

nodes.label: S. Kuppuswami Sastri
nodes.summary: An Indologist and philosopher, S. Kuppuswami Sastri studied at St. Peter's College, Tanjore, and the University of Madras, alongside traditional teachers Brahmendra Sarasvati and Nilakanta Sastri. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and later as Professor at Presidency College.

nodes.summary: Vishva Bandhu was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Founder-Principal of Dayanand Brahma Mahavidyalaya (1921), Director of Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College (1934), and long-time Director of the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute (~1934–1973).

nodes.summary: Klaus Wille is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He has worked as a researcher at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2026) and cataloged manuscripts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Seishi Karashima
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, Karashima studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including von Hinüber and Ji Xianlin. He held posts at the Eastern Institute and Soka University (~1996–2019).

nodes.label: Florinda De Simini
nodes.summary: Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Turin (~2009–2013). She has held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies (2013), the University of Hamburg (~2015–2016), and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2016).

nodes.summary: Vincenzo Vergiani is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Raffaele Torella (~1995–2001). He held positions at the University of Cambridge as Professor of Sanskrit (~2010) and as project head (~2011–2015).

nodes.label: Elena Mucciarelli
nodes.summary: Elena Mucciarelli works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Tübingen, she held a post there (2016–2017) before becoming Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition and Gonda Lecturer at the University of Groningen in 2020.

nodes.label: Francesco Sferra
nodes.summary: Francesco Sferra is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella. He has held appointments at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" as professor (circa 2002) and director (circa 2020), and at University of Naples Federico II.

nodes.label: K. Sambasiva Sastri
nodes.summary: K. Sambasiva Sastri (1879–1946) was an Indology scholar. Succeeding T. Ganapati Sastri, he served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library from around 1925 to 1934.

nodes.label: C. Kunhan Raja
nodes.summary: C. Kunhan Raja was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. In 1927, he became the first University Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Madras, and later directed the Adyar Library.

nodes.label: K. Madhava Krishna Sarma
nodes.summary: K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was an Indologist who was a research student under C. Kunhan Raja. He was affiliated with the Adyar Library and Research Centre and served as curator of the Anup Sanskrit Library (attested 1946).

nodes.label: Lily de Silva
nodes.summary: Lily de Silva worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Julius Berugoda (attested 1970) and M. Sri Rammandala, and held posts at the University of Ceylon (attested 1970 and 2008).

nodes.label: University of Ceylon
variants: Department of Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon

nodes.label: Madeleine Biardeau
nodes.summary: Madeleine Biardeau (1922–2010) was an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at ENS de Sèvres and under K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. She served as Professor of Indian Religions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989).

nodes.label: Isaline Blew Horner
nodes.summary: Isaline Blew Horner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Newnham College and Cambridge under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held posts at Newnham College (1918, 1923), Cambridge (1939–1949), and the Pali Text Society (1942, 1959–1981).

nodes.label: Heramba Chandra Chackravarty
nodes.summary: Heramba Chandra Chackravarty is an Indologist who studied under Manindra Mohan Bose. He served as a Lecturer at City College, Kolkata, attested in 1977.

nodes.label: Nalinaksha Dutt
nodes.summary: Nalinaksha Dutt was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Chittagong College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta (Ph.D.), and University of London (D.Litt). He served as Head of Pali at Calcutta (~1923–1958) and President of The Asiatic Society (1959–1961).

nodes.label: Mysore Hiriyanna
nodes.description: Indian philosopher, Sanskrit scholar and authority on Indian aesthetics
nodes.summary: Mysore Hiriyanna was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Madras Christian College under Perisamy Tirumalacharya and Kashi Sesharamasastry, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College and the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

nodes.label: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
variants: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.image: Photograph of Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan presented to First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy in 1962.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.description: 2nd President and 1st Vice President of India, Indian philosopher and politician (1888–1975)
nodes.summary: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975), a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religion, studied at Madras Christian College and University of Madras. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu Universities and Chancellor of Delhi.

nodes.label: Alex Watson
nodes.summary: Alex Watson is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Oxford and SOAS, supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Harvard University as Preceptor in Sanskrit, and Ashoka University.

nodes.label: Kei Kataoka
nodes.summary: Kei Kataoka specializes in Indology and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo and National Sanskrit University, he held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, the University of Tokyo, Fukuoka University, and Kyushu University, where he became a professor.

nodes.label: Hanazono University
variants: 花園大學社會福祉學科
International Research Institute for Zen Studies, Hanazono University

nodes.label: Seizan Yanagida
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Yanagida studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto Universities under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu. He held posts at Hanazono University (1949–1995), Kyoto University (1976–1986), and Chubu University (~1988–1994).

nodes.label: Katsumi Okimoto
nodes.summary: Katsumi Okimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as professor, director, and professor emeritus at Hanazono University between roughly 1986 and 2014.

nodes.label: Masaaki Hattori
nodes.summary: Masaaki Hattori (b. 1924) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta, he taught at Kyoto University (1961–1988) and served as dean of letters at Hanazono University (~1994–1996).

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale
nodes.summary: Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (1901–1991) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn. He held professorships at Fergusson College and the University of Delhi, and taught at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Kemo Jin
nodes.summary: Kemo Jin was an Indologist, Sinologist, and linguist. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and became Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

nodes.label: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi
nodes.summary: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Harvard under George David Birkhoff and held mathematics professorships at Banaras Hindu University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.

nodes.label: Jambuvijaya
nodes.description: Jain monk from India who edited Jain ancient literature

nodes.label: Leonard van der Kuijp
variants: Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp
nodes.summary: Leonard van der Kuijp is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. and D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He taught at the University of Washington and became Department Chair at Harvard University in 1995.

nodes.label: Peter Schwabland
nodes.summary: Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed an M.A. at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp in 1994.

nodes.label: Lambert Schmithausen
variants: L. シュミットハウゼン
ランベルト・シュミットハウゼン
nodes.jawiki: ランベルト・シュミットハウゼン
nodes.summary: Lambert Schmithausen worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1959–1963) and Paul Hacker (~1963–1966). He served as an associate professor at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and on the Advisory Board at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

nodes.label: Karin Preisendanz
nodes.summary: Karin Preisendanz is an Indologist and philosopher who completed her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held positions at the University of British Columbia (1990–1993) and became a professor at the University of Vienna in 1999.

nodes.label: Anne MacDonald
nodes.summary: Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, having studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, Lambert Schmithausen, and Karin Preisendanz. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and Vienna.

nodes.label: David P. Jackson
variants: ディヴィッド・ポール・ジャクソン
nodes.summary: David P. Jackson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. He served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg from 1992 to 2007.

nodes.label: Kazuo Kano
nodes.summary: Kazuo Kano (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned degrees at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg, holding posts at Hamburg, Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Michael Zimmermann
variants: ミヒャエル・ツィンマーマン
nodes.summary: Michael Zimmermann is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hamburg (~1993–2000) and studied at Soka University. He held positions at Stanford University (2003) and Hamburg (~2007) as professor and director.

nodes.label: Stanford University
variants: Zentrum für biomedizinische Ethik der Universität Stanford

nodes.label: Lourens P. van den Bosch
nodes.summary: Lourens P. van den Bosch worked in indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Groningen (1965–1971) and Utrecht University (~1970–1978) under Jan Gonda and other teachers, and held an assistant post at Groningen (1968–1971).

nodes.label: Johannes Hendrik Hospers
nodes.description: professor of Semitic languages and archaeology of the Near East, Groningen University (1921-1993)

nodes.label: Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld
nodes.summary: Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld specialized in Indology. He studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

nodes.label: Gerald James Larson
nodes.summary: Gerald James Larson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, later serving as professor at UC Santa Barbara and Rabindranath Tagore Professor Emeritus at Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Toru Funayama
nodes.summary: Toru Funayama is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner (1991–1992). He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

nodes.label: Sara L. McClintock
nodes.summary: Sara L. McClintock is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied at Columbia, Lausanne, CIHTS, and Harvard (PhD 2002), working with Tom Tillemans, among others, and held faculty posts at UW–Madison (attested 2003) and Emory (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Virendra Kumar Varma
nodes.summary: Virendra Kumar Varma is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under traditional teachers Ramnath Dixit and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and later taught Kamala Prasad Tripathi.

nodes.label: William L. Ames
nodes.summary: William L. Ames works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Caltech and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Collett Cox, later holding posts at Washington, California Institute of Integral Studies, and JFK University.

nodes.label: David Seyfort Ruegg
nodes.summary: David Seyfort Ruegg specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at EPHE under Jean Filliozat and Louis Renou, he held chairs and professorships at Leiden University (1966–1972), the University of Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1993–1996).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Hopkins
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Hopkins was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and the 14th Dalai Lama, earning a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968-1972). He served at the University of Virginia (1973-2005).

nodes.label: Anne Carolyn Klein
nodes.summary: Anne Carolyn Klein is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia (PhD), training under Jeffrey Hopkins and several Tibetan masters. She held posts at Harvard (~1984–1985) and Rice University (~1987), where she chaired religious studies.

nodes.label: John D. Dunne
nodes.summary: John D. Dunne works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel. His appointments include Emory University (~2005–2016) and a Distinguished Chair at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999).

He held posts at the EPHE, EFEO, Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan, Commission Archéologique de l'Indochine, and University of Paris.

nodes.label: Sergey Oldenburg
variants: セルゲイ・フョードロウィッチ・オルデンブルク

nodes.description: Russian scholar of Sanskrit and Buddhism (1863-1934)
nodes.summary: Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University, head of the Russian Academy of Sciences, and director of the Asiatic Museum.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Errington
nodes.description: specialist on the archaeology of Gandhara and the collections of Charles Masson, and a numismatist specialising in Asian coins
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Errington specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studies at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar, she served as curator of South and Central Asian pre-Islamic coins at the British Museum from 1993.

nodes.label: Shailendra Bhandare
nodes.summary: Shailendra Bhandare is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He held posts as a curator at the British Museum, a fellow at Fitzwilliam Museum and St Cross College, and Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022).

nodes.label: Joe Cribb
nodes.summary: Joe Cribb (born 1947) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of London and Queen Mary University (~1967–1970), he served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010).

nodes.label: Daud Ali
nodes.summary: Daud Ali is an Indologist and historian educated at William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS University of London (~1995–2008) and became associate professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.

nodes.label: T. Ganapati Sastri
nodes.summary: T. Ganapati Sastri (1860–1926) was an Indologist who earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Tübingen (c. 1924). He served as Curator of the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library and Editor of the Trivandrum Sanskrit Series (c. 1908–1925).

nodes.label: Martin Delhey
nodes.summary: Martin Delhey is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (-2002). He has held posts at Hamburg, Göttingen, Ryukoku, Shandong, and IIBS.

nodes.label: S. Bhaskaran Nair
nodes.summary: S. Bhaskaran Nair worked in Indology at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, where he held posts as general editor (attested 1944, 1992) and deputy director (attested 1974–1977, 1986).

nodes.label: Hirananda Sastri
nodes.summary: Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at DAV College and Oriental College, he served with the Archaeological Survey of India, as Government Epigraphist, and as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State (1934–1942).

nodes.label: Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti, an epigraphist and Indologist, studied at Calcutta, Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as Government Epigraphist and later as Director General of Archaeology in India (1948–1950).

nodes.label: John A. Ardussi
nodes.summary: John A. Ardussi works in Tibetology and history/archaeology, having studied under MA supervisor Turrell V. Wylie and earned a PhD from Australian National University. His career includes posts at ELDEC Corporation and the CNRS.

nodes.label: Karma Ura
nodes.summary: Karma Ura is a historian and Tibetologist who studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.

nodes.label: Arthur Llewellyn Basham
nodes.summary: Arthur Llewellyn Basham was a historian and Indologist who studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He served as Professor at SOAS and the University of London, and later headed the Asian Civilizations department at Australian National University (~1965–1978).

nodes.label: Lionel David Barnett
nodes.summary: Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist educated at Liverpool and Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), as Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1906–1917), and Lecturer at SOAS (1917–1948).

nodes.label: Knut A. Jacobsen
nodes.summary: Knut A. Jacobsen (born 1956) works in religious studies and Indology. After earning his PhD at UC Santa Barbara (~1990–1994), he held professorships at the University of Bergen (from 1996) and the University of Oslo (~1996–1999).

nodes.label: Angelika Malinar
nodes.summary: Angelika Malinar (b. 1961) works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Tübingen, and has held posts at the Free University of Berlin, SOAS University of London, and the University of Zurich.

nodes.label: Vasudha Narayanan
nodes.summary: Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned degrees from the universities of Madras, Mumbai, and Harvard. She founded the University of Florida, where she became Distinguished Professor of Religion around 1982.

nodes.label: R. T. Vyas
nodes.summary: R. T. Vyas is an Indologist who served as General Editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1988) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1993–1994).

nodes.label: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Calcutta and Dhaka universities. He served as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1927) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1927–1952).

nodes.label: P. H. Joshi
nodes.summary: P. H. Joshi is an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, attested between 1976 and 1988, with affiliation further attested in 2002.

nodes.label: Gerhard Oberhammer
variants: G. オーバーハンマー
nodes.summary: Gerhard Oberhammer worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Innsbruck and the Sorbonne under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan, subsequently holding positions at Utrecht University and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Heinz Bechert
variants: ハインツ・ベッヘルト

nodes.summary: Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz, learning under Ernst Waldschmidt and Erich Frauwallner. After assistant and docent posts, he served as Chair of Indology at Göttingen (1965–2000).

nodes.label: Gustav Roth
nodes.summary: Gustav Roth was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several universities, earning his doctorate at Munich (1949–1952) and studying at Patna (1952–1956). He served at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

nodes.label: Syed Hasan Askari
nodes.summary: Syed Hasan Askari was a historian and Indologist who studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University. He served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.

ジャヤスヴァル研究所

nodes.label: Madhusudan Kaul Shastri
nodes.summary: Madhusudan Kaul Shastri was an Indologist. He served as Superintendent of the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1918–1934 and 1943–1945).

nodes.label: Pushpendra Kumar
nodes.summary: Pushpendra Kumar, an Indologist who studied under Satya Vrat Shastri, served as a Sanskrit lecturer at the University of Delhi (~1965–2001) and as Principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Raja Ram Shastri
nodes.summary: Raja Ram Shastri (1904–1991) worked in Indology. He served as a Member of the Lok Sabha from circa 1971 to 1977 and was attested as Chairman of the Managing Committee at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University in 1976.

nodes.label: Hiram W. Woodward
nodes.summary: Hiram W. Woodward (b. 1940) specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and Yale, he held academic posts at Silpakorn, Michigan, and Vermont, and served as curator of Asian art at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

nodes.label: Charles Henry Tawney
nodes.summary: Charles Henry Tawney (1837–1922) was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1856–1860). He held posts at Trinity College (1860), Presidency University (1866–1872, 1875–1892), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1880), and the India Office Library (1892/1893–1903).

nodes.label: Louis Renou
nodes.summary: Louis Renou was an indologist and linguist. He studied at the Sorbonne, ENLOV, and EPHE under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch. He held professorships and directorships at the University of Lyon, the University of Paris/Sorbonne, and EPHE.

nodes.label: Jean Filliozat
nodes.summary: Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He served at EPHE, held a chair at Collège de France (1951–1978), and directed both the EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

nodes.label: Richard Hauschild
nodes.summary: Richard Hauschild was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Jena, and Tübingen under Johannes Hertel and Albert Debrunner. He spent his career at the University of Jena, serving as Lektor (1938) and professor (1951–1967).

nodes.label: Albert Debrunner
nodes.summary: Albert Debrunner was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Jacob Wackernagel and Ferdinand Sommer. He held professorships at the universities of Zurich, Greifswald, Bern, Jena, and Basel.

nodes.label: Noriyuki Kudo
nodes.summary: Noriyuki Kudo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University, where he also lectured (attested 1999–2000), he served as associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2026).

nodes.label: Lore Sander
nodes.summary: Lore Sander (born 1936) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1960–1967) and held positions at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and Free University of Berlin (1994).

nodes.label: Toshihiro Wada
nodes.summary: Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as a professor at Nagoya University from circa 1989 to 2020.

nodes.label: Junsho Kato
nodes.summary: Junsho Kato works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Juntaka Kato, Akira Hirakawa, Hajime Nakamura, and Étienne Lamotte, earning a PhD from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha, Reitaku, and Nagoya universities.

nodes.label: Musashi Tachikawa

nodes.label: Johannes Bronkhorst
nodes.summary: Johannes Bronkhorst works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Pune (PhD under S. D. Joshi, ~1976–1979) and Leiden (doctorate ~1979–1980). He held posts at the Kern Institute (~1980–1987) and Lausanne (1987–2011; ~1987–2025).

nodes.label: K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar

nodes.summary: K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar (1880–1960) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Between approximately 1935 and 1938, he served as Principal of Banaras Hindu University and Central Hindu College.

nodes.label: Thinlay Ram Shashni
nodes.summary: Thinlay Ram Shashni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. At the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, he served as an editor (attested 1997, 2007) and as Associate Professor, IN-charge/HoD (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Marion Rastelli
nodes.summary: Marion Rastelli works in Indology and religious studies. She completed her doctoral studies under Gerhard Oberhammer and has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2019) and the University of Vienna as a lecturer (attested 2020–2026).

nodes.label: Peter C. Bisschop
nodes.summary: Peter C. Bisschop (born 1972) is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Groningen under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He was a lecturer at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010) and an editor at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Nirajan Kafle
nodes.summary: Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop. He held posts at the Nepal Research Centre, the University of Naples "L'Orientale", and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Timothy Lubin
nodes.summary: Timothy Lubin is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1994. He has held positions at Washington and Lee University (attested 2012–2020) and collaborated on the DHARMA project.

nodes.label: John Forbes Watson

nodes.label: Piotr Balcerowicz
nodes.summary: Piotr Balcerowicz is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his degrees from the University of Warsaw, Banaras Hindu University, the University of Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences. He has held professorships at SWPS University and the University of Warsaw.

nodes.label: Marek Mejor
nodes.summary: Marek Mejor is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He held a junior research fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982), and served as a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

nodes.label: Charles Willemen

nodes.label: Akira Yuyama
nodes.summary: Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts, Leiden, and ANU under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later directing the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Popatbhai Ambashankar Mankad
nodes.summary: Popatbhai Ambashankar Mankad was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. His career included serving as State Engineer in Junagadh, Chief Engineer for Jodhpur State, and Chief Officer and Engineer for the Hyderabad Municipality.

nodes.label: Luise Hercus
nodes.summary: Luise Hercus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Anne's College and Australian National University. She taught at St Anne's College, held a fellowship at the University of Adelaide, and was a Sanskrit lecturer at Australian National University (c. 1969–1991).

nodes.label: Tissa Rajapatirana
nodes.summary: Tissa Rajapatirana (1933–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1966–1974) under Jan Willem de Jong. He later worked in ANU's Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Yasuo Matsunami
nodes.summary: Yasuo Matsunami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1992–2006) and as an advisor to the Śrāvakabhūmi Study Group.

nodes.label: Hisao Takahashi
nodes.summary: Hisao Takahashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He spent his career at Taisho University as an assistant (c. 1974–1982), lecturer (c. 1989–1996), and professor (c. 1996–2015).

nodes.label: Takayuki Hirosawa

nodes.label: Ryosho Hayashi
nodes.summary: Ryosho Hayashi worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, studying at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He spent his career at Taisho University, becoming a professor in 1975, dean of literature in 1981, and president from 1990 to 1994.

nodes.label: Huimin

nodes.label: Shunkyo Katsumata

nodes.label: Kyosho Hayashima

nodes.label: Minoru Hara
