nodes.summary: Shun'ei Hirai (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He spent his career at Komazawa University, serving as professor, vice president in 1986, and later professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Komazawa University
variants: 駒沢大学仏教学部仏教学科

nodes.label: Yoshihide Yoshizu
nodes.summary: Yoshihide Yoshizu was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto, later becoming a professor there in 2001 and conducting research at the University of Virginia in 1985.

nodes.label: Noriaki Hakamaya
nodes.summary: Noriaki Hakamaya specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served as professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011) and Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006).

nodes.label: So Takahashi
nodes.summary: So Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He served at Meijo University as an associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and professor (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Asatoshi Kamiya
nodes.summary: Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973) and served as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin High School (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Dwarikadas Shastri
nodes.summary: Dwarikadas Shastri was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Bauddhadarśanācārya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He founded Bauddha Bharati and served as a joint editor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

nodes.label: K. V. Ramesh
nodes.summary: K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Epigraphical Society of India, Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (1981–1987), and Honorary Director at ORI Mysore (2012).

nodes.label: Bahadur Chand Chhabra
nodes.summary: Bahadur Chand Chhabra specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University, he held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966), Government Epigraphist for India (~1945–1953), and Panjab University (~1965–1973).

nodes.label: P. Swaminathan
nodes.summary: P. Swaminathan is an Indologist who earned an M.Litt. at the University of Madras under V. Raghavan in 1956. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at the National Sanskrit University, attested in 1965.

nodes.label: Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala
nodes.summary: Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala (1904–1967) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and Lucknow. He curated the Mathura Museum, directed the State Museum Lucknow, was Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India, and founded the Prakrit Text Society.

nodes.id: I:Sanskrit-Wörterbuch der buddhistischen Texte aus den Turfan-Funden
nodes.label: Sanskrit-Wörterbuch der buddhistischen Texte aus den Turfan-Funden
variants: Sanskrit-Worterbuch der buddhistischen Texte aus den Turfan-Funden

nodes.label: Michael Schmidt
nodes.summary: Michael Schmidt worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held dictionary and staff positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1979, 1992, 2008) and worked with the KOHD project and University of Göttingen.

nodes.label: E. Gene Smith
nodes.summary: E. Gene Smith was a Tibetologist who studied at Adelphi, Hobart and William Smith, University of Utah, and University of Washington under Turrell V. Wylie. He worked at the Library of Congress and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (~1999–2010).

nodes.label: Sam van Schaik
nodes.summary: Sam van Schaik is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Manchester. He has held positions at SOAS University of London and the British Library as Head of the Endangered Archives Programme.

nodes.label: Lama Jampa Thaye
nodes.summary: Lama Jampa Thaye is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester and studied under Karma Thinley Rinpoche, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and the 16th Karmapa, later joining the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute faculty.

nodes.label: Karma Thinley Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who served as abbot at the Young Lamas Home School around 1962 and at Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

nodes.label: Susan Whitfield
nodes.summary: Susan Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology. After completing her PhD at SOAS (1995), she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and became Professor at the University of East Anglia.

nodes.label: Imre Galambos
nodes.description: Scholar of medieval Chinese and Tangut manuscripts
nodes.summary: Imre Galambos works in Sinology, Central Asian studies, and history. After degrees from ELTE and UC Berkeley, he worked at the British Library (2002–2012) and Cambridge (2012–2023), later holding posts at Hamburg and Zhejiang University (~2023).

nodes.label: B. N. K. Sharma
nodes.summary: B. N. K. Sharma specialized in Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from the University of Madras and Presidency College, Chennai, and studied under Satyadhyana Tirtha. His career included posts at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, and Ramnarain Ruia College.

nodes.label: Radha Burnier
nodes.summary: Radha Burnier (1923–2013) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at Kalakshetra and Banaras Hindu University, and served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1954–1980).

nodes.label: K. Kunjunni Raja
nodes.summary: K. Kunjunni Raja was an Indologist and linguist who earned PhDs from the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja and the University of London under John Brough. In 1951, he became Professor and Head of Sanskrit at Madras.

nodes.label: Arvind Sharma
nodes.summary: Arvind Sharma is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard Divinity School. He held posts at the University of Queensland (1976), the University of Sydney (1980), and was appointed Birks Chair in Comparative Religion at McGill University in 1994.

nodes.label: Katherine K. Young
nodes.summary: Katherine K. Young is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. She earned an M.A. from the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. from McGill University, where she became a professor around 1978.

nodes.label: Masahiro Inami
nodes.summary: Masahiro Inami (b. 1960) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Hiroshima University and held teaching posts at Tokyo Gakugei University (attested ~1993 and ~2008).

nodes.label: Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Academy of Sciences of the USSR
Russische Akademie der Wissenschaften in Sankt Petersburg
russische kaiserliche Akademie der Wissenschaften in St. Petersburg
Russische Akademie der Wissenschaften in St. Petersburg

nodes.label: Otto Rosenberg
variants: オットー・ローゼンベルグ
オットー・カール・ユリウス・ローゼンベルク
nodes.jawiki: オットー・カール・ユリウス・ローゼンベルク
nodes.summary: Otto Rosenberg specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology. He studied at St. Petersburg and Bonn under Theodore Stcherbatsky, Sergey Oldenburg, Hermann Jacobi, and Rudolf Lange. He held a professorship at Saint Petersburg State University from 1911 to 1919.

nodes.label: Albrecht Wezler
variants: アルブレヒト・ヴェッツラー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist and philosopher who completed his doctorate at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1965) under Paul Thieme. He served as a director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and the Nepal Research Centre (1982–2004).

nodes.label: Wolfgang Morgenroth
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Morgenroth was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD under Richard Hauschild at the University of Jena and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He held posts at Jena, Greifswald, and Humboldt University of Berlin, later visiting Pune and Potsdam.

nodes.label: Dominic Goodall
nodes.summary: Dominic Goodall is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at Wolfson College, Oxford, and at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2000).

nodes.label: Diwakar Acharya
variants: ディヴァーカル・アーチャーリヤ
nodes.summary: Diwakar Acharya is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler. His posts include Kyoto University (2006–2016) and a professorship and fellowship at the University of Oxford from 2016.

nodes.label: S. A. S. Sarma
nodes.summary: S. A. S. Sarma is an Indologist who held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2004 and 2024.

nodes.label: Wolfson College, Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学 ウルフソン校
ウォルフソン・カレッジ

nodes.label: N. R. Bhatt
nodes.summary: N. R. Bhatt was an Indology scholar who held positions at the French Institute of Pondicherry and was a member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 1966).

nodes.label: Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat
nodes.summary: Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (1936–2024) was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the EFEO and French Institute of Pondicherry (1963–1967), the École Pratique des Hautes Études as Chair of Sanskrit (1967–2004), and was President of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (2010).

nodes.label: Colette Caillat
nodes.description: French professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar (1921–2007)
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Colette Caillat studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at the CNRS (~1956–1966), University of Lyon (1960–1966), Sorbonne (1967–1988), and directed the Institut de civilisation indienne (~1972–1990).

nodes.label: François Gros
nodes.summary: François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon from around 1951 to 1956. He served as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1977 to 2002.

nodes.label: Michael Hahn
nodes.summary: Michael Hahn (1941–2014) was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He held major posts at the University of Bonn and the University of Marburg.

nodes.label: Raffaele Torella
nodes.summary: Raffaele Torella (b. 1950) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raniero Gnoli (~1970–1974). He served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome (~1981–2020) and was Direttore responsabile of Rivista degli Studi Orientali (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Sapienza University of Rome
variants: Oriental School of the University of Rome
Università degli Studi di Roma "La Sapienza"

nodes.label: Jan-Ulrich Sobisch
nodes.summary: Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche. He held a professorship at the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006) and worked at Hamburg and Munich.

nodes.label: G. V. Srinivasa Rao
nodes.summary: G. V. Srinivasa Rao worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Senior Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945, later retiring as Senior Epigraphical Assistant for the Government Epigraphist for India.

nodes.label: Paul Harrison
variants: Paul HARRISON ポール・ハリソン
nodes.description: academic in religious studies at Stanford
nodes.summary: Paul Harrison works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Auckland (MA 1970–1976) and the Australian National University (PhD ~1974–1979 under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana), later holding posts at Auckland, Canterbury, and Stanford.

nodes.label: Harry Falk
nodes.summary: Harry Falk is an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gaya Charan Tripathi. He taught at the University of Freiburg (~1980–1990) and served as professor and director at the Free University of Berlin from 1993 to 2012.

nodes.label: Ingo Strauch
nodes.summary: Ingo Strauch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Free University of Berlin in 2000. He held a post at Free University of Berlin (attested 2008) and became a professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa
nodes.summary: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions at Taisho University as a researcher, specially appointed lecturer, and instructor, as well as a visiting post at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Jundo Nagashima
nodes.summary: Jundo Nagashima is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams, also studying under Seitatsu Matsunami and Alexis Sanderson. He has held research and lecturer posts at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Joseph A. Marino
nodes.summary: Joseph A. Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox. He was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mark Allon
nodes.summary: Mark Allon specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman (~1990–1994), he worked at SOAS (~1994–1998) and became an Associate Professor at the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: Oskar von Hinüber
nodes.summary: Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist Oskar von Hinüber studied at Mainz, Tübingen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg, and under Paul Thieme. He held positions at Mainz (1965–1981) and Freiburg (Chair in Indic Studies, 1981–2006), and directed the Nepal Research Centre.

nodes.label: Rupert Gethin
nodes.summary: Rupert Gethin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. He held posts at the University of Bristol (from 1987), the Pali Text Society, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Camillo Alessio Formigatti
nodes.summary: Camillo Alessio Formigatti studied at Milan and completed a PhD at Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and Jürgen Hanneder. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he held posts at SOAS, Cambridge, Oxford, the Bodleian Library, and Hamburg.

nodes.label: Osamu Hayashima
nodes.summary: Osamu Hayashima, a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg (1992). He held posts at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Hans T. Bakker
nodes.description: b. 1948; teaches Sanskrit, Philosophy, and Indian Religions, U. of Groningen
nodes.summary: Hans T. Bakker, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied under Jacob Ensink (~1970–1984). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1988–1996) and the University of Groningen (~1996–2013), and served as a curator at the British Museum (2014).

nodes.id: I:Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region

variants: Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region
Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (series)

nodes.label: Lhagpa Phuntshogs
nodes.summary: Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991) and as secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), becoming Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center in 2000.

nodes.label: Dramdul
nodes.summary: Dramdul works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Director of the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2004–2012) and editor in chief of Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013–2020).

nodes.label: Pascale Hugon
nodes.summary: Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2006), University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), and Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Toshikazu Watanabe
nodes.summary: Toshikazu Watanabe works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011–2015) and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

nodes.label: Kokugakuin University
variants: Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics at Kokugakuin University
國學院大學文学部哲学科

nodes.label: Takashi Iwata
nodes.summary: Takashi Iwata is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg, and served as associate professor (~1985–1990) and professor (~1990–2014) at Waseda University.

nodes.label: J. S. Negi
nodes.summary: J. S. Negi is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi, conducted research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University around 1977, and served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Geshe Ngawang Samten
nodes.summary: Geshe Ngawang Samten studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1980) and Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1980–1990). Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he served as Chief Editor at CIHTS (~1987–2021) alongside several visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Lata Deokar
nodes.summary: Lata Deokar works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She served as a Research Assistant at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2001–2004) and as Visiting Faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Toshiki Osada
nodes.summary: Toshiki Osada is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1974–1978). He held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1991–2003) and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2020).

nodes.label: Toshifumi Goto
nodes.summary: Toshifumi Goto is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982. He studied under Karl Hoffmann, Johanna Narten, and others, later serving as professor at Osaka University and Tohoku University.

nodes.label: Osaka University

大阪大学文学部大学院

nodes.label: Tomoyasu Oshima
nodes.summary: Tomoyasu Oshima works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto (attested 2012) and served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Naoko Nishimura
nodes.summary: Naoko Nishimura is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She earned her PhD at Tohoku University (1993–2002) under Toshifumi Goto, Hirofumi Isoda, and Shinkan Murakami, and later served there as a specialized researcher (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Peter Schreiner
nodes.summary: Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Paul Hacker at Münster (1972) and his Habilitation at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, SOAS, and the University of Zurich, becoming Professor Emeritus (~2010).

nodes.label: August Hjalmar Edgren
nodes.summary: August Hjalmar Edgren (1840–1903) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and under William Dwight Whitney at Yale. He taught at Yale, Lund, and Nebraska-Lincoln, and served as Rector of the University of Gothenburg (1891–1893).

nodes.label: Kenji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University and under doctoral supervisors Diwakar Acharya and Yuko Yokochi. He held posts at Kyoto University and as a fellow at the University of Naples Federico II.

nodes.label: Somadeva Vasudeva
nodes.summary: Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who earned a PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Columbia University as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit, and Kyoto University as a visiting scholar.

nodes.label: Andrey Klebanov
nodes.summary: Andrey Klebanov specializes in Indology and linguistics. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, held posts at Hamburg (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2018–2021), and taught Kenji Takahashi.

nodes.label: James L. Fitzgerald
nodes.summary: James L. Fitzgerald (born 1948) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Edwin Gerow and J. A. B. van Buitenen, holding faculty posts at the University of Tennessee and Brown University.

nodes.label: Yuto Kawamura
nodes.summary: Yuto Kawamura specializes in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), Kyoto University as a postdoc (2015–2018), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

nodes.label: John J. Makransky
nodes.summary: Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under numerous teachers, including Lobsang Tendzin and Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Boston College, and Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Ram Shankar Tripathi
nodes.summary: Ram Shankar Tripathi worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He headed the Buddhist philosophy department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1974-1998) and served as Dean of the Faculty of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1998-2004).

nodes.label: Sempa Dorje
nodes.summary: Sempa Dorje is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1977, 1990–1998).

nodes.label: Lobsang Tenzin
variants: Gyurme Kensur Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tenzin
nodes.summary: Lobsang Tenzin (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Drepung Monastery. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987), director of CIHTS (1988–2001), and Chancellor of Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.

nodes.label: Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College (~1934–1952), Sanskrit College and University (1952), and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Shiv Nath Sharma
nodes.summary: Shiv Nath Sharma worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1947) and as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).

nodes.label: Anukul Chandra Banerjee
nodes.summary: Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calcutta under Nalinaksha Dutt and Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, later chairing Pali there and directing the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Prabodh Chandra Bagchi
nodes.summary: Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1898–1956) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist who completed a doctorate at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi. He held professorships at the University of Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Jean Przyluski
nodes.description: French linguist and scholar of religion
nodes.summary: Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer. He held professorships at INALCO, EPHE, and Collège de France.

nodes.label: Paul Pelliot
variants: ポール・ユジェーヌ・ペリオ
nodes.summary: Paul Pelliot studied in Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. An expert in Sinology, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies, he taught at EFEO (1900) and held the Central Asian chair at Collège de France (1911–1945).

nodes.label: Reinhold Grünendahl
nodes.summary: Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983–1984) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Sanskrit College and University
variants: Department of Post Graduate Training and Research, Sanskrit College, Calcutta
Department of Postgraduate Training and Research, Sanskrit College, Calcutta

nodes.label: Kali Kinkar Datta
nodes.summary: Kali Kinkar Datta (1905–1982) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Honorary Director (1959–1966) and Joint Director (1987) of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute and as Vice-Chancellor of Patna University (1973).

nodes.label: Anant Sadashiv Altekar
nodes.description: historian, archaeologist, and numismatist from Maharashtra, India
nodes.summary: Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He served as professor and department head at Banaras Hindu University (1930–1952), university professor at Patna University (1952–1959), and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

nodes.label: Amarasvar Thakur
nodes.summary: Amarasvar Thakur was an Indologist who served as General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series and held a post at the University of Calcutta, attested in 1936.

nodes.label: Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who served as General Editor for the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and as a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

nodes.label: Indiana University Bloomington
variants: Inner Asian and Uralic National Resource Center
Indiana University Research Institute for Inner Asian Studies
Department of Central Eurasian Studies at Indiana University

nodes.label: Charles Ramble
nodes.summary: Charles Ramble (b. 1957) studied at Durham and Oxford under Michael Aris. Active in Tibetology and religious studies, he held posts at Tribhuvan University, Oxford (2000–2009), the University of Chicago (2008), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2009).

nodes.label: Gareth Sparham
nodes.summary: Gareth Sparham is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar, later teaching Tibetan language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

nodes.label: Ashok Aklujkar
nodes.summary: Ashok Aklujkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (c. 1965–1970), later serving in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

nodes.label: David Reigle
nodes.description: author and an independent scholar of Sanskrit scriptures of India and their Tibetan translation
nodes.summary: David Reigle works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and was affiliated with the Asian Humanities Press in 2006.

nodes.label: Rajendralal Mitra
nodes.summary: Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Medical College, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta, and served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885) of The Asiatic Society, and director of Wards' Institution (1856–1881).

nodes.label: Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt
nodes.summary: Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist who held academic positions as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).

nodes.label: Csaba Kiss
nodes.summary: Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu
nodes.summary: Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and as an editorial board member for Studies on the History of Śaivism (both attested 2021).

nodes.label: Annette Schmiedchen
nodes.summary: Annette Schmiedchen is a scholar of Indology and history who earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, holding posts at both institutions.

nodes.label: Judit Törzsök
nodes.summary: Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She taught at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III, the University of Lille, and became a professor at EPHE in 2018.

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Honjo
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Honjo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Kobe Women's University, Bukkyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

nodes.label: Xuezhu Li

nodes.label: Noa Ronkin
nodes.summary: Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) under Richard Gombrich, studied under Shlomo Biderman, and served as Lecturer and Research Fellow at Stanford University (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Stephen Batchelor
nodes.summary: Stephen Batchelor works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Songgwangsa, Tibet Institute Rikon, and the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives under Richard Gombrich, Kusan Sunim, and others. He led Sharpham College (~1992–2000) and joined Bodhi College (~2015).

nodes.label: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani
nodes.summary: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai (c. 1948–1953) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He was a Sanskrit professor at MS University of Baroda (1967–1980) and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1975–1981).

nodes.label: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad
nodes.summary: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad is a philosopher, Indologist, and religious studies scholar. He completed a doctorate at Oxford, held research fellowships at Trinity College, Oxford and Clare Hall, Cambridge, and became a Distinguished Professor at Lancaster University.

nodes.label: Dayananda Saraswati

He studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and under Virajanand Dandeesha, P. S. Subramania Iyer, Veeraraghavachariar, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, and Swami Tapovan Maharaj.

nodes.label: Peter Harvey
nodes.summary: Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2000–2015).

nodes.label: Damien Keown
nodes.summary: Damien Keown (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his degrees from Lancaster and Oxford, served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, and co-founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics.

nodes.description: American Theravada Buddhist monk and scholar (born 1944)
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Brooklyn College (B.A.) and Claremont Graduate University (Ph.D.). He served as Editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of the Buddhist Association of the United States in 2013.

nodes.label: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah
nodes.summary: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon under Bryce Ryan, Cornell University, and Harvard University. He held posts at the University of Ceylon, Cambridge, Chicago, and Harvard.

nodes.label: John S. Strong
nodes.summary: John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (circa 1972–1977) under Frank E. Reynolds and J. A. B. van Buitenen, later serving as professor at Bates College.

nodes.label: Shuken Ito
nodes.summary: Shuken Ito (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He held academic posts there from 1973 onward, becoming a professor in 1991, and visited Aichi Gakuin University in 1998.

nodes.label: Satoru Harada
nodes.summary: Satoru Harada (born 1947) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held positions at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), the Eastern Institute (attested 1982), and Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).

nodes.label: Ram Chandra Kak
nodes.summary: Ram Chandra Kak worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Sri Pratap College and under John Marshall. He was an Archaeological Survey of India superintendent (~1914-1919) and served as Jammu and Kashmir's Chief Secretary and archaeological superintendent (1919-1929).

nodes.label: R. Ramanujachari
nodes.summary: R. Ramanujachari worked in philosophy and Indology. He was Professor of Philosophy at Annamalai University (attested 1938–1940) and served as Editor of the Journal of the Annamalai University (attested 1950).

nodes.label: Stephen F. Teiser
nodes.summary: Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University under Alan Sponberg and Denis Twitchett, later teaching at Middlebury College and Princeton, where he became a professor in 2005.

nodes.label: Sarah E. Fraser
nodes.summary: Sarah E. Fraser specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, she held appointments as an Associate Professor at Northwestern University (1996) and Directrice d'Études at EPHE (2000).

nodes.label: Gherardo Gnoli
nodes.description: Italian historian of religions and Iranologist (1937–2012)
nodes.summary: Gherardo Gnoli studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1954–1958) in Iranian/Central Asian and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Naples (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008), and served as president of IsMEO (1979–1995) and IsIAO (1995–2011).

nodes.label: Ulrich Pagel
nodes.summary: Ulrich Pagel specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held a post at SOAS University of London attested between 2013 and 2020.

nodes.label: Sean D. Gaffney
nodes.summary: Sean D. Gaffney specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS University of London under Philip Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, David Seyfort Ruegg, and doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski, later holding a post at SOAS (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Jampa Samten
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jampa Samten served as a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1987). At the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, he served as Director (attested 2003–2004) and Professor (attested 2015, 2026).

nodes.label: John Brough
nodes.summary: John Brough, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at London and Cambridge.

nodes.label: Edward Conze
nodes.summary: Edward Conze was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Cologne under Max Scheler, also studying under Max Walleser. He held posts at London, Wisconsin-Madison, Washington, UC Berkeley, Lancaster, and the Buddhist Society.

nodes.label: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar
nodes.summary: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He taught at Fergusson College, served as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001), and held professorial and dean roles at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Edwin Gerow
nodes.summary: Edwin Gerow studied Indology and philosophy under J. A. B. van Buitenen, Louis Renou, George V. Bobrinskoy, and V. Ranganathan. He held posts at the University of Washington (~1966–1978) and Reed College (~1978–2001), also editing the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Tanaka

nodes.label: Rosane Rocher
nodes.summary: Rosane Rocher is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned an MA at Université libre de Bruxelles (~1955–1959) and studied under Ludo Rocher. She worked at the NFSR (1961–1970) and became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1970).

nodes.label: Akira Saito
nodes.summary: Akira Saito (b. 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the Australian National University, and held professorships at the University of Tokyo (2000–2016) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2016).

nodes.label: Klaus-Dieter Mathes
nodes.summary: Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and habilitated at the University of Hamburg, later serving as a professor at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: David Higgins
nodes.summary: David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has held research positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.summary: Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye (1813–1899) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, notably Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1840–1892), Tekchok Dorje (~1833–1868), Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo (~1833–1853), and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (~1853–1870).

nodes.label: K. A. Subramania Iyer
nodes.summary: K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Lionel David Barnett, earning degrees from London and Paris. He served as professor and Sanskrit department head at the University of Lucknow from 1921 to 1960.

nodes.label: Paul Thieme
nodes.summary: Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Hermann, Sieg, Andreas, Schulze, Lüders, and Mishra. His career included posts at Breslau, Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt, Yale (1954–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973).

nodes.label: Murray Barnson Emeneau

nodes.summary: Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) specialized in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, he taught Latin at Yale and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley from 1940 to 1971.

nodes.label: Batakrishna Ghosh
nodes.summary: Batakrishna Ghosh was an Indologist and linguist who completed doctoral studies under Hanns Oertel between 1933 and 1935. He served as a librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and edited the Bulletin of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh
nodes.summary: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College under R. D. Ranade, Dr. Bhune, Sukhlal Sanghvi, and Muni Jinvijaya. He served as professor at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1939) and edited Puratattva (~1922–1926).

nodes.label: Ramchandra B. Athavale
nodes.summary: Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith, L. D. Arts College (attested 1938), and S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women (attested 1938).

nodes.label: Shridhar Tryambak Pathak
nodes.summary: An Indologist, Pathak held posts as a Shastri at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1921) and as a Sanskrit teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

nodes.label: V. W. Paranjpe
nodes.summary: V. W. Paranjpe (1887–1976) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Superintendent of the Publication Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, succeeding Shripad Krishna Belvalkar, and was attested as Professor Emeritus at Deccan College.

nodes.label: Shripad Krishna Belvalkar
nodes.description: Indian historian and scholar of Sanskrit
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Belvalkar studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1937) and served as Secretary (~1918–1943) and General Editor of the Mahabharata (1948–1961) at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Dineschandra Sircar
nodes.summary: Dineschandra Sircar was an Indologist and historian who served as Lecturer and Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (1937, 1962). He also served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Dipak Ranjan Das
nodes.summary: Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He held posts at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1966) and the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Enshu Kurumiya
nodes.summary: Enshu Kurumiya is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD at Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong. He was attested as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1981 to 1985.

nodes.label: Yukio Sakamoto
nodes.summary: Yukio Sakamoto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University. He was a professor at Toyo University and served as professor, president, and institute director at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Yosho Nomura
nodes.summary: Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1957 to 1986 and director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

nodes.label: Rama Nath Sharma
nodes.summary: Rama Nath Sharma is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raghunatha Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi, completing his PhD at the University of Rochester (~1971). He held professorships at the University of Rochester (1971-1976) and the University of Hawaiʻi (1976).

nodes.label: Ramaprasada Tripathi
nodes.summary: Ramaprasada Tripathi was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held affiliations at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested in 1976 and 2001).

nodes.label: Tampalawela Dhammaratana
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies scholar Tampalawela Dhammaratana studied at Sunethradevi Pirivena, University of Kelaniya, University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, and Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin. He also completed postdoctoral studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études mentored by Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Pāsādika
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Pāsādika is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Magadh University and Punjabi University. His posts include positions at Punjabi University, Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, University of Marburg, and President of Linh Son Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Joseph Walser
nodes.summary: Joseph Walser is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini. He held a post at Loyola University Chicago (attested 1998).

nodes.label: P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri
nodes.description: Indian philologist and scholar of Sanskrit literature and Vedas
nodes.summary: P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under A. Chinnaswami Sastri (~1928–1934). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1935–1942) and as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1956–1967).

nodes.label: J. S. Pade
nodes.summary: J. S. Pade was an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the University of Chicago (attested 1963) and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1966).

nodes.label: Jonathan A. Silk
nodes.summary: Jonathan A. Silk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, as well as at Ryukoku and Kyoto Universities. He held posts at Michigan, Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Richard Bowring
nodes.summary: Richard Bowring (born 1947), a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, earned his BA, doctorate, and Litt.D at Cambridge. He taught at Columbia, Princeton, and Cambridge (where he was later Emeritus Professor), and served as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

nodes.label: Vincent Eltschinger
nodes.summary: Vincent Eltschinger works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Lausanne (PhD 2003 under Tom Tillemans) and Vienna (Habilitation ~2007–2014), he served at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia and the EPHE (~2015).

nodes.label: Muzaffar Alam
nodes.description: historian at the University of Chicago
nodes.summary: Muzaffar Alam works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he taught from ~1973 to 2001. Around 2001, he joined the University of Chicago as Bobrinskoy Professor.

nodes.label: Eun-su Cho
nodes.summary: Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. Cho taught at the University of Michigan until 2004 and became professor at Seoul National University in 2004.

nodes.summary: Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He has held research and teaching posts at the British Museum, Freie Universität Berlin, the University of Munich, and the University of Bonn.

nodes.summary: Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Oxford and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and served on the faculty at Boston University from 1990 to 2024.

nodes.label: Isabelle Ratié
nodes.summary: Isabelle Ratié works in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at Leipzig (~2009–2013), Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).

nodes.label: Johan Elverskog

nodes.label: Karen Christina Lang
nodes.summary: Karen Christina Lang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who completed graduate studies at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. She served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1991–2026).

nodes.label: Stefan Larsson

nodes.label: Stephan Licha
nodes.summary: Stephan Licha is a scholar of Buddhist studies and japanology who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London. He held postdoctoral positions at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, and is attested on the faculty at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Benedetta Lomi

nodes.label: Bryan D. Lowe

nodes.label: Marcus Bingenheimer
nodes.summary: Marcus Bingenheimer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Würzburg, Nagoya University, and Heidelberg University, and held posts at the Chung-Hwa Institute, Dharma Drum Institute, and Temple University (2012–2015).

nodes.label: Siniruddha Dash
nodes.summary: Siniruddha Dash is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as director at the University of Madras (2000–2014) and later as director of the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation in 2020.

nodes.label: Asko Parpola

nodes.label: Theodore Riccardi
nodes.summary: Theodore Riccardi was an Indologist and linguist. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1974–1976 and 1990) and served as guest editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society in 1989.

nodes.label: Prayag Raj Sharma
nodes.summary: Prayag Raj Sharma works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at Tribhuvan University, including as Dean of the Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies (attested 1973) and as Professor (attested 1976–1990).

nodes.label: Satish Chandra
nodes.summary: Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad (around 1940–1948) and held posts at Aligarh Muslim University (around 1953–1961) and the University of Rajasthan (around 1961–1970).

nodes.label: David Burton
nodes.summary: David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). He held posts at Keble College, Oxford (attested 2001) and Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Guy Newland

nodes.label: Elizabeth Napper
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).

nodes.label: Joshua W. C. Cutler
nodes.summary: Joshua W. C. Cutler is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).

nodes.label: John Ronald Newman

ケンブリッジ大学セント・ジョンズ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Charles Cutler Torrey
nodes.summary: Charles Cutler Torrey (1863–1956) was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900) and was a professor at Yale University (1900–1932).

nodes.label: Hanns Oertel
nodes.summary: Hanns Oertel (1868–1952) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate under William Dwight Whitney at Yale University, where he taught until 1917, and later held chairs at the University of Marburg and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Philadelphia Divinity School
variants: フィラデルフィア神学校

nodes.label: Abraham Yohannan
nodes.summary: Abraham Yohannan studied at Columbia University (~1895–1898) and held a post there from ~1894 to 1925, working in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as religious studies.

nodes.label: Noémie Verdon
nodes.summary: Noémie Verdon works in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2015 under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and later held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2018–2019).

nodes.label: Seema Alavi
nodes.summary: Historian Seema Alavi earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1991). She held teaching and professorial appointments at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1992–1994), Jamia Millia Islamia (~1994–2007), the University of Delhi (~2007–2021), and Ashoka University (~2021).

nodes.label: Blain Auer
nodes.summary: Blain Auer works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He held a post as professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018) and served on the editorial board of Perspectives on Islamicate South Asia.

nodes.label: Jacob P. Dalton
nodes.summary: Jacob P. Dalton specializes in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and held posts at the British Library, SOAS, Yale (2005), and UC Berkeley (attested 2011–2026).

nodes.label: Potprecha Cholvijarn
nodes.summary: Potprecha Cholvijarn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from Chulalongkorn University and the University of Bristol, studying under Rupert Gethin. He was attested as a special lecturer at Chulalongkorn University in 2011.

nodes.label: Shōyū Hanayama
nodes.summary: Shōyū Hanayama (1931-1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950-1957). He served as vice president at Musashino University (~1968-1995) and chairperson of the Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai until 1995.

nodes.label: Alois Anton Führer
nodes.summary: Alois Anton Führer was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Julius Jolly and Georg Bühler. He served at St. Xavier's College, the State Museum in Lucknow, and as Archaeological Surveyor for the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Bapu Deva Sastri
nodes.description: Indian scholar in Sanskrit and mathematics and translator
nodes.summary: Bapu Deva Sastri worked in Indology. He studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundiraja Misra, and Sevarama, and later taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

nodes.label: Akiko Murakawa
nodes.summary: Akiko Murakawa is an Indologist. She studied under doctoral supervisor Harry Falk, supervisors Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, and Muneo Tokunaga, and teachers Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, and Kazuhiko Yoshida.

nodes.label: Kazuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Osaka, and Cornell universities under Jay Jasanoff and Teizo Iyanaga, holding posts at Nagoya City Women's College, Kyoto University, and Nagoya City University.

nodes.label: Muneo Tokunaga
variants: Muneo Tokunaga (徳永 宗雄, Tokunaga Muneo)
nodes.summary: Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was a scholar in Indology and computational fields. He studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University (PhD), and held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1980–1988) and Kyoto University (~1988–2009).

nodes.label: Raghu Vira
nodes.summary: Raghu Vira (1902–1963) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Punjab, London, and Leiden, headed Sanskrit at Sanatan Dharma College (~1930–1946), and founded the International Academy of Indian Culture.

nodes.label: Eugène Obermiller
nodes.summary: Eugène Obermiller (1901–1935) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Dondub Buddhayin, later serving as Section Secretary at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1935).

nodes.label: Paul Carus
nodes.summary: Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Greifswald, Strasbourg, and Tübingen (Ph.D. ~1874–1876), taught at Kriegsschule Dresden (~1876–1881), and edited for The Open Court and The Monist (~1887–1919).

nodes.label: Michel Bitbol
nodes.summary: Michel Bitbol is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paris Diderot University under Pierre Mills (~1980–1985). He served as a CNRS research director (~1997) and held posts at Oxford, IHPST (~1997–2010), Paris 1, and the École Normale Supérieure (~2010).

nodes.label: Karel Werner
nodes.summary: Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, earning a doctorate at Palacký University Olomouc. He lectured at Durham University (1969–1990) and served as a professor at Masaryk University (1993–1998).

nodes.label: Nirmal C. Sinha
nodes.summary: Nirmal C. Sinha served as the editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested in 1978 and 1988).

nodes.label: Junkichi Imanishi
nodes.summary: Junkichi Imanishi is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served as associate professor at Hokkaido University, Chancellor of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and Director of the IIBS.

nodes.label: Min Lin
nodes.summary: Min Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed postgraduate studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006). In 2026, he is attested as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Takudo Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Takudo Ishikawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held posts as a research fellow at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005–2006) and as a faculty member at Taisho University (attested 2015, 2026).

nodes.label: Jodo Shu Research Institute
variants: 浄土宗総合研究所 (Jodo-shu Sogo Kenkyujo)

nodes.label: Michihiro Ikeda
nodes.summary: Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He taught at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and served as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006).

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Sueki
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Sueki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He undertook short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library and held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1982–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996).

nodes.label: Hidenori Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Hidenori Kitagawa worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studying under Hakuju Ui. He was a Rockefeller Foundation fellow (1952–1953) and served as a professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969).

nodes.label: Patna University
variants: Department of History and Archaeology at Patna University

nodes.label: Rewa Prasad Dwivedi
nodes.image: Sahitya Ratna (The Gem of Literary World) citation Conferred on Acharya Rewa Prasad Dwivedi.jpg
nodes.summary: Rewa Prasad Dwivedi (1935–2021) was an Indology scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University. He also served there as Head of Sahityavidya from circa 1977 to 1995.

nodes.label: John Marshall
nodes.summary: Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Marshall studied at Cambridge, the British School at Athens, and under Arthur Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1902–1931) and was an honorary fellow at King's College, Cambridge.

nodes.label: Harold Hargreaves
nodes.description: British archaeologist; active in British India
nodes.summary: Harold Hargreaves was an archaeologist and Indologist. He served as headmaster of Government High School, Amritsar, and held multiple positions with the Archaeological Survey of India, including Superintendent of the Frontier Circle and Deputy Director General (1928–1931).

nodes.label: Biraja Sankar Guha
nodes.summary: Biraja Sankar Guha studied at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, and Harvard University (AM 1920, PhD 1924). He served as Anthropologist at the Zoological Survey of India (1927) and Director of the Anthropological Survey of India (1945–1954).

nodes.label: John Allan
nodes.summary: John Allan was an Indologist and historian who studied at the universities of Edinburgh and Leipzig. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum and taught Sanskrit at University College London, SOAS, and Edinburgh.

nodes.label: W. W. Tarn
nodes.image: William Woodthorpe Tarn, print, c. 1905 (Elliott & Fry) retouched.png
nodes.description: British classical scholar and historian of classical antiquity (1869–1957)

ネパール国立古文書館

nodes.label: Alf Hiltebeitel
variants: アルフ・ヒルテバイテル
nodes.summary: Alf Hiltebeitel specialized in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Haverford College and the University of Chicago, where he studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner, before spending his career at George Washington University (appointed 1968, 1974, and 1981).

nodes.label: Adam Bowles
nodes.summary: Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at La Trobe University under Greg Bailey by 2004 and is attested as senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland from 2016 to 2018.

nodes.label: Achyutananda Dash
nodes.summary: Achyutananda Dash works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University, attested in 1999.

nodes.label: James W. Benson
nodes.summary: James W. Benson is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999), the University of Oxford (attested 1999), and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy
nodes.summary: Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy worked in Indology, history-archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at Wycliffe College, UCL, and under Caroline Rhys Davids, he directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon and served as curator and research fellow at Boston's Museum of Fine Arts.

nodes.label: T. Venkatacharya
variants: ヴェンカターチャーリヤ
nodes.summary: T. Venkatacharya was an Indology scholar who held positions at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (attested 1971) and as Professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979).

nodes.label: Corrado Pensa
nodes.summary: Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli, and held a professorship at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).

nodes.label: Ernest Bender
nodes.summary: Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig Harris, and Henry Hoenigswald. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania (1950–1989) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

nodes.id: I:Journal of the American Oriental Society
nodes.label: Journal of the American Oriental Society
variants: Journal of the American Oriental Society

nodes.label: Stanley Insler
nodes.summary: Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Columbia, Tübingen, and Yale under Paul Thieme, and served as Edward E. Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale from circa 1974 to 2012.

nodes.label: Marc Aurel Stein
variants: マーク・オーレル・スタイン
nodes.summary: Marc Aurel Stein (1862–1943) was an archaeologist, Indologist, and Iranian specialist. After earning his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, he headed Oriental College (1888–1899) and served with the Archaeological Survey of India (1904, 1910–1912).

nodes.label: Jason Birch
nodes.summary: Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied under Peter Oldmeadow at the University of Sydney and earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Oxford, SOAS as a postdoctoral fellow, and the University of Alberta.

nodes.label: Jürgen Hanneder
nodes.summary: Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who studied at Munich, Bonn, and Marburg, earning his PhD under Michael Hahn in 1996. He worked at Bonn and Halle-Wittenberg before becoming a professor at the University of Marburg in 2007.

nodes.label: Alexander Cunningham
variants: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.jawiki: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.description: British army engineer and amateur archaeologist (1814-1893)
nodes.summary: Alexander Cunningham specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Christ's Hospital, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and under James Prinsep. He founded the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as its first director (1861–1865) and later Director-General (1871–1885).

nodes.label: Erik Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik Zürcher was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, also studying under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and Édouard Chavannes. He served as director at Leiden University (1961–1993).

nodes.label: Petra Kieffer-Pülz
nodes.summary: Petra Kieffer-Pülz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. A pupil of Heinz Bechert, she held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), the Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz (~2000), and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society (~2005).

nodes.label: Chikushi Jogakuen University
variants: 筑紫女学園大学人間文化研究所

nodes.label: C. Peter Bankart
nodes.summary: C. Peter Bankart works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He has held posts as a Visiting Researcher at Dartmouth College and at Wabash College (attested 2003).

nodes.id: I:University of the District of Columbia
nodes.label: University of the District of Columbia
variants: University of the District of Columbia

nodes.label: Dartmouth College
variants: Department of Religion at Dartmouth College

nodes.label: Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held positions as Pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1941–1943).

nodes.label: Albert Grünwedel
variants: アルベルト・グリュンヴェーデル
nodes.jawiki: アルベルト・グリュンヴェーデル
nodes.summary: Albert Grünwedel was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and archaeologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Munich (1876–1883) under numerous scholars, later serving at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1881–1921; director from 1904) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1891).

nodes.label: Ethnological Museum of Berlin
variants: ベルリン民族学博物館

nodes.label: Auguste Barth
nodes.summary: Auguste Barth was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Strasbourg. He held a post at Collège Poincaré Saverne (~1856–1860) and was a member of the Institut de France (~1893–1916).

nodes.label: Renate Syed
nodes.summary: Renate Syed is an Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982) under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner. She was attested as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

nodes.label: Dieter Schlingloff
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, Dieter Schlingloff earned his doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and his habilitation at Humboldt University. His academic posts included Kiel University (1968–1971) and the University of Munich (1972–1996).

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm
nodes.summary: An Indologist and Tibetologist, Friedrich Wilhelm studied under Paul Thieme and completed his doctorate at the University of Munich (ca. 1951–1956). He held posts at Munich as Privatdozent (1963) and Professor (1969–1998).

nodes.label: Gritli von Mitterwallner
nodes.summary: Gritli von Mitterwallner worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her Dr. phil. (1964) and habilitation (1971) at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.

nodes.label: Wouter J. Hanegraaff
nodes.summary: Wouter J. Hanegraaff is a religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University from circa 1982 to 1995. He held a post at the University of Amsterdam circa 1999.

nodes.label: P. Pratap Kumar
nodes.summary: P. Pratap Kumar is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a professorship at the University of KwaZulu-Natal (attested 2010) and was a visiting professor at Colorado College (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Michio Yano
nodes.summary: Michio Yano (born 1944) is an Indologist and historian. He earned his doctorate at Kyoto University, where he also studied under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi, and studied at Brown University under David Pingree (~1974–1976). He was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (1973–2015).

nodes.label: Takao Hayashi
nodes.summary: Takao Hayashi is an Indologist and historian who studied at Tohoku University, Kyoto University, and Brown University under David Pingree. He held research and lecturing posts before serving as assistant professor (1986–1989) and professor (1995–2015) at Doshisha University.

nodes.label: Catholic University of America
variants: The Catholic University of America (Washington, DC)

nodes.label: Anthony Kennedy Warder
nodes.summary: Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at SOAS under John Brough and William Stede. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh before serving at the University of Toronto from 1963 to 1990.

nodes.label: L. A. Ravi Varma
nodes.summary: L. A. Ravi Varma, an Indologist educated at Madras Medical College, served as Honorary Director of the Oriental Manuscripts Department at the University of Kerala from circa 1938 to 1943.

nodes.label: University of Kerala
variants: Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, Trivandrum
Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, University of Kerala

nodes.label: Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis
nodes.summary: Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1934–1939) and later held posts at SOAS University of London (~1964–1981) and Leiden University (1978–1986).

nodes.label: Sarva Daman Singh
nodes.summary: Sarva Daman Singh is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who served as Professor of History at the University of Queensland, attested in 1958 and 1987.

nodes.label: Govind Chandra Pande
nodes.image: The Vice President Shri Bhairon Singh Shekhawat presenting 13th "Saraswati Samman" award to Prof. G.C. Pande on his book 'Bhagirathi' at a function organised by K.K. Birla foundation in New Delhi on September 6, 2004.jpg
nodes.summary: Govind Chandra Pande was a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as vice-chancellor of the University of Allahabad and University of Rajasthan, visiting professor at BHU, and chairman of the IIAS and Allahabad Museum.

nodes.label: Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar
nodes.summary: Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar (1893–1964) worked in Indology and philosophy. He was principal of Sir Parashurambhau College and served as professor and Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Dipak Kumar Barua
nodes.summary: Dipak Kumar Barua is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at the University of Calcutta as Assistant Lecturer in Pali (~1964–1974) and faculty Dean (1987), and later served as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1996–2003).

nodes.label: Antonello Palumbo
nodes.summary: Antonello Palumbo works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. He held a research post at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2004) and taught at SOAS University of London (attested 2005–2010).

nodes.label: Anantalal Thakur
nodes.summary: Anantalal Thakur was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Calcutta and with several traditional teachers. He held professorships at the Mithila Institute (1952–1969) and directed the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

nodes.label: Satkari Mookerjee
variants: サトカリ・ムカージー
サトカーリ・ムケルジー
nodes.summary: Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Ashutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (around 1948–1956) and as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

nodes.label: Hajime Sakurabe
nodes.summary: Hajime Sakurabe (1925–2012) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, earning a PhD. He held posts at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara and was professor at Otani University.

nodes.label: Rigzin Lhundup
nodes.summary: Rigzin Lhundup was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested in 1959 and 1987).

nodes.label: Umesha Mishra
nodes.summary: Umesha Mishra was an Indologist and philosopher who served at the University of Allahabad from circa 1923 to 1959. He was founder secretary of Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha and director of the Mithila Institute from circa 1951 to 1961.

Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research

nodes.label: Janardan Mishra
nodes.summary: Janardan Mishra was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Director of the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning, with his tenure attested in 1959 and 1987.

nodes.label: Chintaharan Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Chintaharan Chakravarti (1900–1972) was an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Presidency University. He also held posts at Bethune College, attested in 1941, and served as publication secretary at Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat, attested in 1960.

nodes.label: Aryadeva
nodes.description: 3rd century Sri Lankan philosopher and writer
nodes.summary: Aryadeva was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nagarjuna and Shakyamitra. He was associated with the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning.

nodes.label: University of Sussex
variants: University of Sussex's School of African & Asian Studies

nodes.label: Andrew J. Nicholson
nodes.summary: Andrew J. Nicholson specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Sri Narayana Mishra and served as Associate Professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sri Narayana Mishra
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, Mishra studied under Anantalal Thakur. He served at Banaras Hindu University as Lecturer, Reader, and ultimately Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Thomas Edward Colebrooke
nodes.summary: Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an Indology and history scholar educated at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Wannaporn Rienjang
nodes.summary: Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the British Museum, University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).

nodes.label: Peter Stewart
nodes.summary: Peter Stewart is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his degrees at Clare College, Cambridge. He held positions at Reading, the Courtauld Institute of Art, and the University of Oxford (appointed Associate Professor in 2011).

nodes.label: P. V. Ramanujaswami
nodes.summary: P. V. Ramanujaswami was an Indologist who served as Director of the Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1944 and 1954.

nodes.label: Finnian M. M. Gerety
nodes.summary: Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under Michael Witzel and Masato Fujii, and later held positions at Yale University (2017–2018) and Brown University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Michael Witzel
nodes.summary: Michael Witzel is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Karl Hoffmann, Paul Thieme, Hanns-Peter Schmidt, Johanna Narten, Jununath Pandit, and F. B. J. Kuiper. He held chairs of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1978–1986) and Harvard University (from 1986).

nodes.label: Gregory Nagy
nodes.summary: Gregory Nagy (born 1942) is a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his studies at Indiana University Bloomington (~1958–1962) and Harvard University (~1962–1966), where he later held an academic post starting around 1969.

nodes.label: James McHugh
nodes.summary: James McHugh specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, Oxford (under Benson, Gombrich, Sanderson, Smith, and Teichman), and Harvard (PhD under McCrea, Monius, and Patil), holding posts at Cornell and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar
variants: Khan dkar Tshul khrims skal bzań

nodes.label: Benjamin Fleming
nodes.summary: Benjamin Fleming is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the City University of New York (attested 2021).

nodes.label: E. Baer
nodes.description: American women's studies academic and historian

nodes.label: Henry Hoenigswald
nodes.summary: Henry Hoenigswald (1915–2003) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the universities of Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence between 1932 and 1937, and later held a post at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1948 to 1985.

nodes.label: Alexander Wynne
nodes.description: British sanskritist and religious studies scholar, works on the history of Buddishm
nodes.summary: Alexander Wynne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later serving as a Junior Research Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (2002–2006).

nodes.label: St John's College, Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学セント・ジョーンズ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Paul Williams
nodes.summary: Paul Williams is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Sussex and Oxford, was Bowra Research Fellow at Wadham College, and later served as Emeritus Professor of Indian and Tibetan Philosophy at the University of Bristol (~1980–2011).

nodes.label: Doris Meth Srinivasan
nodes.summary: Doris Meth Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Hunter College and the University of Pennsylvania, she held posts at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Stony Brook University, Columbia, Barnard, George Washington, and George Mason.

nodes.label: Julius Dutoit
nodes.summary: Julius Dutoit was a scholar in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Adalbert Kuhn and Ernst Kuhn, studying with the latter from circa 1898 to 1902.

nodes.label: Klaus Bruhn
nodes.summary: Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who studied under Walther Schubring and Ludwig Alsdorf at the University of Hamburg. He served as professor of Indology and Indian philology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991/1993.

nodes.label: Gudrun Bühnemann
variants: グドルン・ビューネマン
nodes.summary: Gudrun Bühnemann works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Münster, Bonn, and Vienna (under Ernst Steinkellner), held research posts in India and Japan, and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.
