Presidency College an der University of Calcutta

nodes.label: Dragomir Dimitrov
nodes.summary: Dragomir Dimitrov works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his degrees at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, held posts there and with the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project, and at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Nicolas Revire
nodes.summary: Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University (2012–2013) under supervisors including Peter Skilling and Claudine Bautze-Picron, and held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016–2017).

nodes.label: Thammasat University
variants: Faculty of Sociology and Anthropology, Thammasat University

nodes.label: Gérard Colas
nodes.summary: Gérard Colas is an Indologist. He has held research posts at the CNRS (attested 2004, 2009) and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).

nodes.label: D. S. Subbaramaiya
nodes.summary: D. S. Subbaramaiya worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.

nodes.label: Florin Deleanu
variants: デレアヌ フロリン
nodes.jawiki: デレアヌ フロリン
nodes.summary: Florin Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bucharest, Waseda, Peking, and Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. His posts include Kansai Medical University (1994–2001), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Kazufumi Oki
nodes.summary: Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After completing doctoral coursework at Kyoto University, he served on the faculty at Shuchiin University, where he is attested from 1982 to 2013.

nodes.label: Shuchiin University
variants: 種智院大学密教資料研究所

nodes.label: Shun'ei Mori
nodes.summary: Shun'ei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University, attested in 1990, and as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College, attested in 1995.

nodes.label: Takayasu Higuchi
nodes.summary: Takayasu Higuchi (1919–2015) studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942), where he later served as professor of archaeology (~1953–1983). In his fields of history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he directed Sen-oku Hakuko Kan, Sen-oku Matsurokan, Kashihara Archaeological Institute, and the Research Centre for Silk Roadology.

nodes.label: Shoshin Kuwayama
nodes.summary: Kuwayama is a scholar in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1966), where he served as Assistant Professor (~1978–1989) and Professor Emeritus at the Institute for Research in the Humanities.

nodes.label: Meiji Yamada
nodes.summary: Meiji Yamada, a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962) and served there as a professor (attested between 1963 and 2007).

nodes.label: Marcel Hofinger
nodes.summary: Marcel Hofinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte.

nodes.label: Étienne Lamotte
variants: エティエンヌ・ラモット
エティエンヌ・ラモート
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Lamotte studied at KU Leuven, EPHE, and Collège de France under Louis de La Vallée Poussin, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He taught at KU Leuven (1932–1974) and served as president of UCLouvain (1950–1959).

nodes.label: Jikido Takasaki
nodes.summary: Jikido Takasaki specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University. He held positions at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa University, Osaka University, Waseda University, and served as President of Tsurumi Women's University.

nodes.label: Yuichi Kajiyama
nodes.summary: Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Kyoto University and studied in India, the UK, and Austria. He held professorships at Kyoto University (1956–1988), Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

nodes.label: Cristina Pecchia
nodes.summary: Cristina Pecchia specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She earned her PhD from Sapienza University of Rome (~1999–2003), researched at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and lectures at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Joel Tatelman
nodes.summary: Joel Tatelman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford in 1996 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: Kate Crosby
nodes.summary: Kate Crosby is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at St Peter's College, Oxford, Cardiff University, the Buddhist Institute, SOAS University of London, and King's College London.

nodes.label: Steven Collins
nodes.summary: Steven Collins was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, held posts at Bristol and Indiana University, and became Chester D. Tripp Professor in the Humanities at the University of Chicago (1991).

nodes.label: Sally Mellick Cutler
nodes.summary: Sally Mellick Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford in 1993 and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1996–1997).

nodes.label: Dilli Raman Regmi
nodes.summary: Dilli Raman Regmi was an Indologist and historian who earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D.Litt. from Patna University (~1941–1961). He taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith from circa 1945 to 1947.

nodes.label: Yutaka Iwamoto
nodes.summary: Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under Toru Haneda and Hidenaka Tanaka. He held professorships at Kyoto University (~1946), Tokai University (~1966–1977), Tokyo University of Science, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka University (~1980–1986).

nodes.label: Ryosaburo Sakaki
nodes.summary: Ryosaburo Sakaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He taught at Ryukoku University, the Third Higher School, and as a professor at Kyoto University from 1908.

nodes.label: Christian K. Wedemeyer
nodes.summary: Christian K. Wedemeyer is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA and PhD at Columbia. He held posts at Columbia, Antioch, Copenhagen (2000–2003), and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).

nodes.label: Atul Chandra Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Atul Chandra Chatterjee (1874–1955) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Charles Henry Tawney at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, then attended King's College, Cambridge, before serving in the Indian Civil Service (~1897–1931).

nodes.label: Ernest John Henry Mackay
nodes.summary: Ernest John Henry Mackay was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Bristol. He served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Mandatory Palestine (1919–1922) and Special Officer for Exploration for the Archaeological Survey of India (circa 1926–1932).

nodes.label: J. L. Shaw
nodes.summary: J. L. Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Bimal Krishna Matilal and earned a degree from Rice University (1969–1973). He was on the faculty at Victoria University of Wellington from circa 1974 to 2014.

nodes.label: Robert P. Goldman
nodes.summary: Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, Shivram Dattatray Joshi, and T. S. Srinivasa Sastri. He spent his career at UC Berkeley (~1971–2021), becoming professor emeritus in 2021.

nodes.label: Maureen L. P. Patterson
nodes.summary: Maureen L. P. Patterson was an Indology scholar and South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago, with her post attested in 1984 and 2007.

nodes.label: Sally J. Sutherland Goldman
nodes.summary: Sally J. Sutherland Goldman works in Indology and linguistics. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri, and served at UC Berkeley, becoming Senior Lecturer Emerita.

nodes.label: Jey Flick
nodes.summary: Jey Flick works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sheldon Pollock (attested 1984–2007) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Naomichi Nakada
nodes.summary: Naomichi Nakada is an Indologist and philosopher who completed his doctoral studies under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and also studied under Ram Chandra Pandeya.

nodes.label: André Padoux
nodes.summary: André Padoux (1920–2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Swami Lakshman Joo, Louis Renou, Georg Morgenstierne, Alf Sommerfelt, and Olivier Lacombe. He held posts at Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964) and CNRS (1959, ~1964–1985).

nodes.label: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917) and held the Carmichael Professorship at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).

nodes.label: Turrell V. Wylie
variants: タレル・ヴァール・ワイリー
nodes.summary: Turrell V. Wylie (1927–1984) worked in Tibetology, linguistics, and sinology. He studied at the University of Washington and under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche, later serving as Professor of Tibetan Language and Civilization at Washington.

nodes.label: Tryambakarama Sastri
nodes.summary: Tryambakarama Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Lakshmana Sastri Dravida, earned a Vedantacharya from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and served as headmaster (pradhanadhyapaka) at Government Sanskrit Pathashala, Jamnagar (attested 1932).

nodes.label: Gopinath Kaviraj
nodes.summary: Gopinath Kaviraj worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, having studied under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachuramani, and at Allahabad and Maharani College. He served Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as librarian (1914–1920), principal (1923–1937), and Yoga-Tantra head (1964–1969).

nodes.label: Narayana Shastri Khiste
nodes.summary: Narayan Sastri Khiste was an Indology scholar who served as librarian (adhyaksha) at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1932) and later as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).

nodes.label: Nhu Lien
nodes.summary: Nhu Lien specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under the teacher Ādiccavaṃsa.

nodes.label: Oliver Philipp Frey
nodes.summary: Oliver Philipp Frey is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and later held an academic post there.

nodes.label: Yasutaka Muroya
nodes.summary: Yasutaka Muroya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He worked as a project research associate at the University of Vienna and the University of Leipzig, and as a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Alessandro Graheli
nodes.summary: Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has held positions at the University of Vienna, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the University of Toronto as a Part-time Assistant Professor.

nodes.label: Chlodwig H. Werba
nodes.summary: Chlodwig H. Werba (born 1947) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He has been affiliated with the University of Vienna, where he served as professor, attested between 1990 and 2022.

nodes.label: Elisa Freschi
nodes.summary: Elisa Freschi is an Indologist and philosopher who earned her doctorate under Raffaele Torella. She held positions at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Vienna, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Saraju Rath
nodes.summary: Saraju Rath is an Indologist and linguist who held positions at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

nodes.label: Heike Oberlin
nodes.summary: Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen, Kerala Kalamandalam, and the University of Würzburg. She held academic posts at Tübingen (2005–2008), Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and Sapienza University of Rome (2025).

nodes.label: Barbara Gerke
nodes.summary: Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She has held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Thomas Kintaert
nodes.summary: Thomas Kintaert is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at the University of Vienna, attested in 2009 and serving as a Lecturer attested from 2022 to 2026.

nodes.label: Dominik Haas
nodes.summary: Dominik Haas works in Indology and religious studies, completing doctoral studies under Marion Rastelli. He has held posts as a DOC Fellow at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia and at the University of Vienna (attested 2022).

nodes.label: Dennis A. Johnson
nodes.summary: Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012) and was affiliated with its South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library.

nodes.label: Sung Yong Kang
nodes.description: Scholar of South Asian Religious Traditions
nodes.summary: Sung Yong Kang is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Seoul National University and the University of Hamburg. Kang held posts at the University of Vienna (~2006–2008) and Seoul National University (~2008, attested 2022).

nodes.label: Axel Michaels
nodes.summary: Axel Michaels is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and Kiel University. He held posts at Kiel, the Nepal Research Centre, the University of Bern, and Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Bernhard Kölver
nodes.summary: Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Frankfurt and Cologne, among other universities. He held posts at the University of Cologne (1966–1970, 1972–1976), Kiel University (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

nodes.label: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri
nodes.summary: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Madras (ca. 1929–1946) and later held posts at Annamalai and Mysore.

nodes.label: G. Srinivasa Murti
nodes.summary: G. Srinivasa Murti worked in Indology and served as director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1938–1949 and 1971).

nodes.label: Ryutaro Tsuchida
nodes.summary: Ryutaro Tsuchida (born 1947) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo and under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg. He was an assistant at Marburg (~1980–1983) and became a professor and professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Ute Hüsken
nodes.summary: Ute Hüsken is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at Göttingen. She was a professor at the University of Oslo from 2007 to 2017 before becoming a professor at Heidelberg University in 2017.

nodes.label: Shinkō Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Shinkō Mochizuki studied at Bukkyo University, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. He held leadership posts including president at Shukyo University (1914–1928) and professor and dean at Taisho University (~1926–1942), and was elected to the Japan Academy in 1947.

nodes.label: Sensho Murakami
nodes.summary: Sensho Murakami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani and Toyo Universities under teachers including Ryomon and Yukitada Takeda. He taught at Tokyo Imperial University (professor 1917–1923) and Otani University (lecturer 1926–1928).

nodes.label: Eun Maeda
nodes.summary: Eun Maeda (1857–1930) was a Japanese scholar of Buddhist studies who taught Kozui Otani. He served as president of both Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Seigai Omura
nodes.summary: Working in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Seigai Omura studied at Tokyo University of the Arts under Kanō Tomonobu and Umpei Shinma. He served as professor at Tokyo University of the Arts (1905) and founded the Bussho Kankōkai.

nodes.label: Astrid Zotter
nodes.summary: Astrid Zotter is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Leipzig. She held positions at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018) and Heidelberg University (attested 2023).

nodes.label: Richard Schechner
nodes.jawiki: リチャード・シェクナー
nodes.summary: Richard Schechner studied at Cornell University, the University of Iowa, and Tulane University. Around 1967, he became a University Professor at the Tisch School of the Arts at New York University.

nodes.label: Jan Nattier
nodes.summary: Jan Nattier is a scholar of Buddhist, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She studied at Indiana and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and others, later teaching at Macalester, Hawaiʻi, Stanford, Indiana (1992–2005), and Soka University (2004–2010).

nodes.summary: John R. McRae was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held teaching and professorial posts at Cornell, Indiana University Bloomington, Soka University, and Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Kanno
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Kanno (born 1952) studied at the University of Tokyo in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He directed the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology at Soka University (~2003–2009) and held posts at the Institute of Oriental Philosophy.

nodes.label: Saphalya Amatya
nodes.summary: Saphalya Amatya works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Amatya served as Chief Exploration Officer at the Department of Archaeology (attested 1974) and as Editor of Ancient Nepal (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Lobsang Jamspal
nodes.summary: Lobsang Jamspal (born 1936) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. His career includes posts at Delhi, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Columbia University (attested 1985–1990), and CIHTS.

nodes.label: Waso Harada
nodes.summary: Waso Harada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku University and Koyasan University under teachers including Esho Mikogami and Hiroo Kashiwagi, he later held posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.

nodes.label: Karunapati Tripathi
nodes.summary: Karunapati Tripathi was an Indologist who served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and President of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan.

nodes.label: Mandan Mishra
nodes.summary: Mandan Mishra was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (~1967–1989), Vice-Chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1993–1997), and held a post at the University of Rajasthan.

nodes.label: Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi
nodes.summary: Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi, an Indology scholar, studied under Karunapati Tripathi and served as Publication Officer at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Jay Jasanoff
nodes.summary: Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who earned his bachelor's degree at Harvard. He served as assistant professor at UC Berkeley, full professor at Cornell (1981–1985), and Diebold Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Philology at Harvard from 1998.

variants: コーネル大学アジア研究学部

nodes.label: Karunesh Shukla
nodes.summary: Karunesh Shukla is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under V. P. Upadhyaya. He served as Reader and later Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

nodes.label: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha
nodes.description: Indian archeologist and historian from Bihar
nodes.summary: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha studied at Patna University and SOAS University of London (Ph.D. under Lionel David Barnett). He served as Head of Department at Patna University (1958) and Honorary Joint Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1968–1975).

nodes.label: Vishwa Nath Pathak
nodes.summary: Vishwa Nath Pathak was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held a professorship at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1973–1987).

nodes.label: Francis Gladwin
variants: フランシス・グラッドウィン
nodes.description: British scholar of the Persian language
nodes.summary: Francis Gladwin worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (circa 1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College circa 1801–1805.

nodes.label: Nyanaponika Thera
nodes.summary: Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at the University of Ceylon. He co-founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as its leader, editor (1958–1984), and president (1958–1988).

nodes.label: Satoshi Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, lecturing at Bukkyo University (~1993–2002) before becoming a Professor and later President (2014) at Kyoto Bunkyo University.

nodes.label: Virendra Kumar Verma
nodes.summary: Virendra Kumar Verma is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ramanatha Dikshita and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and taught Kamala Prasad Mishra.

nodes.label: Ramanatha Dikshita
nodes.summary: Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indologist who worked in the Sadholal research division at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944) and served as Head of the Veda Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1970).

nodes.label: Milo Cleveland Beach
nodes.summary: Milo Cleveland Beach is an art historian and Indologist educated at Harvard College and Harvard University. His career included posts at the Fogg Museum, Williams College, the Smithsonian Institution, and as director of the National Museum of Asian Art (~1988–2001).

nodes.summary: Eberhard Fischer is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who completed his PhD at the University of Basel (~1960–1965). He served as director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and president of Rietberg-Gesellschaft (~2001).

nodes.label: Jan Fontein
nodes.summary: Jan Fontein (1927–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin, and held curatorial posts at the Rijksmuseum and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

nodes.label: B. N. Goswamy
nodes.summary: B. N. Goswamy was an Indian scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Panjab University (~1952–1958), later serving in the Indian Administrative Service (~1956–1958) and on the faculty of Panjab University (~1965–1993).

nodes.label: Jean-François Jarrige
nodes.summary: Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Lycée Claude Fauriel, École du Louvre, and the University of Paris. He served as director and head of the Guimet Museum from 1986 to 2008.

nodes.label: Kyōtarō Nishikawa
nodes.summary: Kyōtarō Nishikawa worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Keio University (circa 1949–1953), he served as Director-General of the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1990–1997) and at Kanagawa Prefectural Museum (~2002–2012).

nodes.summary: Adele Schlombs is a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. She held a post at the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln from ~1991 to 2022.

nodes.label: Roderick Whitfield
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies, Roderick Whitfield held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was Professor Emeritus (attested 2011) and active through at least 2022.

nodes.label: Joanna Gottfried Williams
nodes.summary: Joanna Gottfried Williams, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. She spent her career at the University of California, Berkeley, serving as a professor from ~1967 to 2003.

nodes.label: Daniel M. Stuart
nodes.summary: Daniel M. Stuart is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He held posts at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Chhimed Rigdzin
nodes.summary: Chhimed Rigdzin worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Choying Khyabdel. He conducted research at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (circa 1954–1957) and served as Professor of Tibetan at Visva-Bharati University (circa 1957–1987).

variants: Visva-Bharati University, Department of Indo-Tibetan Studies

nodes.label: Namkhai Norbu
nodes.summary: Namkhai Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khamdre Shedra, and held professorships at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (~1964–1992) and the University of Naples (1962–1992).

nodes.label: K. Ammini Amma
nodes.summary: K. Ammini Amma was an Indology scholar who conducted research at the University of Madras, where she is attested as a research student in 1940 and 1971.

nodes.label: Zhongxin Jiang
nodes.summary: Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965), he held posts at Peking University (~1965–1978) and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002).

nodes.label: Jinzhang Peng
nodes.summary: Jinzhang Peng was an archaeologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He was deputy director in the Department of History at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and later served as archaeological institute dean and professor at Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).

nodes.label: Qing Duan
nodes.description: Chinese scholar of Indian and Iranian languages; Professor of Indo-Iranian Studies and Boya Chair Professor of Peking University
nodes.summary: Qing Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1982–1986) under Ronald Eric Emmerick, later serving as professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

nodes.label: George Abraham Grierson

nodes.summary: A linguist and indologist, Grierson studied at Shrewsbury School and Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1907), headed the Linguistic Survey of India as Superintendent (1898–1928), and was a Governor at SOAS (1917–1925).

nodes.label: Baburam Saksena
nodes.summary: Baburam Saksena was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. An advanced student at Banaras Hindu University in 1921, he later served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University (~1964–1968).

nodes.label: Sumitra Mangesh Katre
nodes.summary: Sumitra Mangesh Katre was a linguist and Indologist who earned a PhD at the University of London. He founded Deccan College, serving as Chair of Indo-European Philology (1942–1971), and later became Professor Emeritus at UT Austin.

nodes.label: Bhadriraju Krishnamurti
nodes.summary: Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (A.M., Ph.D.) and under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He founded and was Professor at Osmania University, and held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, and the University of Hyderabad.

nodes.label: Eric P. Hamp

nodes.label: John Clifford Holt
nodes.summary: John Clifford Holt works in Buddhist and religious studies. nodes.label: Chandra R. de Silva

nodes.label: Charles Hallisey

nodes.label: Luca Maria Olivieri

nodes.summary: Ryuichi Abe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia under Yoshito S. Hakeda and Philip Boas Yampolsky, he taught at Columbia before becoming Reischauer Institute Professor of Japanese Religions at Harvard.

nodes.label: Juhn Y. Ahn

nodes.label: Carol S. Anderson
nodes.summary: Carol S. Anderson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Gustavo Benavides

nodes.label: James A. Benn
nodes.summary: James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held faculty positions at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.

nodes.label: Patricia Berger
nodes.summary: Patricia Berger works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, served as Curator of Chinese Art at the Asian Art Museum, and held posts at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center.

nodes.label: Stephen C. Berkwitz
nodes.summary: Stephen C. Berkwitz works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya (1995–1997) and held posts at Missouri State University, where he was Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2004), and Ruhr University Bochum.

nodes.label: Carl Bielefeldt
nodes.summary: Carl Bielefeldt studied at UC Berkeley (PhD ~1975-1980) and under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, he served on the faculty at Stanford University from around 1980 until retiring as emeritus around 2013.

nodes.label: Mark L. Blum
nodes.summary: Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held posts at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2004–2006), and later served as Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mathieu Boisvert

nodes.label: George D. Bond

nodes.summary: Takeshi Fujii (born 1955) is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He spent his academic career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1987–2021), rising from assistant to professor and professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Marui
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Marui (born 1952) specializes in Indology and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo (PhD 2011), Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. He taught at Musashino University and the University of Tokyo (1992–2018).

nodes.label: François Grimal
nodes.summary: François Grimal is an Indologist who has held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Anne-Marie Esnoul
nodes.summary: Anne-Marie Esnoul was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Masson-Oursel. She held posts at the CNRS, EPHE, and Institut de civilisation indienne.

nodes.label: Lilian Silburn
nodes.summary: Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel (~1938–1948) and Swami Lakshman Joo (1948). She held positions at the CNRS as Boursière (~1945–1948) and researcher (~1948–1978).

nodes.label: Gösta Liebert
nodes.summary: Gösta Liebert was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lund University and the University of Gothenburg under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He held posts at Lund, Uppsala University, and Gothenburg (Professor, 1955–1982).

nodes.label: Stig Wikander
variants: スティグ・ヴィカンデル
nodes.jawiki: スティグ・ヴィカンデル
nodes.description: Swedish historian of religion and iranologist (1908–1983)
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies, Wikander studied at Uppsala, Copenhagen, Paris, and Berlin, earning his doctorate under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He taught at Lund (1941–1953) and held a chair at Uppsala (1953–1974).

nodes.label: Karl Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, and held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1983).

nodes.label: Mieko Kajihara
nodes.summary: Mieko Kajihara is an Indologist who studied under Michael Witzel (attested 1997) and earned a PhD from Harvard University in 2002.

nodes.label: Shingo Einoo
nodes.summary: Shingo Einoo is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg (~1980–1986). His career includes positions at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1979–1989), the University of Tokyo, and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (~1989–2013).

nodes.label: Mark Hale
nodes.summary: Mark Hale works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He has held academic posts at Harvard University (attested 1987) and Concordia University (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Concordia University
variants: Concordia University's Institute for Canadian Jewish Studies
Centre for Iranian Studies at Concordia University

nodes.label: Anirban Dash
nodes.summary: Anirban Dash works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a post as a research assistant (attested 2003–2005) and later as an associate professor of Sanskrit (attested 2026) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Yoshitaka Iriya
nodes.summary: Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) studied Sinology at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, headed the Department of Chinese Literature at Nagoya University, and was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University.

Research Institute for Zen Culture (Zenbunka kenkyujo)

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Kaneiwa
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Kaneiwa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts at Bukkyo University, attested in 2001 and 2013.

nodes.label: Ming Chen
nodes.summary: Ming Chen is a scholar of Indology, sinology, and Buddhist studies who has served as a professor at Peking University (attested 2001, 2013).

nodes.label: S. Sankararama Sastri
nodes.summary: An Indologist, S. Sankararama Sastri served as a Pandit in the Publication Section of the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 1943) and as a Pandit at the University of Kerala (attested 1944).

nodes.label: Robert Ford Campany
nodes.summary: A scholar of Sinology and religious studies, Robert Ford Campany was a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006). He later held posts at the University of Southern California (~2006–2010) and Vanderbilt University in 2010.

nodes.label: Daniel B. Stevenson
nodes.summary: Daniel B. Stevenson is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at Columbia University. He held assistant professorships at Butler University and the University of Kansas, and served as a Guest Scholar at Soka University.

nodes.label: Harald Hauptmann
nodes.description: German praehistorian and near eastern archaeologist
nodes.summary: Archaeologist Harald Hauptmann studied at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg, and FU Berlin. His main posts included the German Archaeological Institute (1966–1971), Heidelberg Academy of Sciences (1989), Heidelberg University (1980–1994), and the German Archaeological Institute at Istanbul (1994–2001).

nodes.label: Karl Jettmar
nodes.summary: Karl Jettmar was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna and later held appointments at Weltmuseum Wien, University of Vienna, Mainz University, and Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Institut de civilisation indienne
variants: Institut de Civilisation Indienne du Collège de France
Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne
Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the University of Paris

nodes.label: James W. Heisig
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・ハイジック
nodes.summary: James W. Heisig (born 1944) works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Divine Word College, Loyola, Notre Dame, and Cambridge (PhD ~1969–1973), he held posts at Divine Word College and Nanzan University, including the Nanzan Institute (~1978–2005).

nodes.label: Paul F. Knitter
nodes.summary: Paul F. Knitter worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1962–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1968–1972), later holding a post at Union Theological Seminary (~2007–2017).

nodes.label: Luciano Petech
nodes.summary: Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Lector in Italian at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984).

nodes.label: Jigme Pema Wangchen
nodes.summary: Jigme Pema Wangchen is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dzi Gar Khenpo Nor Yang, Drukpa Khenpo Ngawang Chödrak, and Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog.

nodes.label: Zhiru Shi
nodes.summary: Zhiru Shi (born 1964) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. After earning an MA at the University of Michigan and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, Shi taught at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014).

nodes.label: Scott Hurley
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Scott Hurley earned his PhD from the University of Arizona in 2001, where he studied under Elizabeth Harrison.

nodes.label: University of Arizona
variants: Center for Buddhist Studies at the University of Arizona

nodes.label: Kazumi Yoshizaki
nodes.summary: Kazumi Yoshizaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Toyo University and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Christopher Minkowski
nodes.summary: Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist who studied at Harvard, Delhi, and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor at Cornell University (1989–2006) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford and Balliol College (2005–2023).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Rau
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Rau worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig under Friedrich Weller (~1940–1944) and earned his doctorate at Marburg under Johannes Nobel (1946–1949). He held professorships at Frankfurt (1955) and Marburg (1958–1987).

nodes.label: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak
nodes.image: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak introducing himself for Voice intro project.jpg
nodes.summary: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University (circa 1959–1961). He founded and served as director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages (circa 1969–1989) and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

nodes.label: Central Institute of Indian Languages
variants: Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysore

nodes.label: Motoi Ono
nodes.summary: Motoi Ono (born 1958) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima, completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tsukuba, and earned a Dr.phil. from the University of Vienna before joining Tsukuba's faculty around 1999.

Center for the Study of Hindu Traditions

nodes.label: Manabendu Banerjee
nodes.summary: Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society. He also worked at Jadavpur University as the Co-ordinator of DSA Sanskrit, attested in 2003.

nodes.label: Adam Hardy
nodes.summary: Adam Hardy specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying architecture at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1971–1974), he held professorships at De Montfort University (~1993–2005) and Cardiff University (~2005).

nodes.label: Bernard Goldman
nodes.summary: Bernard Goldman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1952–1955) and held a post at Wayne State University (~1956–1989).

nodes.label: David Dean Shulman
nodes.description: Israeli-American indologist, historian of religion, and poet
nodes.summary: David Dean Shulman is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. under John Ralston Marr at SOAS, University of London (1972–1976). He held multiple positions at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, including Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion from 1985.

nodes.label: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
variants: Center for the Study of Christianity der Hebräischen Universität Jerusalem
Franz Rosenzweig Minerva Research Center for German-Jewish Literature and Cultural History

nodes.label: D. Srinivasachar
nodes.summary: D. Srinivasachar was an Indology scholar who succeeded Rudrapatna Shamasastry. Attested from 1931 to 1933, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore.

nodes.label: Henk Bodewitz
nodes.summary: Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist. He earned his degrees, including a PhD under Jan Gonda, at Utrecht University. He served as assistant professor and chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1966; 1976–1992) and as professor at Leiden University (~1972–1976; 1992–2002).

nodes.label: Victor H. Mair
variants: ヴィクター・ヘンリー・メア
nodes.summary: Victor H. Mair is a sinologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dartmouth, Washington, SOAS, and Harvard under Patrick Hanan and James Robert Hightower. He held posts at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania, where he started in 1979.

nodes.label: Richard W. Lariviere
nodes.summary: Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (PhD). He served as dean at UT Austin, provost at Kansas, president of the University of Oregon, and president of the Field Museum.

nodes.label: Kenyu Mitomo
nodes.summary: Kenyu Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley, studying under teachers including Akira Hirakawa. He was Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968–2015).

nodes.label: Yutaka Kanazawa
nodes.summary: Yutaka Kanazawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Ryukoku University in 2010, studying under Shoryu Katsura, co-supervisor Masaaki Noni, and teachers Kōgi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, and Isao Shimizu.

nodes.label: Kōgi Kudara
nodes.summary: Kōgi Kudara was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1978 to 2004 and was an editor for the Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Masaaki Noni
nodes.summary: Masaaki Noni worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Gadjin Nagao and held posts at Ryukoku University, serving as assistant professor (attested 2003) and later as professor (attested 2013–2014).

nodes.label: James Duerlinger
nodes.summary: James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock, and held a post at the University of Iowa as Professor Emeritus in 1971.

nodes.label: Rita Langer
nodes.summary: Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004). She has held posts at the University of Bristol.

nodes.label: Eduard Müller
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Eduard Müller completed his Inauguraldissertation at the University of Leipzig (~1871–1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern (~1886–1908).

nodes.label: Jacques May
nodes.summary: Jacques May was a scholar in Buddhist studies, indology, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Constantin Régamey (~1952–1957) and served as editor-in-chief at Hōbōgirin (~1968–1981) and professor at the University of Lausanne (~1968–1992).

nodes.label: Malati J. Shendge
nodes.summary: Malati J. Shendge was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, R. D. Vadekar, and received guidance from Akira Hirakawa.

nodes.label: Jan E. M. Houben
nodes.summary: Jan E. M. Houben specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Dutch Research Council (attested 1999), Leiden University (attested 2000–2002), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études as a directeur d’études (attested 2009–2012).

nodes.label: Christopher I. Beckwith
variants: クリストファー・I・ベックウィズ
nodes.jawiki: クリストファー・ベックウィズ
nodes.summary: Christopher I. Beckwith is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State University and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, later serving as an editor and faculty member at Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Elliot Sperling
nodes.summary: Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history. Educated at Queens College and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lynn Struve, he served as associate professor at Indiana University (1987–2015).

nodes.label: Anne-Marie Blondeau
nodes.summary: Anne-Marie Blondeau is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein as well as traditional teachers Dagpo Rinpoche, Yonten Gyatso, and Geshe Ngawang Dakpa. She held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

nodes.label: Pema Tsering
nodes.summary: Pema Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Shenphen Nangwa. He served as an editorial consultant at the University of Bonn, attested in 1982.

nodes.label: Helga Uebach
nodes.summary: Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich in 1967. She served as an editorial consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1964.

Kommission für Zentralasiatische Studien der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften
Bayer. Akademie der Wissenschaften, Kommission für zentralasiatische Studien

nodes.label: Per Kværne
nodes.summary: Per Kværne (born 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Oslo under Nils Simonsson. He held posts at the University of Bergen and the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: Alexander W. Macdonald
nodes.summary: Alexander W. Macdonald was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the CNRS (~1956–1989), the Musée de l'Homme, and served as Professor at Paris Nanterre University (~1975–1991).

nodes.label: Michael L. Walter
nodes.summary: Michael L. Walter worked in Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Larry William Moses, was a research fellow at Lumbini International Research Institute (2000), and served as an editorial consultant and cataloger at Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Jampa Losang Panglung
nodes.summary: Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery and completed his Magister and doctorate at the University of Munich, later serving in dictionary and research roles at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Ian Mabbett
nodes.summary: Ian Mabbett (1939–2020) was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford. He served as Reader in History at Monash University (~1965–2004) and Professor at Aichi Bunkyo University in 2000.

nodes.label: David P. Chandler
nodes.image: Professor David Chandler gives expert testimony on 18 July 2012 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: David P. Chandler is a historian who studied at Harvard, Yale, and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Monash University (circa 1972–1997), the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Cornell University, and Johns Hopkins University.

nodes.label: H. Kikuchi
nodes.summary: H. Kikuchi, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, was a research student at the University of Delhi studying under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (attested 1966).

nodes.label: Technical University of Darmstadt
variants: Institut für Cellulosechemie mit Holzforschungsstelle der Technischen Hochschule Darmstadt

nodes.label: Purna Harsha Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Purna Harsha Bajracharya worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 1972, he was attested as Chief Research Officer at both the Archaeological Survey of India and the Department of Archaeology.

nodes.label: Shujun Motegi
nodes.summary: Shujun Motegi (born 1951) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and at Kyoto University. He later served as a professor of ethics at Shinshu University, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Jürgen Neuß
nodes.summary: Jürgen Neuß is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2007, having studied under Harry Falk.

nodes.label: Anne Feldhaus
nodes.description: American academic researching Marathi Philology and Ethanography
nodes.summary: Anne Feldhaus worked in Indology and religious studies, earning a doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania after studying at Manhattanville University. In 1981, she was appointed Distinguished Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University, where she became emeritus.

nodes.label: David Drewes
nodes.summary: David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia in 2006 under Karen Christina Lang and served as an Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Manitoba (attested 2008–2010).

nodes.label: Ram Chandra Pandeya
nodes.summary: Ram Chandra Pandeya was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and T. R. V. Murti. At the University of Delhi, he was Head of Buddhist Studies (~1966-1973) and an acharya (~1973-1996).

nodes.label: T. R. V. Murti
nodes.description: Indian academic, philosopher, writer and translator
nodes.summary: T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later directing its Centre for Advanced Study in Philosophy and teaching at Oxford and McMaster.

nodes.label: Simo Parpola
nodes.summary: Simo Parpola is a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Helsinki. He was an associate professor at the University of Chicago (1977–1979) and became a professor at Helsinki in 1978.

nodes.label: Geshe Gendun Lodro
nodes.summary: Geshe Gendun Lodro was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Drepung Monastery and Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Khensur Ngawang Legden, later holding posts at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Dagpo Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Born in 1932, Dagpo Rinpoche works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche, and later taught scholars including David Seyfort Ruegg and Anne-Marie Blondeau.

nodes.label: T. S. Rukmani
nodes.summary: T. S. Rukmani is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She held positions at Miranda House (attested 1983–1989) and served as Chairperson of Hindu Studies in the Department of Religion at Concordia University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Kathryn R. Blackstone
nodes.summary: Kathryn R. Blackstone is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held attested academic posts at Victoria University of Wellington in 1998 and the University of Manitoba in 1999.

nodes.label: Tessa J. Bartholomeusz
nodes.summary: Tessa J. Bartholomeusz was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Florida State University and the University of Virginia (PhD). She taught at the University of Virginia, Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis, and Florida State University.

nodes.label: David Brick
nodes.summary: David Brick is an Indology scholar who studied under Patrick Olivelle (attested 2009). He served as a professor at Yale University, attested between 2012 and 2018.

nodes.label: Richard S. Cohen
nodes.summary: Richard S. Cohen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied under Luis Oscar Gómez and Walter M. Spink. He is an Associate Professor of South Asian Religious Literatures at the University of California, San Diego.

nodes.label: Michael Friedrich
nodes.summary: Michael Friedrich (born 1955) is a Sinologist who earned his PhD from the University of Munich. After working at Munich (1983–1986), he was a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

nodes.label: Jörg B. Quenzer
nodes.summary: Jörg B. Quenzer works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2016, 2026) and served as an editorial board member for Studies in Manuscript Cultures (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Stefan Anacker
nodes.summary: Stefan Anacker was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison circa 1965–1970, where he studied under Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: Roger R. Jackson
nodes.summary: Scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology Roger R. Jackson earned degrees from Wesleyan and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. 1983). He taught at Fairfield University (attested 1986) and Carleton College (attested 1990–2017).

nodes.label: Peter N. Gregory
variants: ビーター・N・グレゴリー
ピーター・N・グレゴリー
nodes.summary: Peter N. Gregory works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi (1981) and held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Kuroda Institute, and Smith College.

nodes.label: Bruce Cameron Hall
nodes.summary: Bruce Cameron Hall specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1980 and served as an assistant editor at the College of William & Mary (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Bunga Fukui
nodes.summary: Bunga Fukui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1978–2004).

nodes.label: Nirmal Chandra Sinha
nodes.summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He served as founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987) and Centenary Professor at the University of Calcutta (1971).

nodes.label: Walter Bruno Henning
nodes.jawiki: ヴァルター・ブルーノ・ヘニング
nodes.summary: Walter Bruno Henning (1908–1967) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. After studying at the University of Göttingen, he held academic posts at SOAS University of London (~1936–1961), Columbia University, and UC Berkeley (~1961–1967).

nodes.label: Gustav Haloun
nodes.summary: Gustav Haloun was a sinologist and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Vienna, Leipzig (under August Conrady), and Charles University. He held positions at Halle-Wittenberg and Göttingen before serving as Chair of Chinese at Cambridge from 1938 to 1951.

nodes.label: Kiyoshi Okano
nodes.summary: Kiyoshi Okano is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University, serving as an associate professor (attested 2002) and later as a professor of Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

nodes.label: Dipesh Chakrabarty
variants: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.jawiki: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.summary: Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian and philosopher who earned a PhD from the Australian National University. He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1983–1995) and became the Lawrence A. Kimpton Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

nodes.label: Sanjay Subrahmanyam
nodes.summary: Sanjay Subrahmanyam is a historian who studied at the University of Delhi, including St. Stephen's College and the Delhi School of Economics. He held chairs and teaching posts at EHESS, the University of Oxford, Collège de France, and UCLA.

nodes.label: Thomas Oberlies
nodes.summary: Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme, and held positions at Tübingen (attested 1988), Zurich (1990), Freiburg (attested 2001), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Achard
nodes.summary: Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

nodes.label: Pierre Arènes
nodes.summary: Pierre Arènes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under André Bareau and held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2003–2004).

nodes.label: Françoise Pommaret
variants: フランソワーズ・ポマレ
nodes.summary: Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian educated at INALCO, the Sorbonne, and the University of Paris. Her career includes posts as Director of Langues et cultures de l'aire tibétaine (around 2001) and Director of Research at the CNRS (appointed 2002).

nodes.label: Katia Buffetrille
nodes.summary: Katia Buffetrille specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald and held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études, Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale, and Études mongoles, sibériennes, centrasiatiques et tibétaines.

nodes.label: Akira Shimada
nodes.summary: Akira Shimada works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi under Rajeev Lochan and under Daud Ali, later holding posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York at New Paltz.

nodes.label: Amar Singh
nodes.summary: Amar Singh works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied under Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963) and completed doctoral studies under Anthony Kennedy Warder, also studying with Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and others.

nodes.label: Nicolas Morrissey
nodes.summary: Nicolas Morrissey is an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004). He holds a post at the University of Georgia.

nodes.label: Peter Zieme
nodes.summary: Peter Zieme worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (1960–1965), he served at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (1965–2007) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1992–2007).

nodes.label: Dondub Buddhayin
nodes.summary: Dondub Buddhayin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who served as abbot of Ganden Dargye Ling and Chilttai Monastery.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson
nodes.image: Jeffrey Masson appearing on "After Dark", 23 September 1989.jpg
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his BA and PhD (~1964-1970) at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at the University of Toronto, Sigmund Freud Archives, UC Berkeley, and University of Auckland.

nodes.label: Edward C. Dimock Jr.
nodes.summary: Edward C. Dimock Jr. was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard and Yale. He taught linguistics and Asian languages at the University of Chicago (1966–1993) and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972–1986).

nodes.label: Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) was a philosopher and Indologist. He earned his B.A. at the University of Calcutta, studying under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta, and later served as a philosophy teacher at City College, Kolkata, and visiting professor at Calcutta.

nodes.label: Niharranjan Ray
nodes.summary: Niharranjan Ray studied at Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden. A scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he served as Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts at the University of Calcutta and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Indian Institute of Advanced Studt, Shimla
Indian Institute of Advanced Study, Shimla
Indian Institute of Advanced Studies, Shimla

nodes.label: Vladimir Balabushevich
nodes.summary: Vladimir Balabushevich (1900–1970) was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970 and 1990).

nodes.label: Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov
nodes.summary: Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1936–1941). He was affiliated with the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1960–1998).

nodes.label: Maulana Azad College
variants: Department of Sanskrit, Central Calcutta College

nodes.label: Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology who held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from around 1967 to 1999.

nodes.label: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970–1975) and lectured in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982, 1994).

nodes.label: Vidyasagar College
variants: Department of Sanskrit, Vidyasagar College, Calcutta

nodes.label: José Ignacio Cabezón
nodes.summary: José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Caltech, Sera Monastery, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, he taught at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) before becoming Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.

nodes.label: Georges B. J. Dreyfus
nodes.summary: Georges B. J. Dreyfus studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and earned his doctorate at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he was appointed Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College.

nodes.label: Thupten Jinpa
nodes.image: HH the Dalai Lama enlightened translator, Dr. Thupten Jinpa.jpg
nodes.summary: Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned a Geshe Lharam at Ganden Shartse and a B.A. from Cambridge. He held posts at Ganden, Girton College, Stanford, and the Institute of Tibetan Classics, which he founded.

nodes.label: Danielle Feller
nodes.summary: Danielle Feller is an Indologist who earned her PhD from the University of Lausanne through 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst. She also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.

nodes.label: Ryudo Suita
nodes.summary: Ryudo Suita is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer and held an academic post at Bukkyo University between 1997 and 2020.

nodes.label: Ryoken Nawa
nodes.summary: Ryoken Nawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University and as a lecturer at Osaka University.

nodes.id: I:Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine, Banaras Hindu University
nodes.label: Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine, Banaras Hindu University
variants: Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine, Banaras Hindu University

nodes.label: Taranatha Tarkavachaspati
nodes.summary: Taranatha Tarkavachaspati (1812–1885) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University from around 1845 to 1873, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Victor Turner
variants: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.summary: Victor Turner was an anthropologist of religion who studied at University College London and the University of Manchester. He held appointments at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute, Manchester, Cornell University (1963), the University of Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (1977).

nodes.label: Georges Dumézil
variants: ジョルジュ・デュメジル
nodes.jawiki: ジョルジュ・デュメジル
nodes.summary: Georges Dumézil studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss. Specializing in linguistics and religious studies, he held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Mircea Eliade
variants: ミルチャ・エリアーデ
nodes.jawiki: ミルチャ・エリアーデ
nodes.description: Romanian-American historian, writer, philosopher and professor at the University of Chicago (1907–1986)
nodes.summary: Mircea Eliade was a scholar of religion, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bucharest under Nae Ionescu, studied at Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, and held professorships at the Sorbonne and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Angelo Brelich
nodes.summary: Angelo Brelich (1913–1977) was a scholar in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Erzsébet University (~1932–1937) and subsequently held an academic post at Sapienza University of Rome (~1958–1977).

nodes.label: Daniel Baum
nodes.summary: Daniel Baum is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and his doctorate at Leiden University under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky.

nodes.label: Alexander Lubotsky
nodes.summary: Alexander Lubotsky specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University under Robert S. P. Beekes, becoming full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.

nodes.label: Durga Prasad Dikshit
nodes.summary: Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Lucknow, studying under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri as well as R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.

nodes.label: Baij Nath Puri
nodes.summary: Baij Nath Puri was an Indian scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his M.Litt. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford, he served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1956–1976).

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi
nodes.summary: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Deccan College and Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and was Honorary Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Nagpur University (1957–1966).

nodes.label: Margaret Cone
nodes.summary: Margaret Cone is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts attested in 1996 at the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge.

nodes.label: Ludwig Alsdorf
nodes.summary: Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctorates under Walther Schubring and Heinrich Lüders. He held posts at Allahabad, Münster, and Humboldt University of Berlin before holding the chair of Indian history and culture at Hamburg (1950–1972).

nodes.label: Mahesh Research Institute
variants: Mahesh Research Institute of Indian Philosophy

nodes.label: Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj
nodes.summary: Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff at Dakshinamurti Peetha (attested 1980). He founded the Mahesh Research Institute and Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha.

nodes.label: Maggie Bickford
nodes.summary: Maggie Bickford specializes in Sinology and art history/archaeology. She studied at Bennington College, Yale, and Princeton, and held posts as Professor of East Asian Studies at Brown University (around 1987 and 1993) and Member at the Institute for Advanced Study (~1997–1998).

nodes.label: Phyllis Granoff
nodes.summary: Phyllis Granoff (born 1947) works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University (c. 1973) and served as Professor at McMaster University (c. 1976–2004) before becoming Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (2004).

nodes.label: Shin Fujinaga
nodes.summary: Working in indology and philosophy, Shin Fujinaga held an attested post at Hiroshima University (1992) and posts at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 1991, and as Associate Professor in 2000).

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College
nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College
variants: 都城工業高等専門学校

nodes.label: Gavin Flood
nodes.summary: Gavin Flood (b. 1954) studied at Lancaster University (circa 1976–1988). Active in Indology and religious studies, he held posts at Lampeter (circa 1991–2003), Stirling (circa 2003–2005), the University of Oxford (2005–2015), and Yale-NUS College (2016).

nodes.label: Kenneth R. Valpey
nodes.summary: Kenneth R. Valpey works in religious studies, indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, taught Ravi M. Gupta, and held an academic post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry
nodes.description: Kannada writer, lexicographer, grammar expert, critic and editor
nodes.summary: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Mysore under teachers including K. V. Puttappa, D. L. Narasimhachar, and Harogadde Manappa Nayak, later serving there as lecturer and Professor (1984–1994).

nodes.label: A. K. Ramanujan
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and linguistics, he studied at Mysore and Indiana University Bloomington. He taught at MS University of Baroda and Deccan College before a long career at the University of Chicago (1962–1993), also visiting Harvard.

nodes.label: D. R. Nagaraj
nodes.summary: D. R. Nagaraj (1954–1998) was an Indology scholar who studied at Bangalore University (~1973–1978) and subsequently held a post there (~1978–1998). He taught Sheldon Pollock.

nodes.label: Thomas R. Trautmann
nodes.summary: Thomas R. Trautmann is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and served at the University of Michigan, where he was attested as co-director in 1980 and affiliated in 1991.

nodes.label: Lata S. Bapat
nodes.summary: Lata S. Bapat works in philosophy and Indology. She completed her PhD under M. P. Marathe at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1985, where she also served as a Research Associate in Buddhist Philosophy (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Deccan Education Society
variants: デカン・エデュケーション・ソサエティー

nodes.label: Institute of Buddhist Studies, Tring
variants: The Institute of Buddhist Studies, Tring
