nodes.label: Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium
variants: Académie royale des Sciences, des Lettres et des Beaux-Arts de Belgique
Königliche Akademie der Wissenschaften, Literatur und Schönen Künste Belgiens

nodes.label: Laxmanshastri Joshi
nodes.summary: Laxmanshastri Joshi (1901–1994) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati from circa 1916 to 1923 and served as Director of Prajna Pathashala from circa 1948 to 1994.

nodes.label: Péter-Dániel Szántó
nodes.summary: Péter-Dániel Szántó is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at Oxford, All Souls College, and Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: Alfonsa Ferrari
nodes.summary: Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Giuseppe Tucci, Carlo Formichi, Theodor Bloch, Louis Renou, Jacques Bacot, and Marcelle Lalou, conducting research and later teaching Sanskrit (1952) at Sapienza University of Rome.

nodes.label: Jacques Bacot
nodes.image: Tchraker lama, Jacques Bacot et moines.png
nodes.summary: Jacques Bacot was a tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1919) and the University of Paris (~1936–1958), also serving as president of Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: Marcelle Lalou
nodes.summary: Marcelle Lalou (1890–1967) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. She later taught at the EPHE from 1938 to 1963.

nodes.label: P. B. Annangaracharya
nodes.summary: P. B. Annangaracharya worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Asuri Ramanujacharya and served as Head Pandit at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1954).

nodes.label: Mark McClish
nodes.summary: Mark McClish is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Patrick Olivelle. He held a post at Birmingham-Southern College (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Alan Butterworth
nodes.summary: Alan Butterworth was an Indologist and historian. He was educated at Elizabeth College and Balliol College, Oxford (c. 1883–1885), and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1885 to 1918.

nodes.label: Richard Carnac Temple
nodes.summary: Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) studied at Harrow and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. Working in Indology and archaeology, he edited *Indian Antiquary* (~1884–1910), founded *Panjab Notes and Queries* (1883), and served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps.

nodes.label: Stephanie W. Jamison
nodes.summary: Stephanie W. Jamison is an indologist and linguist. She completed her doctoral work at Yale University under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill. She taught at Harvard University and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA circa 2002.

nodes.label: Joel Peter Brereton
nodes.summary: Joel Peter Brereton (born 1948) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Stanley Insler in 1971 and held posts at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 2004, emeritus ~2020).

nodes.label: Martha Ann Selby
nodes.summary: Martha Ann Selby is an Indologist who served as Series Editor for South Asia Research (attested 2014). She is Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin and Sangam Professor and Department Chair at Harvard University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: University of Missouri
variants: University of the State of Missouri

nodes.label: Calvert Watkins
variants: キャルバート・ワトキンズ
nodes.jawiki: キャルバート・ワトキンズ
nodes.summary: Calvert Watkins was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Friends Seminary, Harvard (PhD 1959), EPHE, and DIAS. He spent his career as a professor at Harvard University (1959-2003) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2003-2013).

nodes.label: Satkari Sharma Vangiya
nodes.summary: Satkari Sharma Vangiya is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ramachandra Shastri Vyakaranacharya, Ramachandra Jha, and Ramachandra Sastri.

nodes.label: David B. Gray
nodes.summary: David B. Gray specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. His appointments include a postdoctoral fellowship at Rice University and teaching at Santa Clara University.

nodes.label: Ulrike Roesler
nodes.summary: Ulrike Roesler is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned her PhD from the University of Münster. She taught at Freiburg and Marburg, and later became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford.

nodes.label: Roland Steiner
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and Tibetology, Roland Steiner studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990) and served as assistant professor at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Roger Bischoff
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Roger Bischoff studied under traditional teachers Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin. He served as an assistant teacher at the International Meditation Centre (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Mother Sayamagyi
nodes.summary: Mother Sayamagyi (1925–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under and succeeded Sayagyi U Ba Khin, and taught Roger Bischoff.

nodes.label: Radboud University Nijmegen
variants: Faculty of Theology of the Radboud University Nijmegen

nodes.label: Matthew Clark
nodes.summary: Matthew Clark completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (1999–2004) in Indology and religious studies, where he studied under Daud Ali and George Botterill.

nodes.label: Edward James Rapson
nodes.summary: Edward James Rapson, an Indologist, linguist, and historian/archaeologist, studied at St John's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum's Coin Room (1887–1906) and was Professor of Sanskrit at University College London (1903) and Cambridge (1906–1936).

nodes.label: Stanley Cecil Sutton
nodes.summary: Stanley Cecil Sutton (1907–1993) was an Indology and history scholar who served as Librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and at the India Office Records (attested 1974).

nodes.label: Muhammad Ashraf Khan
nodes.summary: Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He has served as Deputy Director at Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums in Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Quaid-i-Azam University
variants: Taxila Insititute of Asian Civilizations, Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad
Taxila Institute of Asian Civilizations at Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad

nodes.id: I:Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh
nodes.label: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh
variants: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Andhra Pradesh
Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums

nodes.label: Zarawar Khan
nodes.summary: Zarawar Khan works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He earned an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).

nodes.label: Satoshi Naiki
nodes.summary: Satoshi Naiki is a scholar of archaeology, history, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Kyoto University, where he also served as an Assistant Professor (attested 2016–2020).

nodes.label: Jessie Pons
nodes.summary: Jessie Pons is a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University by 2011 and was attested as a Junior Professor at Ruhr University Bochum in 2019.

nodes.label: Masakazu Tanaka
nodes.summary: Masakazu Tanaka (b. 1955) works in religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University and earned his Ph.D. from the London School of Economics, later serving as assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and vice president at the Professional Institute of International Fashion.

nodes.label: Sita Krishna Nambiar
nodes.summary: Sita Krishna Nambiar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bonn under the doctoral supervision of Paul Hacker.

nodes.label: Norman Mosley Penzer
nodes.summary: Norman Mosley Penzer was a scholar in Indology and other fields. In 1925, he was attested as a Fellow of the Royal Anthropological Institute, Royal Geographical Society, and Geological Society, and as a member of the Folklore and Royal Asiatic societies.

nodes.id: I:Royal Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Royal Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland
Valerie Stoker
nodes.summary: Valerie Stoker is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who holds a post at Wright State University. She studied under traditional teachers D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi.

nodes.label: Sangay Dorji
nodes.summary: Sangay Dorji works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tengtho Monastery and Semtokha Rigney School, Dorji later taught at Semtokha Rigney School and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (attested 1999–2004).

nodes.label: Yongtong Tang
nodes.summary: Yongtong Tang was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Tsinghua and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt, later holding posts at Southeast University, Peking University, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

nodes.label: Nalini Balbir
nodes.summary: Nalini Balbir is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat (~1976–1980). She held posts at the CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (from 1988), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2000).

nodes.label: Kalpana K. Sheth
nodes.summary: Kalpana K. Sheth is an Indologist who completed her doctoral studies under Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani. She held a post at the L.D. Institute of Indology.

nodes.label: Chandrabhal Tripathi
nodes.summary: Chandrabhal Tripathi (1929–1996) was an Indologist. He earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1957–1960), held a post there (~1960–1974), and served as a professor at the Free University of Berlin (~1974–1994).

nodes.label: Henry Sullivan Jarrett
nodes.summary: Henry Sullivan Jarrett (1839–1919) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Heinrich Blochmann and served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners at Fort William from circa 1870 to 1892.

nodes.label: Louis Dumont
nodes.summary: Louis Dumont worked in indology and religious studies, studying at EPHE, the Institut d'ethnologie, and under Marcel Mauss, Walther Schubring, and Alain Froment. He held posts at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires, Oxford (1951–1955), and EHESS (1955).

nodes.label: A. Anantacharya
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and philosophy, he served as a Pandit at the Karnataka State Archaeology Department and was attested as head of Yatiraja Mutt in 1926.

nodes.label: Paul E. Muller-Ortega
nodes.summary: Paul E. Muller-Ortega is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He held posts at Michigan State University (attested 1992) and the University of Rochester (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Jayandra Soni
nodes.summary: Jayandra Soni works in Indology and philosophy. He earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, later holding posts at Banaras Hindu University, McMaster, the University of Marburg (1991–2012), and the University of Innsbruck (circa 2012–2017).

nodes.label: Michael Torsten Much
nodes.summary: Michael Torsten Much is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He was a visiting Alexander von Humboldt Foundation fellow at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Ariane Macdonald
nodes.summary: Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1972) and taught Amy Heller and Yoshiro Imaeda.

nodes.label: Taitetsu Unno
nodes.summary: Taitetsu Unno was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo, and served as Jill Ker Conway Professor Emeritus of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).

nodes.label: Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla
nodes.summary: Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar and served as Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

nodes.label: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar
nodes.summary: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College from around 1914 to 1945 and as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from around 1945 to 1976.

nodes.label: Eun Hino
nodes.summary: Eun Hino (born 1981) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a master's degree at the University of Tokyo (~2005–2007). Hino held posts at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2015) and Musashino University (~2015–2018).

nodes.label: Mai Mishiro
nodes.summary: Mai Mishiro is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She held affiliations with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested in 2011) and Waseda University (attested in 2016).

nodes.label: Amalananda Ghosh
nodes.summary: Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1937–1938). He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968) and was a fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1968–1971).

nodes.label: Karnatak University
variants: Museum of Art and Archaeology, Karnatak University, Dharwad

nodes.label: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson
nodes.summary: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Trinity College Dublin (~1857–1861), he served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

nodes.label: Taichi Tado
nodes.summary: Taichi Tado specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held teaching posts at Waseda University (attested 2020), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020–2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Michael Jerryson
nodes.summary: Michael Jerryson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from UC Santa Barbara under Mark Juergensmeyer. He held faculty posts at Eckerd College (~2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).

nodes.label: Mark Juergensmeyer

nodes.summary: Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD in Buddhist Textual Studies at Mahidol University (attested 2021) under doctoral supervisor Giuliano Giustarini and co-supervisors Peter Skilling and Kengo Harimoto.

nodes.label: Ven. Dhammapāla

nodes.label: Mitsuji Fukunaga

nodes.label: Yinggang Sun
nodes.summary: Yinggang Sun is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held a post at Fudan University (attested 2014) and serves as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.summary: Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Wu earned a PhD from Cardiff University under doctoral supervisor Max Deeg (attested 2012) and held a postdoctoral position at the University of Tokyo (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Oliver Petersen
nodes.summary: Oliver Petersen (born 1961) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang (~1983–2003) and held a post at the Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg beginning around 1983.

nodes.label: Ryosuke Furui
nodes.summary: Ryosuke Furui is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and holds a professorship at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Shivram Dattatray Joshi
nodes.summary: Shivram Dattatray Joshi specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Shankashastri Marulkar, Maheshwarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard, later serving as professor and director at Savitribai Phule Pune University and department head at Deccan College.

nodes.label: Govind Vinayak Devasthali
nodes.summary: Govind Vinayak Devasthali was an Indologist who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar. His career included posts as professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

nodes.label: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam
nodes.summary: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested there in 1967). He also served as Reader at Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha and Principal at Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan (attested 1973).

nodes.label: Shinobu Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her PhD from Nagoya University in 1995 and served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shogo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Shogo Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University, where he taught from circa 1989 and served as professor from circa 2002 to 2024, later affiliating with Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and Taisho University.

nodes.label: Yael Bentor
nodes.summary: Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington under scholars including Gregory Schopen, she has taught Indian Studies (attested 1995–2000) and held a professorship (attested 2026) at Hebrew University.

nodes.label: Takahiro Kato
nodes.summary: Takahiro Kato is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his doctoral dissertation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 2011. He holds posts as professor at the University of Tokyo and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Parimal G. Patil

nodes.label: David Slakter

nodes.label: Peter Masefield

nodes.label: Vimla Karnatak
nodes.summary: Vimla Karnatak is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Gajanan Shastri Musalgaonkar. She served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Banaras Hindu University (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Munish Chandra Joshi

nodes.label: Puthezhethu Rama Menon

nodes.label: Kanti Chandra Pandey

nodes.label: Purushottama Bilimoria

nodes.label: J. N. Farquhar

nodes.label: Ester Bianchi

nodes.label: Fernand Meyer

nodes.label: Burton Stein
nodes.summary: Burton Stein was a historian and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa from around 1966 to 1988 and at SOAS University of London as a Professorial Research Associate from around 1989 to 1996.

nodes.label: Richard M. Eaton
nodes.summary: Richard M. Eaton is a scholar of history and Indology. He studied at the College of Wooster (~1958–1962) and served as Professor of History at the University of Arizona (~1972).

nodes.description: Hindi novelist, literary historian, essayist, critic and scholar from India

nodes.label: Krishna Sharma
nodes.summary: Krishna Sharma is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She served as Principal of Gargi College and held an appointment as a Visiting Scholar at Stanford University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Romila Thapar
nodes.summary: Historian and Indologist Romila Thapar studied under A. L. Basham at SOAS (doctorate ~1955–1958). She held professorships at the University of Delhi (1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991, 1993).

nodes.label: David R. Loy
nodes.summary: David R. Loy works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Carleton, King's College London, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore, he taught at NUS (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

nodes.summary: Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was an Indologist and historian. He served at the University of Calcutta as Carmichael Professor and Head of the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture (attested 1939) and later of History and Ancient Indian History and Culture (attested 1965).

nodes.summary: N. A. Gore was an Indologist who served as Librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957–1958) and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).

nodes.label: Olivier de Bernon
nodes.summary: Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Pierre L. Lamant. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1990) and as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2001–2002).

nodes.label: Miri Albahari
nodes.summary: Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, later holding posts at New South Wales and Western Australia.

nodes.label: Gadjin Nagao
variants: Gadjin Masato Nagao 長尾雅人
nodes.summary: Gadjin Nagao was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, he held the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971) and taught at Kyushu University and abroad.

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Anālayo
nodes.description: German Buddhist monk, scholar, and meditation teacher (born 1962)
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Anālayo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Ceylon (PhD) and University of Marburg (Habilitation). He has held posts at the University of Hamburg, Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy, and Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

nodes.label: Jinhua Chen
nodes.summary: Jinhua Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research under Noritoshi Aramaki at Kyoto University, he became a professor of East Asian Buddhism at the University of British Columbia (attested 2008–2018).

nodes.label: Jagannath Upadhyaya
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Jagannath Upadhyaya was a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1980–1983) and became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies in 1985.

nodes.label: Thomas E. Wood
nodes.summary: Thomas E. Wood is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his BA and PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. He held posts at California State University, Fresno, and SUNY New Paltz.

nodes.label: Amar Nath Pandeya
nodes.summary: Amar Nath Pandeya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Delhi (attested 1968) and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Michiko Yusa
nodes.summary: Michiko Yusa (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctorate under Raimon Panikkar at UC Santa Barbara (~1976–1983) and served as a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).

nodes.label: Edeltraud Harzer
nodes.summary: Active in Indology and philosophy, Edeltraud Harzer studied at Charles University, the University of Washington (PhD), and under traditional teachers Sri Narayana Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Thich Nhat Hanh
variants: ティク・ナット・ハン
nodes.jawiki: ティク・ナット・ハン
nodes.summary: Thich Nhat Hanh was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Báo Quốc Temple, Saigon University, Princeton, and Columbia. He held posts at Columbia, Princeton, Cornell, and Vạn Hạnh University.

nodes.label: Hideaki Nakatani
nodes.summary: Hideaki Nakatani is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Kyoto University and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Gadjin Nagao and Yutaka Ochihara. He was attested as a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.

nodes.label: Sieglinde Dietz
nodes.summary: Sieglinde Dietz specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Michael Hahn in 1980 and held a post at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1990.

nodes.label: Giacomella Orofino
nodes.summary: Giacomella Orofino is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Sapienza University of Rome under Raniero Gnoli, and began teaching at "L'Orientale" around 1998.

nodes.label: Günter Grönbold
nodes.summary: Günter Grönbold worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Bavarian State Library from around 1974 to 2008, where he headed the Oriental Section from around 1987 to 2008.

nodes.label: Bavarian State Library
variants: kgl. bayer. Hof- und Staatsbibliothek in München

nodes.label: Nicholas Justin Allen
nodes.summary: Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies under Rodney Needham at the University of Oxford, where he served as Reader in Social Anthropology from 1976 and held posts at Wolfson College.

nodes.label: Sherry B. Ortner
nodes.summary: Sherry B. Ortner is an anthropologist in Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Bryn Mawr College and the University of Chicago. She held academic posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: George Adolphus Jacob
nodes.summary: An Indologist, George Adolphus Jacob served as a colonel in the Bombay Staff Corps (attested 1888) and the Indian Army (attested 1909), and was a Fellow at the University of Mumbai (attested 1894).

nodes.label: Motohiro Yoritomi
nodes.summary: Motohiro Yoritomi (1945–2015) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (BA, MA, PhD) under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He held professorships at Shuchiin University and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

nodes.label: James Hadley
nodes.summary: James Hadley (1821–1872) worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Fairfield Academy and Yale, where he studied under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, he taught at Middlebury College and served as Professor of Greek at Yale from 1845 to 1872.

nodes.label: Francis Woodman Cleaves
nodes.description: American orientalist historian. mongolist and sinologist (1911-1995)
nodes.summary: Francis Woodman Cleaves worked in sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Dartmouth, Harvard, and under Paul Pelliot, and served as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

nodes.label: Krishna Kanta Handiqui
nodes.image: Krishna Kanta Handique 1983 stamp of India.jpg
nodes.summary: Krishna Kanta Handiqui (1898–1982) was an Indologist educated at Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jorhat College (1930–1948) and as Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).

nodes.label: Har Dutt Sharma
nodes.summary: Har Dutt Sharma was an Indologist who served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi and held an affiliation attested at Hindu College, Delhi (1957).

nodes.label: Suryakumar Bhuyan
nodes.summary: Suryakumar Bhuyan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Cotton University, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and SOAS University of London (PhD 1936), he served as Principal of Cotton University and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1957–1960).

nodes.label: Banikanta Kakati
nodes.summary: Banikanta Kakati worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He later served as a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and as Dean of Arts at Gauhati University (1948).

nodes.label: Amrit Madhav Ghatage
nodes.summary: Amrit Madhav Ghatage was an Indologist and linguist. He was Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College (~1961–1978) and Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1993–2003).

nodes.label: Khakyab Dorje
variants: 15世カルマパ・カキャブ・ドルジェ
nodes.summary: Khakyab Dorje (1871–1922) was an active figure in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and others, and taught prominent students including Kalu Rinpoche and Karsé Kongtrul.

nodes.label: Shindo Kusumoto
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and indology, Shindo Kusumoto completed a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

nodes.label: Yoshihiko Sakurai
nodes.summary: Yoshihiko Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2001). Sakurai has served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center.

nodes.id: I:Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center

variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派教学伝道研究センター

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Ueno
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Ueno works in Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004), where he also held a post, and served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Ohryu Matsushima
nodes.summary: Ohryu Matsushima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and later held a post there.

nodes.label: Jae-gwon Kim
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Jae-gwon Kim earned a PhD from Ryukoku University in 2007 and subsequently held a post there.

nodes.label: Shodo Fujita
nodes.summary: Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

nodes.label: Martin Straube
nodes.summary: Martin Straube specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies and studied under Michael Hahn. As of 2026, he holds posts at the Göttingen Academy, International Institute for Buddhist Studies, University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Albrecht Hanisch
nodes.summary: Albrecht Hanisch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Michael Hahn and earned a doctoral degree at the University of Marburg (2000). He held posts at the Nepal Research Centre and the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

nodes.label: Karl Ferdinand Johansson
nodes.summary: Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University in 1880. He later served as a professor at Uppsala University (~1899–1925) and taught Helmer Smith and Jarl Charpentier.

nodes.label: Nathuram Premi
nodes.description: Indian author of Jainism and Hindi literature

nodes.label: Entai Tomomatsu
nodes.summary: Entai Tomomatsu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio University around 1917–1920. He held a post at Taisho University and founded the Publishing Association of Abhidharmakosa-vyakhya.

nodes.label: Émile Durkheim
variants: エミール・デュルケーム
nodes.jawiki: エミール・デュルケーム
nodes.summary: Durkheim worked in religious studies and related fields, studying at the École Normale Supérieure and under Wilhelm Wundt in Leipzig. He held posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902), EPHE (1905), and the Sorbonne as professor (~1902–1917).

nodes.label: Paul J. Griffiths
nodes.summary: Paul J. Griffiths studied at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and earned a PhD from UW–Madison under Minoru Kiyota. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, he held chairs at the University of Illinois Chicago (2000–2007) and Duke University (~2007–2017).

nodes.label: Mary Shepherd Slusser
nodes.description: American anthropologist, archaeologist and art historian (1918 - 2017)
nodes.summary: Mary Shepherd Slusser (1918–2017) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. After earning degrees from the University of Michigan and Columbia University (PhD ~1950), she worked at the U.S. State Department and the National Museum of African Art.

nodes.label: Mario D'Amato
nodes.summary: Mario D'Amato (born 1969) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1994–2000) under Paul J. Griffiths, and held posts at Hampshire College (~2001–2006) and Rollins College (~2006).

variants: University of California, Irvine Seminar in Experimental Critical Theory
カリフォルニア大学アーバイン校

nodes.label: Megumu Honda
nodes.summary: Indologist and philosopher Megumu Honda studied at the Fourth Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and Yale University under Johannes Rahder, Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells. He later served as professor and professor emeritus at Doho University.

nodes.label: Fourth Higher School
variants: Fourth Higher School in Ishikawa Prefecture

nodes.label: Joachim Prandstetter
nodes.summary: Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna under Gerhard Oberhammer, completing his Magister degree by 1994.

nodes.label: Charles DiSimone
nodes.summary: Charles DiSimone works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his PhD from the University of Munich by 2016, he held a post there (attested 2021) and serves as a co-director and permanent member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: P. D. Premasiri
nodes.summary: P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ceylon, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (PhD 1980) under several scholars including David J. Kalupahana. He held various academic posts at the University of Ceylon from 1963 to 2010.

nodes.label: Mahinda Deegalle
nodes.image: Mahinda Deegalle in the video 'Imagine a Buddhist AI...'.png
nodes.summary: Mahinda Deegalle (born 1961) studied at the University of Ceylon, Harvard, and the University of Chicago under Diana L. Eck, Frank E. Reynolds, and Wendy Doniger. He held posts at IIBS, McGill, Bath Spa, and Colgate University.

nodes.label: Stephen J. Laumakis
nodes.summary: Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West, and served as Associate Professor in the Philosophy Department at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2008–2013).

nodes.label: Roger T. Ames
nodes.summary: Philosopher and sinologist Roger T. Ames earned degrees from UBC, NTU, and SOAS under D. C. Lau. He served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1978–2016) and editor of Philosophy East and West (~1987–2016).

nodes.label: Peter D. Hershock
nodes.summary: Peter D. Hershock (born 1958) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies and studied at Yale University. He served as Asian Studies Development Program Coordinator at the East-West Center and held an affiliated post at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

nodes.label: Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Edward Byles Cowell and served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1882, 1894, and 1914).

nodes.label: Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan
nodes.summary: Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent für Indologie at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1997.

nodes.label: Steven Neal Weinberger
nodes.summary: Steven Neal Weinberger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins in 2003, and was affiliated with the University of Virginia (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Denma Lochö Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. After studying at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College under various masters, he served at the University of Calcutta, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and as Abbot of Namgyal Monastery.

nodes.label: Geshe Tenzin Dhargye
nodes.summary: A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Tenzin Dhargye studied at Sera Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He taught at the University of Virginia (1999–2000) and became director of Tibetzentrum Österreich in 2008.

nodes.label: Masahiro Shimoda
nodes.summary: Masahiro Shimoda (b. 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Delhi. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023) and joined Musashino University in 2023.

nodes.label: Gendun Chophel
nodes.summary: Gendun Chophel (1903–1952) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso circa 1921–1927. He held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941 and taught Horkhang Sonam Palbar.

variants: ケンブリッジ大学ダーウィンカレッジ

nodes.label: Jules Bloch
nodes.summary: Jules Bloch was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He held chairs at the Collège de France (1936–1951) and the University of Paris (circa 1937–1951).

nodes.label: Leonard Zwilling
nodes.summary: Leonard Zwilling was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and completed his studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1976.

nodes.label: Richard P. Hayes
nodes.summary: Richard P. Hayes is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, also studying under Shoryu Katsura and T. Venkatacharya. He held posts at Toronto, McGill, and New Mexico.

nodes.label: Tadashi Tani
nodes.summary: Tadashi Tani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University, studied under Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University, and served as professor at the National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).

nodes.label: Kaiun Shirodate
nodes.summary: Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002) at Otani University.

nodes.label: Hans Harder
nodes.summary: Hans Harder (born 1966) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg, completing his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das in 1997. He worked at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007) and joined Heidelberg University in 2007.

nodes.label: Ellen M. Raven
nodes.summary: Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She held posts at Leiden University (attested 2003, 2018) and served on the editorial board of Gonda Indological Studies (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Élisée Reclus
nodes.summary: Élisée Reclus studied at the Faculté libre de théologie protestante de Montauban (1848–1849) and held a post at the New University of Brussels (~1894–1905).

nodes.summary: Lobsang Shastri works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

nodes.summary: John Powers is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Holy Cross, McMaster, and Virginia (Doktorgrad 1984–1991), he held posts at Australian National University (1995, 2008), Deakin University (2016–2022), and Melbourne (2022).

nodes.label: Ralf Kramer
nodes.summary: Ralf Kramer (born 1971) specializes in Tibetology. He studied at the University of London and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson, later working as Tibetan librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and Aris Librarian at the Bodleian Library (circa 2006).

nodes.summary: J. G. Jennings was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Principal of Muir Central College and as Director of Public Instruction for the Department of Public Instruction, Bihar and Orissa, attested in 1918.

H. Sesha Aiyangar
nodes.summary: H. Sesha Aiyangar worked in Indology and linguistics and held posts at the University of Madras in its Kannaḍa and Canarese departments (attested 1938 and 1957).

nodes.label: N. Venkataramanayya
nodes.summary: N. Venkataramanayya was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader in Indian History at the University of Madras (attested 1957) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh.

nodes.label: M. Seshagiri Sastri
nodes.summary: M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1899), and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University (attested 1899).

nodes.label: Joseph Needham
nodes.summary: Joseph Needham worked in sinology and history/archaeology. Educated at Oundle School and the University of Cambridge (Gonville and Caius College), he served as a Cambridge reader (1933–1966), Fellow of Gonville and Caius (~1924–1995), and Director of the Needham Research Institute (~1987–1990).

nodes.label: Edgar Thurston
nodes.summary: Edgar Thurston studied at Eton College (~1869–1874) and King's College London (~1874–1877). Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1885–1908).

nodes.label: R. N. Gadre
nodes.summary: R. N. Gadre is an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Sir Parashurambhau College and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (both attested 1958).

nodes.label: Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia
nodes.summary: Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia (b. 1894) worked in Indology and religious studies. In 1947, he was attested as Professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as a Ph.D. teacher in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai.

nodes.label: Mahadev Govind Ranade
nodes.jawiki: マハーデーヴ・ゴーヴィンド・ラーナデー
nodes.description: Indian scholar, social reformer and author (1842-1901)
nodes.summary: Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842–1901) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and Government Law College, Mumbai, and founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885.

nodes.label: Anna Moreshwar Kunte
nodes.description: expert doctor, scholar of Dnyaneswari, he wrote a book on Ayurveda called 'Vagbhat'

nodes.label: Walpola Rahula
nodes.summary: Walpola Rahula (1907–1997) studied at Vidyalankara Pirivena, Calcutta, Ceylon, and Paris. Specializing in Buddhist studies and history, he served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964–1969) and professor at Northwestern University (1964).

nodes.label: Kim Plofker
nodes.summary: Kim Plofker (born 1964) works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD under David Pingree at Brown University in 1995. Her positions include posts at MIT (2000–2004) and Union College, where she became an associate professor in 2019.

nodes.label: Agathe Keller
nodes.summary: Agathe Keller is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She has held affiliations with REHSEIS (attested 2006), the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2017), and Paris Diderot University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Clemency Montelle
nodes.summary: Clemency Montelle is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar based at the University of Canterbury, where she held posts in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.

nodes.label: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma
nodes.description: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma, Dept. of Sanskrit, Aligarh Muslim U., Aligarh-202002
nodes.summary: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history scholar. He studied at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University, and earned a PhD at the University of Marburg, later serving as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1977 to 1997.

nodes.label: Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya
nodes.summary: Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was Director of the Mithila Institute (~1955–1961) and General Editor of the Mahabharata at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1961–1972), succeeding Shripad Krishna Belvalkar in 1961.

nodes.label: Michael Jansen
nodes.summary: Michael Jansen was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at RWTH Aachen University, Bonn, Rome, and Delhi. He served as architecture dean at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999), founding rector of GUtech (2007–2008), and president of the Research Centre Indian Ocean.

variants: German team making architectural studies at Mohenjo-daro

variants: Khams sprul bSod nams don grub

nodes.label: Narayan Hemandas Samtani
nodes.summary: Narayan Hemandas Samtani was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (circa 1961–1984).

nodes.label: Prahlad Pradhan
nodes.summary: Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies educated at Patna University and Visva-Bharati University. He held academic posts at Gangadhar Meher University, Utkal University, and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

nodes.label: Andrea Schlosser
nodes.summary: Andrea Schlosser is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned her master's and PhD at the Free University of Berlin. As of 2026, she is affiliated with the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Juliane Schober
nodes.summary: Juliane Schober works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University, attested in 1997 and 2007.

nodes.label: M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati
nodes.summary: M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati (born 1958) studied at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities. She held posts at Silpakorn, Tsukuba, the Asian Art Museum, Sonoma State, California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), Yale-NUS College (2016), and Nanyang Technological University (2022).

nodes.label: Christoph Emmrich
nodes.summary: Christoph Emmrich is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels in 2004, held a post there in 2001, and is attested as an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Natasha Heller
nodes.summary: Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After receiving her PhD from Harvard (2005), she held positions at UC Berkeley, UCLA as Assistant Professor, and the University of Virginia as faculty.

nodes.label: Justin McDaniel
nodes.summary: Justin McDaniel is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and held an endowed chair at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2026).

nodes.label: University of California, Riverside
variants: カリフォルニア大学リバーサイド校

nodes.label: Vesna Wallace
nodes.summary: Vesna Wallace is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair at the University of Oxford and posts at Berkeley and the University of California, Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: Charles Duroiselle
nodes.summary: Charles Duroiselle (1871–1951) was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a superintendent for the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940) and Burma Circle (ASI), and as a professor at the University of Rangoon (~1920).

nodes.label: J. Robert Oppenheimer
nodes.jawiki: ロバート・オッペンハイマー
nodes.summary: J. Robert Oppenheimer (1904–1967) studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, and studied under Arthur W. Ryder. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, the Manhattan Project, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

nodes.label: Roy W. Perrett
nodes.description: philosopher at the University of Melbourne
nodes.summary: Roy W. Perrett is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Canterbury (~1970–1975) and the University of Otago (~1978–1981). He held positions at Massey University (~1986–2005), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~2003–2005), and the University of Melbourne (~2005–2010).

nodes.id: I:Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
nodes.label: Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
variants: Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
The Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities

nodes.label: Tamara Cohen
nodes.summary: Tamara Cohen works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto by 2023 under supervisors Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder, having also studied under Joel Tatelman, Bryan Levman, Libbie Mills, and others.

nodes.label: Libbie Mills
nodes.summary: Libbie Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. She held an attested post teaching Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto in 2020.

nodes.label: George V. Bobrinskoy
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist George V. Bobrinskoy studied at the Lutheran Theological Seminary at Philadelphia and at Yale University under Franklin Edgerton. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as Sanskrit instructor, assistant professor, and linguistics department chair.

nodes.label: Narada Maha Thera
nodes.image: Portrait Of Most Venerable Narada Maha Thera (1898-1983).jpg
nodes.summary: Narada Maha Thera was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo. He served as Superior at Vajirarama, Colombo, from around 1962 to 1983.

nodes.label: Masamichi Ichigo
nodes.summary: Masamichi Ichigo (b. 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Susumu Yamaguchi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Gadjin Nagao, later holding posts at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.

nodes.label: Susumu Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Susumu Yamaguchi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University, Paris, and Kyoto, under Lévi, Sasaki, Teramoto, and de La Vallée Poussin. He served as professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

nodes.label: Rosina Pastore
nodes.summary: Rosina Pastore works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne, supervised by Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere while serving as an assistant, and later became an affiliated researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: James Mallinson
nodes.image: James Mallinson at Khalili Lecture Theatre SOAS.jpg
nodes.summary: James Mallinson (born 1970) is an Indologist educated at Eton, SOAS, and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS and Oxford, becoming Boden Professor of Sanskrit and Director of Graduate Studies at Wolfson College in 2023.

nodes.label: University of Erlangen-Nuremberg
variants: International Research Consortium of "Fate, Freedom, and Prognostication in East Asia and Europe"
Internationalen Kolleg für Geisteswissenschaftliche Forschung der Universität Erlangen

nodes.label: Mabel Haynes Bode
nodes.summary: Mabel Haynes Bode (1864–1922) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at the University of Bern and studied widely across Europe before lecturing on Pali at University College London and SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Vijaya Indra Suri
nodes.summary: Vijaya Indra Suri was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who succeeded Vijaya Dharma Suri (attested 1933) and founded the Prakrit Text Society.

nodes.label: Cynthia Talbot
nodes.summary: Cynthia Talbot (born 1952) studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1981–1988). A specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology, she joined the University of Texas at Austin around 1995, where she is now Professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Constantin Régamey
nodes.summary: Constantin Régamey (1907–1982) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. Educated at Warsaw and Paris, he lectured at Warsaw (1936) before serving as professor of Slavic and Oriental languages and cultures at the University of Lausanne (1949–1957).

nodes.label: Paul Groner
nodes.summary: Paul Groner specialized in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a PhD from Yale University and studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa (1971–1974), later serving as professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2026).

nodes.label: Stanley Weinstein
variants: スタンリー・ワインスタイン
nodes.jawiki: スタンリー・ワインスタイン
nodes.summary: Stanley Weinstein specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kodo Sawaki and Gyokusen Hosaka, the University of Tokyo, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at Komazawa, SOAS, London, and Yale.

nodes.label: Hari Damodar Velankar
nodes.summary: Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944–1948) and Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).

nodes.label: A. S. Gadre
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, A. S. Gadre served as Director of Archaeology for the Archaeology Department of Baroda State, attested in 1944.

nodes.label: Hubert Durt
nodes.summary: Hubert Durt was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Étienne Lamotte (~1961–1970). He was a professor at EFEO (~1970–2001) and ICPBS (~2001–2011), and directed the Hobogirin Institute (~1981).

nodes.label: Józef Maria Bocheński
nodes.summary: Józef Maria Bocheński was a philosopher who studied at Jagiellonian University, the University of Fribourg, and the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas. He held posts at the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas (~1934–1940) and Fribourg (~1945–1972).

nodes.label: Emmanuel Levinas
nodes.jawiki: エマニュエル・レヴィナス
nodes.summary: Emmanuel Levinas (1906–1995) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Strasbourg and Freiburg, the latter under Martin Heidegger. He held academic posts at the University of Poitiers (~1961–1967), Fribourg, and the University of Paris (~1973–1979).

nodes.label: Surendranath Majumdar Sastri
nodes.summary: Surendranath Majumdar Sastri was an Indology and history scholar who studied under traditional teacher Hara Prasad Sastri and served as a Reader at Patna University (attested 1924).

nodes.label: Hara Prasad Sastri
nodes.summary: Hara Prasad Sastri was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Principal at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and Joint Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).

nodes.label: Guy G. Stroumsa
nodes.summary: Guy G. Stroumsa works in religious studies. After studying at Paris, Hebrew University, EPHE, and Harvard (PhD 1978), he held various posts at Hebrew University (1978–2009) and served as Emeritus Professor of the Study of Abrahamic Religions at Oxford (2009–2013).

nodes.label: Yohei Kawajiri
nodes.summary: Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. Kawajiri held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013 and 2022) and the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Bill M. Mak
nodes.summary: Bill M. Mak held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2017) and the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

nodes.label: Kenneth G. Zysk
nodes.summary: Kenneth G. Zysk is an indologist and historian/archaeologist. He earned an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. at Australian National University. He held posts at Eastern Michigan University, UC Los Angeles, Wisconsin-Madison, Toronto, and the University of Copenhagen.

nodes.label: Su Bai
nodes.summary: Su Bai worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He completed graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under scholars including Rong Geng and Yongtong Tang, and later served as a professor there from 1948 to 2004.

nodes.label: Men-Tsee-Khang
variants: Tibetan Institute of Medicine and Astrology

nodes.label: B. Alan Wallace
nodes.description: American author, translator, teacher, researcher, interpreter, and Buddhist practitioner
nodes.summary: B. Alan Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst, Stanford (under Carl Bielefeldt), and Tibetan monastic institutions, later teaching at Institut des Hautes Études Tibétaines, Rabten Choeling, and UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: Victoria and Albert Museum
variants: ヴィクトリア&アルバート博物館

nodes.label: Gisela Freund
nodes.summary: Prehistorian Gisela Freund studied at the philosophy faculty of the German University of Prague (~1939–1944). She later served as Head of the Department of Prehistory at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1969–1987).

nodes.label: Stanley Wolpert
nodes.summary: Stanley Wolpert was an indology and history scholar. He studied at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, becoming an associate professor in 1963 and department chair in 1967.

nodes.label: Roderick M. Chisholm
nodes.summary: Philosopher Roderick M. Chisholm studied at Brown University (1934–1938) and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1938–1942). He taught at the Barnes Foundation (~1946) and Brown (~1947–1986), also serving as president of the Metaphysical Society of America in 1973.

nodes.label: Philip L. Quinn
nodes.summary: Philip L. Quinn worked in philosophy and religious studies, earning degrees from Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (~1970–1985), became the John A. O'Brien Professor of Philosophy at Notre Dame in 1985, and presided over the APA (1994–1995).

nodes.label: Ernest Sosa
nodes.summary: Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He was a professor at Brown University from 1964 and Board of Governors Professor of Philosophy at Rutgers University (1998–2006).

nodes.label: Suryanarayana Shukla
nodes.summary: Suryanarayana Shukla was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at Rajgopal Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya under Nandakishore Pandey, Ramanujacharya, and Shridatta Pandey.

nodes.label: Yutaka Ochihara
nodes.summary: Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991), an Indologist and linguist, studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania, training under Louis Renou and W. Norman Brown. He held posts at Kyoto University (1957; 1972–1986) and Collège de France (1985).

nodes.label: Xianda
nodes.summary: Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong by 2016, with doctoral supervision under K. L. Dhammajoti in 1995.

nodes.label: K. L. Dhammajoti
nodes.summary: K. L. Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA from the University of Kelaniya under Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. He held positions at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and served as a committee chairman at Hong Kong University.

nodes.label: Clare Hall, University of Cambridge
variants: Clare Hall the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Adrián Muñoz
nodes.summary: Adrián Muñoz works in Indology and religious studies. His career includes appointments as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (attested 2011) and as lecturer of South Asian Religions at El Colegio de México (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Klaus Karttunen
nodes.description: Finnish ethnologist, indologist and university teacher
nodes.summary: Klaus Karttunen is an Indology, linguistics, and history scholar who studied at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. He held research and docent positions at the Academy of Finland and the University of Helsinki.

nodes.label: Gergely Hidas
nodes.summary: Gergely Hidas works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Csaba Töttössy, and Ferenc Ruzsa, later holding posts at Eötvös Loránd University and the British Museum.

nodes.label: Virendra Nath Misra
nodes.summary: Virendra Nath Misra was an archaeology and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953–1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961), later serving as Director of the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1981–2000).

nodes.label: Rosalind Lefeber
nodes.summary: Rosalind Lefeber is an Indologist who completed her doctoral dissertation at the University of Toronto under supervisors Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith, and also studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She later held a post at Toronto (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Barbara Stoler Miller
nodes.summary: Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist who studied at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Stella Kramrisch, and Royal W. Weiler. She taught at Barnard College and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Barnard College
variants: バーナード・カレッジ

nodes.label: Joanna Jurewicz
nodes.summary: Joanna Jurewicz is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. She has held posts as professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2006 and 2026).

nodes.label: Sue Hamilton
nodes.summary: Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and Richard Gombrich, and held a post at King's College London (attested 2001–2003).

nodes.label: Whitney Cox
nodes.summary: Indologist and religious studies scholar Whitney Cox studied at the University of Virginia and University of Chicago, working under Sheldon Pollock and others. Cox held posts at SOAS (~2007–2013) and became a professor at the University of Chicago (~2013).

nodes.label: Washington and Lee University
variants: Department of Religion at Washington and Lee University

nodes.label: Ethan Kroll
nodes.summary: Ethan Kroll worked in Indology and other fields. He held posts attested in 2012 at Baker McKenzie and as an editorial board member for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies.

nodes.label: Victor Henry
nodes.summary: Victor Henry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Douai, the University of Lille, and École Centrale de Lille, before being appointed professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris in 1888.

nodes.label: Kyoko Fujii
nodes.summary: After studying at the University of Tokyo, Buddhist and Indology scholar Kyoko Fujii held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1998–2007) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2007–2019), later directing the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2020–2026).

nodes.label: Mizuho Okita
nodes.summary: Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Tokai University, under Katsuhiko Kamimura, and earned her doctorate under Atsuhiko Yoshida at Gakushuin University, later lecturing at Meisei University (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Atsuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: Atsuhiko Yoshida (b. 1934), a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology, studied at Seikei and Tokyo Universities, Strasbourg, and under Georges Dumézil at the CNRS (~1960–1967). He later served as professor at Seikei (1970) and Gakushuin (2006).

nodes.label: Kazuo Matsumura
nodes.summary: Kazuo Matsumura (born 1953) works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976) and held positions at Tenri University (~1986–1997) and Wako University (~2004–2019).

nodes.label: Wako University
variants: 和光大学人文学部芸術学科

nodes.label: Przemysław Szczurek
nodes.summary: Przemysław Szczurek is an Indologist who held posts at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań and at the University of Breslau, where he served as Professor of Indology (~2004).

nodes.label: Prods Oktor Skjærvø
nodes.summary: Prods Oktor Skjærvø is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Oslo, the Sorbonne, and Mainz, he held professorships at the University of Mainz (1980–1985) and Harvard University (~1991–2015).

nodes.label: Émile Benveniste
variants: エミール・バンヴニスト
エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.jawiki: エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.summary: A scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Benveniste studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Sylvain Lévi. He held chairs at EPHE (1927–1969) and the Collège de France (1937–1969).

nodes.label: Marianne Yaldiz
nodes.summary: Marianne Yaldiz is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She served as Director at the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and Director at the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).

キングス・カレッジ・ロンドン

nodes.label: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, Schaeffer earned degrees from Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, Washington, and Harvard (PhD, 2000). He held faculty posts at the University of Alabama (2000–2004) and joined the University of Virginia in 2005.

nodes.label: Srikanth Kaul
nodes.summary: Srikanth Kaul was an Indology and history scholar. In 1967, he is attested as a professor at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir and as holding a post at Government Degree College, Sopore.

nodes.label: James Haughton Woods
nodes.summary: James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, Mukunda Shastri Adkar, and Charles Rockwell Lanman, later serving as a professor at Harvard University from ~1903 to 1934.

nodes.label: Yinke Chen
nodes.summary: Yinke Chen was a sinologist, historian, and linguist who studied at institutions including Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard. He held major posts at Tsinghua University, Peking University, Academia Sinica, and Sun Yat-sen University.

nodes.label: Elizabeth A. Cecil
nodes.summary: Elizabeth A. Cecil is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald and has held posts at Leiden University and Florida State University (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Dániel Balogh
nodes.summary: Dániel Balogh works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He has been affiliated with the British Museum (attested 2021) and served as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Metropolitan Museum of Art
variants: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
Department of Asian Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art

nodes.label: Richard Payne
nodes.summary: Richard Payne works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held positions at the University of Chicago (attested 2021) and Numata Center.

nodes.label: Rijksmuseum
variants: Museum of Asiatic Art in Amsterdam

nodes.label: Vincent Tournier
nodes.summary: Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seishi Karashima and Cristina Scherrer-Schaub, earning his PhD from the EPHE (2012). His posts include the EFEO (attested 2021) and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen der Universität Berlin
Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen in Berlin
Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen at the University of Berlin

nodes.label: Qian Lin
nodes.summary: Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington, where she earned her PhD under Collett Cox and Richard G. Salomon. She held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2026).

nodes.label: R. Sathyanarayana
nodes.summary: R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) was a scholar of Indology who completed a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

nodes.label: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and served as a Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Nobuchiyo Kotani
nodes.summary: Nobuchiyo Kotani (1944–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, Hajime Sakurabe, and Ichijo Ogawa, later serving as professor at Otani University (~1987–2014).

nodes.label: Otani University Junior College
variants: 大谷大学短期大学部仏教学科

nodes.label: Kazuo Hyodo
nodes.summary: Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, later serving as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1983–2014).

nodes.label: Taku Fukuda
nodes.summary: Taku Fukuda (born 1963) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He has held positions at Doho University, Nagoya University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Yamagiwa
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Yamagiwa (1952–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a lecturing post at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and a professorship at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Enga Teramoto
nodes.summary: Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He held teaching posts as a lecturer at Kyoto University (~1908–1923) and professor at Otani University from 1915.

nodes.label: Yoshihiro Matsunami
nodes.summary: Yoshihiro Matsunami is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a professorship at Taisho University (attested 1991–1999) and served as its president in 2001.

nodes.label: Kumataro Kawada
nodes.summary: Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Tokyo Imperial University, he taught at Japan Women's University, Tokyo University of Literature and Science, the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and became professor emeritus at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Radhika Herzberger
nodes.summary: Radhika Herzberger (b. 1938) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (~1976–1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal and served as Director of Rishi Valley School (~1980–2012).

nodes.label: Alexander Studholme
nodes.summary: Alexander Studholme is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin.

nodes.label: Sibnath Sarma
nodes.summary: Sibnath Sarma is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held a post at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir and served as Professor in the Department of Philosophy at Gauhati University (attested 1999-2012).

nodes.label: Raffaele Catà
nodes.summary: Raffaele Catà works in philosophy and Indology. He completed his laurea at the University of Bologna (2011–2012) under the supervision of Manlio Iofrida and Saverio Marchignoli.

nodes.label: Manlio Iofrida
nodes.summary: Manlio Iofrida is a philosopher who studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore (~1970–1975). He held academic posts at the University of Pisa (~1979–1987) and the University of Bologna (~1988).

nodes.label: Ruriko Sakuma
nodes.summary: Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University. She has held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Madhusudan Gupta
nodes.summary: Madhusudan Gupta (1800–1856) worked in Indology and medicine. He studied at Sanskrit College and the Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, later teaching Ayurveda at Sanskrit College (~1830–1835) and holding a post at Medical College and Hospital (~1835–1856).

nodes.label: Pramod P. Joglekar
nodes.summary: Pramod P. Joglekar is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served on the Regulating Council of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and is attested in 2026 as Professor of Bioarchaeology at Deccan College.

nodes.label: Shilpa Sumant
nodes.summary: Working in indology, Shilpa Sumant was an Editor and Member of the Regulating Council at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and a member at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kripa Shankar Shukla
nodes.summary: Kripa Shankar Shukla (1918–2007) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He held an academic post at the University of Lucknow until 1959 and was attested there again in 1976.

nodes.label: Sukhlal Sanghvi
nodes.description: Jain Scholar and Philosopher from India
nodes.summary: Sukhlal Sanghvi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Shri Yashovijaya Jain Sanskrit Pathshala and under Balakrishna Mishra. He held posts at Gujarat Vidyapith (1922) and was Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University (1934–1944).

nodes.label: Embar Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indology scholar who served as editor for the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1926) and pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, holding later posts at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal, and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Vadodara.

nodes.label: Claude Jacques
nodes.summary: Claude Jacques specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying under George Cœdès (~1955–1969). He served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient and taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1997).

nodes.label: Georg Buddruss
nodes.summary: Buddruss worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1950-1954), studied at the University of Tübingen, and served as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1963-1995).

nodes.label: Hanns-Peter Schmidt
nodes.summary: Hanns-Peter Schmidt (1930–2017) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and served as professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from 1965 to 2000.

Marco Ferrante
nodes.summary: Marco Ferrante is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who held posts at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2014) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Leo M. Pruden
nodes.summary: Leo M. Pruden (1937–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Taitetsu Unno and at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa, and taught at Brown University, the Nyingma Institute, and the University of Oriental Studies.

nodes.label: Kyokuga Saeki
nodes.summary: Kyokuga Saeki (1828–1891) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Reiga and Gen'yū. He served as the 143rd elder of Sennyu-ji and taught students including Shundo Sugihara.

nodes.label: Ryotai Shibuya
nodes.summary: Ryotai Shibuya was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.

nodes.label: Kojun Fukui
nodes.summary: Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Waseda University under Sokichi Tsuda (~1921–1924, PhD 1949). He served as professor at Waseda (1941–1969) and as president of Taisho University (1972–1975).

nodes.label: Ryojun Okubo
nodes.summary: Ryojun Okubo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Morito Ninomiya and held a post at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Gyoei Fukuda
nodes.summary: Gyoei Fukuda was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1928), Toyo University, and served as president of Taisho University (~1940–1943).

nodes.label: Julius Lipner
nodes.summary: Julius Lipner is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Jadavpur, Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis. He taught at the University of Birmingham before serving as Professor of Hinduism at the University of Cambridge (1975–2013).

nodes.label: Harold G. Coward
nodes.summary: Harold G. Coward is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from McMaster University. He served as a professor at the University of Calgary (ca. 1973–1992) and as director at the University of Victoria (ca. 1992–2004).

nodes.label: Per Kjeld Sørensen
nodes.summary: Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Copenhagen under Erik Haarh. He was a lecturer at Copenhagen (1982–1989) and professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).

nodes.label: Erik Haarh
nodes.summary: Erik Haarh was a Tibetologist and linguist who completed a doctorate at the University of Copenhagen. He worked as a librarian and department head at the Royal Danish Library (1956, 1962) before serving as a department head and professor at Aarhus University (1969, 1983).

nodes.label: Alex McKay
nodes.summary: Alex McKay is a historian and Tibetologist who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1995. He has held research fellowships at SOAS, University College London, and the International Institute for Asian Studies.
