nodes.label: Ferenc Ruzsa
nodes.summary: Ferenc Ruzsa works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (~1971–1975) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982), where he took up a post in ~1989.

nodes.label: Toshio Sako
nodes.summary: Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Columbia University. His teachers included Alex Wayman, Yasunori Ejima, and Jikido Takasaki.

nodes.label: Yonten Gyatso
nodes.summary: Yonten Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, completed a diplôme at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and served there as a research advisor in Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Hisataka Ishida
nodes.summary: Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser, later serving as a full-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Tsuruji Sahoda
nodes.summary: Tsuruji Sahoda was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1922–1925) and held positions at Ritsumeikan University (~1928–1949) and Osaka University (~1949–1963).

nodes.label: Hiroo Kashiwagi
nodes.summary: Hiroo Kashiwagi, born in 1933, completed his doctoral course at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963) in Buddhist studies. He taught Waso Harada, was president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College, and held posts at Mie Chukyo and Koyasan universities.

nodes.label: Makio Takemura
nodes.summary: Makio Takemura is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned master's and doctoral degrees at the University of Tokyo and studied under Ryōmin Akizuki. He served as professor at the University of Tsukuba and president of Toyo University (2009–2020).

nodes.label: Kakushō Ujiie
nodes.summary: Kakushō Ujiie (d. 1985) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Tribhuvan University. He held a professorship at Koyasan University (attested 1970 and 1984–1985).

nodes.label: Esho Mikogami
nodes.summary: Esho Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1973 to 2003 and was president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

nodes.label: Alexandra van der Geer
nodes.summary: Alexandra van der Geer specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, Fabio Martini, John de Vos, and Paul Y. Sondaar, and held a visiting post at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

nodes.label: Kalidas Nag
nodes.summary: Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Scottish Church College (~1914–1919), Calcutta University (~1923–1955), and was General Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1942–1946).

nodes.label: Ole Holten Pind
nodes.summary: Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2004–2009) under Ernst Steinkellner and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Kiyoshi Kato
nodes.summary: Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at Otani University, where he studied under Enga Teramoto, and later worked at Higashi Honganji in 1935 and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School in 1938.

nodes.label: Fumi Yao
nodes.summary: Fumi Yao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Tokyo in 2011 and holds posts at the University of Tokyo and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal
nodes.summary: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Allahabad and the University of Oxford. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta in 1917 and as president of the Numismatic Society of India.

nodes.label: Daw Ohn
nodes.summary: Daw Ohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics. She studied at the University of Rangoon and served there as a Tutor in Pali, attested in 1977.

nodes.label: Susumu Kajiura
nodes.summary: Susumu Kajiura is a specialist in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post as an assistant at Kyoto University in 1999 and was head of humanities research at the Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Arinde L. Jonker
nodes.summary: Arinde L. Jonker specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), studying under Peter C. Bisschop, Daniele Cuneo, and Jonathan A. Silk.

nodes.label: Richard Jay Kohn
nodes.summary: Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (by 1988), studying under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa and traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Dor Bahadur Bista
nodes.summary: Dor Bahadur Bista is a Tibetology scholar who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He was a professor at Tribhuvan University from approximately 1975 to 1993 and served on the board of governors of ICIMOD.

nodes.label: David Gellner
nodes.summary: David Gellner is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held positions at the University of Oxford, including Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology at Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Bruce McCoy Owens
nodes.summary: Bruce McCoy Owens specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held appointments at Columbia University (attested 1988) and as an associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf
nodes.summary: Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf was an anthropologist, Indologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Vienna under Leo Frobenius and Robert von Heine-Geldern, and at the LSE. He was a professor at Osmania University and Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London.

nodes.label: David Llewellyn Snellgrove
nodes.summary: David Llewellyn Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Southampton and Cambridge. He was a professor at SOAS, University of London from 1950 to 1982 and founded the Institute of Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Michael Oppitz
nodes.summary: Michael Oppitz is a scholar of Tibetology and related fields. He held an appointment at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1987–1988) and served as a director (Leiter) at the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).

nodes.label: Mark Tatz
nodes.summary: Mark Tatz specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, completing a PhD at the University of British Columbia (1978) under Leon Hurvitz while also studying under traditional teachers. He later served as Professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Shudo Ishii
nodes.summary: Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University, progressing from assistant in 1971 to professor in 1984, and served as acting head of Matsugaoka Bunko.

nodes.label: Kotatsu Fujita
nodes.summary: Kotatsu Fujita (1928–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, he studied under Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served at Hokkaido University (~1968–1991) and Sapporo Otani Junior College (1992).

nodes.label: Yoshihiko Nasu
nodes.summary: Yoshihiko Nasu works in Buddhist studies. Nasu served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and held leadership roles at Kongojushinkai and Kongozyu (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Bradford Lyman Phillips
nodes.summary: Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned degrees from the University of Virginia (B.A. 1989, PhD 2004) and Harvard University (M.T.S. 1993), studying under David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, Jeffrey Hopkins, and others.

nodes.label: David Germano
nodes.summary: David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. He has served as a faculty member and Associate Professor at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Cecil Y. Lang
nodes.summary: Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at Yale University (~1949–1959), the University of Chicago (~1967–1970), and served as Professor of English at the University of Virginia (~1970–1991).

nodes.label: Michael Aris
nodes.summary: Michael Aris (1946–1999) was a scholar in Tibetology and history. He studied at Durham University and the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove, later holding positions at Oxford and Harvard, and founding the International Association for Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Diana L. Eck
nodes.summary: Diana L. Eck is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD 1976 under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), she served as a professor of comparative religion and Indian studies at Harvard from ~1976 to 2024.

nodes.label: Benjamin C. Ray
nodes.summary: Benjamin C. Ray (born 1940) is a religious studies scholar. He held a long career at the University of Virginia, including an appointment as Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in Religious Studies (attested 2000 and 2026).

nodes.label: David Gordon White
nodes.summary: David Gordon White is an Indologist and historian of religion who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago (~1979–1988). He taught at the University of Virginia before serving as professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara from 1996.

nodes.label: Taiken Kimura
nodes.summary: Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue, later becoming a professor of Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1912.

nodes.label: Ryugen Tanemura
nodes.summary: Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held teaching posts at Nishogakusha University and Taisho University, as well as a research position at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.

nodes.label: Kenichi Kuranishi
nodes.summary: Kenichi Kuranishi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as an associate professor at Taisho University and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Kazutoshi Soma
nodes.summary: Kazutoshi Soma works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Meiji Yamada and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Kenryu Tsukinowa
nodes.summary: Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and tibetology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He served as professor at Koyasan University (1926), Seizan College, and Shuchiin University (1955), and became Professor Emeritus at Ryukoku University in 1956.

nodes.label: Zuiei Ito
nodes.summary: Zuiei Ito (1942–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning doctorates from the University of Tokyo and Waseda University. He was a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1980 to 2013.

Yutaka Yuda
nodes.summary: Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1969) and earned a doctorate at Rissho University (-1990). He held posts at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

nodes.label: Zuiryu Nakamura
nodes.summary: Zuiryu Nakamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Susumu Yamaguchi and Kenryu Tsukinowa. He served as professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1945 and was former director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

nodes.label: Yasuaki Nara
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Nara studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at Calcutta. He served at Komazawa University from 1960 and later directed the Soto Zen Research Center (2000).

nodes.label: Zesho Machida
nodes.summary: Zesho Machida is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as betto at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku (attested 1990) and was professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).

nodes.label: Masao Shizutani
nodes.summary: Masao Shizutani was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He held posts as assistant professor (助教授) at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

nodes.label: Josho Nozawa
nodes.summary: Josho Nozawa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1950).

nodes.label: George Chemparathy
nodes.summary: An Indologist and philosopher, George Chemparathy studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1962–1968) and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as professor at Utrecht University (~1974–1993).

nodes.label: Tetsuro Watsuji
nodes.summary: Tetsuro Watsuji was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and held professorial chairs in ethics at Kyoto University (1925–1949) and the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).

nodes.label: Nichidatsu Fujii
nodes.summary: Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who founded Nipponzan-Myohoji. He studied at Rissho University, Taisho University, Koyasan University, Horyuji Kangakuin, and Kennin-ji, and taught Gyoryo Maruyama.

nodes.label: Tomoyuki Uno
nodes.summary: Tomoyuki Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

nodes.label: Kyo Kano
nodes.summary: Kyo Kano studied Indology and philosophy at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. Kano served as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and as an associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Leslie S. Kawamura
nodes.summary: Leslie S. Kawamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther and served as a professor, later Professor of Buddhist Studies, at the University of Calgary from circa 1976 to 2011.

nodes.label: Kosei Ishii
nodes.summary: Kosei Ishii (1950–) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at Waseda University, completing a doctorate under Akira Hirakawa. He was an assistant professor at Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006) and a professor of Buddhism at Komazawa University (2006–2021).

nodes.label: Takeshi Hasegawa
nodes.summary: Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1998), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ekkyo Uno
nodes.summary: Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Shinichi Tsuda
nodes.summary: Shinichi Tsuda works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned a PhD at the Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, later holding posts at Toyo Bunko, Eastern Institute, and ICPBS.

nodes.label: Kosei Tada
nodes.summary: Kosei Tada (1938–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served at Taisho University (~1970–2009) and as board chairman of the Society for Buddhist Cultural Studies (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Ryota Nakamura
nodes.summary: Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and served as a graduate researcher at Toyo University in 2015. In the same year, he held a research post at the Shinran Buddhist Center.

nodes.label: Amy Sims Miller
nodes.summary: Amy Sims Miller specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA at Wesleyan University and an MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, alongside studies with various traditional and academic teachers.

nodes.label: Janice Dean Willis
nodes.summary: Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her BA and MA at Cornell and a PhD at Columbia under Alex Wayman. She held faculty appointments at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).

nodes.label: Yiu Wing Chan
nodes.summary: Yiu Wing Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong in 2013 under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Eric M. Greene
nodes.summary: Eric M. Greene is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf. He served as assistant professor and associate professor of religious studies at Yale University.

nodes.label: Tensei Kitabatake
nodes.summary: Tensei Kitabatake was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (-1955). He spent decades at Ryukoku University, ultimately serving as president (1995–1999), and later served as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).

nodes.label: Robert F. Rhodes
nodes.summary: Robert F. Rhodes works in Buddhist studies and Japanology and was a PhD candidate at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University, attested during 1993–2000 and 2012–2014.

nodes.label: Fumio Ouchi
nodes.summary: Fumio Ouchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He completed a doctorate at Otani University, where he served as associate professor (~1988–1999) and professor (~1999–2013).

nodes.label: Kei Okusa
nodes.summary: Kei Okusa is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in literature from Otani University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2026.

nodes.label: Atsuyoshi Keika
nodes.summary: Atsuyoshi Keika (b. 1944) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who served at Otani University as a lecturer (attested 1990) and professor (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Kenryu Nishio
nodes.summary: Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University and served as Professor Emeritus at Hanazono University (attested 2014, 2026).

nodes.label: Taikyo Tanigawa
nodes.summary: Taikyo Tanigawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Koyasan University and completed a Ph.D. at Toyo University in 1994. He has held positions as associate professor and professor at Koyasan University, attested from 1980 through 2026.

nodes.label: Guohui Shi
nodes.description: Buddhist abbot of Dharma Drum Mountain
nodes.summary: Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyu Mitomo and studied under Sheng Yen, Hoyo Watanabe, and other teachers.

nodes.label: Mary Anne Cartelli
nodes.summary: Mary Anne Cartelli specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Philip Boas Yampolsky.

nodes.label: Huawen Bai
nodes.summary: Huawen Bai worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1951–1955) and subsequently served there as a professor (~1955–2000).

nodes.label: Keikyo Nakamikado
nodes.summary: Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a research collaborator at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shuji Takayama
nodes.summary: Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies researcher who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and researcher at Bukkyo University (attested 2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2006), and Musashino University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Koshin Suzuki
nodes.summary: Koshin Suzuki (1959–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He served there as a researcher (attested 1995–1998).

nodes.label: Midori Nishino
nodes.summary: Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006). She subsequently served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2010–2015).

nodes.label: Takako Abe
nodes.summary: Takako Abe is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026) at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Sungdoo Ahn
nodes.summary: Sungdoo Ahn is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. Ahn served as Director at Geumgang University and as a professor at Seoul National University.

nodes.label: Changhwan Park
nodes.summary: Changhwan Park works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, under Noritoshi Aramaki and Shoryu Katsura, and completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He was a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

nodes.label: Eunyoung Choe
nodes.summary: Eunyoung Choe (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Korea University. Choe served as an HK Professor at Geumgang University, attested between 2013 and 2015.

nodes.label: Sungtaek Cho
nodes.summary: Sungtaek Cho is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Cho held posts at Stony Brook University and Korea University, serving as Director (2003) and Professor (attested 2017) at the latter.

nodes.label: Ulrich Timme Kragh
nodes.summary: Ulrich Timme Kragh (born 1969) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and held posts at Copenhagen, Geumgang University, IIAS, and the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: Justin Ritzinger
nodes.summary: Justin Ritzinger specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, later holding posts at Oberlin College, Dharma Drum Mountain, Dharma Drum Institute, and Academia Sinica.

nodes.label: Ching Keng
nodes.summary: Ching Keng is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (~2003–2009) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, also studying at UT Austin. Around 2011, he became an associate professor at National Chengchi University.

nodes.label: Jörg Plassen
nodes.summary: Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held professorships at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Enichi Ocho
nodes.summary: Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He worked as a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture (1931) and became an honorary professor at Otani University (1949–1976).

nodes.label: Yukihiro Okada
nodes.summary: Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Okada studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn. Career posts include positions at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College and adviser at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Chijun Hamada
nodes.summary: Chijun Hamada was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1978, he held posts as an assistant at Taisho University and as a researcher at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

nodes.label: Ryusho Hikata
nodes.summary: Ryusho Hikata (1892–1991), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor and dean at Kyushu University and president of Fukuoka Women's University.

nodes.label: Shozen Kumoi
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Kumoi studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. He taught at Otani University (1948–1981, later emeritus) and Bukkyo University (1982).

nodes.label: Warren Crawford Cowgill
nodes.summary: Warren Crawford Cowgill was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Stanford University and Yale University, where he completed his PhD in circa 1957 and served as professor of linguistics starting in 1956.

nodes.label: George Eugene Dunkel
nodes.summary: A linguist and indologist, Dunkel completed his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1975–1978) and Princeton University (1978–1986) before taking the chair of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Zurich in 1986.

nodes.label: H. Craig Melchert
nodes.summary: H. Craig Melchert is a linguist who studied at Michigan State University, the Defense Language Institute, the National Cryptologic School, and Harvard University. He held posts at UNC Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and UCLA (2007–2015).

nodes.summary: Alan Nussbaum is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University from approximately 1969 to 1976 and served as a faculty member at Cornell University from around 1985 to 2021.

nodes.label: Donald A. Ringe
nodes.summary: Donald A. Ringe is a linguist who earned his PhD at Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill. He taught classics at Bard College (1983–1985) before joining the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

nodes.label: Karen Katsumoto

nodes.label: Esho Sasaki
nodes.summary: Esho Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who served as an assistant professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Senmyo Naniwa
nodes.summary: Senmyo Naniwa earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University and studied under Genjun Sasaki, Mohan G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, and P. V. Bapat. In 2005, he was a researcher at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and professor at Bukkyo University.

nodes.label: Martin Seeger
nodes.summary: Martin Seeger works in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2004 under Barend Jan Terwiel, held a post there as of 2004, and served on the Pali Text Society Council as of 2026.

nodes.label: Barend Jan Terwiel
nodes.summary: Barend Jan Terwiel works in history, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University, holding posts at ANU, the University of Munich, the University of Hamburg, and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi
variants: M. マイトリムルティ
nodes.summary: Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, and held posts at the University of Leipzig, Heidelberg University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Yoshito S. Hakeda
nodes.summary: Yoshito S. Hakeda (1924–1983) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he was a professor and an associate professor in East Asian Languages and Cultures and Religion.

nodes.label: Satkari Mukhopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, with posts attested in 1999 and 2026.

nodes.label: Genjun Sasaki
nodes.summary: Genjun Sasaki (1915–1999) studied at Kyoto University. Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Hamburg (1956), Otani University (attested 1974–1976 and 1987–1995), Harvard University, and Osaka University (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Clark Ruff
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Clark Ruff is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Missouri State University and UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, was a director at the University of California, and joined Marshall University in 2002.

nodes.label: Barbara A. Holdrege
nodes.summary: Barbara A. Holdrege specializes in religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, including Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: William F. Powell
nodes.summary: William F. Powell is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. His career includes posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he was attested in 1986 and as Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies and Research Professor.

nodes.label: Shinjo Suguro
nodes.summary: Shinjo Suguro was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He was vice director at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (1980) and professor at Rissho University (~1970–1996).

nodes.label: Nobuhiko Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Nobuhiko Kobayashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University and under Yutaka Ochihara. He has held positions at the University of Toronto (attested 1969), Kyoto University (attested 1979), and Taisho University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: George Baumann

nodes.label: Lars Martin Fosse

nodes.summary: An indologist and linguist, Hart earned a PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard (~1964–1971). nodes.label: Craig Jamieson

nodes.label: Susanne Mrozik

nodes.label: Walter Slaje

nodes.label: John D. Smith
nodes.summary: John D. Smith is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (1975) before joining the University of Cambridge as University Lecturer (1984) and Professor (2001–2007).

nodes.label: Yukari Kimura
nodes.summary: Yukari Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Kimura completed doctoral studies under Kenyu Mitomo and is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Minori Nishimura
nodes.summary: Minori Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at Taisho University. He held positions at Taisho University, the Sanko Cultural Institute, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Shindai Sekiguchi
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shindai Sekiguchi studied at Taisho University (~1928–1934). He later held professorships at Taisho University (~1950–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1986).

nodes.label: Akira Suganuma
nodes.summary: Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1959–1962), where he served as assistant (~1962–1967) and associate professor (1991–1994), and taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1981).

nodes.label: Kyoshun Todo
nodes.summary: Kyoshun Todo was a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and later as a professor (attested 1988–1992).

nodes.label: Narimoto Tamayama
nodes.summary: Narimoto Tamayama was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1974 and 1988).

nodes.label: Kodo Nomura

nodes.label: Yusho Wakahara
nodes.summary: Yusho Wakahara works in Buddhist studies and Indology. nodes.label: Akifumi Naito

nodes.label: Zensho Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Zensho Kitagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served at Rissho University as a lecturer (attested 1976) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026), and has been affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Kaji
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Kaji (1936–) is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and Tohoku University. He held academic posts including professor at Osaka University (1984–1998) and specially invited professor at Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).

nodes.label: Kosho Mizutani

nodes.label: Akira Sadakata
nodes.summary: Akira Sadakata (b. 1936) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris (1963), later serving as associate professor and professor at Tokai University (~1969–2006).

nodes.label: Mayumi Nasu
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Mayumi Nasu has held posts at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) as a lecturer and at Koyasan University (attested 2026) as a specially appointed associate professor.

nodes.label: Sudan Shakya

nodes.label: Kangei Okamoto

nodes.label: Takamatsu Yoshie

nodes.label: Stephen Jenkins
nodes.summary: Stephen Jenkins specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. nodes.label: Seiji Kimura
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Seiji Kimura studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He subsequently held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).

nodes.summary: Swami Lakshman Joo worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Maheshwar Nath Razdan from 1926 to 1933. He later founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.

nodes.label: Bettina Bäumer
nodes.summary: Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who studied in Munich, Vienna, and other universities, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. She held posts at BHU, the Alice Boner Institute, the University of Vienna, and the Abhinavagupta Research Library.

nodes.label: Jaideva Singh
nodes.summary: Jaideva Singh worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Srikrishna Harihirlekar, Nankoo Bhaya Telang, and Swami Lakshman Joo. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chaired the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

nodes.label: Edward Winslow Bastian
nodes.summary: Edward Winslow Bastian is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied as a research scholar at Banaras Hindu University and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, supervised by Geshe Lhundup Sopa alongside traditional Tibetan teachers.

nodes.label: Norio Koyama
nodes.summary: Norio Koyama works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami, later serving as professor at Taisho University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: John E. Cort
nodes.summary: John E. Cort is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed degrees at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and Harvard University (~1979–1984), and he has served as a Professor at Denison University since ~1993.

nodes.label: Shubhachandra
nodes.summary: Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Karnatak University, attested in 2001, and in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore, attested in 2002.

nodes.label: Royce Wiles
nodes.summary: Royce Wiles is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post there.

nodes.label: Derek F. Maher
nodes.summary: Derek F. Maher is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has taught at Virginia, UNC Greensboro, and East Carolina University.

nodes.label: Jules Brooks Levinson

nodes.label: Richard B. Martin

nodes.summary: Daishun Ueyama (1934–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his academic career at Ryukoku University as an associate professor, professor, and university president.

nodes.label: Akira Fujieda

nodes.label: Paul B. Donnelly

nodes.label: Hokei Izumi

nodes.label: Hoyo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Hoyo Watanabe studied at Rissho University (~1952–1961), where he later taught Guohui Shi. In Buddhist studies, he served at Rissho University as professor (~1974–2004), faculty dean (attested 1984–1985), and special honorary professor (~2004–2021).

nodes.label: Koken Sasaki
nodes.summary: Koken Sasaki (1931–2008) studied at Rissho University (~1950–1960) in Buddhist studies and Sinology. His career at Rissho University included roles as assistant professor (~1967–1975), chair of Buddhist studies (~1975–2002), and professor emeritus (~2002–2008).

nodes.label: Senkyo Sakawa
nodes.summary: Senkyo Sakawa studied at Rissho University (completed ~1965) and worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He served at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra and as a professor at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Yakupitiyage Karunadasa
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, Karunadasa earned a BA from the University of Ceylon and a PhD from London under David Friedman. He directed the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and held visiting professorships at Hong Kong, SOAS, Calgary, and Toronto.

nodes.label: Yinshun
nodes.summary: Yinshun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and earned a doctorate from Taisho University. He taught at the Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association (1949–1952), and taught Cheng Yen.

nodes.label: Huifeng
nodes.summary: Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Daniel Veidlinger
nodes.summary: Daniel Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999), and held a post at California State University, Chico (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Hideo Mineshima
nodes.summary: Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Yamagata High School, Taisho University, and Waseda University. He was a lecturer, assistant professor, and professor at Waseda University (1968–1998), and later served at Bunkyo Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Zenno Ishigami
nodes.summary: Zenno Ishigami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Taisho University (~1949–1956). He held professorial posts at Taisho University (1963–2000), served at Dongguk University, and was president of Shukutoku University Junior College (2002–2014).

nodes.label: Susumu Otake
nodes.summary: Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2001) under Makio Takemura. He has held lecturer appointments at Kyoto University (attested 2008), Hanazono University (attested 2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (attested 2012–2013).

nodes.label: Dan Arnold
nodes.summary: Dan Arnold works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago and held faculty appointments at McGill University and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Theodore Riccardi Jr.
nodes.summary: Theodore Riccardi Jr. is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2014 and Professor Emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: Satoru Noriyama
nodes.summary: Satoru Noriyama studied Buddhist studies under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).

nodes.label: Silvio Vita
nodes.summary: Silvio Vita specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, studying at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University. He directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2001–2023) and was a professor at the University of Naples Federico II (~2000–2023).

nodes.label: Shoshin Ichishima
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Ichishima served as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and worked as a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

nodes.label: Ryushin Uryuzu
nodes.summary: Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1957) in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1975–2003).

nodes.label: Tarthang Tulku
nodes.summary: Tarthang Tulku is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Tarthang Monastery and under teachers including Tarthang Choktrul, holding posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and the Nyingma Institute as Head Lama (~1972).

variants: Yeshe De Buddhist Research and Translation Project

nodes.label: Yohei Furukawa
nodes.summary: Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Takatsugu Hayashi. He is attested as an associate professor at Soka University in 2026.

nodes.label: Takatsugu Hayashi
nodes.summary: Takatsugu Hayashi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi (Ph.D.). He held posts at Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, Hosen Gakuen College, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Takao Kagawa
nodes.summary: Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

nodes.label: Shoju Inaba
nodes.summary: Shoju Inaba was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1958 to 1981 and also worked as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Michitoshi Barada
nodes.summary: Michitoshi Barada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held appointments at Otani University (attested 1992), Eastern Institute (attested 2000), and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2000–2003, 2026).

nodes.label: V. Raghavan
nodes.summary: V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served on the faculty at the University of Madras and founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, serving as its secretary.

nodes.label: Shigeaki Watanabe
nodes.summary: Shigeaki Watanabe works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held posts at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990) and the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic positions at Hokkaido University (~1993–2004), Tohoku University (~2004–2019), and Toyo Bunko.

nodes.label: Atsushi Uno
nodes.summary: Atsushi Uno (b. 1922), an Indologist and philosopher, studied at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu Universities under T. R. V. Murti, Raghunath Giri, and others. He held professorships at Tokai (1971), Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai (~1986–1993).

nodes.label: Raghunath Giri
nodes.summary: Raghunath Giri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He served as a department head (科長) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

nodes.label: Endo Asai
nodes.summary: Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as a professor at Rissho University (1972) and later as president of Minobusan University (1998–2002).

nodes.label: Noriaki Inoue
nodes.summary: Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University until 1953, where he later served as professor (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Shuyu Sakurai
nodes.summary: Shuyu Sakurai (born 1916) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1940-1943) and served as an emeritus professor at Komazawa University (~1950-1994).

nodes.label: Takushu Sugimoto
variants: すぎもと・たくしゅう
nodes.summary: Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935) studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, Teruji Ishizu, and Ichiro Hori, completing a PhD under Birendra Prasad Sinha. He held professorships at Kanazawa University, Komazawa University, and Kinjo University.

nodes.label: Yutaka Takagi
nodes.summary: Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University from circa 1975 to 1999.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi
nodes.summary: Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a linguist and Tibetologist. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington under Christopher I. Beckwith and others, later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1997–2017).

nodes.label: Hisashi Sato
nodes.summary: Hisashi Sato, a scholar of Tibetology and history, studied at Kyoto University (c. 1933–1936). He was later a professor at Kyoto University (c. 1964–1977), Komazawa University, and Toyo University, and also held a post at Bukkyo University (c. 1977–1984).

nodes.label: Tatsuo Nishida
nodes.summary: Tatsuo Nishida was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology who completed his doctorate at Kyoto University. He served as professor and dean at Kyoto University, president of the Linguistic Society of Japan (1979–1981), and professor at NACSIS (1992–1994).

nodes.label: Helmut Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Freiburg, Humboldt University (Dr. phil. under Heinrich Lüders), and Marburg, he also studied under Giuseppe Tucci and others. His posts included the Prussian Academy, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University (1969–1980).

nodes.label: Hideyo Ogawa
nodes.summary: Hideyo Ogawa (b. 1954) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He served as an assistant professor (around 1990–1998) and professor (around 1998–2020; attested 2026) at Hiroshima University, where he taught Shindo Kusumoto.

nodes.label: Yoshihito Muroji
nodes.summary: Yoshihito Muroji is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. Muroji has held posts at Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Shiga University of Medical Science.

nodes.label: Hiromi Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies who taught Shindo Kusumoto and held posts at Ryukoku University, including as full-time lecturer attested in 1987 and attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Toshihiko Kimura
nodes.summary: Toshihiko Kimura specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University (~1959–1963), he taught there as a lecturer and held posts at Tokai Gakuin University (~1979–1989) and Shitennoji University (~2011).

nodes.label: Toshihide Unebe
nodes.summary: Toshihide Unebe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Issai Funahashi. He held a professorship at Doho University, attested in 1991.

nodes.label: Hideto Ono
nodes.summary: Hideto Ono (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Masaaki Nitta
nodes.summary: Masaaki Nitta (b. 1936) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1962–1968) and served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (~1975–1992) and Fukui Prefectural University.

nodes.summary: Taiken Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University. He served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Beatrix Pfleiderer
nodes.summary: Beatrix Pfleiderer was an Indologist who studied at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, Heidelberg University, the University of Hamburg, Viadrina, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

nodes.label: Tsultrim Kelsang
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Kelsang specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), with additional research affiliations at Ryukoku University and the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center in 2015.

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Kimura
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1983–2001) and served as president of Tsurumi Women's University (~2000–2012).

He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura, Yoshiro Tamura, and Kyosho Hayashima, later serving as professor there (1995–2009) and at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2009–2015).

nodes.label: Hajime Okayama
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist studies scholar and bhikku
nodes.summary: Hajime Okayama (1948–2022) focused on Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Peking University, and CASS under Xianlin Ji. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo from 1995 to 2012.

nodes.label: Koyu Tamura
nodes.summary: Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) specialized in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After earning his master's and doctoral degrees at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Nishogakusha University (1965) and Toyo University (assistant professor in 1972; professor emeritus 1977–2000).

nodes.label: Ryoshu Misaki
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Misaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from around 1947 to 1952. He spent his career there from around 1958 to 1992, becoming an emeritus professor.

nodes.label: Takao Maruyama
nodes.summary: Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University. He served as associate professor and professor at Rissho University (~1967–1986), professor at Mejiro University (~1986–2000), and professor at Shinshu University.

nodes.label: Ryuzan Nishimoto
nodes.summary: Ryuzan Nishimoto (1891–1974) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1916, he studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa.

nodes.label: Weizhong Huang
nodes.summary: Weizhong Huang is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. Huang was affiliated with the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and holds a professorship at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Noboru Ueda
nodes.summary: Noboru Ueda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shoko Watanabe
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology, Watanabe studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Ernst Leumann, and earned a degree from Toyo University. He held professorships at Taisho and Toyo Universities.

nodes.label: Xinchuan Huang
nodes.summary: Xinchuan Huang was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher who studied at Peking University (~1953–1958). He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from circa 1978 to 1998, with his affiliation attested through 2007.

nodes.label: Robert DeCaroli
nodes.summary: A specialist in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Robert DeCaroli earned his MA and PhD at UCLA under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper. He lectured at UCLA and Loyola Marymount before joining George Mason University around 2004.

nodes.label: Ravindra Singh Bisht
nodes.summary: Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Lucknow, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University. He served in the Haryana archaeology department and was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (c. 1983–2004).

nodes.label: Eishu Miyazaki
nodes.summary: Eishu Miyazaki was a specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Rissho University (~1933–1938) under Gyoo Kageyama, later holding posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (~1949–1984).

nodes.label: Gyoko Iotani
nodes.summary: Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1968–1978). He served at Rissho University as associate professor, professor, and emeritus professor (~1982–2017), and held a post at Minobusan University (~2017).

nodes.label: Taisei Iwata
nodes.summary: Taisei Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gen'ichi Yamazaki
nodes.summary: Gen'ichi Yamazaki (1935–2015) studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1955–1959, doctorate 1991). Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, he was a researcher at Toyo Bunko (circa 1966–1977) and professor at Kokugakuin University (2006).

nodes.label: Ippei Okamoto
nodes.summary: Ippei Okamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at Toyo University (attested 2014) and was attested in 2026 as a visiting researcher (客員所員) at Minobusan University.

nodes.label: Taido Kitamura
nodes.summary: Taido Kitamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and held a post at Shuchiin University (attested 1994–1999).

nodes.label: Koichi Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Koichi Yokoyama (1940–2023) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and under Gyōin Hashimoto. He served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University from circa 1974 to 2006.

nodes.label: Tetsujiro Inoue
nodes.summary: Tetsujiro Inoue was a philosophy and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as professor and dean at the University of Tokyo and as president of Daito Bunka University.

nodes.summary: Ryokei Kaginushi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters at Otani University.

nodes.label: Iwao Shima
nodes.summary: Iwao Shima (1950–2007) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya University from roughly 1969 to 1978 and later served on the faculty at Kanazawa University from circa 1989, becoming a professor in 1996.

nodes.label: Kokan Fujita
nodes.summary: Kokan Fujita (1944–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

nodes.label: Yujun Endo
nodes.summary: Yujun Endo (1939–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who taught Kokan Fujita and Ryuichi Abe. Endo held faculty positions at Taisho University (attested 1991, 2014) and served as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Hitoshi Inui
nodes.summary: Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He has served at Koyasan University as a lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and as a professor (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Ryugen Taga
nodes.summary: Ryugen Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He spent his career at Rissho University as a lecturer, associate professor, professor from around 1975 to 2002, and president from around 1992 to 1995.

nodes.label: Kiyoaki Okuda
nodes.summary: Kiyoaki Okuda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf around 1968–1973. He served as a professor at Shitennoji University from roughly 1975 to 2008 and directed the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute.

nodes.label: Shoji Mori
nodes.summary: Shoji Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, worked at the Okurayama Institute, and served as associate professor (circa 1978–1988) and professor (circa 1988–2009) at Toyo University.

nodes.label: Kyosho Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kyosho Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. Around 1974, he served as an associate professor at Musashino University.

nodes.label: Paul B. Courtright
nodes.summary: Paul B. Courtright is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He held posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998, 2026), where he is Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: Daniel Stuart Capper
nodes.summary: Daniel Stuart Capper is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert P. Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Robert P. Scharlemann
nodes.summary: Robert P. Scharlemann was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University. He held faculty posts at the University of Southern California (~1965–1966), University of Iowa (~1966–1981), and University of Virginia (~1981–2004).

nodes.label: Chizen Akanuma
nodes.summary: Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kōkōdō and Otani University. He co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921 and was a professor at Otani University in 1919.

nodes.label: Raffaello Orlando

nodes.label: Akihiro Oda

nodes.label: Hitoshi Kato
nodes.summary: Hitoshi Kato is a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 1992 he held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Nara University of Education, and Otani University, and he later held an affiliation at Osaka University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Anthony W. Barber
nodes.summary: Anthony W. Barber is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984. He held a post attested at the University of Calgary in 1998.

nodes.label: Wang Pachow
nodes.summary: Wang Pachow was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Isamu Kanaji
nodes.summary: Isamu Kanaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at both Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College.

nodes.label: Issaien Ikeyama
nodes.summary: Issaien Ikeyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji Junior College.

nodes.label: Koki Kawagishi
nodes.summary: Koki Kawagishi (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University (both attested 1976).

nodes.label: Mitsuyuki Ishida
nodes.summary: Mitsuyuki Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later taught at Ryukoku University (attested 1956, 1976 as professor) and served as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Eisei Kojima
nodes.summary: Eisei Kojima was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as president (学長) of Doho University and as a professor (教授) at Ryukoku University (both attested 1976).

nodes.label: Shunpaku Nakao
nodes.summary: Shunpaku Nakao specialized in Buddhist studies. He served at Shuchiin University, holding the posts of assistant professor as attested in 1963 and professor as attested in 1976.

nodes.label: Ryōshō Taira
nodes.summary: Ryōshō Taira was a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic posts at Taisho University, including being attested as professor emeritus in 1976.

nodes.label: Kanchu Onoue
nodes.summary: Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a teacher at Hikone Higashi High School, attested in 1963, and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin, attested in 1976.

nodes.label: Tetsuei Sato
nodes.summary: Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later served as a professor at Taisho University, Gifu Kyoritsu University (circa 1972), and as an emeritus professor at Ryukoku University (circa 1970–1982).

nodes.label: Keiichi Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Keiichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, earning a literature doctorate, and held positions at Kokugakuin University as lecturer (1986), associate professor (1988), and professor (1995).

nodes.label: Shobha Rani Dash

nodes.label: Makoto Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Makoto Yoshimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, completed his doctoral course at Waseda University (~1993–1998). Around 2004, he served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Ryogon Fukuhara
nodes.summary: Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and the Humboldt University of Berlin under teachers including Shun'ichi Takagi. He lectured at Humboldt University and served as a professor at Ryukoku University from around 1953 to 1978.

nodes.label: Taijun Inokuchi
nodes.summary: Taijun Inokuchi is a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He served as a lecturer and committee member at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1987) and as representative of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Yusen Kashiwahara
nodes.summary: Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor from circa 1972 to 1987.

nodes.label: Shuyu Kanaoka
nodes.summary: Shuyu Kanaoka (1927-2009) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, where he earned a doctorate in 1962 and later served as an assistant professor (~1968-1992).

nodes.label: Hiromu Kitanishi
nodes.summary: Hiromu Kitanishi (1925–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor from around 1971 to 1991.

nodes.label: Encho Tamura
nodes.summary: Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. Educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities, he held faculty posts at Kyushu University and Kumamoto University (~1977–1982), and directed the Kyushu Historical Museum (~1982–1992).

nodes.label: Yoshiro Tamura
nodes.summary: Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo, Rissho University, and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Joryu Chiba
nodes.summary: Joryu Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology who studied at Ryukoku University. He spent his career primarily at Ryukoku University (1950–1989) and led institutions including the Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute and Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies.

nodes.label: Satoshi Hayashima
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hayashima works in the field of Buddhist studies. He was a research student at Ryukoku University around 2013–2014 and later served as a lecturer there from 2015 to 2017.

nodes.label: Michihiko Komine
nodes.summary: Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964–1977). He served at Taisho University as an assistant (~1978–1983) and professor (~1993–2015), as professor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014), and led the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Akio Minoura
nodes.summary: Akio Minoura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an associate professorship at Otani University (attested 2007–2013), conducted research abroad at Stanford University (2012–2013), and is attested as faculty at Otani Academic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Junzo Inagaki
nodes.summary: Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as section chief at Otani University.

nodes.label: Giyu Nishi
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies scholar Giyu Nishi studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, Sylvain Lévi, Hakuju Ui, and Taiken Kimura. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo (1926) and as a professor at Toyo University (1927).

nodes.label: Seishin Kato
nodes.summary: Seishin Kato studied at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. Active in Buddhist studies, he served as professor and president of Buzan University, professor and president of Toyo University, and president of Taisho University.

nodes.label: Nobuo Otsuka
nodes.summary: Nobuo Otsuka (1957–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1982–1987) and later served there as a researcher (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Takayasu Kimura
nodes.summary: Takayasu Kimura (born 1934) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University and held posts at Taisho University (attested 1995) and the Institute of Modern Religious Education of Shingon Buzan (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Hideaki Kimura
nodes.summary: Hideaki Kimura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He also held a researcher post at Taisho University, attested in 1995.

nodes.label: Masahiro Takano
nodes.summary: Masahiro Takano (b. 1960) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a librarian (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Keiya Noguchi
nodes.summary: Keiya Noguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He taught as a lecturer and professor at Shuchiin University and served as a lecturer and institute director at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Takashi Maeda
nodes.summary: Takashi Maeda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2006).

nodes.label: Mitsutoshi Moriguchi
nodes.summary: Mitsutoshi Moriguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).

nodes.label: Hideomi Yaita
nodes.summary: Hideomi Yaita (b. 1953) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he later served as a lecturer (attested 1995), and worked as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies around 1986.

nodes.label: Shinya Moriyama
nodes.summary: Shinya Moriyama works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed an MA at the University of Tokyo, studied under Eli Franco, and earned a Dr.Phil from the University of Vienna (~1999–2006). He was appointed to Shinshu University (~2009).

nodes.label: William M. Gorvine
nodes.summary: William M. Gorvine is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Connecticut College and completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by David Germano.

nodes.label: Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe
nodes.summary: Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1991, 2004, and from 2014 to 2019.

nodes.label: Takashi Ogawa
nodes.summary: Takashi Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo. He became an associate professor at Komazawa University in 1991.

nodes.label: Kenji Kinugawa
nodes.summary: Kenji Kinugawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1971 to 1980 under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

nodes.label: Kenryo Minowa
nodes.summary: Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Aichi Gakuin University (2000–2010), the University of Tokyo (professor from 2010), and Rissho University (professor, 2025).

nodes.label: Ikuro Hattori
nodes.summary: Ikuro Hattori specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, holding a PhD from Pune University. He served as a researcher (attested 2003) and senior researcher (attested 2026) at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, and as a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Takayoku Kimura
nodes.summary: Takayoku Kimura (born 1947) studied at Komazawa University in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1978), a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Michihiko Yajima
nodes.summary: Michihiko Yajima (born 1958) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1992) and as professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Gyoei Takahashi
nodes.summary: Gyoei Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Rissho University (attested 2003–2004 and 2026) and served as a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Kaiten Nukariya
nodes.description: Religious scholar and ordained Zen Buddhist monk
nodes.summary: Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934), a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, studied under Ryodo Nukariya, at Komazawa, First Higher School, and Keio. He lectured at Harvard (~1913–1915) and became the first president of Komazawa University (1925–1934).

variants: 関西大学人権問題研究室

nodes.label: Nathmal Tatia
nodes.summary: Nathmal Tatia was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Literature from the University of Calcutta, studying under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982-1990).

nodes.label: Jain Vishva Bharati Institute
variants: ジャイナ研究所 (Jain Viśva Bharati)

nodes.label: Rita M. Gross
nodes.summary: Rita M. Gross (1943–2015) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at UW–Milwaukee and the University of Chicago (PhD). She held positions at UW–Madison (~1977–1979) and UW–Eau Claire (~1979–1998) as Professor of Philosophy and Religious Studies.

nodes.label: Shumpei Ueyama
nodes.summary: Shumpei Ueyama (1921–2012) was a philosopher and historian educated at Kyoto University, where he later served as professor from 1968. He also served as president of Kyoto City University of Arts and director of the Kyoto National Museum.

nodes.label: Sen Wang
nodes.summary: Sen Wang studied at Peking University from around 1931 to 1935. Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he held a professorship at Minzu University of China from around 1952 to 1985.

nodes.label: Paul L. Swanson
nodes.summary: Paul L. Swanson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and earned a PhD from UW–Madison under Minoru Kiyota (attested 1985), later becoming a professor at Nanzan University (attested 1991–2009).

nodes.label: Taiken Kyuma
nodes.summary: Taiken Kyuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna in 1999 and served as Associate Professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).

nodes.label: Akira Omine
nodes.summary: Akira Omine (1929–2018) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and Heidelberg University, and held posts at Kyoto University (1959), Osaka University of Foreign Studies (1966–1973), Osaka University (1980–1992), and Ryukoku University (1992).

nodes.label: Yumi Nakamoto
nodes.summary: Yumi Nakamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Nakamoto held a research post at Ryukoku University in 2012 and was a graduate research student there in 2014.

nodes.label: Jokai Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Jokai Hiraoka (1923–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and held posts at Shuchiin University and Otemae University (circa 1966–1993).

nodes.label: Ryojin Soga
nodes.summary: Ryojin Soga was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shinshu and Otani universities and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as a professor at Toyo University and Otani University, where he was also president from 1961 to 1967.

nodes.label: Alexander Gardner
nodes.summary: Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2006 under Donald S. Lopez Jr., also studying under Robert H. Sharf and Janet Gyatso, and joined the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

nodes.label: Robert H. Sharf
nodes.summary: Robert H. Sharf works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from the University of Toronto and the University of Michigan, later holding faculty posts at McMaster, Michigan, and UC Berkeley, where he was appointed Distinguished Professor around 2004.

nodes.label: Champa Thupten Zongtse
nodes.summary: Champa Thupten Zongtse worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, where he was attested in 1991 and served as a lecturer in 2009.

nodes.label: Erich Heintel
nodes.summary: Erich Heintel was a philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He served as an extraordinary and later ordinary professor of philosophy at the University of Vienna from 1952 to 1982.

nodes.label: Tsuyoshi Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Tsuyoshi Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and held a post as a project researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Hiromichi Kato
nodes.summary: Hiromichi Kato, born in 1944, works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a graduate student under Ryogon Fukuhara, taught Collett Cox, and held a lecturer post at Ryukoku University attested in 1987.

nodes.label: Shin'ya Yasutomi
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shin'ya Yasutomi studied at Waseda University and Otani University. He held academic posts at Otani University (~1985–2010, 2014) and served as director at Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute and the Eastern Buddhist Society.

nodes.label: Ryoichi Kondo
nodes.summary: Ryoichi Kondo was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Komazawa University and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Lobsang Gyatso
nodes.summary: Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso. He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1973, serving as its head (~1973–1997).

nodes.label: Geshe Rabten
nodes.description: tibetan Buddhist geshe born in Tibet
nodes.summary: Geshe Rabten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and founded Rabten Choeling in 1977.

nodes.label: Migmar Tsering
nodes.summary: Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as head of Sakya College (attested 1991–2003) and held posts at CIHTS (attested 1990) and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Joseph Hackin
nodes.summary: Joseph Hackin was an archaeologist and scholar of Asian studies who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot in Paris. He served as curator at the Guimet Museum (1913–1941) and directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan beginning in 1934.

nodes.label: René Grousset
nodes.summary: René Grousset (1885–1952), a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology, studied at the University of Montpellier (~1903–1906). He held posts at the Guimet Museum, Musée Cernuschi, École du Louvre, and Louvre Museum.

nodes.label: Bunzaburo Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Bunzaburo Matsumoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Rikkyo University and Kyoto University, where he also served as the second president and directed the Institute for Research in Humanities.

nodes.label: Giei Honda
nodes.summary: Giei Honda studied at Kyoto University (~1911–1914) in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served on the faculty at Kyoto University (1929; 1935–1948) and held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.

nodes.label: Shuntaro Matsuyama
nodes.summary: Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930-2014) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, including under Naoshiro Tsuji, and later taught at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, Tama Art University, and Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1970-2001).
