Rikizan Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Rikizan Ishikawa (1943–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1971. He served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at Komazawa University from around 1980 to 1997.

nodes.label: Masashi Nagai
nodes.summary: Masashi Nagai studied Buddhist studies at Komazawa University (~1965–1969, PhD 1998). He served at Komazawa University as lecturer (1984), assistant professor (1988, 1994), professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019), and directed the Museum of Zen Culture and History (~2007–2011).

nodes.label: Rosan Ikeda
nodes.summary: Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1960–1964, ~1963–1969). He spent his academic career at Komazawa University (1969–2012, professor 1983–2012) and served as director at the Soto Zen Research Center (2009).

nodes.label: Ichiro Katayama
nodes.summary: Ichiro Katayama is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Komazawa and Otani Universities under Kogen Mizuno. He served as assistant professor (1975) and professor (1985–2013) at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Tatsugen Sato
nodes.summary: Tatsugen Sato was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate at Komazawa University in 1978. He held academic appointments at Ryukoku University (attested 1974) and Komazawa University, serving as professor (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Morten Schlütter
variants: モルテン・シュルター
nodes.summary: Morten Schlütter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He has held teaching posts at Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, and the University of Iowa, where he is an associate professor.

nodes.label: Shigeki Kudo
nodes.summary: Shigeki Kudo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His academic appointments include serving as an assistant at Kyoto University, an associate professor at Shuchiin University, and an associate professor at Shitennoji University.

nodes.label: Makoto Kitada
nodes.summary: Makoto Kitada is an Indologist and linguist who completed doctoral studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Kitada has been affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010) and Osaka University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Dan Martin
nodes.summary: Dan Martin is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington under Elliot Sperling. He held positions at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Carnegie Mellon University.

nodes.label: Ryuyu Saito

nodes.label: Yasuo Sano

nodes.label: Anna-Pya Sjödin
nodes.summary: Anna-Pya Sjödin is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007. Her doctoral supervisors included Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and she also studied under Barbro Eriksson.

nodes.label: Gunilla Gren-Eklund
nodes.summary: Gunilla Gren-Eklund worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and held a post at Uppsala University from around 1978 to 2003.

nodes.label: Kosuke Nakazawa
nodes.summary: Kosuke Nakazawa (b. 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held positions at Rissho University as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026), and at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Ahmad Hasan Dani

nodes.summary: Ahmad Hasan Dani was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Anant Sadashiv Altekar, under Mortimer Wheeler, and at the University of London under K. de B. Codrington. nodes.label: Klaus Mylius
variants: クラウス・ミューラーダイス
nodes.summary: Klaus Mylius was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and habilitated at the University of Leipzig. He held teaching posts at Leipzig (1970–1991) and Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).

nodes.label: Gessho Sasaki
nodes.summary: Gessho Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served at Otani University as lecturer, professor, and president (1924–1925), and founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921.

nodes.label: Koichi Hokazono
nodes.summary: Koichi Hokazono works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University, later holding posts at Kagoshima International University (attested 1991–2000) and Kyushu University (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Ryuken Sato
nodes.summary: Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2014, he was attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an adviser at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.

nodes.label: Akitoshi Saito
nodes.summary: Akitoshi Saito worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as professor and later professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 1982, 2014) and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Kotetsu Yoshida
nodes.summary: Kotetsu Yoshida (b. 1941) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Ryushin Kitao
nodes.summary: Ryushin Kitao (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as a professor at Shuchiin University in 2014 and 2026.

nodes.label: Yumi Katayama
nodes.summary: Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Katayama was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin
nodes.summary: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Monastery and Gyume Tantric College.

nodes.label: Frank-Richard Hamm
nodes.summary: Frank-Richard Hamm worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring and at the International Academy of Indian Culture, he held posts at Hamburg (1948–1952, 1957–1964) and became a professor at Bonn in 1965.

nodes.label: Daniel Cozort
nodes.summary: Daniel Cozort specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and taught at Bates College and Dickinson College.

nodes.label: Yeshe Thupten
nodes.summary: Yeshe Thupten worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1982, he held a post at Middlebury College and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia. His students include Daniel Cozort, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and Joe Bransford Wilson.

nodes.label: Geshe Palden Drakpa
nodes.summary: Geshe Palden Drakpa specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as Librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, attested in 1988.

nodes.label: Zhaohua Yang
nodes.summary: Zhaohua Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Université catholique de Louvain
variants: Institut Orientaliste de l'Université Catholique de Louvain
Institut Orientaliste of the University of Louvain

nodes.label: Jowita Kramer
nodes.summary: Jowita Kramer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Göttingen, Hamburg, and Munich. She held positions at Munich (~2005–2012, 2017–2021) and other universities, and was appointed Professor at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

nodes.label: George R. Elder
nodes.summary: George R. Elder was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University, where he completed his doctoral work under supervisor Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: Ikuhisa Takigawa
nodes.summary: Ikuhisa Takigawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University, and was attested in 2002 as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

nodes.label: Angelika Krebs
nodes.summary: Philosopher Angelika Krebs (b. 1961) studied at Freiburg, Oxford, Konstanz, UC Berkeley, and Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt, and Basel (2001), with visiting positions at Freiburg, Zurich, Princeton, and Munich.

nodes.label: Thomas A. Tweed
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Tweed specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. After completing a PhD at Stanford (~1980–1984) under William R. Hutchison, he served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

nodes.label: William A. Clebsch
nodes.description: American church historian, developer of religious studies, and university professor (1923-1984)

nodes.label: Van Austin Harvey
nodes.image: Van A. Harvey and a dog.jpg
nodes.summary: Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Occidental, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale. He chaired programs at Southern Methodist and Pennsylvania, and was the George Edwin Burnell Professor of Religious Studies at Stanford (~1978–1996).

nodes.label: Lee Yearley
nodes.summary: Lee Yearley is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and sinology who taught Thomas A. Tweed. He held appointments at Stanford University as Professor (attested 1989–1992) and later as Emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gordon Dester Kaufman
nodes.summary: Gordon Dester Kaufman was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University. He held posts at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity from 1963.

nodes.label: William R. Hutchison
nodes.summary: William R. Hutchison (1930–2005) was a scholar of religious studies and history. He earned degrees from Oxford (~1951–1953) and Yale (~1953–1956), later holding posts at Yale, Hunter College, Wisconsin-Madison, American University (~1960–1968), and Harvard (1968).

nodes.label: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche (b. 1968) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and earned a PhD from Harvard (~1997–2004) under Leonard van der Kuijp, later founding the United Trungram Buddhist Foundation and Fellowship.

nodes.label: Chitai Takenaka
nodes.summary: Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1964–1968). He served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and as a professor at Tokoha University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Hideki Kiyoshima
nodes.summary: Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Delhi and held a lecturer post at Kindai University, attested in 1989.

nodes.label: Jun Takashima
nodes.summary: Jun Takashima is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He held posts at Aichi Prefectural University and served as Professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2020).

nodes.label: Yasumasa Sekine
nodes.summary: Yasumasa Sekine is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Watase
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Watase (1941–) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a master's degree at Kyoto University (~1964–1966). He served as an assistant professor at Tokai University (~1985–2007) and as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2010).

nodes.label: Issei Suzuki
nodes.summary: Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and subsequently held a post as a professor there.

nodes.label: Ryoshu Michihata
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Michihata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University, where he later taught from around 1947 to 1967, and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University from around 1967 to 1980.

nodes.label: Mizumaro Ishida
nodes.summary: Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.

nodes.label: Rosemarie Fuchs
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Fuchs is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche
variants: mKhan po Tshul khrims rgya mtsho
Mkhan po Tshul khrims rgya mtsho
nodes.summary: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, serving as principal shedra teacher at Rumtek Monastery (~1977–1986) and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery (1992).

nodes.label: Tenzin Dorjee
nodes.summary: Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Geshe Sonam Rinchen, Geshe Dawa, and Geshe Lobsang Tsephel. He held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

nodes.label: T. Shrinivas Shastri
nodes.summary: T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar who held positions at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, including Pandit (attested 1993) and Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kyojun Shimizutani
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies scholar Kyojun Shimizutani studied at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. He held professorships at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), and served as head priest of Senso-ji (~1952–1979).

nodes.label: Margaret R. Miles
nodes.summary: Margaret R. Miles (born 1937) works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at San Francisco State University (BA) and Graduate Theological Union (PhD), and held posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and Graduate Theological Union (dean 1996–2001).

nodes.label: National Institute of Japanese Literature
variants: 国文学研究資料館文献資料部

nodes.label: Tokyo Woman's Christian University
variants: 東京女子大学文理学部

nodes.label: Leela Aditi Wood
nodes.summary: Leela Aditi Wood specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Michigan by 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: Thomas E. Crow
nodes.summary: Art historian Thomas E. Crow studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, directed the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and became Rosalie Solow Professor of Modern Art at NYU in 2007.

nodes.label: Marvin Eisenberg
nodes.summary: Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was an art historian and scholar. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and held a long-term post at the University of Michigan (~1949–1988).

nodes.label: Cyrus Stearns
nodes.summary: Cyrus Stearns is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA under Turrell V. Wylie and a PhD from the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under traditional teachers and working as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.

nodes.label: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima
variants: Sde gzhung Rin po che, Kun dga' bstan pa'i nyi ma
デシュン・リンポチェ
nodes.image: Buddhist scholars - Dezhung Rinpoche III seated on a stool, Chris Wilkinson, student seated at the feet of his lama, wearing Buddhist robes, malas, likely Seattle, Washington, USA (16134833232) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ngawang Nyima, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

nodes.label: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche
variants: Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che, Ngag dbang legs bshad rgya mtsho
Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che
nodes.summary: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Geshe Tsechok, and Kunga Chophel, and became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery in 1928.

nodes.label: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche
variants: Dil mgo Mkhyen brtse Rin po che, Rab gsal zla ba
キャブジェ・ディルゴ・ケンツェ・リンポチェ
nodes.description: Buddhist Vajrayana master, scholar, poet, and teacher (1910–1991)
nodes.summary: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, and succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991.

nodes.label: Jong-Nam Choi
nodes.summary: Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Shitennoji University, he completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Lambert Schmithausen and studied under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

nodes.label: Edward Garrett
nodes.summary: Edward Garrett is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his Ph.D. at UCLA under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, mentored postdoctorally by Anna Szabolcsi. He held research assistant posts at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

nodes.label: Carson T. Schütze
nodes.summary: Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1997.

nodes.label: Dominique Sportiche
nodes.summary: Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, from around 1987.

nodes.label: Anna Szabolcsi
nodes.summary: Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. She served at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (~1978–1990), UCLA (~1990–1999), and New York University (~1999).

nodes.label: Naomi Appleton
nodes.summary: Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. After completing her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, she was a postdoctoral fellow at Cardiff and became a professor and co-director at Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Anna Aurelia Esposito
nodes.summary: Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and Tübingen (MA, 1998). She served as Assistant Professor at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and later held a post at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jonathan Geen
nodes.summary: Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctorate under Phyllis Granoff at McMaster University. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

nodes.label: Ryusei Keira
nodes.summary: Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his thesis at the University of Lausanne in 2003 under the doctoral supervision of Tom Tillemans.

nodes.label: Koichi Shinohara
nodes.summary: Koichi Shinohara (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He served as professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and as senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004–2017).

nodes.id: I:The Okurayama Institute for the Study of Cultural Sciences
nodes.label: The Okurayama Institute for the Study of Cultural Sciences
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Hidetoshi Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies. At Taisho University, he held posts as a researcher (attested 1998), research student (attested 2006), lecturer (attested 2008), and chief research fellow (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Hirofumi Toda
nodes.summary: Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University from around 1978 to 2002 and was affiliated with the Lotus Sutra Institute.

nodes.label: Hiroko Matsuoka
nodes.summary: Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She pursued doctoral studies at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held posts at the University of Leipzig (attested 2016) and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Zeff Bjerken
nodes.summary: Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned a PhD at the University of Michigan in 2001 under Donald S. Lopez Jr., later holding a post at the College of Charleston.

nodes.label: T. Griffith Foulk
nodes.summary: T. Griffith Foulk specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, taught at Michigan (c. 1987–1995), and served as Riggs Professor of Religion at Sarah Lawrence College.

nodes.label: Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak
nodes.summary: Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries under Sangye Tenzin and Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen, later serving at Menri, Triten Norbutse, SOAS (1961), and Munich (1969).

nodes.label: Makoto Nagai
nodes.summary: Makoto Nagai was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon University, Toyo University, Kamakura Women's University, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College.

nodes.label: Shun Hidaka
nodes.summary: Shun Hidaka is a Buddhist studies researcher who served as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Rajendra Chandra Hazra
nodes.summary: Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indology scholar who earned his BA at the University of Dhaka and completed doctoral studies under Sushil Kumar De. He lectured at Jagannath University and Dhaka, later serving at Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

nodes.label: Izumi Hoshi
nodes.summary: Izumi Hoshi (born 1967) is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo between 1987 and 1997. She joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as assistant professor in 1997 and served as director from 2019 to 2023.

nodes.label: Michiyo Hoshi
nodes.summary: Michiyo Hoshi (born 1941) specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).

nodes.id: I:Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa
nodes.label: Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa
variants: アジア・アフリカ言語文化研究所

nodes.label: Ngawang Thondup
variants: ガワン・トゥンドゥプ

nodes.label: Temba Gyaltsen
variants: テンバ・ギェンツェン

nodes.label: Jitsushyu Oshika
nodes.summary: Jitsushyu Oshika worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

nodes.label: Yasuo Goto
nodes.summary: Yasuo Goto is a Buddhist studies scholar who held lecturer posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1991 and 2006) and served as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ronald Y. Nakasone
nodes.summary: Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1973–1980). He served at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1988–1995) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Werner Abraham
nodes.summary: Linguist Werner Abraham studied at TU Wien, the University of Innsbruck, and the University of Vienna (PhD ~1965). He held posts at Illinois, Tübingen, and Munich, and was appointed professor of German linguistics and medieval studies at Groningen in 1971.

nodes.label: Tarab Tulku
nodes.summary: Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served at the University of Copenhagen from around 1962 to 1998 and as a curator at the Royal Danish Library from approximately 1962 to 2000.

nodes.label: Hartmut Buescher
nodes.summary: Hartmut Buescher is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhal Tripathi and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.

nodes.label: Eric David Mortensen
nodes.summary: Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Harvard University in 2003 under Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.

nodes.label: Kimberley C. Patton
nodes.summary: Kimberley C. Patton (born 1958) works in religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1986–1992) and taught there, serving as assistant professor (~1994–2001) and professor of the comparative and historical study of religion (~2001).

nodes.label: Yoshiki Motoaki
nodes.summary: Yoshiki Motoaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Motoaki held a post at Otani University (attested 2013) and has been affiliated with the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Christopher S. George
nodes.summary: Christopher S. George is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler, Geshe Wangyal, and Pema Gyaltsen, founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, and was a professor at IASWR (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Geshe Wangyal
nodes.summary: Geshe Wangyal specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Agvan Dorjiev and at Drepung Monastery. He taught at Columbia University (~1962–1972) and founded the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, serving there from ~1958 to 1983.

nodes.label: Ryojun Mitomo
nodes.summary: Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College and as a faculty professor of social welfare at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Richard F. Nance
nodes.summary: Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago in 2004. He has held assistant and associate professor posts in religious studies at Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Atsushi Ibuki
nodes.summary: Atsushi Ibuki (b. 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and became a professor at Toyo University around 2005.

nodes.id: I:Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies
Tomoyuki Komine
nodes.summary: Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He also served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Daiju Sasaki
nodes.summary: Daiju Sasaki (born 1977) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from 1996 to 2006. He held teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and ~2018) and at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Fumio Shoji
nodes.summary: Fumio Shoji specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University from ~1998 to 2008 and later held posts there as an assistant professor (~2012–2017) and associate professor (~2017).

nodes.label: Kenta Suzuki
nodes.summary: Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 2015–2016).

nodes.label: Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College
variants: 北海道武蔵女子短期大学

nodes.label: Kimiaki Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kimiaki Tanaka (born 1955) works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Oxford, and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. He held posts at Tokyo, Beijing Center for Japanese Studies, Keio University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Humanities Information Studies Institute
variants: 一般財団法人人文情報学研究所

nodes.label: Tensho Miyazaki
nodes.summary: Tensho Miyazaki (1978–) is a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2006–2011). He held research posts at Toyo University (~2011–2014) and the University of Tokyo (~2014).

nodes.label: Masahide Mori
nodes.summary: Masahide Mori (b. 1962) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Nagoya University and SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, later holding positions at Nagoya University, Koyasan University, and Kanazawa University.

nodes.label: Tsutomu Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Yamaguchi is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Hokkaido University. He has held researcher posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2015, 2026).

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Hotta
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Hotta focuses on Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, where he was also attested as a manager in 2007, and served as a fixed-term assistant professor at Otani University in 2015.

nodes.label: Hoshu Mitsuhara
nodes.summary: Hoshu Mitsuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1982) and later professor emeritus (attested 2004) at Koyasan University.

nodes.label: Arjo Vanderjagt
nodes.summary: Arjo Vanderjagt is a philosopher who studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

nodes.label: Seiji Kumagai
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Seiji Kumagai completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2004–2008) and became an associate professor there (~2013).

nodes.label: Yoshio Kawakatsu
nodes.summary: Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University and under Paul Demiéville. He worked as a library-track assistant at Kyoto University from around 1948 until 1984.

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu
nodes.summary: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He held professorships at Hanazono University (1919), Ryukoku University (1929), Kyoto University (1943–1953), and Kyoto City University of Arts (1953).

nodes.label: Serinity Young
nodes.summary: Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and held posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Carole McGranahan
nodes.summary: Carole McGranahan is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Colgate University and the University of Michigan, completing her PhD under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler. In ~2001, she joined the University of Colorado Boulder.

nodes.label: Nicholas Dirks
nodes.summary: Nicholas Dirks (born 1950) is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Wesleyan University (~1968–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981), and held posts at Caltech (~1982–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

nodes.label: Ann Laura Stoler
nodes.summary: Ann Laura Stoler works in history and archaeology. Educated at Barnard College and Columbia University, she taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and University of Michigan (1989–2004), becoming Gründungsdirektorin at The New School in 2004.

nodes.label: Samuel M. Grupper
nodes.summary: Samuel M. Grupper works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.

nodes.label: Join Saeki
nodes.summary: Join Saeki (1867–1952) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Jōchō Chihaya and at Sennyu-ji. He held posts at Horyu-ji, Kangakuin, the University of Tokyo, and the Japan Academy.

nodes.label: Shoko Takeuchi
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Takeuchi studied at Ryukoku University, where he later served as professor emeritus (attested 1987–1995).

nodes.label: Yasutoshi Murakami
nodes.summary: Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1963–1971). He held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1974–1999) and Koyasan University (~1999–2006), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Takatoshi Ito
nodes.summary: Takatoshi Ito is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1981 and 1991.

nodes.label: Guangchang Fang
nodes.summary: Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from 1986 to 2004, and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.

nodes.label: Michael J. Walsh
nodes.summary: Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a B.Soc.Sc. from the University of Cape Town and an M.A. from UC Santa Barbara, where he later pursued doctoral studies under William F. Powell.

variants: Research Center for Monsoon Asia, National Tsing Hua University

variants: 大阪教育大学教育学部

nodes.label: Osaka Prefecture University
variants: Osaka Prefecture University and Graduate School

nodes.label: Atsuuji Ashikaga
nodes.summary: Atsuuji Ashikaga (1901–1983) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Ryosaburo Sakaki, completed degrees at Doshisha and Kyoto Universities, and held multiple professorial and administrative posts at Kyoto University from 1930.

nodes.label: T. Chandrasekharan
nodes.summary: T. Chandrasekharan was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), where he succeeded T. R. Chintamani.

nodes.label: Kunio Mugitani

nodes.label: Sherab Gyatso

nodes.label: Ho-chin Yang

nodes.label: Susumu Shimazono

nodes.label: Bryan J. Cuevas

nodes.label: Donald Phillip Verene
nodes.summary: Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who studied at Knox College and earned his doctorate at Washington University in St. Louis. He chaired at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting appointments at Pembroke College, Oxford, and Sapienza University of Rome.

nodes.label: Henk Blezer
nodes.image: Henk Blezer - Foto door Dan Martin.jpg
nodes.summary: Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his degrees at Leiden University (1987–1997), where he later served as a postdoctoral researcher and university lecturer, alongside a post at the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

nodes.label: Karma Phuntsho
nodes.summary: Karma Phuntsho, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, Michael Aris, and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held research and fellow positions at the University of Cambridge from 2003 to 2008.

nodes.label: Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz
nodes.summary: Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University, the University of Oxford, and under Kazi Dawa Samdup.

nodes.label: Kazi Dawa Samdup
nodes.image: Walter Evans-Wentz and Lama Kazi Dawa Samdup photographed circa 1919.jpg
nodes.summary: Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu. He later served as headmaster of Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and lectured at the University of Calcutta (1920).

nodes.label: Bhutia Boarding School
variants: ダージリンのブーティアボーディングスクール

nodes.label: James A. Santucci
nodes.summary: James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts at California State University (attested 1998) and served as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Ryoko Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Ryoko Mochizuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1958 to 1963 and served as a lecturer at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Sensho Kimura
nodes.summary: Sensho Kimura studied at Otani University from around 1962 to 1971. Working in Buddhist studies and Sinology, he later served as a professor at Otani University from around 1988 to 2008.

nodes.label: Yasuo Inamoto
nodes.summary: Yasuo Inamoto is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1995–2004) before taking up a post at Kyoto University in ~2004.

nodes.label: Tadao Yoshikawa
nodes.summary: Tadao Yoshikawa is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Kyoto University. His academic posts include assistant professor at Kyoto University, professor at Ryukoku University (2002), and director of the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (c. 2003–2011).

nodes.label: Masaaki Tsuchiya
nodes.summary: Masaaki Tsuchiya (b. 1960) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1979–1984) and held a post at Senshu University around 1995.

nodes.label: Yuzo Mizoguchi
nodes.summary: Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) was a sinologist and philosopher educated at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held academic posts at Tokyo, Saitama, Hitotsubashi, and Daito Bunka universities, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

nodes.label: Marina Illich
nodes.summary: Marina Illich is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 2006 under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

nodes.label: Angela Zito
nodes.summary: Angela Zito works in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1979–1989) and became an associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University around 1996.

nodes.label: John Stratton Hawley
nodes.summary: John Stratton Hawley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Amherst and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (circa 1968–1974), he held posts at Bowdoin College (circa 1974–1977) and Columbia University (Professor from circa 1986).

nodes.label: Kathryn H. Selig Brown
nodes.summary: Kathryn H. Selig Brown specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan by 2000, studying under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink.

nodes.label: John C. Huntington
nodes.summary: John C. Huntington was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University, with his tenure attested between 1987 and 2000.

nodes.label: Noboru Karashima

nodes.label: Naoya Funahashi
nodes.summary: Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions as a research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and at Otani University (attested 1981).

nodes.label: Eugene Watson Burlingame
nodes.summary: Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held appointments at the University of Pennsylvania (~1910–1914), Johns Hopkins University (~1914–1917), and Yale University (~1917–1932).

nodes.label: Thomas Burrow
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Thomas Burrow studied at Cambridge and SOAS. He held posts at the British Museum (1937–1944) and SOAS (1938–1948) before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit and fellow at the University of Oxford from 1944 to 1976.

nodes.label: Furman University
variants: ファーマン大学 Furman University

nodes.label: Yuki Takatsukasa

nodes.label: Huiyu Zhang
nodes.summary: Huiyu Zhang is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Rei Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University and later served there as a professor (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Hoong Teik Toh
nodes.summary: Hoong Teik Toh is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Toh earned a PhD from Harvard University by 2004, studying under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

nodes.label: Gray Tuttle
nodes.summary: Gray Tuttle is a Tibetologist, sinologist, and historian who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard in 2002. At Columbia University, he has served as Associate Professor (attested 2008–2015) and Leila Hadley Luce Professor of Modern Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yudru Tsomu
nodes.summary: Yudru Tsomu is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who earned a PhD at Harvard University under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and advisors Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn. Tsomu taught Hoong Teik Toh and Cameron David Warner.

nodes.label: Gyurme Dorje
nodes.summary: Gyurme Dorje was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Edinburgh and SOAS, earning his PhD under Philip Denwood (~1982–1987), held fellowships at SOAS/University of London (1991–1996), and worked as a translator for Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).

nodes.label: Barbara Nimri Aziz
nodes.summary: Barbara Nimri Aziz works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran.

nodes.label: Aung San Suu Kyi

nodes.summary: Aung San Suu Kyi, active in Tibetology and other fields, studied at Lady Shri Ram College, University of Delhi, St Hugh's College, and SOAS University of London. She held a post at the United Nations (~1969–1971).

nodes.label: Kojiro Yoshikawa
nodes.summary: Kojiro Yoshikawa (1904–1980) was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and later as board chairman of Toho Gakkai (~1973–1980).

nodes.label: Tokuryu Yamauchi
nodes.summary: Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Freiburg under Nishida, Husserl, and Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Annemarie von Gabain
nodes.summary: Annemarie von Gabain was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin, she held posts there from 1935 to 1945 and was a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1950 to 1966.

nodes.label: Johannes Nobel
nodes.summary: Johannes Nobel worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Greifswald and Berlin (PhD under Heinrich Lüders, 1908–1911). He held positions at Berlin (1921, 1927) and the chair of Indology at Marburg (1928–1955).

nodes.label: Harvey B. Aronson
nodes.summary: Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism.

nodes.label: Tibet House, New Delhi
variants: Tibet House cultural center in New Delhi

nodes.label: Shunei Tsuboi
nodes.summary: Shunei Tsuboi (1923–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Bukkyo University, attested in 1963 and 1972.

nodes.label: Honsho Ueda
nodes.summary: Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1963 and 1992), Minobusan University (attested 1996), and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Shoku Bando
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Bando studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg (1984–1986). In 1987, he held appointments at the Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

nodes.label: Shodo Yamagami
nodes.summary: Shodo Yamagami is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He served at Kyoto Sangyo University as an associate professor (circa 1978–1988) and as a professor (circa 1988–2010).

nodes.label: Kōichi Kozaka
nodes.summary: Kōichi Kozaka is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas
nodes.summary: Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas studied at the University of Mysore, University of Mumbai, and University of Oxford. A specialist in Indology, he held appointments at Oxford, MS University of Baroda, and University of Delhi, and chaired the ISEC (1972–1979).

nodes.label: W. H. R. Rivers
nodes.description: English anthropologist, neurologist, ethnologist and psychiatrist (1864-1922)
nodes.summary: W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) studied at Tonbridge School, St Bartholomew's, and the University of London. Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held medical and academic posts at Cambridge, University College London, and St John's College.

nodes.label: Peter Haskel

nodes.label: Brian Gregory Baumann
nodes.summary: Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara (2005) and teaches Mongolian at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Joseph Goldstein

nodes.label: Philip Kapleau

nodes.label: Etsuaki Teraishi
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and philosophy, Etsuaki Teraishi held posts at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, attested in 1999, and as a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, attested in 2001.

nodes.label: Kensuke Okamoto
nodes.summary: Kensuke Okamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2006) and is attested as a Ryukoku University professor at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute in 2026.

nodes.label: Saswati Mutsuddy
nodes.summary: Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served as an assistant professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Yutaka Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Yutaka Kawasaki specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Having studied under Seio Okuda, Kawasaki held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Junko Matsumura
nodes.summary: Junko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an MA at the Australian National University (1980) and a doctorate at the University of Göttingen (1990). Matsumura is attested as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Yusho Miyasaka
nodes.summary: Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe, he held posts at Koyasan University (1954, 1965–1967), Nagoya University (1977–1984), Chisan Denpōin (1987), and Shuchiin University (2001).

nodes.label: Ryosho Tanaka
nodes.summary: Ryosho Tanaka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University. He served Komazawa as a professor from 1964, dean, museum director, and president in 2009, and was also a professor at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Chikyo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor, attested in 1970, and later as a part-time lecturer, attested in 1980.

nodes.label: Shinjo Hinonishi
nodes.summary: Shinjo Hinonishi worked in Buddhist and religious studies and studied under Shigeru Gorai. He spent his career at Koyasan University, where he served as assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Akira Mukai
nodes.summary: Akira Mukai (b. 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral course and served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (attested 1978), later serving as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Takanori Fukita
nodes.summary: Takanori Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies. He was a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017) and later served as a specially appointed lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hironari Tanaka
nodes.summary: Hironari Tanaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies (attested 2015–2020) and held a post at Bukkyo University. He was also a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mohan G. Dhadphale
nodes.summary: Mohan G. Dhadphale is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Saroja Bhate
nodes.summary: Saroja Bhate (born 1942) is an Indologist and linguist. She served as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1978–2002) and as Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Laura Harrington
nodes.summary: Laura Harrington is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., Gary A. Tubb, Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Tenzin Norbu, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory Hillis.

nodes.label: Tenzin Norbu
nodes.summary: Tenzin Norbu is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a post at Columbia University and served as an assistant professor and department head at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gregory Hillis
nodes.summary: Gregory Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned an MA at the University of Virginia. He held a post at Virginia (attested 2002) and is attested at UC Santa Barbara in 2026.

nodes.label: Satoshi Ito
nodes.summary: Satoshi Ito (born 1961) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1990) and became a professor at Ibaraki University around 2004.

nodes.label: Osamu Izumoji
nodes.summary: Osamu Izumoji is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Charles Goodman
nodes.summary: Charles Goodman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard (completed by 2002) and served as an associate professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Allan Gibbard
nodes.description: American philosopher and social choice theorist
nodes.summary: Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College and Harvard University. He held academic appointments at the University of Chicago, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Michigan from 1977 to 2016.

nodes.label: Monica Esposito
nodes.description: Italian translator and historian of Chinese Religion, Daoism (1962-2011)
nodes.summary: Monica Esposito was a sinologist and religious studies scholar. She completed a PhD at Paris Diderot University and University of Paris, and became an Associate Professor at Kyoto University in 2003 after postdoctoral fellowships in Venice, Paris, and Kansai.

nodes.label: François Lachaud
nodes.summary: François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who has served as a professor at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2008 and 2013.

nodes.label: Michael Puett
nodes.summary: Michael Puett is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He was appointed Associate Professor (~1995) and later Walter C. Klein Professor of Chinese History and Anthropology (~2013) at Harvard.

nodes.label: Jean-Noël Robert
nodes.summary: Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Bernard Frank and at INALCO. He held posts at the CNRS, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and served as professor at the Collège de France (2011–2022).

nodes.label: Eikan Taki
nodes.summary: Eikan Taki specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been a member of Taisho University and served as a lecturer (講師) at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ryoshu Kouda
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Kouda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami and held researcher appointments at Taisho University in 1998 and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute in 2006.

nodes.label: Satoshi Kono
nodes.summary: Satoshi Kono (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

nodes.label: Nobukatsu Komai
nodes.summary: Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Paul G. Hackett
nodes.summary: Paul G. Hackett works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as South Asia Bibliographer and Tibetan Collection curator at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and later at Columbia University in Buddhist studies (2003) and Classical Tibetan (2016).

nodes.label: Masaaki Chikusa
nodes.summary: Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University (PhD 1980), he held assistant and associate posts there between 1968 and 1993, later becoming a professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

nodes.label: University of California, Santa Cruz
variants: Oakes College, University of California at Santa Cruz

nodes.label: Wayne Proudfoot
nodes.summary: Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a Master of Theology and a Ph.D. from Harvard University. He taught at Fordham University (~1970–1972) and served as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (~1972–2018).

nodes.label: G. Thomas Tanselle
nodes.summary: G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University (~1951–1955). He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978), served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006), and was adjunct professor of English at Columbia University (~1978–2007).

nodes.label: 14th Dalai Lama
variants: His Holiness the Fourteenth Dalai Lama
His Holiness the Dalai Lama Tenzin Gyatso
nodes.description: 14th Dalai Lama, the spiritual and temporal leader of Tibetans
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, he studied under mentors including Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists (1989) and the Mind and Life Institute (1990).

nodes.label: Jigdal Dagchen Sakya
nodes.summary: Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and held a post at the University of Washington (~1960–1963).

nodes.label: Dicastery for Interreligious Dialogue
variants: ヴァチカンの非キリスト教宗教研究部門

nodes.label: Bunkyo Aoki
nodes.summary: Bunkyo Aoki was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and under Kozui Otani. In 1951, he succeeded Tokan Tada as a Tibetan language lecturer at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Ekai Kawaguchi
variants: Ekai Kawaguchi (河口慧海, Kawaguchi Ekai)
nodes.summary: Ekai Kawaguchi was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College. He served as rector at Gohyaku Rakan-ji (~1891) and professor at Toyo University (1916).

nodes.label: Lynn Struve
nodes.summary: Lynn Struve (born 1944) is a scholar of sinology and history. She studied at the University of Washington (c. 1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (c. 1967–1974), and served on the faculty at Indiana University Bloomington (c. 1977–2010).

nodes.id: I:Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences
nodes.label: Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences
variants: Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences

nodes.label: Hiromi Habata
nodes.summary: Hiromi Habata (b. 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg, she held posts at the University of Munich, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Takayasu Suzuki
nodes.summary: Takayasu Suzuki (born 1964) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1989–1998) and served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (~2004–2017).

nodes.label: Yamaguchi Prefectural University
variants: 山口県立大学国際文化学部

nodes.label: Shinten Sakai
nodes.summary: Shinten Sakai specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

nodes.label: Günter Schweiger
nodes.summary: Günter Schweiger worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna University of Economics and Business under Gert Klingenschmitt and held posts at JKU Linz and WU Vienna (1974–2009), alongside several visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Gert Klingenschmitt
nodes.summary: Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he also worked, before holding a chair at the University of Regensburg.

nodes.label: Rosemarie Lühr
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Lühr is a linguist and Indologist who completed her Promotion at Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1970–1977) and Habilitation at Regensburg (~1977–1984). She held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994) and Jena (1994–2013), and was honorary professor at Humboldt University (2013).

nodes.label: Michael Janda
nodes.summary: Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist. He earned his PhD from the University of Vienna and completed his Habilitation at the University of Zurich, holding posts at Zurich (1995) and the University of Münster (2002).

nodes.label: Harumi Hirano Ziegler
nodes.summary: Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her MA and PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, completing her doctorate under the supervision of Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Tairyo Makita
nodes.summary: Tairyo Makita was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto universities. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1946; 1949–1976), Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University, and president of Saitama Institute of Technology (1997).

nodes.id: I:École Nationale des Langues Orientales Vivantes
nodes.label: École Nationale des Langues Orientales Vivantes
Rolf Alfred Stein
nodes.summary: Tibetologist and sinologist Rolf Alfred Stein studied under Chavannes, Pelliot, Maspero, and Demiéville, among others. He was directeur d'études at the EPHE (1951–1975) and professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).

nodes.label: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay
nodes.summary: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Drepung Monastery, SOAS, and the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove and Rolf Alfred Stein. He held posts at SOAS, CNRS, and the International Association for Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Hidetaka Nakatani
nodes.summary: Hidetaka Nakatani specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under the supervision of Gadjin Nagao.

nodes.label: Klemens Karlsson
nodes.summary: Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Uppsala University by 2000, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schalk.

nodes.label: Susan L. Huntington
nodes.summary: Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She was a professor at Ohio State University from approximately 1971 to 2011.

nodes.label: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan
nodes.summary: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2003, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

nodes.label: Masako Keta
nodes.summary: Masako Keta (b. 1953) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi and held posts at Kanazawa University before serving as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).

nodes.label: Keiji Nishitani
nodes.summary: Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a Kyoto School philosopher who studied under Nishida, Tanabe, and Heidegger at Kyoto University and Freiburg. He held a lectureship at Otani University (~1928–1935) and served as professor at Kyoto University (1943–1964).

nodes.label: Kitaro Nishida
nodes.summary: Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz. He held posts at the Fourth Higher School (1899–1909) and served as professor of philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

nodes.label: Om Prakash
nodes.summary: Om Prakash is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and held positions at Kirori Mal College, the University of Delhi, and the Delhi School of Economics.

nodes.label: Dasharatha Sharma
nodes.summary: Dasharatha Sharma was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Delhi. He headed history at Hindu College, was Reader at Delhi (~1960–1969), Professor and Dean at Jai Narain Vyas (1966), and Director of Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1970–1976).

nodes.label: Leah Judith Zahler
nodes.summary: Leah Judith Zahler specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981), and also studied under Harvey B. Aronson, Joe Bransford Wilson, and Geshe Wangyal.

nodes.label: University of North Carolina Wilmington
variants: University of North Carolina at Wilmington

nodes.label: Lati Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Lati Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who earned his Geshe Lharampa at Ganden Shartse Monastery and studied at Gyuto Monastery. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1976–1984) and visited the University of Virginia (1976).

nodes.label: Mikisaburo Mori
nodes.summary: Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University (literature doctorate, 1962). He held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka High School, Osaka University (1950, 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1980).

nodes.label: Touhoi Fok
nodes.summary: Touhoi Fok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Otani University, later lecturing at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1972–1988).

nodes.label: Egaku Maeda
nodes.summary: Egaku Maeda studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen Junior College, Meijo University, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

nodes.label: Fumimaro Watanabe
nodes.summary: Fumimaro Watanabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Hammalawa Saddhatissa. He later served as professor at Kindai University (1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).

nodes.label: Genryu Kagoshima
nodes.summary: Genryu Kagoshima (1912–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1931 to 1934. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from circa 1957 to 1983.

nodes.label: Chaesong Kim
nodes.summary: Chaesong Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995), studying under Yasunori Ejima.

nodes.label: Phrapongsak K.
nodes.summary: Phrapongsak K. is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 2015, he held research positions at Ryukoku University and the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.

variants: アジア仏教文化研究センター

variants: 真言宗豊山派総合研究院宗学研究所

nodes.label: Eshun Otsuka
nodes.summary: Eshun Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was a research student (研究生) at Taisho University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nosei Fuji
nodes.summary: Nosei Fuji specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Dongguk University and held appointments at Daegu University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Ryukoku University, where he was professor of Buddhist studies (attested 2011–2013).

nodes.label: Peter Ebbatson
nodes.summary: Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

nodes.label: Hu Shih
nodes.summary: Hu Shih studied at Cornell and Columbia University under John Dewey and Kaiten Nukariya. Working in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, he served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

nodes.label: John Dewey
nodes.description: American philosopher, psychologist, and educational reformer (1859–1952)
nodes.summary: Philosopher John Dewey studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1884–1894), University of Minnesota (~1888–1889), University of Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).

nodes.label: Noriaki Hosoda
nodes.summary: Noriaki Hosoda works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. His career includes posts as assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003) at Hokkaido University, and professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Haruhiko Masaki
nodes.summary: Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Gakushuin University and completed master's and doctoral courses at the University of Tokyo, later serving as a professor at Nagasaki University from approximately 1977 to 2003.

nodes.label: Shokin Furuta
nodes.summary: Shokin Furuta was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tokyo University and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He served as professor at Hokkaido University and Nihon University, and became director of Matsugaoka Bunko in 1966.

nodes.label: Shōkō Kabutogi
nodes.summary: Shōkō Kabutogi (1912-1985) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University, graduating by 1936, and later served there as a professor from around 1956 to 1982.

nodes.label: Taion Satomi
nodes.summary: Taion Satomi is a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Rissho University in 1933. He served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College, attested in 1972.

nodes.label: Nobumasa Hibi
nodes.summary: Nobumasa Hibi (1932–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Rissho University (completing studies in 1959) and later served there as an assistant professor (attested 1972).

nodes.label: Taishun Mibu
nodes.summary: Taishun Mibu was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who graduated from Taisho University in 1937. He later served as library director at Taisho University, attested in 1972.

nodes.label: Senchu Murano
nodes.summary: Senchu Murano studied Buddhist studies at Rissho University (~1930–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1952 to 1978.

nodes.label: Natalie Maxwell
nodes.summary: Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1972–1975) under Stephan V. Beyer, having also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.

nodes.label: Stephan V. Beyer
nodes.summary: Stephan V. Beyer is a Buddhist studies and tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1971 to 1980 and worked at Sidley Austin.

nodes.label: David M. Knipe
nodes.summary: David M. Knipe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, holding appointments as professor and chair of religious studies.

nodes.label: Robert J. Miller
nodes.summary: Robert J. Miller was a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1989) and also held a professorship at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

nodes.label: Awadh Kishore Narain
nodes.summary: Awadh Kishore Narain specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, holding key academic posts at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

nodes.label: Jun Fujii
nodes.summary: Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a doctoral degree in literature at the University of Tokyo (~2000–2005). He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University (~2011–2017).

nodes.label: John W. Schroeder
nodes.summary: John W. Schroeder specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon under Hee-jin Kim and doctoral supervisor Don Levi, he held posts at Oregon, the College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.

nodes.label: Sheng Yen
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist monk, religious scholar, and writer (1931–2009)
nodes.summary: Sheng Yen (1931–2009) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University under mentors including Dongchu and Lingyuan. He held positions at Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Shuntaro Kondo
nodes.summary: Shuntaro Kondo (born 1974) is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Ryukoku University by 2011 and served there as a part-time lecturer as attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Douglas S. Duckworth
nodes.summary: Douglas S. Duckworth (b. 1971) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at James Madison University and the University of Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins), and served as an assistant professor at East Tennessee State University (~2008–2013).

nodes.label: Rangjung Yeshe Institute
variants: Rangjung Yeshe Institute, the Centre for Buddhist Studies at Kathmandu University
