nodes.label: Thomas Doctor
nodes.summary: Thomas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and conducted doctoral research at the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, later holding a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Erik Pema Kunsang
nodes.summary: Erik Pema Kunsang is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications (circa 1980) and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

nodes.label: George de Roerich
variants: ユーリー・ニコラエーヴィチ
ユーリイ・リョーリフ
nodes.summary: George de Roerich studied at the University of London, Harvard, and the Sorbonne, training under scholars including Sylvain Lévi. A Tibetologist and Indologist, he directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute and led a department at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

nodes.label: Anagarika Dharmapala
variants: アナガーリカ・ダルマパーラ
nodes.jawiki: アナガーリカ・ダルマパーラ
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Buddhist revivalist and writer (1864-1933)
nodes.summary: Anagarika Dharmapala was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at institutions including S. Thomas' College and Royal College, Colombo. He founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 as well as the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

nodes.label: Horkhang Sonam Palbar
nodes.summary: Horkhang Sonam Palbar was a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Tsadru Ngawang Losang and Gendun Chophel (~1946-1951).

nodes.label: Albion Moonlight Butters
nodes.summary: Albion Moonlight Butters is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Harvard, CIHTS, and Columbia University (PhD 2006) under numerous teachers and supervisors, including Robert A. F. Thurman, Noel Q. King, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

nodes.label: Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche (1938–2010) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries under teachers including Tubten Tsondru and Dudjom Rinpoche, and chaired the Nyingma section at CIHTS (~1967–1984).

nodes.label: Shintaro Kitano
nodes.summary: Shintaro Kitano works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and as a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Gelek Rimpoche
nodes.summary: Gelek Rimpoche (1939–2017) studied at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School (circa 1960–1963), and Cornell (1964). In Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he directed Tibet House in New Delhi (1965) and founded Jewel Heart in 1988.

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Inada
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who taught Jay L. Garfield. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and chaired both the Numata Center (1996–1999) and Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (until 1999).

nodes.label: Todd A. Gibson
nodes.summary: Todd A. Gibson works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Jongcheol Lee
nodes.summary: Jongcheol Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Seoul National University and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Academy of Korean Studies
variants: 韓国精神文化研究院 韓国学大学院

nodes.label: Thomas A. Forsthoefel
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Forsthoefel works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Georgetown, Loyola Chicago, and a PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Katherine Janiec Jones
nodes.summary: Katherine Janiec Jones works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

nodes.label: W. Randolph Kloetzli
variants: W・ランドルフ・クレツリ
nodes.summary: W. Randolph Kloetzli earned his PhD at the University of Chicago and worked in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including J. A. B. van Buitenen and lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

nodes.label: Milton Kleintop
variants: ミルトン・クライントップ

nodes.label: Joseph Haroutunian
variants: ジョセフ・ハロウトゥニアン
nodes.summary: Joseph Haroutunian was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Columbia University and Union Theological Seminary. He held academic posts at Wellesley College, McCormick Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

nodes.label: Gyosho Takahashi
nodes.summary: Gyosho Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Kino
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Kino was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He founded Shinnyokai and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).

nodes.label: Tanso Hirose
nodes.summary: Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar in Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku from around 1797 to 1801 and under Hōdō, and he founded the Kangien academy in 1801.

nodes.label: Hokai
nodes.summary: Hokai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.

nodes.label: Masao Abe
variants: Masao Abe (阿部 正雄, Abe Masao)
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist, professor in religious studies
nodes.summary: Masao Abe (1915–2006) specialized in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia, and held professorships at Kyoto Women's University, Otani University, Kyoto University, and Nara University.

nodes.label: Alberto Todeschini
nodes.summary: Alberto Todeschini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has held posts as a guest at Kyoto University and at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Sojo Hirano
nodes.summary: Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996). He taught Sonja Arntzen and Yoel Hoffmann.

nodes.id: I:Research Institute of Soto Zen Studies
nodes.label: Research Institute of Soto Zen Studies
Xuesong Zhang
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Xuesong Zhang earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008). In 2015, Zhang held an attested post as associate professor at Renmin University of China.

nodes.label: Hsing Yun
nodes.summary: Hsing Yun studied at Tianning Temple, Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy, and Taiwan Buddhist Academy under Zhikai, Ruoshun, and Yinshun. A Buddhist leader, he founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as abbot (~1967–1985), and held posts at Baita Elementary, Huazang Temple, and Chinese Culture University.

nodes.label: Fo Guang Shan
variants: Fo Guang Shan Buddhist monastic order

nodes.label: Taixu
nodes.summary: Taixu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Renshan Yang. He served as leader of Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927) and founded several institutions, including Wuchang Buddhist Institute and the World Fellowship of Buddhists.

nodes.id: I:Tohoku Society for Indology and Study of Religion
nodes.label: Tohoku Society for Indology and Study of Religion
Takao Yamagata
nodes.summary: Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (circa 1952–1960). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (circa 1969–2003) and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions.

nodes.label: Velcheru Narayana Rao
nodes.description: Indian author, critic, and literary translator
nodes.summary: Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist who studied at Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1971 and held visiting professorships at the University of Chicago and Emory University.

nodes.label: Takanobu Takahashi
nodes.summary: Takanobu Takahashi is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University. He served as associate professor at Shitennoji University (1991) and the University of Tokyo (1996, 1999–2016).

nodes.label: Tadashi Toda
nodes.summary: Tadashi Toda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

nodes.label: Kevin A. Vose
nodes.summary: Kevin A. Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Bates College and the University of Virginia, completing his doctoral studies under supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.

nodes.label: Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa
nodes.summary: A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).

台灣大學音樂學研究所

nodes.label: Esho Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Esho Yamaguchi worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and held posts at Ritsumeikan University and as a professor at Osaka University from circa 1970 to 1982.

nodes.label: Kosaku Hamada
nodes.summary: Kosaku Hamada (1881–1938) worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905), where he worked (~1909–1913) before holding a post at Kyoto University (~1913–1938).

東方文化学院東京研究所

nodes.label: Kazuo Osumi
nodes.summary: Kazuo Osumi (born 1933) is a scholar of Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held posts at Hokkaido University (1964) and Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).

nodes.label: Masatoshi Konishi
nodes.summary: Masatoshi Konishi studied at International Christian University (~1957–1961), University of Calcutta (~1961–1965), University of Tokyo (~1965–1970), and Rikkyo University (PhD 2009). A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, he taught at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

nodes.label: Toshio Yamazaki
nodes.summary: Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Hannan University, the University of Tokyo (circa 1948–1977), and Chuo University (circa 1977–1987).

nodes.label: Keinin Hayashi
nodes.summary: Keinin Hayashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and was formerly a lecturer at Waseda University.

nodes.label: Myles Dillon
nodes.description: Irish academic, historian, philologist and celticist (1900–1972)
nodes.summary: Myles Dillon worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at University College Dublin and in Europe under scholars including Osborn Bergin and Rudolf Thurneysen. He held posts at Trinity College Dublin, UCD, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and directed DIAS (1960–1968).

nodes.label: James Kenneth Powell II
nodes.summary: James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned degrees from Northwestern University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under David Tracy, David M. Knipe, Isshi Yamada, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

nodes.label: Ichiro Numata
nodes.summary: Ichiro Numata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He is attested in 2026 as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Tomomichi Nitta
nodes.summary: Tomomichi Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as full-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012) and professor at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Chang-geun Hwang
nodes.summary: Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and doctoral supervisor Morten Schlütter.

nodes.label: Changpei Luo
nodes.summary: Changpei Luo (1899–1958) was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held positions at Northwest University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Xiamen University, before serving at Peking University (~1929–1949).

nodes.label: Bruce Lincoln
nodes.summary: Bruce Lincoln is a historian of religions and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Haverford and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, he held faculty posts at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Clinton B. Seely
nodes.summary: Clinton B. Seely was an Indology scholar who held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he became Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jeffrey J. Kripal
nodes.summary: Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and the University of Chicago (~1989-1993, PhD). In ~2002, he held a chair and department headship at Rice University, which he founded in 2014.

nodes.label: Tony K. Stewart
nodes.summary: Tony K. Stewart is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011–2021).

nodes.label: Hisashi Matsumura
nodes.summary: Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and later served as an assistant professor at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Kazuo Oyamada
nodes.summary: Kazuo Oyamada is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tamagawa University from around 1970 to 1974 and held a post at Rissho University from circa 1987 to 2018.

nodes.label: Koyo Shimizu
nodes.summary: Koyo Shimizu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Sayori Tsubota
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology, Sayori Tsubota was a PhD student at Osaka University (attested 2020) and later served as a JSPS Postdoctoral Fellow (PD) at Tohoku University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Chijo Akamatsu
nodes.summary: Chijo Akamatsu was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto and at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Keijo Imperial, Ryukoku, Koyasan, Hanazono, and Yamaguchi Universities.

nodes.label: Tokuno Oda
nodes.summary: Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Junjirō Takakusu and Gaju Ikehara. He held teaching posts at Fukui Chugakko (1879–1882) and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Mokurai Shimaji
nodes.summary: Mokurai Shimaji was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Chō Sanshū. He served as Geschäftsführer at Nishi Hongan-ji (1870), founded Chiyoda Jogakuen (1888), and was the 25th head priest of Gankyo-ji (1892–1905).

nodes.label: Enryo Inoue
nodes.summary: Enryo Inoue was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He later served as a researcher there and founded Toyo University, serving as lecturer and manager.

nodes.label: Joen Imai
nodes.summary: Joen Imai is a scholar of Buddhist studies who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested in 2010 and 2026).

nodes.label: Gikyo Ito
nodes.summary: Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology, earning his doctorate at Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (assistant in 1940, lecturer in 1947, professor 1968–1972) and later at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

nodes.label: Koji Kamioka
nodes.summary: Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) studied Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara (~1957–1963). He taught as a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and was a staff member at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

nodes.label: Norihiko Uchida
nodes.summary: Norihiko Uchida worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Yutaka Ochihara and held an assistant post at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, attested in 1962.

nodes.label: Masanori Shono
nodes.summary: Masanori Shono specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Yumiko Ishihama
nodes.summary: Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from ~1980 to 1989 and held an academic post there around 1997.

nodes.label: Shinkai Sugawara
nodes.summary: Shinkai Sugawara was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (graduated 1951) and earned a doctorate from Taisho University (1991). He served as professor emeritus at Waseda University.

nodes.label: Jikai Fujiyoshi
nodes.summary: Jikai Fujiyoshi worked in Buddhist studies. He was a member at Kyoto University (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Ryodo Kudo
nodes.summary: Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a full-time lecturer at Taisho University and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University.

nodes.label: Lance E. Nelson
nodes.summary: Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986 and held a post as a professor at the University of San Diego (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Anand Venkatkrishnan
nodes.summary: Anand Venkatkrishnan specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at Columbia University in 2015 and serves as an assistant professor at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Manabu Asano
nodes.summary: Manabu Asano is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a PhD student at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020) and serves as a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

variants: アーユルヴェーダ研究会

nodes.label: Tsutomu Hatai
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Hatai worked in Indology. He served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society (attested 1987), succeeding Hiroshi Maruyama.

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Okazaki
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Okazaki is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed his PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and held posts at Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Hiroshima Prefectural Takamiya high schools (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Otoya Tanaka
nodes.summary: Indologist Otoya Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1926–1930). He later held a professorship at Chuo University from circa 1957 to 1974.

nodes.label: Kiyozo Kazama
nodes.summary: Kiyozo Kazama is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held positions at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

nodes.label: Fujio Taniguchi
nodes.summary: Fujio Taniguchi works in Buddhist, Indological, and Tibetan studies. He earned a PhD from Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa and others, and held an affiliation with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Geshe Sonam Rinchen
variants: Dge bshes bsod nams rin chen
nodes.summary: Geshe Sonam Rinchen was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, later serving as resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from 1978.

nodes.label: Kojun Saito
nodes.summary: Kojun Saito (1930–2002) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).

nodes.label: Junkei Washio
nodes.summary: Junkei Washio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied at Toyo University (~1887–1891). He later served as a professor at Toyo University and Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Miyako Notake
nodes.summary: Miyako Notake is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who has served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015 and 2026).

nodes.label: Michio Kamikawa
nodes.summary: Michio Kamikawa (1960–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1980–1988) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University from ~1998 to 2021.

nodes.label: Yoshitoyo Ohara
nodes.summary: Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Ohara held a post at Kyoto University attested in 2006 and a post at Kyoto National Museum attested in 2016.

nodes.label: Isao Nishitani
nodes.summary: Isao Nishitani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and as an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kodo Yotsuya
nodes.summary: Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Komazawa University as a master's student under Shiro Matsumoto and obtained his PhD at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Eishun Fushimi
nodes.summary: Eishun Fushimi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.

nodes.label: Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber
nodes.summary: Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at Peking University under Kemo Jin and Zhongxin Jiang, and served as Director at the University of Freiburg in 2010.

nodes.label: Taiki Mibu
nodes.summary: Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Harushige Kōzu
nodes.summary: Harushige Kōzu was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and served as professor and dean of humanities at Musashi University from 1968.

nodes.label: Toru Haneda
nodes.summary: Toru Haneda was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology who studied at Tokyo and Kyoto universities. He held multiple posts at Kyoto University (1909–1948), the Toho Gakkai (1947), and the Institute of Eastern Culture (~1947–1955).

nodes.label: Shingen Takagi
nodes.summary: Shingen Takagi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and Rissho University (PhD) under Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) at Koyasan University.

nodes.summary: Gisho Nakano, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and obtained a doctorate from Kyushu University. He served as professor and president at Koyasan University and taught at Peking University.

nodes.summary: William Roxburgh (1751–1815) worked in Indology, studying at Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Aberdeen. His posts included Madras Medical Service, Samalkot Experimental Farm, and head of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1793).

nodes.label: Ryuta Kikutani
nodes.summary: Ryuta Kikutani (born 1978) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2020), and was attested as an associate professor at Koyasan University in 2026.

nodes.label: Sonja Glauch
nodes.summary: Sonja Glauch (b. 1967) is a scholar of linguistics. She completed her Magister, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she was an Akademische Oberrätin in 2007, and held visiting professorships in Vienna and Munich.

nodes.label: Eva Tichy
nodes.summary: Eva Tichy is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg, later holding the chair of Indo-European studies at Freiburg (1993–2017).

nodes.summary: Arindam Chakrabarti, a scholar in philosophy and Indology, earned his DPhil from the University of Oxford. He taught at Delhi, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (Professor attested 2009–2014, Emeritus attested 2026), and Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Keishin Okamura
nodes.summary: Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He taught at Koyasan University (1959–1973; 2005–2009) and served as a professor at Kochi University (~1965–1995).

nodes.label: Naoji Okuyama
nodes.summary: Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies (~1980–1985) and held teaching posts (~1985–1992) at Tohoku University, later serving as a professor at Koyasan University (~1999).

nodes.label: Munenobu Sakurai
nodes.summary: Munenobu Sakurai (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University, later serving as an associate professor at Iwate University (~1994–2004) and as a professor at Tohoku University (~2005).

nodes.label: Takanori Unno
nodes.summary: Takanori Unno specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at Nagoya University, where he also served as an assistant, and later held teaching posts at Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music and Meijo University.

nodes.label: Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music
Ikko Arai
nodes.summary: Ikko Arai specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Komazawa University, supervised for his MA by Shiro Matsumoto, and studied under Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen (2004), Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

nodes.label: Tetsuhiko Shibata
nodes.summary: Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

nodes.label: Takashi Yamada
nodes.summary: Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He served as an associate professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Toru Kumeji
nodes.summary: Toru Kumeji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He has held positions at the Center for Open Humanities Data and as a senior researcher at the Humanities Information Studies Institute (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hidenaka Tanaka
nodes.summary: Hidenaka Tanaka was a linguist who studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo, Oxford, and Kyoto University. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University (1920; 1931–1946), and Kyoto Women's University (~1950–1974).

nodes.summary: Kozui Otani (1876–1948) worked in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Gakushuin, Kyoritsu Gakusha, and under Eun Maeda, served as the 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914), and founded Kojukai in 1919.

nodes.label: Yuko Kamishima
nodes.summary: Yuko Kamishima specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After studying at Indiana University, Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, Kamishima held posts at Waseda University (2006–2016) and became a professor at Ritsumeikan University in 2016.

nodes.label: Koji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1953–1957) and earned a doctorate from Bukkyo University (by 1991). He served at Bukkyo University as assistant professor (~1968–1980) and professor (~1980–2005).

nodes.label: Theophil Gubler

nodes.summary: Ikuko Tazaki works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. As of 2017, she held posts as a special researcher (特別研究員) at Otani University and as a collaborative researcher (連携研究員) at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Toshio Ando
nodes.summary: Toshio Ando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1929 to 1932. He held posts at Doho University and Otani University (circa 1949–1973).

nodes.label: Hotetsu Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Hotetsu Matsumoto specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and serves as a professor and director at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Fumio Matsuda
nodes.summary: Fumio Matsuda works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He has held posts at Komazawa University and the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Shoko Miyabayashi
nodes.summary: Shoko Miyabayashi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed his undergraduate and master's studies at Taisho University. He joined Taisho University as a lecturer in 1960 and served as Dean of Buddhist Studies from 1978 to 2002.

nodes.label: Sarah Shaw
nodes.summary: Sarah Shaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. She has held affiliations with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Lance S. Cousins
nodes.summary: Lance S. Cousins worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, Boonman Poonyathiro, and K. R. Norman. He held posts at Manchester, Oxford, and Wolfson College, and was President of the Pali Text Society (2002–2003).

nodes.label: Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay
nodes.summary: Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin and held a post at the University of Calgary, attested in 1992.

nodes.summary: Hans-Werbin Köhler was an Indology scholar who studied under Eduard Hermann and completed his doctorate under Ernst Waldschmidt.

nodes.label: Eduard Hermann
nodes.summary: Specialist in linguistics and Indology Eduard Hermann studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Jena (PhD under Berthold Delbrück). He held posts at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and Göttingen (1917–1937), joining the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1918.

nodes.label: G. P. Malalasekera
nodes.summary: G. P. Malalasekera specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede, later serving as lecturer and Dean of Oriental Studies at the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera
nodes.summary: Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS (PhD under William Stede), later heading Sanskrit at Ceylon and holding posts at Pennsylvania and Harvard.

nodes.summary: Thanon Chitkament is a researcher in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under the guidance of Vishwas D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Thích Minh Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Minh Châu was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He served as a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1953–1957) and Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University (~1964–1975).

nodes.label: Tatiana Oranskaia
nodes.summary: Tatiana Oranskaia is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968–1974) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan. She held teaching posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

nodes.label: Arthur William Ryder
nodes.summary: Arthur William Ryder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig (Ph.D. c. 1900–1901) under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) and Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (c. 1906–1938).

nodes.label: Mamata Dash
nodes.summary: Mamata Dash is a scholar in the field of Indology who completed her studies at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

nodes.label: Mark Singleton
nodes.summary: Mark Singleton is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge and studied under Elizabeth De Michelis. He has served as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Eivind Kahrs
nodes.summary: Eivind Kahrs is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge (attested 2010), and is a Council member of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Elizabeth De Michelis
nodes.summary: Elizabeth De Michelis works in religious studies and Indology. She earned an MA from SOAS and a PhD from the University of Cambridge (~1996–2001), where she was director in 2000, and held a post at Oxford.

nodes.label: Suzanne Newcombe
nodes.summary: Suzanne Newcombe is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate at Cambridge. She has held posts at the LSE, Cambridge, Inform, King's College London, and the Open University as senior lecturer in Religious Studies.

nodes.label: Gangzhun
nodes.summary: Gangzhun is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Qinghai Nationalities University until 1989, he earned a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under MA supervisor Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Jinbo Shi
nodes.summary: Jinbo Shi is a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Minzu University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under Jingru Wang, he held appointments at CASS from 1975, Minzu University, and North Minzu University.

nodes.label: Soma Thera

nodes.label: Steven Heine
nodes.summary: Steven Heine is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University, and held academic posts at Villanova, La Salle, Pennsylvania State University (~1989–1997), and Florida International University (1997).

nodes.label: Raoul Birnbaum
nodes.summary: Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He held a post at Santa Clara University (attested 2012) and served as professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017).

nodes.label: Christopher S. Queen
nodes.summary: Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. At Harvard University, he served as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lecturer on the Study of Religion (circa 1989) and lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions (attested 2013).

nodes.summary: Manfred Mayrhofer was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz. He served as an ordentlicher Professor at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

nodes.label: August Fischer
nodes.summary: August Fischer (1865–1949) was a scholar of linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1886–1889) and held a post at the University of Leipzig (~1900–1930).

nodes.label: Cyril Henry Philips
nodes.summary: Cyril Henry Philips (1912–2005) studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS. Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served as Director of SOAS from 1957 and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

nodes.label: Ying-shih Yü
nodes.summary: Ying-shih Yü was a historian, philosopher, and sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard. He held professorships at Harvard (1969), Yale (1977–1987), and Princeton (1987–2001), and served as Pro Vice-Chancellor of The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1973–1975).

nodes.label: Samuel Beal
nodes.summary: Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Trinity College, Cambridge, and Durham University. He was headmaster at Bramham College, examined Buddhist Chinese books for the India Office Records, and served as professor at University College London.

nodes.label: Cornelis Petrus Tiele
nodes.jawiki: コルネーリス・ティーレ
nodes.summary: Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) was a religious studies scholar educated at Amsterdam and the Remonstrant Seminary. He was a professor at the Remonstrant Seminary (1873) and served as professor of the history of religions at Leiden University (1877–1901).

nodes.label: Teruji Ishizu
nodes.summary: Teruji Ishizu was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tohoku University, serving as president (1963–1966), and later served as president of Miyagi University of Education and professor at Keio and Komazawa universities.

nodes.label: Ichiro Hori
nodes.summary: Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo, where he was professor emeritus (1965–1971). He also taught at Tohoku University (~1952–1965).

nodes.id: I:Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III
nodes.label: Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III
Sangye Tenzin
nodes.summary: Sangye Tenzin was a scholar and practitioner in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who served as Abbot of Menri Monastery and was attested as a doctoral student at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Geshe degree at the Dialectic School of Menri and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, later serving as its president, and was a Rockefeller Fellow at Rice University (1991).

nodes.label: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima
variants: H. H. Menri Khen Rinpoche Lungdog Denpa Nyima
nodes.summary: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (1927–2017) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso and earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery. He founded Menri Monastery, serving as its abbot from 1969.

nodes.label: Geshe Tshondru Kongpel
nodes.summary: Geshe Tshondru Kongpel was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his Geshe studies at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

nodes.label: Rice University
variants: Center for Cultural Studies, Rice University
Center for Cultural Studies at Rice University

nodes.label: Kongojushinkai
variants: 社会福祉法人金剛樹心会

nodes.label: Hermann Hirt
nodes.summary: Hermann Hirt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg and Leipzig. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig (1891–1912) before becoming a professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Giessen (1912–1936).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Streitberg
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Streitberg worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Münster, Leipzig (under Karl Brugmann and Ernst Windisch), and Berlin. He held posts at Fribourg (~1889–1898), Münster (1899), Munich (~1909–1920), and Leipzig (1898, 1920–1925).

nodes.id: I:Directorate of Archaeology, Archives and Museums, Madhya Pradesh
nodes.label: Directorate of Archaeology, Archives and Museums, Madhya Pradesh
variants: Department of Archaeology, Museums and Archives in Madhya Pradesh

nodes.label: Karl Benedikt Hase
nodes.summary: Karl Benedikt Hase (1780–1864) was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at Jena and Helmstedt. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (1816–1864), and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

nodes.label: Erich Haenisch
variants: エーリヒ・ヘーニシュ
nodes.jawiki: エーリヒ・ヘーニシュ
nodes.summary: Erich Haenisch was a sinologist, Iranian/Central Asian scholar, and Tibetologist who studied under Wilhelm Grube at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at the universities of Göttingen, Leipzig, Berlin, and Munich.

nodes.label: Chhime Rigdzing
nodes.summary: Chhime Rigdzing specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Saraswathi Mahal Library
variants: Thanjavur Maharaja Serfoji's Saraswathi Mahal Library

nodes.label: Jack Goody
nodes.summary: Jack Goody worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at St Albans School and St John's College (~1946–1954), and later served as a professor at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1984).

nodes.label: S. N. Savadi
nodes.summary: An Indologist, S. N. Savadi held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, with affiliations attested in 1953 and 1969.

nodes.label: Sao Htun Hmat Win
nodes.summary: Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhaddanta Narada and at Harvard University. He taught at the University of Rangoon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

nodes.id: I:International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies
nodes.label: International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies

nodes.label: Subhash Kak
nodes.image: Subhash Kak at Single Photon Workshop, Geneva, July 2015.jpg
nodes.summary: Subhash Kak, active in Indology and other fields, studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under P. V. Indiresan. He held professorships at Louisiana State University (1979) and Oklahoma State University (2007).

nodes.label: Robert B. Ekvall
nodes.description: missionary, explorer, ethnographer, curator of Asian ethnology (1898-1983)
nodes.summary: Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) was a Tibetologist who held posts at the University of Chicago (~1953–1956), the University of Washington (1958), and the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (~1963–1978).

nodes.label: Tübingen University Library
variants: テュービンゲン大学図書館

nodes.label: Christopher Wallis
nodes.summary: Christopher Wallis is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Rochester, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt. He was a guest lecturer at Naropa University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Peri Sarveswara Sharma
nodes.summary: Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Wilhelm Rau (~1966–1971) and held a post at the University of Marburg (~1971–1991).

nodes.label: Karl Richard Lepsius
nodes.jawiki: カール・リヒャルト・レプシウス
nodes.summary: Karl Richard Lepsius worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin, he held a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1846–1884) and served as Chief Librarian at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1873–1884).

nodes.id: I:Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland
nodes.label: Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland
variants: Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland

nodes.label: John Myrdhin Reynolds
nodes.summary: John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche (circa 1971–1987), Namkhai Norbu (circa 1979), and Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak.

nodes.label: Johannes Rahder
nodes.summary: Johannes Rahder worked in Indology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earning a doctorate at Utrecht (~1920–1926). He held posts at Utrecht (professor, 1930–1931), Leiden (chair of Japanese, 1931–1946), and Yale (professor, 1947–1965).

nodes.label: Paul Tedesco
nodes.summary: Paul Tedesco was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied philology at the University of Vienna (1916–1921), held a post at Princeton (~1938–1944), and served as a professor at Yale University (1952–1966).

nodes.label: Rulon Wells
nodes.summary: Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and held a long-term academic post at Yale University (~1945–1989).

nodes.label: Walter Clawiter
nodes.description: born:1923|died:1970|; Clawiter, Walter 1923-1970; Clawiter; Clawiter, Walter ....-1970; Clawiter, Walter, m. 1970

nodes.label: Zhihua Yao
nodes.summary: Zhihua Yao works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After completing a PhD under Malcolm David Eckel at Boston University (~1997–2002), Yao served as Professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005) and Associate Professor at CUHK (~2005).

nodes.label: Ronald Inden
nodes.summary: Ronald Inden is an Indologist and historian who taught Daud Ali. He spent his career at the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he is Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2026).

nodes.label: C. M. Naim
nodes.summary: C. M. Naim was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1957 to 1960. He spent his career at the University of Chicago from around 1961 to 2001, becoming Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: John D. Kelly
nodes.summary: John D. Kelly is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He holds a career at the University of Chicago (attested 2007, 2026), where he serves as Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and Social Sciences.

nodes.label: Christopher Pinney
nodes.image: The President, Shri Pranab Mukherjee presenting the Padma Shri Award to Prof. Christopher Pinney, at an Investiture Ceremony-II, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on April 20, 2013.jpg
nodes.summary: Christopher Pinney is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He has held academic posts at the Australian National University, University College London as professor of anthropology and visual culture, University of Chicago, Northwestern University, University of Cape Town, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

nodes.label: Godabarish Mishra
nodes.summary: Godabarish Mishra was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Ravenshaw College (~1906–1910) and the University of Calcutta (~1910–1912). He taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and directed at the University of Madras.

nodes.id: I:B.J. Institute of Learning and Research
nodes.label: B.J. Institute of Learning and Research
variants: B. J. Institute of Learning and Research

nodes.label: Swami Siddheswarananda
nodes.summary: Swami Siddheswarananda was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras and held a post with the Ramakrishna Order from circa 1920 to 1957.

nodes.label: K. Srinivasan
nodes.summary: K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College. He also held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

nodes.label: Khammai Dhammasami
nodes.image: ၸဝ်ႈၶူးလူင်ထမ်ႇမသႃႇမိ.jpg
nodes.summary: Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000–2004). He served as a professor at ITBMU (~2003) and as Fellow and Trustee at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (~2004).

nodes.label: Volker Grabowsky
nodes.summary: Volker Grabowsky studied at Kiel University and Chiang Mai University. A historian, he held posts at the University of Passau, National University of Laos, University of Münster, and the University of Hamburg, where he became chair professor in 2009.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Guthrie
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Canterbury in 1994 and served as a tutor in religious studies at the University of Otago (~2006).

nodes.label: Peter Gyallay-Pap
nodes.summary: Peter Gyallay-Pap works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the London School of Economics by 1990 and was an adjunct at Adams State University (attested 2007).

variants: ロンドン・スクール・オブ・エコノミクス
