London School of Economics and Political Science
ロンドン大学経済政治学院（LSE）

nodes.label: Ian Harris
nodes.summary: Ian Harris (1952–2014) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge and Lancaster University. He taught at St Martin's College (~1986–2007) and served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Cumbria (~2007–2014).

nodes.label: University of Cumbria
variants: University College of St. Martin, Lancaster

nodes.label: Peter Koret
nodes.summary: Peter Koret works in Buddhist studies and related fields. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Hugo David
nodes.summary: Hugo David is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2012. He held a fellowship at the University of Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of EFEO in 2015.

nodes.label: Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi
nodes.summary: Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields, having studied under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit, with PhDs from Central Sanskrit University and National Sanskrit University. He held posts at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, Pondicherry, Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

nodes.label: N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya
nodes.summary: N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya specialized in Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice Chancellor of National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and was a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1994–2017).

nodes.label: Stewart McFarlane
nodes.summary: Stewart McFarlane works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held posts in the Department of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (attested 1991 and 2001).

nodes.label: Bret W. Davis
nodes.summary: Bret W. Davis specializes in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, held research posts at Kyoto and Otani, and served as a philosophy professor at Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).

nodes.label: Masakatsu Fujita
nodes.summary: Masakatsu Fujita (b. 1949) specializes in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1968–1978), where he later headed the Department of the History of Japanese Philosophy (~2001–2014).

nodes.label: Jake H. Davis
nodes.summary: Jake H. Davis is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Marlboro College, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the CUNY Graduate Center. He has taught at Brown University (attested 2013–2018) and held appointments at NYU and BCBS.

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Pandita
nodes.native: ဆရာတော် ဦးပဏ္ဍိတ
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Pandita (1921–2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw. He served as a meditation teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeding Mahasi Sayadaw (1982–1991), and founded Panditarama Meditation Center, serving as abbot.

nodes.label: William Edelglass
nodes.summary: William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held teaching posts at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and served as a visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

nodes.label: Alan Fox
nodes.summary: Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his PhD from Temple University, he taught at the University of Delaware as professor (1992) and associate professor of philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

nodes.label: Marc Tiefenauer
nodes.summary: Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2016 under the doctoral supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

nodes.label: Christine Chojnacki
nodes.summary: Christine Chojnacki specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and served as professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Emi Matsushita
nodes.summary: Historian Emi Matsushita earned a BA from Nanzan University, a diploma from the University of East Anglia, and an MA from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts with the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State.

nodes.label: University of East Anglia
variants: Sainsbury Institute for the Study of Japanese Arts and Cultures (SISJAC), University of East Anglia
イースト・アングリア大学

nodes.label: G. B. Palsule
nodes.summary: G. B. Palsule was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Martine Kropman
nodes.summary: Martine Kropman is an Indology scholar. She conducted doctoral research at the University of Groningen and is an external PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop as of 2026.

nodes.label: Dale S. Wright
nodes.summary: Dale S. Wright (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann, and served as a professor at Occidental College from around 1980 to 2017.

nodes.label: Sarah Lawrence College
variants: サラ・ローレンス大学

nodes.label: Michel Mohr
nodes.summary: Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. His posts include the University of Geneva (1987–1992), Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (attested 2008–2012).

nodes.label: Mario Poceski
nodes.summary: Mario Poceski works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at UCLA (2000) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held posts at the University of Iowa (2001) and the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

nodes.label: David E. Riggs
nodes.summary: David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from UCLA. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and was a researcher at Nichibunken (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Albert Welter
nodes.summary: Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at McMaster University (~1980–1986) under Koichi Shinohara, Yün-hua Jan, and Ryosho Tanaka. He held posts at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2013) and the University of Arizona (2013).

nodes.label: Anthony Tribe
nodes.summary: Anthony Tribe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Steven Collins, and Paul Williams. He held posts at Montana and Arizona.

nodes.label: John Nemec
nodes.summary: John Nemec is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn (PhD, 2005) under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher, he is an Associate Professor at the University of Virginia (attested 2020–2026).

nodes.label: Zenno Ikuno
nodes.summary: Zenno Ikuno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Elke Rogersdotter
nodes.summary: Elke Rogersdotter works in history/archaeology and Indology. She earned her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006) under doctoral supervisor Thomas B. Larsson, supervisor Bozena Werbart, and co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.

nodes.label: Vasant Shinde
nodes.summary: Vasant Shinde is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who held posts as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer
nodes.description: American Archaeologist, worked on the Indus Valley Civilization sites and other places in South Asia
nodes.summary: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is an archaeologist and Indologist. After attending Woodstock School, he earned his BA from the University of California, Berkeley, and joined the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he became Professor of Anthropology circa 1985.

nodes.label: German Archaeological Institute
variants: Abteilung Istanbul des Deutschen Archäologischen Instituts

nodes.label: Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne
nodes.summary: Scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne studied at the University of Ceylon (BA 1952) and University of London (PhD ~1956). He taught at the University of Ceylon (1952–1973) and served as professor and dean at Kelaniya.

nodes.label: David Friedman
nodes.summary: David Friedman (1903–1984) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies philosopher. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS, University of London (~1950–1970) and was attested as Professor at the University of London in 1969.

nodes.label: Jing Yin
nodes.summary: Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995) and served as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

nodes.label: Hisayoshi Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Hisayoshi Miyamoto is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. He has held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi
nodes.summary: Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya in Indology and religious studies. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidasa Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Steven Edward Lindquist
nodes.summary: Steven Edward Lindquist works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2005 under Patrick Olivelle, alongside several traditional teachers, and held a post at Concordia University.

nodes.label: Matthew R. Sayers
nodes.summary: Matthew R. Sayers earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008) in Indology and religious studies. He held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Rosalind O'Hanlon
nodes.summary: Rosalind O'Hanlon is an Indologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. from SOAS (~1977–1982). She was an Emeritus Fellow at Clare College, Cambridge (~1983), and served as Professor in Indian History and Culture at Oxford (~2001–2015).

nodes.label: Juhyung Rhi
nodes.summary: Juhyung Rhi specializes in Buddhist studies, art history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, Rhi became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University in 1992.

nodes.label: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
nodes.summary: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales was an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at Cambridge and SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden, he held positions at King's College Bangkok, the Greater India Society (~1934-1941), and the Royal Asiatic Society (1964-1968).

nodes.label: Tej Ram Sharma
nodes.summary: Tej Ram Sharma is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Travis L. Smith
nodes.summary: Travis L. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley under Vasudha Dalmia, Robert P. Goldman, and Sally J. Sutherland Goldman, and earned his PhD at Columbia University under John Stratton Hawley in 2007, later lecturing at UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: David Max Moerman
nodes.summary: David Max Moerman is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held academic posts at Barnard College and Columbia University, serving as professor and department chair.

nodes.label: Vasudha Dalmia
nodes.description: professor of Hindi and Modern South Asian Studies
nodes.summary: Vasudha Dalmia (born 1947) is an Indologist and historian educated at Miranda House, Cologne, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Heidelberg. She lectured at Tübingen and served as the Magistretti Distinguished Professor at UC Berkeley (2001–2012) and Tandon Professor at Yale (2013–2014).

nodes.label: Bisheshwar Nath Reu
nodes.summary: Bisheshwar Nath Reu studied under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha and worked in Indology and archaeology. He served at the Sumer Public Library (attested 1933) and headed the Government Museum Jodhpur and the Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre.

nodes.label: C. S. Srinivasachariar
nodes.summary: C. S. Srinivasachariar was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932-1933).

nodes.id: I:R. D. and D. J. College
nodes.label: R. D. and D. J. College
Haridas Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Haridas Bhattacharyya studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. In philosophy and religious studies, he held posts at Scottish Church College (1915), University of Calcutta (1917), University of Dhaka (1921), and Banaras Hindu University (1947).

nodes.label: T. N. Ramachandran
nodes.summary: T. N. Ramachandran (1901–1973) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (c. 1925–1934) and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

nodes.label: Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Presidency, Allahabad, Calcutta, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit universities under Ganganatha Jha, he served as professor at the University of Allahabad (1924–1956) and directed the Research Institute at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Sonam Kachru
nodes.summary: Sonam Kachru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold and held posts including at the Max Planck Institute before becoming Assistant Professor at Yale University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kashinath Trimbak Telang
nodes.description: Indian judge, Indologist, writer and translator (1850–1893)
nodes.summary: Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indologist who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served as a fellow at Elphinstone College, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1892–1893), and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

nodes.label: Mahesh A. Deokar
nodes.summary: Mahesh A. Deokar works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He has served as Professor and Head at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2011–2021) and as Regional Representative for the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

nodes.id: I:Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
nodes.label: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
variants: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies

nodes.label: Lawrence J. McCrea
nodes.summary: Lawrence J. McCrea is an Indologist, philosopher, and linguist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. He serves as a Professor at Cornell University (attested 2026) and taught Whitney Cox and James McHugh.

nodes.label: Anne E. Monius
nodes.summary: Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She earned her undergraduate and graduate degrees at Harvard University, studying under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart, and taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard (from 2002).

nodes.label: Jayashree D. Sathe
nodes.summary: Jayashree D. Sathe is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who served as editor in chief and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: Lawrence E. Sullivan
nodes.summary: Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar in religious studies and history and archaeology. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as Professor in the Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Joseph M. Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Joseph M. Kitagawa was a scholar of religion, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Joachim Wach. He spent his career at the University of Chicago from 1951, serving as Dean of the Divinity School.

nodes.id: I:Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing
nodes.label: Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing
variants: 島根県立国際短期大学

nodes.label: Shoshun Hayashidera
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, Hayashidera has held posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and Hokkaido University, where he is a professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hirotomo Teranishi
variants: Teranishi Hirotomo 寺西 宏友
nodes.summary: Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as director at Soka University (attested 2010–2012).

nodes.label: Herbert Härtel
nodes.summary: Herbert Härtel specialized in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1953–1986), directed the Museum of Asian Art (1963–1986), and taught at Freie Universität Berlin (1965–1986).

nodes.label: Annette L. Heitmann
nodes.summary: Annette L. Heitmann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Vienna, studying under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg.

nodes.label: Eshin Nishimura
nodes.summary: Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Hanazono University, under Zenkei Shibayama, at Pendle Hill Quaker Center, and at Kyoto University. He taught at Carleton College and served as director at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Ensho Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Ensho Kobayashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Hanazono University, where he is attested as a professor in 1988 and as professor emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: Henri Cordier
nodes.image: Gustave Caillebotte - Henri Cordier - Google Art Project.jpg
nodes.description: French linguist, historian, ethnographer, author, editor and Orientalist (1849–1925)
nodes.summary: Henri Cordier was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and at Sciences Po (~1886–1925).

nodes.label: Noël Peri
nodes.summary: Noël Peri worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He taught Western music at Tokyo University of the Arts (1896–1906) and served as a resident and secretary-librarian at the École française d'Extrême-Orient starting in 1907 and 1911.

nodes.label: Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises
variants: ベルギー中國學高等研究所
パリ大學中國學高等研究所

nodes.label: Gaston Renondeau
variants: ガストン・ルノンドー
nodes.image: Major Gaston Renondeau - Allied missions at Vladivostock LCCN2014708663 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Gaston Renondeau (1879–1967) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique circa 1899–1901.

nodes.label: Marcel Granet
nodes.summary: Marcel Granet (1884–1940) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises.

nodes.label: Étienne Balazs
variants: エティエンヌ・バラ―シュ
エティエンヌ・バラーシュ
nodes.summary: Étienne Balazs, a Sinologist and historian, earned his doctorate under Otto Franke (1923–1930). He was a research director at the CNRS from 1949 and served as professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).

nodes.label: Otto Franke
nodes.summary: Sinologist and Indologist Otto Franke studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held the inaugural chair of Chinese Language and Culture at Hamburg/Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut (1910–1923) and was Professor of Sinology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1923–1931).

nodes.label: Jacques Gernet
nodes.summary: Jacques Gernet was a sinologist and historian who studied at Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at CNRS, EPHE, the University of Paris, EFEO, Paris Diderot University (~1970–1973), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

nodes.label: André Bareau
nodes.summary: André Bareau (1921–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the École normale d'Auteuil, Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France, supervised by Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at CNRS, EPHE, Collège de France, and Institut de civilisation indienne.

nodes.label: Bernard Frank
variants: ベルナール・フランク
nodes.summary: Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He held posts at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and served as chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

nodes.label: Michel Soymié
nodes.summary: Michel Soymié was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at INALCO (~1948–1952) and held positions at the CNRS, EFEO, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he held a chair from ~1966 to 1992.

nodes.id: I:Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Sezione di Studi Orientali
nodes.label: Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Sezione di Studi Orientali
Kenji Shimada
nodes.summary: Kenji Shimada was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1938 to 1941 and later held a research post there from circa 1949 to 1981.

nodes.label: Atsushi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa (b. 1951) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Joseph E. Schwartzberg
nodes.summary: Joseph E. Schwartzberg was a scholar of Indology and history who studied at Brooklyn College, the University of Maryland, the Sorbonne, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hartshorne. He served as professor at the University of Minnesota from 1964 to 2000.

nodes.label: Julia Leslie
nodes.summary: Julia Leslie was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. She founded and held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1992 to 2004.

nodes.label: Palmira Brummett
nodes.summary: Palmira Brummett specializes in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at the University of Chicago and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, later serving at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011) and Brown University (2011–2016).

nodes.label: Robin Coningham
nodes.summary: Robin Coningham is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at King's College and the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin. He held posts at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (appointed 2005).

nodes.label: Ryuo
nodes.summary: Ryuo (1856–1926) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He taught at Koyasan University and served as an educator at Tō-ji.

nodes.label: Friedrich Hirth
nodes.summary: Friedrich Hirth (1845–1927) worked in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald, and served with the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) before becoming Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University (1902).

nodes.label: William Woodville Rockhill
variants: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.summary: William Woodville Rockhill (1854–1914) was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Lycée Condorcet and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr, and studied under Léon Feer and Philippe Édouard Foucaux (~1877–1883).

nodes.label: Phra Brahmapundit
nodes.native: พระพรหมบัณฑิต
nodes.summary: Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He has served as Abbot of Wat Prayurawongsawat (c. 1996), Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (c. 1997–2018), and President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (c. 2007).

nodes.label: Abaji Vishnu Kathavate
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, Abaji Vishnu Kathavate succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and is attested as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2026.

nodes.label: M. H. Krishna
nodes.image: Portrait photograph of M. H. Krishna.jpg
nodes.summary: M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) studied at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner. An Indologist and historian, he served as Professor and dean at the University of Mysore and department head at Maharaja's College.

nodes.id: I:Department of Archaeology, National Museum and National Library
nodes.label: Department of Archaeology, National Museum and National Library
Geoffrey Samuel
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Samuel earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach, Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, and Peter J. Wilson. He held professorships at the University of Newcastle, Lancaster University, and Cardiff University.

nodes.label: University of Newcastle
variants: University of Newcastle, New South Wales

nodes.label: Sandra Bell
nodes.summary: Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and also held a post at the same institution.

nodes.label: Jules Oppert
variants: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.jawiki: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.summary: Jules Oppert was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who earned his PhD from Kiel University. He taught at INALCO, the University of Paris, and the Collège de France, where he was a professor from 1874 to 1905.

nodes.label: R. Venkatraman
nodes.summary: R. Venkatraman is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under doctoral supervisors N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, and served as a reader there (attested 1990).

nodes.label: Kamil Václav Zvelebil
nodes.summary: Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from Charles University. He held posts at the Czech Oriental Institute, Charles University, University of Chicago, Heidelberg University, Collège de France, and Utrecht University.

nodes.label: V. Kameswari
nodes.summary: V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she has served as an Editorial Committee member and research supervisor.

nodes.label: K. S. Balasubramanian
nodes.summary: K. S. Balasubramanian works in Indology and philosophy. He has served at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Director (attested 2026).

nodes.label: T. V. Vasudeva
nodes.summary: T. V. Vasudeva works in Indology and philosophy and taught S. N. Krishna. He served on the Editorial Committee (attested 2001) and later as Deputy Director (attested 2026) at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

nodes.label: Ralph Lilley Turner
nodes.description: Indic languages philologist and university administrator (1888–1983)
nodes.summary: Ralph Lilley Turner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1907-1913). He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (1920-1922) and the University of London (~1922-1957), where he also served as Director of SOAS (1922-1957).

nodes.label: Harold Walter Bailey
variants: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.jawiki: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.summary: Harold Walter Bailey was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguistics. He studied at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under Frederick William Thomas. He taught at SOAS before holding the Sanskrit chair at Cambridge University (1936–1967).

nodes.label: Bernhard Breloer
nodes.summary: Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist who served as a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1935–1945), where he succeeded Heinrich Lüders.

nodes.id: I:Research Institute of Nichiren Buddhist Studies, Rissho University
nodes.label: Research Institute of Nichiren Buddhist Studies, Rissho University
variants: 立正大学日蓮教学研究所
立正大日蓮教学研究所

nodes.label: Gensho Imanari
nodes.summary: Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) studied at Waseda University (circa 1945–1951, PhD 1983). Working in Japanology and Buddhist studies, he served as assistant professor at Kokushikan University (circa 1965–1970) and professor emeritus at Rissho University (1980–1996).

nodes.label: Gyoshu Chojo
nodes.summary: Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Masumi Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Minobusan University as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhism (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and specially appointed professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kanji Tamura
nodes.summary: Kanji Tamura (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Rissho University, including as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yukio Kotani
nodes.summary: Yukio Kotani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. Kotani served as professor emeritus of comparative literature at Rissho University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Theosophical Society
variants: Kyoto branch of the Theosophical Society

nodes.label: Surama Dasgupta
nodes.summary: Surama Dasgupta was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Surendranath Dasgupta, earning degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge. She served as Reader in the Philosophy Department at the University of Lucknow.

nodes.label: Hofstra University
variants: Department of Philosophy at Hofstra University

nodes.label: University of Luxembourg
variants: Department of Philosophy at the University of Luxembourg

nodes.label: Vitus Angermeier
nodes.summary: Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. He holds a post as Lecturer at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Friedhelm Hardy
nodes.summary: Friedhelm Hardy was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Oxford. He served as Wilde Lecturer at Oxford and as Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London.

nodes.label: A. N. Narasimhia
nodes.summary: Active in linguistics and Indology, he completed his PhD under Ralph Lilley Turner at SOAS (~1930–1933). He held appointments at the University of Mysore, including as librarian and part-time professor of philology at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

nodes.label: Heinrich Hettrich
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hettrich (1947–2020) was a linguist and Indologist educated at Saarland, Giessen, and Munich. He held posts at Saarland, Munich, and Marburg before becoming Chair of Comparative Linguistics at the University of Würzburg in 1989.

nodes.label: Sylvain Brocquet
nodes.summary: Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1980) under Marie-Claude Porcher, and held a post at Aix-Marseille University.

nodes.label: Aix-Marseille University
variants: エクス＝マルセイユ大学

nodes.label: Bard College
variants: Institute of Advanced Theology, Bard College

nodes.label: Albert Lutz
nodes.description: Swiss art historian, director Museum Rietberg
nodes.summary: Albert Lutz is a scholar of Sinology and archaeology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer (~1974–1982) and had a long career at Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art (1982) and director (1998–2019).

nodes.label: Christoph Cüppers
nodes.summary: Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler. He served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute from circa 1993 to 2013.

nodes.label: Christopher Key Chapple
nodes.summary: Christopher Key Chapple works in Indology and religious studies. He served as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982) and held the Doshi Professorship of Indic and Comparative Theology at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

nodes.label: Bloomfield College
variants: Bloomfield College of Montclair State University

nodes.label: Radha Krishna Choudhary
nodes.summary: Radha Krishna Choudhary (1921–1985) studied history at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University. An Indologist and historian, he founded the K. P. Jayaswal Archaeological Museum, headed history at Ganesh Dutt College, and taught at Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University (1974–1984).

nodes.label: Scindia Oriental Institute
variants: Scindia Oriental Institute at Vikram University, Ujjain

nodes.label: Edwin Whitfield Fay
nodes.summary: Edwin Whitfield Fay studied at Rhodes College and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve. A linguist and Indologist, he taught at Washington and Lee University (1893–1899) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 1899).

nodes.label: Rhodes College
variants: South-Western Presbyterian University of Clarksville, Tennessee

nodes.label: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve
nodes.summary: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He was a professor of Greek at the University of Virginia and later taught at Johns Hopkins University.

nodes.label: John Henry Wright
nodes.image: John Henry Wright young age photo.jpg
nodes.summary: Wright worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studying at Dartmouth College and the University of Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, Harvard (circa 1887–1908), and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens.

nodes.label: Herbert Weir Smyth
nodes.summary: Herbert Weir Smyth was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology. He studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe. His academic posts included Bryn Mawr College (1887–1901) and Harvard University, starting as Eliot Professor in 1901.

nodes.label: Minton Warren
nodes.summary: Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist who studied under William Dwight Whitney at Yale and earned a Dr. phil. from Strasbourg. He held professorships at Johns Hopkins (1879–1899) and Harvard (1899), and directed the American Academy in Rome.

nodes.label: James Wilson Bright
nodes.summary: James Wilson Bright (1852–1926) was a linguist who studied at Lafayette College (~1871–1875) and earned his PhD from Johns Hopkins (~1879–1882). He taught at Cornell (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins (1905–1925).

nodes.label: Yukio Yamanaka
nodes.summary: Yukio Yamanaka specializes in Indology and linguistics. Yamanaka was a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Eisaku Okada
nodes.summary: Eisaku Okada, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and held posts at the JSPS (attested 2014), Kyoto University (attested 2015), and Koyasan University (attested 2014 and 2026).

nodes.label: Huanhuan He
nodes.summary: Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhejiang University, the University of Tokyo (attested 2015), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yukihiko Matsumura
nodes.summary: Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and later worked there as a specialist researcher (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Chizan Denbo-in
variants: 真言宗智山派智山伝法院

nodes.label: Hiroshi Tokushige
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Tokushige is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Koyasan University as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and special appointment lecturer (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Davaadorj Purevdorj
variants: ダワードルジ・プルプドルジ

nodes.label: Kaie Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Kaie Mochizuki (b. 1959) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has served as professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and university president (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.

nodes.label: Tomoko Makidono
nodes.summary: Tomoko Makidono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She was a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2015) and a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jianming Hu
nodes.summary: Jianming Hu works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a researcher post at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Soto Zen Research Center
variants: 曹洞宗総合研究センター

nodes.label: Hideyuki Matsumori
nodes.summary: Hideyuki Matsumori works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Soka University (attested 2006), where he later held posts as an assistant professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yongyu Chen
nodes.summary: Yongyu Chen works in Buddhist studies. Educated with a BA from Cornell and as a PhD student at Harvard, Chen served as a professor at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015) and an ArtTable Fellow at Public Art Fund (2025).

nodes.label: Shinran Buddhist Center
variants: 真宗大谷派親鸞仏教センター

nodes.label: Hirotaka Kato
nodes.summary: Hirotaka Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post as a research assistant at Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and an associate professorship at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha
variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派学院

nodes.label: Zijie Li
nodes.summary: Zijie Li works in Buddhist studies. Li studied at Komazawa University and served as a JSPS DC research fellow, both attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Siegfried Lienhard
nodes.summary: Siegfried Lienhard was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna and completed his Habilitation at Stockholm University. He held professorships at Kiel University (1962–1968) and Stockholm University (1968–1990).

nodes.label: Paul Fredericq
nodes.description: historian, teacher, professor and rector from Belgium (1850-1920)
nodes.summary: Paul Fredericq was a historian who studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Voskenslaan, Ghent University, and the University of Liège (~1868–1875). He was a professor at Liège (~1879–1883) and Ghent University (from 1883), where he became Rektor in 1919.

nodes.label: Kisari Mohan Ganguli
nodes.summary: Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indology scholar who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was an Indology scholar. He studied at Sanskrit College and University (~1853–1857) and Presidency University (~1857–1860), later holding posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

nodes.label: Michael Hutt
nodes.description: Professor of Nepali and Himalayan Studies
nodes.summary: Michael Hutt (born 1957) is an Indologist and linguist who completed his BA and doctorate at the University of London. He spent his career at SOAS University of London, serving as Department Head and Associate Dean.

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Mizuno
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Mizuno specializes in Indology and linguistics. After graduating from Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Toyo Bunko, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

nodes.label: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri
nodes.summary: An Indology and philosophy scholar, S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was affiliated with the University of Madras, where he served as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

nodes.label: R. Balasubramanian
nodes.summary: R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri (attested 1988) and served as Director at the University of Madras from around 1978 to 1989.

nodes.label: Siran Upendra Deraniyagala
nodes.summary: Siran Upendra Deraniyagala was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London under Frank Raymond Allchin, and Harvard University. He was Director General of Sri Lanka's Department of Archaeology (~1992–2001).

nodes.label: Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka
variants: Archaeological Survey Department of the Government of Sri Lanka

nodes.label: Tse-fu Kuan
nodes.summary: Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich in 2004. He conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University and held a post at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Alexander Yiannopoulos
nodes.summary: Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and with teachers including Karin Myers, Sherab Sangpo, Khenpo Sherab Dorje, Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Tom Tillemans, John J. Makransky, William S. Waldron, Jay L. Garfield, Douglas S. Duckworth, and Sara L. McClintock.

nodes.label: Yao Wang
nodes.summary: Yao Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and sinology who studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku. Wang held a post as guest professor at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Tibet Academy of Social Sciences
variants: チベット社会科学アカデミー

nodes.id: I:Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
nodes.label: Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
variants: Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau

nodes.label: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski
nodes.summary: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski studied Indology at Banaras Hindu University, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Oxford, completing his PhD (~1975–1979) under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson alongside study with traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Susan J. Rosenfield
nodes.summary: Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004. Her teachers included Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, Kausalya Hart, Shaligram Shukla, Saudamani Deshmukh, James W. Benson, and Thomas Burke.

nodes.label: Bhagavan Das
nodes.summary: Bhagavan Das was an Indologist and philosopher who earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He founded Banaras Hindu University and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith, serving as headmaster of the latter and Honorary Secretary at Central Hindu College.

nodes.label: Priyavrat Sharma
nodes.summary: Priyavrat Sharma was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. His career included serving as Director at Banaras Hindu University, including its Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine.

nodes.label: John W. Spellman
nodes.summary: John W. Spellman (1934–2021) was an Indologist and historian. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (circa 1964–1967) and the University of Windsor (circa 1967–1999).

nodes.label: Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri
nodes.summary: Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri was an Indologist and linguist who served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1991 and 2026).

nodes.label: Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi
nodes.summary: Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University and under Mohammad Habib. He held posts at Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, and was a reader at Australian National University (1967–1986).

nodes.label: Karl Ammer
nodes.summary: Karl Ammer (1911–1970) worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the University of Vienna from circa 1930 to 1935. From circa 1955 to 1970, he served as Director of the Institute of Indology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.

nodes.label: Palace Museum
variants: Institute of Tibetan Cultural Heritage, Palace Museum, Beijing

nodes.id: I:Zhejiang Provincial Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology
nodes.label: Zhejiang Provincial Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology
Jinhua Jia
nodes.summary: Jinhua Jia is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll and Yunji Chen. Jia has held posts at CU Boulder, Harvard, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

nodes.label: International Christian University

国際基督教大学教養学部人文学科

nodes.label: Needham Research Institute
variants: Needham Institute for the History of Science and Technology in East Asia

nodes.label: Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under several teachers, including Gopinath Bhattacharya and Madhusudana Nyāyācārya, and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1969–1974).

nodes.label: Ram Karan Sharma
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned his MA at Patna University and his PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He served as vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974-1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984-1985).

nodes.label: Gyatsho Tshering
nodes.summary: Gyatsho Tshering was a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its acting director in 1972 and director from 1974 to 1998.

nodes.label: Gudrun Melzer
nodes.summary: Gudrun Melzer is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. By 2026, she held research posts at the Göttingen Academy, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Munich.

nodes.label: Annemarie Schimmel
nodes.summary: Annemarie Schimmel studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Marburg under Hans Heinrich Schaeder and Friedrich Heiler. She held professorships at the University of Marburg, Ankara University, and Harvard University.

nodes.id: I:D. G. Ruparel College of Arts, Science and Commerce
nodes.label: D. G. Ruparel College of Arts, Science and Commerce
Ibrahim Shah
nodes.summary: Ibrahim Shah is an archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Peshawar in 2007. He serves as Associate Professor and Chairman of the Department of Cultural Heritage and Tourism Management at Hazara University.

nodes.label: Ihsan Ali
nodes.summary: Ihsan Ali is an archaeology and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin. He was a professor at Peshawar, director of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's archaeology directorate, and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009).

nodes.label: Pratapaditya Pal
nodes.summary: Pratapaditya Pal is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and Cambridge. He served as a curator at the MFA Boston, LACMA, and the Art Institute of Chicago.

nodes.label: Gouriswar Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Gouriswar Bhattacharya was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served on the faculty as a Lehrbeauftragter at the Free University of Berlin from approximately 1974 to 1993.

nodes.label: Charles Burnett
nodes.summary: Charles Burnett (1951–) works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. After earning his BA and doctorate at the University of Cambridge, he held research positions before serving as lecturer and professor (from 1999) at the Warburg Institute.

nodes.label: Jan P. Hogendijk
nodes.summary: Jan P. Hogendijk specializes in the history of science and Indology. He completed his promotion at Utrecht University in 1983 and has held posts at Frankfurt, Utrecht (from 1986; professor from 2005), and Leiden University (2004–2009).

nodes.label: Toke Lindegaard Knudsen
nodes.summary: Toke Lindegaard Knudsen is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Kim Plofker and completed his doctorate under David Pingree in 2008.

nodes.label: Warburg Institute
variants: ヴァールブルク研究所

nodes.label: Shlomo Pines
nodes.description: Israeli scholar of Jewish and Islamic philosophy (1908–1990)
nodes.summary: Shlomo Pines was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin, taught at the University of Paris and the Institut d'Histoire des Sciences et des Techniques, and was a philosophy professor at Hebrew University.

nodes.label: Sang-Kyun Sun
nodes.summary: Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Delhi under the supervision of Sanghasen Singh. In 1995, Sun is attested as a lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College.

nodes.id: I:Sikkim Institute of Higher Nyingma Studies
nodes.label: Sikkim Institute of Higher Nyingma Studies
variants: Sikkim Institute of Higher Nyingma Studies

nodes.label: Suniti Kumar Pathak
nodes.description: Buddhist scholar and professor of Indo Tibetan studies

nodes.label: Jinah Kim
nodes.summary: Jinah Kim works in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley (attested 2007) under Joanna Gottfried Williams, was a Mellon fellow at IAS (2009–2010), and became Professor at Harvard University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gustaaf Houtman
nodes.summary: Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, also studying with Hla Pe and John Okell, and later served as a Senior Teaching Fellow at SOAS.

nodes.label: Pyi Phyo Kyaw
nodes.summary: Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at King's College London by 2014 and served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Gail Hinich Sutherland
nodes.summary: Gail Hinich Sutherland works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

nodes.label: Jagdish Kashyap
nodes.summary: Jagdish Kashyap, an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and under Rahul Sankrityayan. He taught Pāli at BHU and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

nodes.label: Vidya Niwas Mishra
nodes.image: Dr. Vidhyanivas Mishra with Dr. Archana Dwivedi.jpg
nodes.summary: Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya at Allahabad and at Gorakhpur. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1989) and as Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1986–1989).

nodes.label: Richard Peter Hottelet
nodes.summary: Richard Peter Hottelet studied Buddhist studies under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1971).

nodes.label: Marie G. Wanek
nodes.summary: Marie G. Wanek is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania and studied under teacher Sengaku Mayeda.

nodes.id: I:Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente
nodes.label: Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente

Istituto Italiano per l’Africa e l’Oriente in Rome

nodes.label: Geshe Yeshe Tobden
variants: dGe bshes Ye shes stobs ldan
nodes.summary: Geshe Yeshe Tobden studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) under teachers including Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from ~1967 to 1971.

nodes.label: Kelsang Gyatso
variants: dGe bshes sKal bzang rgya mtsho
nodes.summary: Kelsang Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Chambaling, Tashi Lhunpo, Ngamring Chöde, and Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre, and founded the New Kadampa Tradition.

nodes.label: Thubten Zopa Rinpoche
variants: Thub bstan bzod pa rin po che
nodes.image: Kyabje Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche December 2008 Kopan monastery Nepal.jpg
nodes.summary: Thubten Zopa Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dungkar Monastery and under teachers including Thubten Yeshe and the 14th Dalai Lama. He founded several centers and served as spiritual director of the FPMT beginning in 1984.

nodes.label: Case Western Reserve University
variants: Center for Research on Tibet, Case Western Reserve University
School of Medicine, Case Western Reserve University
Adelbert College of Western Reserve University

nodes.label: J. Gordon Melton
nodes.summary: J. Gordon Melton (born 1942) is a religious studies scholar educated at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held professorships at UC Santa Barbara and Baylor University.

nodes.label: Richard Kieckhefer
nodes.summary: Richard Kieckhefer is a historian of religion who studied at Saint Louis University and the University of Texas at Austin. He became a professor of history and religious studies at Northwestern University in 1975 and served as President of Societas Magica (1995–2004).

nodes.label: Carola Roloff
nodes.summary: Carola Roloff is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang and David P. Jackson, earning a degree at the University of Hamburg. Her posts include visiting professor at the University of Hamburg (2018–2025).

nodes.label: Erling von Mende
nodes.summary: Erling von Mende is a sinologist who studied law and Sinology at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne, where he completed his PhD (1969) and Habilitation (circa 1973–1979). He served as a professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin (1983–2007).

nodes.label: Lutz Bieg
nodes.summary: Lutz Bieg (born 1943) is a sinologist who studied at Heidelberg University (Dr. phil., c. 1963–1971) and Freie Universität Berlin (Habilitation, c. 1972–1986). From 1989 to 2008, he served as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Cologne.

nodes.label: Monika Zin
nodes.summary: Monika Zin is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Munich, where she became a professor (~2001–2016), and later led research projects at the Saxon Academy and Leipzig University.

nodes.id: I:Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities
nodes.label: Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities
variants: Saxon Academy of Sciences in Leipzig
Sächsische Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Leipzig
Sächsischen Akademie der Wissenschaften in Leipzig

nodes.label: University of St Andrews
variants: セント・アンドリュース大学

nodes.label: Douglas Osto
nodes.summary: Douglas Osto works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of Washington and a PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He joined Massey University in 2005, serving as Senior Lecturer and Programme Coordinator around 2007.

nodes.label: Dan Lusthaus
nodes.summary: Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding a Ph.D. from Temple University. His career includes posts at Florida State University, the University of Georgia, and a research associateship at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Carola S. Carstens
nodes.summary: Carola S. Carstens works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999) and earned a doctoral degree from the University of Hamburg (–2006).

nodes.label: Ratna Basu
nodes.summary: Ratna Basu is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989 and holds a post as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Michael Balk
nodes.summary: Michael Balk worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He was a doctoral student at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Royal Library of Berlin (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Friedrich Alexander Bischoff
nodes.summary: Friedrich Alexander Bischoff was a sinologist and Tibetologist who earned doctorates at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: William C. Kirby
nodes.summary: William C. Kirby is a sinologist and historian. Educated at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn, he taught at Washington University in St. Louis (1980–1992) before serving at Harvard from 1992 as Dean and Fairbank Center Director (circa 2006–2013).

nodes.label: Philip A. Kuhn
nodes.summary: Philip A. Kuhn was a historian and sinologist who studied at Harvard and Georgetown. He served on the faculty at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and later as a professor of history and East Asian languages at Harvard University from 1978.

nodes.label: Nicola Di Cosmo
nodes.summary: Nicola Di Cosmo (born 1957) is a sinologist and historian who earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (~1985–1991). He taught at Harvard University (1993–1997) and became the Henry Luce Foundation Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study (~2003).

nodes.label: Amdo Geshe Thupten Gyatso
variants: A mdo dge bshes Thub bstan rgya mtsho

nodes.label: Wm. Theodore de Bary
variants: ウィリアム・セオドア・ド・バリー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・セオドア・ド・バリー
nodes.description: American sinologist and scholar of East Asian philosophy (1919–2017)
nodes.summary: Wm. Theodore de Bary (1919–2017) was a Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology scholar. Educated at Columbia, Harvard, and the U.S. Navy Japanese Language School, he served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia (1953–2017).

nodes.label: Charles Alexander Moore
nodes.summary: Charles Alexander Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher who earned his AB and PhD at Yale University. He served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1936–1967) and founded and edited the journal Philosophy East and West.

nodes.label: William James
variants: ウィリアム・ジェームズ
nodes.image: William James by Alice M. Boughton, c. 1907, platinum print, from the National Portrait Gallery - NPG-NPG 87 37James-000001 (cropped).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ジェームズ
nodes.summary: William James was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Plymouth College and Harvard University, including Harvard Medical School, he held successive posts at Harvard starting in 1872, serving as Professor from 1885.

nodes.label: Maurice O'Connell Walshe
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and linguistics, Maurice O'Connell Walshe studied under Walpola Rahula and held a post at the University of London from around 1947 to 1979.

nodes.label: Ann Heirman
nodes.summary: Ann Heirman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held positions at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and served as a permanent member and director at Ghent University (2003–2012).

nodes.label: Frederick M. Asher
nodes.summary: Frederick M. Asher was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist who served as a professor at the University of Minnesota from circa 1973 to 2021.

nodes.label: Dilip K. Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at the University of Calcutta (1965–1977), University of Delhi (1977–1990), and served as Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Cambridge (1990–2008).

nodes.label: Keisuke Fujii
nodes.summary: Keisuke Fujii is an architectural historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held positions there from 1982 to 2018, rising to professor, and served as visiting professor at Tokyo University of the Arts.

nodes.label: Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute
variants: 長谷川仏教文化研究所

nodes.label: Cathy Cantwell
nodes.summary: Cathy Cantwell is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of Kent in 1989 and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

nodes.label: Esho Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Fang-Kuei Li
nodes.summary: Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua, Michigan, and Chicago under Edward Sapir. He held research positions at Academia Sinica and professorships at the University of Washington (1949–1969) and the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: Hellmut Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Hellmut Wilhelm was a sinologist who earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke. He taught at Peking University (~1933–1948) and held the chair of sinology at the University of Washington from 1948 to 1971.

nodes.label: Joseph Rock
variants: ジョセフ・フランシス・チャールズ・ロック
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・フランシス・チャールズ・ロック
nodes.summary: Joseph Rock worked in sinology and Tibetology. He held posts at Mills College (~1908), Mid-Pacific Institute (~1908), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1908; 1911–1920), the United States Department of Agriculture (~1920–1924), and the Army Map Service (1944).

nodes.label: Amy Snyder Ohta
nodes.summary: Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993, and became a professor at the University of Washington around 1995.

nodes.label: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami
nodes.summary: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami specializes in Japanology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and is attested as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington.

nodes.label: Itsuko Nishikawa
nodes.summary: Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology. She studied at Teachers College, Columbia University, and was attested as a teaching professor at the University of Washington in 2026.

nodes.label: Chi-chiang Huang
nodes.summary: Chi-chiang Huang specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned a PhD from the University of Arizona in 1986 under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao and also studied under Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: John Alexander Jorgensen
nodes.summary: John Alexander Jorgensen specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner at Australian National University, where he later held academic posts, and served as a Senior Lecturer at Griffith University.

nodes.label: Miriam Levering
nodes.summary: Miriam Levering was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

nodes.label: Whalen Lai
nodes.summary: Whalen Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a BA from International Christian University and a PhD from Harvard (~1975). He served at the University of Illinois (~1976–1978) and UC Davis (~1978–2005).

nodes.label: Taigen Dan Leighton
nodes.summary: Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned degrees from Columbia University and the Graduate Theological Union. He has taught at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Loyola University Chicago, and several other institutions.

nodes.label: Shohaku Okumura
nodes.summary: Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Komazawa University and under Kosho Uchiyama. He founded the Sanshin Zen Community and Pioneer Valley Zendo, and directed the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).

nodes.label: Ruth Fuller Sasaki
variants: ルース・フラー・エヴェレット
nodes.summary: Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. She studied at the University of Chicago and under D. T. Suzuki, Sokei-an, Zuigan Goto, and Mukai Kono. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America and abbess of Ryōsen-an.

nodes.label: Ryosho Nakamura
nodes.summary: Ryosho Nakamura is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at Kagoshima International University from around 1968 to 1998.

nodes.label: Masanori Nakagawa
nodes.summary: Masanori Nakagawa works in the field of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer (attested 1991) and assistant professor in the Faculty of Literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

nodes.label: M. Shinoda
nodes.image: Linkin Park - From Zero Lead Press Photo - James Minchin III (Mike Shinoda).jpg
nodes.description: American musician, rapper, singer and songwriter
nodes.summary: M. Shinoda (born 1977) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied under Seiren Matsunami, at Agoura High School (c. 1991–1995), and at the Art Center College of Design (c. 1995–1998).

nodes.label: Mun-keat Choong
nodes.summary: Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA), and the University of Queensland, where he earned an MA and PhD under Roderick S. Bucknell.

nodes.label: Roderick S. Bucknell
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Roderick S. Bucknell held positions at the University of Queensland, starting around 1976 and serving as associate professor (attested 1999–2000).

nodes.label: Asim Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.description: indologist; writer; taught at Dept. of Ancient Hist. and Culture, Calcutta U., India
nodes.summary: Asim Kumar Chatterjee is an Indologist and historian who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee (c. 1964–1967). He served as a lecturer in English at Jangipur College and a Senior Research Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Lobsang Dargyay
nodes.summary: Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and the University of Munich, where he earned a Dr.phil. (~1970–1974).

nodes.label: K. V. Raman
nodes.summary: K. V. Raman (1934–2024) studied at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras, and the Archaeological Survey of India. He worked at the ASI (~1957–1976) and the University of Madras (1955; 1976–1995).

nodes.label: Elisa Ganser
nodes.summary: Elisa Ganser is an Indologist attested in 2026 as a Lektorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and a visiting researcher at the University of Zurich.

nodes.label: Dorji Banzarov
nodes.summary: Dorji Banzarov was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École militaire russo-mongole, First Kazan Male Gymnasium, and Kazan Imperial University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski.

nodes.label: Gombojab Tsybikov
nodes.summary: Gombojab Tsybikov was a scholar in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University (~1893–1895) and Saint Petersburg State University (1895–1899), later serving at the Oriental Institute, Vladivostok (~1902–1917) and Far Eastern Federal University (~1918–1922).

nodes.label: Bazar Baradiin
nodes.summary: Bazar Baradiin was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902. He headed the Buryat Scientific Center and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Tsyben Zhamtsarano
nodes.summary: Tsyben Zhamtsarano (1880–1942) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and later headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Mongolian Academy of Sciences
variants: Scientific Committee of the Mongolian People's Republic
Akademie der Wissenschaften der Mongolischen Volksrepublik

nodes.label: Buryat Scientific Center
variants: Scientific Committee of the Buriat Mongolian ASSR

nodes.label: Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar
nodes.summary: Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and has held posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan.

nodes.label: Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya
variants: グルクル・カングリ大学

nodes.label: Kendriya Hindi Sansthan
variants: 中央ヒンディー語研究所
中央ヒンディー語理事会

nodes.label: Anil Vidyalankar
nodes.summary: Anil Vidyalankar (b. 1928) is a scholar in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi. He founded Sandhaan in 1988, serving as its director (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Iwao Nakajima
nodes.summary: Iwao Nakajima (born 1934) studied under Nichiki Kimura and completed a master's degree at Hitotsubashi University. Specializing in Buddhist studies, he worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and served as head at Sandhaan around 1999.

nodes.label: Hitotsubashi University
variants: 一橋大学大学院社会学研究科

nodes.label: Ernst Fürlinger
nodes.summary: Ernst Fürlinger is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He served as Studienleiter at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001) and held multiple researcher and leadership roles at the University for Continuing Education Krems (from 2007).

nodes.label: Lodrö Sangpo
nodes.summary: Lodrö Sangpo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under supervisor Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Robert M. Gimello
nodes.summary: Robert M. Gimello was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Columbia University (~1968–1976). He served on the faculty at the University of Arizona (~1981–1998) and Harvard University (~2001–2007).

nodes.label: Bruce Matthews
nodes.summary: Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After studying at McMaster University, he held posts as a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon (~1971–1973) and as a professor at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

nodes.label: Victor Chan
nodes.image: The Dalai Lama @ The Vancouver Peace Summit.jpg
nodes.summary: Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who studied as a graduate student at the University of Chicago. He served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia (~2002) and founded the Dalai Lama Center in 2005.

nodes.label: Larry DeVries
nodes.summary: Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Minnesota. He held teaching posts at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Washington, a research position at Chicago, and was attested at Langara College in 2005.

nodes.label: Mavis L. Fenn
nodes.summary: Mavis L. Fenn studied at Winnipeg, Calgary, and McMaster (Ph.D. under Graeme MacQueen). A Buddhist and religious studies scholar, she held posts at St. Paul's University College (attested 2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

nodes.label: St. Paul's University College
variants: St Paul's College, University of Waterloo

nodes.label: Robert Florida
nodes.summary: Robert Florida works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later as an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

nodes.label: Baihui Wu
nodes.summary: Baihui Wu worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1945–1951), Peking University (~1952–1957), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of Philosophy (~1978).

nodes.label: Robert Gardner
nodes.summary: Robert Gardner studied at Harvard University (BA ~1943–1947), founded it in 1957, and served there as a professor from 1956 to 1997. He also worked at the Harvard Art Museums and taught medieval art and history at the University of Puget Sound.

nodes.label: R. Gordon Wasson
variants: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.jawiki: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.summary: R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the London School of Economics and Columbia University, later working in journalism and banking, including at J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963) and the American Council of Learned Societies (1951).

nodes.label: Pema Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Pema Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, and taught Christopher S. George, Adam Pearcey, and Rizong Sras Rinpoche.

nodes.label: David Webster
nodes.summary: David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Thibaut d'Hubert
nodes.summary: Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Chicago and is attested as a Vertretungsprofessor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

nodes.label: Manan Ahmed Asif
nodes.description: historian and professor at Columbia University

nodes.label: Yigal Bronner
nodes.summary: Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1993–1999). He became an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2011.

nodes.label: George C. O. Haas
nodes.summary: George C. O. Haas was an Indologist who served as Recording Secretary of the American Oriental Society (~1913–1918) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1916–1918).

nodes.label: Kanai Lal Hazra
nodes.summary: Kanai Lal Hazra (born 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and earned his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune, later becoming a Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Paul Fuller
nodes.summary: Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Paul Dundas and Rupert Gethin, completing a PhD at the University of Bristol. He held a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

nodes.label: John Dowson
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist John Dowson studied under Edwin Norris. He tutored at the East India Company College (~1855–1858) and served as Professor of Hindustani at University College London and the Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877).

nodes.label: Krishna Mohan Banerjee
nodes.summary: Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. Educated at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College, Kolkata, and studying under Alexander Duff, he held posts at Hare School (~1829–1831) and Bishop's College (1852).

nodes.label: Edward Backhouse Eastwick
nodes.summary: Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Charterhouse, Merton College, and Oxford, he was Professor of Hindustani and Telugu at East India Company College (1845) and served in the Foreign Office (~1860–1863).

nodes.label: K. N. Jayatilleke
nodes.summary: K. N. Jayatilleke worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under O. H. de A. Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at the University of Cambridge. He served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon from circa 1951 to 1963.

nodes.label: Ludwig Wittgenstein
variants: ルートヴィヒ・ヨーゼフ・ヨーハン・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.summary: Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at Technische Hochschule Berlin, Manchester, and Cambridge, earning his PhD there in 1929. He served as a lecturer, fellow, and professor of philosophy at the University of Cambridge between 1929 and 1947.

nodes.label: Pentti Aalto
nodes.summary: Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1934–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics (1958–1980).

nodes.label: Kimmo Koskenniemi
nodes.summary: Kimmo Koskenniemi (born 1945) works in computational linguistics. He studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu and served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and BAULT research community director (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Frank Ernest Keay
nodes.birth_place: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames

nodes.label: Thomas Zehnder
nodes.summary: Thomas Zehnder is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD from the University of Zurich, where he studied under Alexander Lubotsky.

nodes.label: Wei-jen Teng
nodes.summary: Wei-jen Teng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Teng has taught at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and Chung-Hwa Institute.

nodes.label: Dylan Esler
nodes.summary: Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London and completed his PhD in 2018 at KU Leuven, where he also served as a research scholar.

nodes.label: Yao-ming Tsai
nodes.summary: Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Tsai completed a PhD at the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.

nodes.label: Sanne Dokter-Mersch
nodes.summary: Sanne Dokter-Mersch works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Leiden University between approximately 2015 and 2021 under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

nodes.label: K. Meenakshi
nodes.summary: K. Meenakshi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD under M. A. Mehendale at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 and was affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

nodes.label: Jiryo Masuda
nodes.summary: Jiryo Masuda worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Unrai Wogihara, served as a professor at the University of Calcutta, and taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.

nodes.label: University College, Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学ユニヴァーシティ・カレッジ
ユニバーシティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: D. N. Shukla
nodes.summary: Indologist D. N. Shukla earned a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor K. A. Subramania Iyer and held an attested post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University in 1958.

nodes.label: Jitendra Nath Banerjea
