nodes.summary: Jitendra Nath Banerjea worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1959).

nodes.label: Tiziana Pontillo
nodes.summary: Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.

nodes.label: Kodo Akino
nodes.summary: Kodo Akino (1858–1934) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under teachers Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership posts at Komazawa University between 1892 and 1909.

nodes.label: Nyoten Jinbo
nodes.summary: Nyoten Jinbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Kodo Yamada
nodes.summary: Kodo Yamada (1866–1933) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.

nodes.label: Totsudo Kato
nodes.summary: Totsudo Kato worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oriental Hall, Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University under teachers including Enryo Inoue and Seiran Ouchi, later teaching at Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon Universities.

nodes.label: Seiran Ouchi
nodes.summary: Seiran Ouchi was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who founded Hoshi Sodan (1874) and Meikyo Shinshi (1875). He held a post at Nishi Hongan-ji and served as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

nodes.label: Sogaku Harada
nodes.summary: Sogaku Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University under teachers including Sotan Oka and Dokutan Sōsan. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from 1911 to 1923.

nodes.label: Tetsuo Otani
nodes.summary: Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He held multiple leadership roles, including president of Komazawa University (2002–2006), chairman of Tsuru University (2013–2016), and president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

nodes.label: Sokuo Eto
nodes.summary: Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Komazawa University, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958) and as a professor at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Joseph Dalton Hooker
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・ダルトン・フッカー
nodes.summary: Joseph Dalton Hooker studied at the University of Glasgow (~1832–1839). He served at the British Geological Survey (1845–1847) and as Director of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew (1847–1885).

nodes.label: John Firminger Duthie
nodes.summary: John Firminger Duthie served as Superintendent of the Saharanpur Botanical Garden from ~1876 to 1903 and as Director of the Botanical Survey of India from ~1891 to 1903.

nodes.label: George Watt
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ワット (植物学者)
nodes.summary: George Watt, an Indologist, studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and the University of Glasgow. He held positions at Glasgow, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, the Indian Museum, and the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Moodeen Sheriff
nodes.description: Indian surgeon and practitioner of native medicine
nodes.summary: Moodeen Sheriff was an Indian medical practitioner and Indologist who studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

nodes.label: Penor Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Palyul Monastery under teachers including Thubten Chökyi Dawa and Karma Tekchok Nyingpo. He founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978 and taught numerous students.

nodes.label: Ram Niwas Pandey
nodes.summary: Ram Niwas Pandey, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology under doctoral supervisor Hit Narayan Jha.

nodes.id: I:Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology
nodes.label: Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology
variants: School of Archaeology at New Delhi

nodes.label: Francis X. Clooney
nodes.summary: Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago, he taught at Boston College (1984–2005) and was appointed Parkman Professor of Divinity at Harvard University in 2005.

nodes.label: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst
nodes.summary: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst works in indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner and held posts at the University of Manchester (attested 2005, and as Honorary Research Fellow attested 2026).

nodes.id: I:Administrative Commission of Cultural Relics of Tibet Autonomous Region
nodes.label: Administrative Commission of Cultural Relics of Tibet Autonomous Region
variants: Administrative Commission of Museum and Archaeological Data, Tibet

nodes.label: Peter Gaeffke
nodes.summary: Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indologist who studied in Regensburg, under Ernst Schwarz at Mainz (PhD 1952), and at the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).

nodes.label: James Morison
nodes.summary: James Morison is an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as Librarian at the Indian Institute, University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

nodes.label: Kenneth Somerled Macdonald
nodes.image: Kenneth S. Macdonald, M.A., D.D. (page 8 crop).jpg

nodes.label: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz
nodes.summary: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz is a scholar of Tibetology, Central Asian studies, and religious studies who completed her PhD and Habilitation at the University of Bonn. In 1999 she became a professor at the University of Bern, later serving as Dean (2007–2010).

nodes.label: Youru Wang
nodes.summary: Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean. Wang held positions at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.

nodes.label: Charles Wei-hsun Fu
nodes.summary: Charles Wei-hsun Fu (1933–1996) studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1960) and the University of Illinois System (~1964–1969). Specializing in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he held a post at Ohio University (~1968–1972).

nodes.label: Mithilesh Chaturvedi
nodes.summary: Mithilesh Chaturvedi is a scholar in Indology and linguistics affiliated with the University of Delhi's Department of Sanskrit (attested 2009) and later recognized as Professor emeritus there (attested 2026).

nodes.label: P. K. Mukhopadhyay
nodes.summary: P. K. Mukhopadhyay worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Ana Agud
nodes.summary: Ana Agud is a linguist and Indologist. She studied at the University of Salamanca (1965–1970) and the University of Tübingen (1970–1974) before becoming a professor in classical and Indo-European philology at Salamanca around 1976.

nodes.label: Masato Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Masato Kobayashi studied linguistics and Indology at Kyoto University (~1989–1995) and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona (~1995–2000). He was a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2003).

nodes.label: Junglan Bang
nodes.summary: Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Dongguk University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg (2012) under Harunaga Isaacson. She also served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Karma Lekshe Tsomo
nodes.description: Buddhist nun, scholar and social activist
nodes.summary: Karma Lekshe Tsomo is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She served as an Assistant Professor at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Numata Professor at Hawaiʻi in 2023.

nodes.id: I:Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
nodes.label: Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
variants: Sakyadhita: International Association of Buddhist Women
Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women

nodes.label: Kunsthistorisches Museum
variants: Münzkabinett des Kunsthistorischen Museums in Wien
Vienna Coin Cabinet at the Kunsthistorisches Museum

nodes.label: Satya Swarup Misra
nodes.summary: Satya Swarup Misra (born 1935) is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.label: Akira Hataya
nodes.summary: Akira Hataya is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Reiner Wiehl
nodes.summary: Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Ordentlicher Professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and as professor of philosophy at Heidelberg University from 1977.

nodes.label: R. P. Paranjpye
nodes.summary: R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

nodes.label: Klaus Rüping
nodes.summary: Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied under Paul Hacker and held an academic post as a lecturer at the University of Münster (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Volker Caumanns
nodes.summary: Tibetologist Volker Caumanns completed his MA at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He has held positions at Munich, LIRI, Bern, Hamburg, and Leipzig.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wackernagel
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wackernagel was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1824–1827) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He taught at Pädagogium Basel (~1833–1835) and held a professorship at the University of Basel (1833–1869).

nodes.label: Haruka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Haruka Yanagisawa was a historian and Indologist who held academic posts at the University of Tokyo from around 1993 to 2007 and at Chiba University.

nodes.label: Nobuhiro Ota
nodes.summary: Nobuhiro Ota (1969–) is an Indologist and historian who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. He has held academic posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, becoming an associate professor in 2007 and professor in 2021.

nodes.label: Akio Tanabe
nodes.summary: Akio Tanabe (b. 1964) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006) and held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (professor, 2015).

nodes.label: Nicolas Tournadre
variants: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.jawiki: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.summary: Nicolas Tournadre is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology who earned his PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège. He held positions at INALCO, Paris 8 University, the University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University.

nodes.label: Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche (1932–1999) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Nyoshul Monastery (~1944) and Katok Monastery, and under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

nodes.label: Khenpo Appey Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khenpo Appey Rinpoche (1927–2010) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dzongsar Monastery under Drakgyab Lodrö, directed Sakya College (1972–1985), and held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (1920–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Samten Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and others, founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery, and taught numerous prominent students.

nodes.label: Asanga Tilakaratne
nodes.summary: Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held multiple leadership roles at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, including Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy (c. 2003–2009), and was attested as Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Alvappillai Veluppillai
nodes.summary: Alvappillai Veluppillai specialized in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Ceylon under K. Kanapathypillai and at Oxford under Thomas Burrow, holding posts at Ceylon, Jaffna, Uppsala, and Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Abdur Rehman
nodes.summary: Abdur Rehman studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani and completed his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. A specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology, he was attested as an assistant professor at the University of Peshawar in 1988.

nodes.label: Pamela Gutman
nodes.summary: Pamela Gutman was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her studies at the University of Vienna and the Australian National University (~1972–1976).

nodes.label: Sakda Hemthep
nodes.summary: Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MPhil at Cardiff University under Max Deeg and Peter Harvey, and is attested as a PhD researcher at Ghent University in 2026.

nodes.label: Jean Dantinne
nodes.summary: Jean Dantinne was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte and held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

nodes.label: Michael Carrithers
nodes.summary: Michael Carrithers (born 1945) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Wesleyan and Oxford, he taught at the London School of Economics, Oxford, and Durham University, becoming Professor of Anthropology in 1992.

nodes.label: Caroline Humphrey
nodes.summary: Caroline Humphrey is an Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies scholar. She earned degrees at Girton College and the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach, and Leeds. She held posts at Cambridge (1978–2010), Girton, and SPRI.

nodes.label: Mary Jaksch
nodes.summary: Mary Jaksch (b. 1947) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland as a student of Peter Harvey, and also studied under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

nodes.label: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez
nodes.summary: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Jane Caple
nodes.summary: Jane Caple is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Leeds and the University of Manchester, where she is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

nodes.label: Calambur Sivaramamurti
nodes.summary: Calambur Sivaramamurti studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at Presidency University (~1928-1934). Active in Indology and archaeology, he held posts at the Government Museum, Chennai (1935-1946), the Indian Museum (1946), and the Archaeological Survey of India (~1946-1955).

nodes.label: Ayinapalli Aiyappan
nodes.summary: Ayinapalli Aiyappan was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Madras. He served as superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1969–1970).

nodes.label: Mortimer Wheeler
nodes.summary: Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist who studied at University College London. He directed the National Museum of Wales, the London Museum (1926–1944), and served as Director-General of Archæology in India (1944–1948) and Honorary Secretary of the British Academy (~1949–1968).

nodes.label: Hermann Beythan
nodes.summary: Hermann Beythan worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai.

nodes.label: Sibani Das Gupta
nodes.summary: Sibani Das Gupta is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate degree at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

nodes.label: John Collinson Nesfield
nodes.summary: Working in linguistics and Indology, John Collinson Nesfield studied at Highgate School and Merton College. He taught at Highgate (1859–1864), Presidency University (~1867–1872), and Krishnagar Government College (~1872–1874), later becoming principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1878).

nodes.label: Rory Mackenzie
nodes.summary: Rory Mackenzie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He has served as a teacher at International Christian College.

nodes.label: Kodo Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kodo Kawamura (1933–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's (~1956–1958) and doctorate (by 1984) at Komazawa University, where he also served as a professor from circa 1968 to 2004.

nodes.id: I:Sutra Translation Committee of the United States and Canada
nodes.label: Sutra Translation Committee of the United States and Canada
variants: Sutra Translation Committee of the United States and Canada

nodes.label: Kurunegoda Piyatissa
nodes.summary: Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1928–2008) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was head of the New York Buddhist Vihara, where his posts are attested in 1998 and 2009.

nodes.label: Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra
nodes.summary: An Indologist who studied under Rāmbhadrācārya, Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra headed the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, was a visiting professor at the University of Indonesia (~1987–1989), and served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~2000–2003).

nodes.label: Pascale Haag
nodes.summary: Pascale Haag specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1997–2002) and Marie-Claire Gay at Paris Nanterre University (~2014–2018), and held a post at the EHESS (~2003).

nodes.label: David L. Haberman
nodes.description: American indologist and historian of religion
nodes.summary: David L. Haberman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder. He held posts at the University of Arizona (circa 1989–1993) and Indiana University Bloomington (circa 1993–2022).

nodes.label: K. Balasubramania Iyer
nodes.summary: K. Balasubramania Iyer was an Indologist who served as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945).

nodes.label: Norvin J. Hein
nodes.summary: Norvin J. Hein was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under Franklin Edgerton and served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in the Divinity School at Yale University, attested in 1965.

nodes.label: John James Jones
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, John James Jones was educated at Aberystwyth University. He served as Deputy-Keeper in the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales from circa 1926 to 1957.

nodes.label: Betty Heimann
nodes.summary: Betty Heimann was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Georg Simmel, Emil Sieg, and Eugen Hultzsch. She held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, the University of Hamburg (1931–1933), the University of London (~1934–1945), and the University of Colombo (1945–1949).

nodes.label: Ivo Fišer
nodes.summary: Ivo Fišer (1929–2011) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He was a lecturer at Charles University around 1960 and was affiliated with the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology around 1970.

nodes.label: Herbert V. Guenther
nodes.summary: Herbert V. Guenther worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Munich and Vienna, he also trained under traditional Tibetan teachers. He held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

nodes.label: Ananda Guruge
nodes.summary: Ananda Guruge was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Ceylon and the University of London, he held posts at NIEPA, California State University, Fullerton, and the University of the West.

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration
nodes.label: National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration
Christoph Anderl
nodes.summary: Christoph Anderl is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned an MA at the University of Vienna and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo under Christoph Harbsmeier, later joining Ghent University as a permanent member around 2014.

nodes.label: Evan Thompson
nodes.summary: Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College and the University of Toronto under teachers including Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco Varela. His main posts include Toronto, York University, and a professorship at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Dan Zahavi
nodes.summary: Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who completed his PhD under Rudolf Bernet at KU Leuven and his Habilitation at the University of Copenhagen. He has served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen and the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Graduate Center, CUNY
variants: City University of New York Graduate Center
Graduate Center, City University of New York
Graduate Center of the City University of New York

nodes.label: Francisco Varela
variants: フランシスコ・ハビエル・バレーラ・ガルシア
フランシスコ・バレーラ
nodes.jawiki: フランシスコ・バレーラ
nodes.summary: Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from the University of Chile and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Chile, CNRS, Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital, and the University of Paris, and co-founded the Mind and Life Institute.

nodes.label: Eleanor Rosch
nodes.summary: Eleanor Rosch studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Roger Brown. She held positions at Connecticut College, Brown University, and was a professor of cognitive psychology at UC Berkeley from 1971.

nodes.label: Karen O'Brien-Kop
nodes.summary: Karen O'Brien-Kop is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned her PhD at SOAS University of London. She held lectureships at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020) and King's College London (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Daniela Bevilacqua
nodes.summary: Daniela Bevilacqua is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University. She served as a post-doctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Paris Nanterre University
variants: University of Paris Ouest Nanterre La Defense
Laboratoire d'Ethnologie et de Sociologie Comparative, Université de Paris X, Nanterre
パリ大学ナンテール分校

nodes.label: Sravana Borkataky-Varma
nodes.summary: Sravana Borkataky-Varma is a religious studies and Indology scholar. After studying at the University of Delhi and completing a PhD at Rice University, she taught at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, and Harvard, and became an instructional professor at the University of Houston.

nodes.label: Mikel Burley
nodes.summary: Mikel Burley works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Essex under J. M. Bernstein, studied under Jonardon Ganeri and Brian Carr, and completed a PhD under John Peacock at Bristol (2005). He is Associate Professor at Leeds (attested 2007–2020).

nodes.label: Philip Deslippe
nodes.summary: Philip Deslippe works in religious studies and Indology. He has been a graduate student (attested 2020–2026) and a teaching associate (attested 2020) at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: Carl W. Ernst
nodes.summary: Carl W. Ernst works in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Stanford University (~1969–1973) and Harvard University (~1973–1981). He taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and served as professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

nodes.label: Gordon Hannington Luce
nodes.summary: Gordon Hannington Luce was a historian, sinologist, and linguist who was educated at Dean Close School and the University of Cambridge (~1908–1911). He served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from around 1923 to 1964.

nodes.label: John Alexander Stewart
nodes.summary: John Alexander Stewart, a scholar of linguistics, studied at the University of Aberdeen. Following service in the Indian Civil Service (1905–1933), he served as Reader in Burmese at the University of London and held a post at SOAS.

nodes.label: Nanigopal Majumdar
nodes.summary: Nanigopal Majumdar was an archaeologist and Indologist. He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).

nodes.label: Sydney Frank Markham
nodes.summary: Sydney Frank Markham was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Wadham College (~1919–1923). He served as Secretary and then President of the Museums Association (~1929–1942).

nodes.label: Ghulam Yazdani
nodes.summary: Ghulam Yazdani studied at Aligarh Muslim University (~1903–1905) in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Government College Lahore, and served as Director of Archæology for the Government of Hyderabad (~1914–1943).

nodes.label: Ramaprasad Chanda
nodes.summary: Ramaprasad Chanda was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Scottish Church College (BA ~1896). He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1917-1919) and was Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum (1921-1932).

nodes.label: Richard K. Payne
nodes.summary: Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean of the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994–2017) and on the faculty of the Graduate Theological Union (~1995).

nodes.label: Jeffrey S. Lidke
nodes.summary: Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at Berry College and the University of Virginia, where he served as visiting assistant professor of religion (attested 2003).

nodes.id: I:Lambakarna Bhatta Institute of Tantric Studies
nodes.label: Lambakarna Bhatta Institute of Tantric Studies
variants: Lambakarna Bhatta Institute of Tantric Studies

nodes.label: Anna Andreeva
nodes.summary: Anna Andreeva is a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University, where she is attested as a permanent member in 2026.

nodes.label: Georgios T. Halkias
nodes.summary: Georgios T. Halkias studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble. He worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, later becoming associate professor at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Kotyk
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University (MA 2015-2016) and Leiden University (PhD -2017) under James A. Benn. He held posts at McMaster University (attested 2019) and the University of Bologna.

nodes.id: I:Institute for the Study of Religions
nodes.label: Institute for the Study of Religions
variants: Institute for the Study of Religions

nodes.label: Judith Simmer-Brown
nodes.summary: Judith Simmer-Brown works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell College, Florida State, Columbia, and Walden University, she taught at several institutions before joining Naropa University in 1977, where she is Distinguished Professor Emerita.

nodes.label: Eric Haruki Swanson
nodes.summary: Eric Haruki Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who held a post at Loyola Marymount University and was attested as a senior visiting scholar at Stanford University in 2026.

nodes.label: Sthaneshwar Timalsina
nodes.summary: Sthaneshwar Timalsina works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1985–1995) and Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (~2001–2005). He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University (~2005–2022), and Stony Brook University (~2022).

nodes.label: John Chadwick
variants: ジョン・チャドウィック
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・チャドウィック
nodes.summary: John Chadwick was a linguist and classical historian educated at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked on the Oxford Latin Dictionary and served as Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Bridget Allchin
nodes.description: English archaeologist, specializing in South Asian archaeology
nodes.summary: Bridget Allchin (1927–2017) was an archaeologist and Indologist. She earned a PhD from University College London under Frederick Zeuner, became a Fellow of Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1978), and co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

nodes.id: I:European Association of South Asian Studies
nodes.label: European Association of South Asian Studies
variants: European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art History
European Association of South Asian Studies (EASAS)
European Association of South Asian Studies
European Association of South Asian Archaeologists

nodes.label: D. C. Sarasvati
nodes.summary: D. C. Sarasvati was an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan and held an appointment as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.

nodes.label: Emmie te Nijenhuis
nodes.summary: Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory and Utrecht University, completing her PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and held a post at Amsterdam.

nodes.label: Shek-Wing Tam
nodes.description: Hong Kong Buddhist scholar, writer, and fortune-teller
nodes.summary: Shek-Wing Tam (1935–2024) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Dudjom Rinpoche, Ying-Kuang Chu, and Yui Chi Lau. He was a professor at Renmin University of China and served on an Academic Advisory Board at Tsinghua University.

nodes.label: Weirong Shen
nodes.summary: Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Shen held teaching posts at the University of Hong Kong and Renmin University of China (~2006–2015).

nodes.label: Henry Chung-hung Shiu
nodes.summary: Henry Chung-hung Shiu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto in 2006, having studied under Shek-Wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

nodes.label: Kapila Vatsyayan
nodes.summary: Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU, co-founded the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, and chaired the India International Centre.

nodes.label: David J. Kalupahana
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Buddhist scholar and philosopher (1936–2014)
nodes.summary: David J. Kalupahana was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Ceylon and completed his PhD at the University of London under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman. He held posts at Ceylon and Hawaiʻi.

nodes.id: I:Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens
nodes.label: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens
variants: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens

nodes.label: Clare Carlisle
nodes.summary: Clare Carlisle is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and became a professor at King's College London in ~2011.

nodes.label: Edward Vernon Arnold
nodes.summary: Edward Vernon Arnold specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1875–1879) and under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen (~1881–1883), later serving as a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).

nodes.label: Bangor University
variants: University College of North Wales in Bangor

nodes.label: Carl Darling Buck
nodes.summary: Carl Darling Buck was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882-1889) and the University of Leipzig (~1889-1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.

nodes.label: Lawrence Heyworth Mills
nodes.summary: Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and held a professorship at the University of Oxford, attested in 1903.

nodes.label: Pulinbihari Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Pulinbihari Chakravarti studied Indology and philosophy under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society (attested 1951).

nodes.label: Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen
variants: Christian Charles Josias, Baron von Bunsen
nodes.summary: Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) worked in linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen (under Heyne), Munich, Leiden, Copenhagen, and under Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as Prussian envoy (~1841–1854).

nodes.label: Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi
nodes.summary: Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi works in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1976), including head of the Research Department (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Donald Eric Capps
nodes.description: American professor and author of pastoral theology (1939–2015)
nodes.summary: Donald Eric Capps (1939–2015) was a religious studies scholar educated at Lewis & Clark College, Yale, and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University, and was a professor at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).

nodes.label: Helen Hardacre
nodes.summary: Helen Hardacre is a scholar of Japanology and religion who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton, Griffith University, and Harvard University, where she was appointed in 1992.

nodes.label: James L. Taylor
nodes.summary: James L. Taylor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Macquarie University by 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Syed Nawab Ali
nodes.description: Persian-English translator who worked as a professor in Baroda
nodes.summary: Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar of history and archaeology. In 1932, he is attested as Principal of Bahauddin College and Professor of Persian at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.

nodes.label: Catherine Prueitt
nodes.summary: Catherine Prueitt is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Rochester and Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, and was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Yoshio Nishiguchi
nodes.summary: Yoshio Nishiguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

nodes.label: Karl Debreczeny
nodes.summary: Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Fabienne Jagou
nodes.summary: Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences under Pierre-Étienne Will and was appointed maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

nodes.label: Rob Linrothe
nodes.summary: Rob Linrothe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1992). He held faculty posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

nodes.label: Paul K. Nietupski
nodes.summary: Paul K. Nietupski works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Abraham Zablocki
nodes.summary: Abraham Zablocki earned a PhD at Cornell University. Working in Tibetology and religious studies, he held a post attested in 2008 at Agnes Scott College.

nodes.label: American Academy of Religion
variants: Tibetan and Himalayan Religions Group of the American Academy of Religion
Confucian Traditions Group of the American Academy of Religion
Buddhism Section of the American Academy of Religion

nodes.label: Bal Krishen Thapar
nodes.summary: Bal Krishen Thapar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of the Punjab, Heidelberg University, and under Mortimer Wheeler. He later served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981).

nodes.label: Henrik Zilliacus
nodes.summary: Henrik Zilliacus (1908–1992) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki from around 1926 to 1936 and held a post there from circa 1944 to 1975.

nodes.label: Franz Ferdinand Schwarz
nodes.summary: Franz Ferdinand Schwarz was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Graz from 1953 to 1958 and later served as a professor there from around 1974 to 1999.

nodes.label: Yaroslav Vasilkov
nodes.summary: Yaroslav Vasilkov is an Indologist who studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (circa 1961–1967). He held posts at Kunstkamera and the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1968), and at Saint Petersburg State University.

nodes.label: Katsutoshi Ono
nodes.summary: Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist educated at Kyoto University. His career included appointments at Kyoto University, the Academy of Oriental Culture, the Nara National Museum, Ryukoku University, and Kansai University.

nodes.label: Alexander Piatigorsky
variants: アレクサンデル・モイシェイェヴィチ・ピアティゴルスキー
nodes.jawiki: アレクサンデル・ピアティゴルスキー
nodes.summary: Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Moscow State University, worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968), and was Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia at SOAS University of London (1990–2001).

nodes.label: J. B. Disanayaka
nodes.summary: J. B. Disanayaka (born 1937) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Colombo from circa 1982 to 2002 and held a post at SOAS University of London around 1996.

nodes.label: Purushottam Mahadev Joshi
nodes.summary: Purushottam Mahadev Joshi was an Indologist and historian. He worked at the University of Mumbai Library (~1935–1947) and later served as Reader in Medieval History at Deccan College (~1965–1970).

nodes.label: Frederick M. Smith
nodes.summary: Frederick M. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor and later professor emeritus at the University of Iowa.

nodes.label: Philip Lutgendorf
nodes.summary: Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Chicago (~1967–1987). He joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies from 2010 to 2018.

nodes.label: Ajahn Sumedho
nodes.summary: Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at the University of Washington and UC Berkeley, and trained under Ajahn Chah (1967–1977). He founded and was abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and was abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).

nodes.label: Ajahn Chah
nodes.native: ชา สุภทฺโท

nodes.id: I:Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences
nodes.label: Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences
variants: Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences
Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences at Stanford University

nodes.label: Satya Vrat Shastri
nodes.image: Ramashish Acharya with Padma Bhushan Satya Vrat Shastri.jpg
nodes.description: Jnanpith Award recipient in Sanskrit. Indian academic
nodes.summary: Satya Vrat Shastri (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of the Punjab and Banaras Hindu University. He served as Department Head and Dean at the University of Delhi and Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

nodes.label: Fabrizia Baldissera
nodes.summary: Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the "Federigo Enriques" Department of Mathematics (1969–2004). She held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1994–2005) and the University of Florence (~2005).

nodes.label: Yun Ji
nodes.summary: Yun Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University in 2006. Ji served as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Georges-Jean Pinault
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Georges-Jean Pinault studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jean Haudry. He taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle and Blaise Pascal University, becoming a professor at EPHE in 1999.

nodes.label: Jason Protass
nodes.summary: Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick and held appointments as a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica and visiting researcher at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Nathan Sivin
nodes.summary: Nathan Sivin worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the Defense Language Institute, MIT, Harvard, and Kyoto University. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977, became Professor Emeritus at the University of Pennsylvania (1977-2006), and was Honorary Professor at CAS (~1999-2022).

nodes.label: Bulcsu Siklós
nodes.summary: Bulcsu Siklós specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of London, studying under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden, and held an attested post at SOAS University of London in 1996.

nodes.label: Yang-Gyu An
nodes.summary: Yang-Gyu An is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hojin (attested 2003) and earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1998 under Richard Gombrich.

nodes.label: Akio Donohashi
nodes.summary: Akio Donohashi (b. 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1974) and served as a professor at Kobe University (1990–1991).

nodes.id: I:Historiographical Institute, the University of Tokyo
nodes.label: Historiographical Institute, the University of Tokyo
University of Cologne
variants: Indological Institute at the University of Cologne
Centre for Advanced Study of Humanities, University of Cologne

nodes.label: Robert E. Morrell
nodes.summary: A scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, Robert E. Morrell studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis, attested in 1985 and 2006.

nodes.label: Washington University in St. Louis
variants: Washington University in St. Louis Missouri

nodes.label: Barbra R. Clayton
nodes.summary: Barbra R. Clayton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying under G. Raj. She has been affiliated with Mount Allison University.

nodes.label: Sarah J. Horton
nodes.summary: Sarah J. Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied under Stanley Weinstein at Yale University and served as an Assistant Professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Melvyn C. Goldstein
nodes.summary: Tibetologist and historian Melvyn C. Goldstein earned his BA at the University of Michigan and his PhD at the University of Washington. From 1968 to 2002, he served as a professor in the Department of Anthropology at Case Western Reserve University.

nodes.label: The New School
variants: The New School for Social Research, New York
The New School for Social Research

nodes.label: Osmund Bopearachchi
nodes.summary: Osmund Bopearachchi studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne University, and Paris-Sorbonne University. He served as Emeritus Director at CNRS (1989) and as Adjunct Professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2014).

nodes.label: Hans Hartog
nodes.summary: Hans Hartog (born 1912) was an Indologist. He studied at Tübingen, Bethel, Munich, and the University of Marburg, earning his PhD (1937–1939) under Friedrich Heiler and studying under scholars including Walther Wüst and Hanns Oertel.

nodes.label: Friedrich Heiler
nodes.summary: Friedrich Heiler (1892–1967) worked in religious studies. He studied at the University of Munich (~1912–1917), where he taught in 1918, before holding posts at the University of Marburg (1920) and the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962).

nodes.label: Walther Wüst
nodes.description: Rector of the University of Munich and SS member (1901-1993)
nodes.summary: Walther Wüst was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich. He served at Munich as Privatdozent and dean, and held posts at the Ahnenerbe and the Deutsche Akademie.

nodes.label: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer
nodes.image: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-2004-0413-501, Prof. Jakob Wilhelm Hauer.jpg
nodes.summary: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at the Basel Mission, Oxford, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He served as professor at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and held a chair at Tübingen (1927–1945).

nodes.label: Kurt Huber
nodes.description: German folk song researcher, professor at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU) in Munich, member of the White Rose (1893-1943)
nodes.summary: Kurt Huber studied at the Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). Working in philosophy and other fields, he served at the University of Munich as an außerordentlicher Professor (1926) and Professor (1938).

nodes.label: Erich Rudolf Jaensch
nodes.summary: Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a scholar of philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen and completed his habilitation at the University of Strasbourg. He served as an ordinary professor of philosophy at Halle-Wittenberg and Marburg.

nodes.label: Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen
nodes.summary: Philosopher Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen studied and habilitated at the University of Munich (1919–1928). He held professorships at Bonn (1934), Munich (1936–1941), and the University of Mainz (ca. 1947–1969).

nodes.label: Wolfgang Schultz
nodes.description: German philosopher, historian and art historian (1881-1936)
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Schultz was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He worked at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and was appointed Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Sommer
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Sommer specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Marburg, Freiberg, and Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen, habilitating at Leipzig. He held professorships at Basel (1902), Rostock (1909–1913), Jena (1913–1924), Bonn (1924–1926), and Munich (1926–1951).

nodes.label: Giovanni Vacca
nodes.summary: Sinologist and historian Giovanni Vacca studied at the universities of Genoa and Florence. He taught Chinese at the University of Florence (1910) before holding positions in East Asian languages, history, and geography at Sapienza University of Rome (1911–1948).

nodes.label: John Kieschnick
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, John Kieschnick held an academic post at the University of Bristol from circa 2005 to 2011 before joining the faculty at Stanford University in circa 2011.

nodes.label: Hellmuth Hecker
nodes.summary: Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD 1948) and under Paul Debes. He served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1956 to 1988.

nodes.label: Indologica Taurinensia
variants: Indologica Taurinensia, The Journal of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies

nodes.label: Daniel Dubuisson
nodes.summary: Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He served as a director of research at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique and at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III.

nodes.label: Elaine Fisher
nodes.summary: Elaine Fisher is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She was a doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2010) and is a faculty member at Stanford University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jonathan Z. Smith
variants: ジョナサン・Z・スミス
nodes.summary: Jonathan Z. Smith (1938–2017) was a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford College, Yale Divinity School, and Yale University. He held positions at Dartmouth College, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Chicago, where he was Dean of the College.

nodes.label: Meinrad Scheller
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist Meinrad Scheller completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch, also studying in Paris. He was a professor at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).

nodes.label: Gregory Max Seton
nodes.summary: Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa, UC Santa Barbara, and Oxford (Wolfson College), completing doctoral work under supervisors Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: Martin Joachim Kümmel
nodes.summary: Martin Joachim Kümmel is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian-Central Asian studies scholar. He earned his degrees at the University of Freiburg, where he was an Assistent and Akademischer Rat (~1999–2007), before becoming a chair holder at the University of Jena (2013).

nodes.label: Helmut Rix
nodes.summary: Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1950), and Tübingen (Habilitation). He held posts at Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau (1955), the University of Regensburg (1966), and served as professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

nodes.label: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng
nodes.summary: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn and serves on the faculty at Fo Guang University.

nodes.label: Fo Guang University
variants: 佛光人文社會學院宗教學系

nodes.label: Peter Moran
nodes.summary: Peter Moran is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Charles Keyes, alongside other academic and traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Thomas Watters
nodes.description: British diplomat in China and Korea, sinologist
nodes.summary: Thomas Watters was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his B.A. studies at Queen's University Belfast (1857–1861) and Queen's University of Ireland (~1857–1861).

nodes.label: Willem van der Molen
nodes.summary: Willem van der Molen works in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983) and held posts at Leiden University (~1984) and the University of Indonesia.

nodes.label: Michael Comans
nodes.summary: Michael Comans works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong, later serving on the faculty at the University of Sydney (~1989–2005).

nodes.label: Swami Dayananda Saraswati
nodes.description: Hindu monk and founder of Arsha Vidya Gurukulam (1930-2015)

nodes.label: Rahul Peter Das
nodes.description: German professor of South Asian studies (born 1954)
nodes.summary: Rahul Peter Das (b. 1954), an Indologist and linguist, studied under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler, completing his degrees and habilitation at Hamburg. He researched and taught at Hamburg, Bonn, and Groningen before becoming a professor at MLU Halle-Wittenberg (~1994–2020).

nodes.label: Stephen Wootton Bushell
nodes.summary: Stephen Wootton Bushell was a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Guy's Hospital Medical School and the University of London, and held medical posts at Guy's Hospital (1866) and Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

nodes.label: Alexander Rogers
nodes.summary: Alexander Rogers worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at East India Company College from circa 1843 to 1845 and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1845 to 1878.

nodes.label: Henry Beveridge
nodes.description: British linguist and Indian Civil Service officer
nodes.summary: Henry Beveridge (1837–1929) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow (c. 1853–1857) and Queen's University Belfast (1856), later serving in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and as President of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

nodes.label: Peterhouse, Cambridge
variants: Peterhouse College of the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Klaus Ludwig Janert
nodes.description: born:1922|died:1994|; Janert, Klaus Ludwig, 1922-1994; Janert, Klaus L.
nodes.summary: Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and habilitated at the University of Tübingen. He worked as an assistant at the University of Göttingen before holding a full professorship at the University of Cologne (1963–1987).

nodes.label: Christophe Vielle
nodes.summary: Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who has held academic posts at KU Leuven as a Sanskrit professor (attested 2009), the Université catholique de Louvain as a professor (attested 2013), and Ghent University as an associate member (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Robert Deliège
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and religious studies, Robert Deliège studied at the University of Oxford from around 1981 to 1986. He held posts at the University of Kerala and became a professor at the Université catholique de Louvain around 1989.

nodes.label: Jacques Scheuer
nodes.summary: Jacques Scheuer was an indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau, and served as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (~1977–2007) and at Centre Sèvres.

nodes.label: Utz Podzeit
nodes.image: Venia Legendi 1997- Dr. Utz Podzeit mit Mechthild.jpg
nodes.summary: Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna. He held a research stay at the University of Madras and served as a university lecturer in Indology at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff
nodes.jawiki: ウルリヒ・フォン・ヴィラモーヴィッツ＝メレンドルフ
nodes.summary: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff (1848–1931) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Bonn and Berlin, and held professorships at the University of Greifswald, University of Göttingen, and Frederick William University Berlin.

nodes.label: David Ludden
nodes.summary: David Ludden is a historian and Indologist who studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia, the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and New York University beginning in 2007.

nodes.label: Allison Busch
nodes.summary: Allison Busch was an Indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She served as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University.

nodes.label: James B. Apple
nodes.summary: James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his graduate education and received his PhD in 1996 from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he studied under doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne.

nodes.label: Henepola Gunaratana
nodes.summary: Henepola Gunaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied at Vidyasekhara Pirivena, Kelaniya, Buddhist Missionary College, and American University (PhD ~1975–1980). He held posts at the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur, Buddhist Vihara Society, and Georgetown University.

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tenzin Negi
variants: Lobsang Tenzin Negi (legal name Satya Dev Negi)

nodes.label: Glenn H. Mullin
nodes.image: Visit of Telo Tulku to Roerich House, U.B. (3861963599).jpg
nodes.summary: Glenn H. Mullin is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Kalu Rinpoche. He founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.

nodes.label: Mel Weitsman
variants: ソウジュン・メル・ウェイツマン

nodes.label: Reb Anderson
nodes.summary: Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He succeeded Baker and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from around 1986 to 1995.

nodes.label: Elena De Rossi Filibeck
nodes.summary: Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian history under Luciano Petech at Sapienza University of Rome (graduated 1971), where she became an associate professor in 1980.

nodes.label: Stefan Mario Maul
nodes.summary: Stefan Mario Maul is an archaeologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and Freie Universität Berlin. He held posts at Freie Universität Berlin, Heidelberg University as Ordinarius for Assyriology from 1995, and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Søren Sørensen
nodes.summary: Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was an Indology scholar. He held teaching posts at the Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1887 until 1902.

nodes.label: Vilhelm Thomsen
variants: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
ヴィルヘルム・ルズヴィ・ペーター・トムセン
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
nodes.summary: Vilhelm Thomsen was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Randers State School and the University of Copenhagen (PhD 1869), he served at Copenhagen as Privatdozent (1869), associate professor (1875), and professor (1887–1913).

nodes.label: Karl Verner
variants: カール・アドルフ・ヴェルナー
nodes.summary: Karl Verner was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and under August Leskien, subsequently working as a librarian at Halle-Wittenberg (~1876–1883) and as a lecturer in Slavic studies at Copenhagen from 1882.

nodes.label: Marianne Winder
nodes.summary: Marianne Winder (1918–2001) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove, holding posts at Nottingham, University of London, and the Wellcome Trust (~1964–1978).

nodes.label: Wellcome Trust
variants: Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine

nodes.label: Nigel Allan
nodes.summary: Nigel Allan, working in history and archaeology, succeeded Marianne Winder and served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Charles Edmund Godakumbura
nodes.summary: Charles Edmund Godakumbura (1907–1977) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and archaeology. He earned multiple degrees including a PhD and D.Litt. from the University of London, taught at SOAS (~1953–1959), and was Commissioner of Archaeology (1956–1967).

nodes.label: Rudolf Geiger
nodes.summary: Rudolf Geiger studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1913–1919) and held a post at the University of Munich (~1948–1963).

nodes.label: Union Theological Seminary
variants: Union Theological Seminary in New York City
Union Theological Seminary in the City of New York
Union Theological Seminary in New York
Union Theological Seminary, New York City

nodes.label: Bhagwan Dash
nodes.summary: Bhagwan Dash was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi (M.A., PhD). He worked as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

nodes.label: Vaibhav Singh
nodes.summary: Vaibhav Singh is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He earned his PhD from the University of Reading in 2017, where he held a post attested in 2018.

nodes.label: Himanshu Prabha Ray
nodes.summary: Himanshu Prabha Ray (b. 1947) works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where she served as associate professor (c. 1980–2012). She also held posts at Munich and the National Monuments Authority.

nodes.label: Geoff Childs
nodes.summary: Childs specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Tsetan Chonjore, and held posts at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis (attested 2003-2005).

nodes.label: Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute
variants: 財団法人西蔵大蔵経研究会

nodes.label: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
nodes.summary: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a sinologist and historian who studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak. He served as lecturer in Chinese at Leiden in 1946 and as professor from 1956 to 1975.

nodes.label: Robert H. Brower
nodes.description: Professor of far east language and literature (1923–1988)
nodes.summary: A Japanologist, Robert H. Brower studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He taught at Minnesota and Stanford, directed the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies (1963–1964), and chaired Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

nodes.label: Arthur F. Wright
nodes.summary: Arthur F. Wright was a historian and scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard, he taught at Stanford (1947–1959) and became the Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale in 1959.

nodes.label: Steven Lukes
nodes.jawiki: スティーヴン・ルークス
nodes.summary: Steven Lukes works in philosophy. He studied at Oxford under Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard and held posts at Balliol College (1966–1987), European University Institute, University of Florence, University of Siena, London School of Economics (~2001–2006), and New York University (~2006–2021).

nodes.id: I:Information Network Focus on Religious Movements
nodes.label: Information Network Focus on Religious Movements
Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana
nodes.summary: Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana is an Indologist who studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore, and the University of Amsterdam. He held posts at the FRLHT, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and served as a visiting associate professor at the University of Toyama.

nodes.label: Amala Institute of Medical Sciences
variants: Amala Cancer Hospital and Research Center

nodes.id: I:Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions
nodes.label: Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions
variants: Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions

nodes.label: Sebastian Pole
nodes.summary: Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related fields. He completed his studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.

nodes.label: Robert E. Svoboda
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, Robert E. Svoboda studied at the University of Oklahoma and mentored under Aghori Vimalananda (~1975–1983). As of 2008, he held adjunct posts at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

nodes.label: Soon-il Hwang
nodes.summary: Soon-il Hwang works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA at Dongguk University under Seung-won Seo, earned a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, and served as an editorial board member at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Kurt A. Behrendt
nodes.summary: Kurt A. Behrendt, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD from UCLA (~1991–1997). At the Metropolitan Museum of Art, he served as Assistant Curator (~2005–2014) and Associate Curator of South Asian Art (~2014).

nodes.label: Fawad Khan
nodes.summary: Fawad Khan is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies who earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University. He served as Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

nodes.id: I:Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
nodes.label: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
variants: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province of Pakistan
Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Govt. of NWFP

nodes.label: Kirby Flower Smith
nodes.description: American classical philologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Kirby Flower Smith (1862–1918) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University (PhD 1889). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and director of the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).

nodes.label: Wataru Ryose
nodes.summary: Wataru Ryose is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota. Ryose also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

nodes.label: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala
nodes.summary: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala (1884–1956) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served as Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1956).

nodes.label: Sukumar Sen
nodes.image: Sukumar Sen linguist 2020 cover of India cr.jpg
nodes.summary: Sukumar Sen was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Calcutta under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala. He served at the University of Calcutta as lecturer (1930) and Khaira Professor (1954), and as Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India.

nodes.label: David Kopf
nodes.summary: David Kopf was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1960 to 1964. He held an academic post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 2003.

nodes.label: Willard Van Orman Quine
variants: ウィラード・クワイン
ウィラード・ヴァン・オーマン・クワイン
nodes.image: Willard Van Orman Quine on Bluenose II in Halifax NS harbor 1980.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ウィラード・ヴァン・オーマン・クワイン
nodes.summary: Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at Oberlin College and Harvard University, where he spent most of his career as Junior Fellow (1933–1936), Assistant Professor (1940), and Pierce Chair of Philosophy (1948–1978).

nodes.label: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri
nodes.summary: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bishop Heber College and the University of Madras (Ph.D.). He held posts at Bishop Heber College, Rajah's College, and Annamalai University (1942–1947).
