nodes.label: Rasmus Rask
variants: ラスムス・クリスチャン・ラスク
nodes.summary: Rasmus Rask was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen. He held library and professorial appointments at Copenhagen between 1814 and 1831, teaching Benjamin Thorpe and Adolf Ivar Arwidsson.

nodes.label: Stella Kramrisch
nodes.summary: Stella Kramrisch was an indology and art history scholar. She completed her doctorate at the University of Vienna under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski. She held appointments at Visva-Bharati University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Pennsylvania (1950–1993).

nodes.label: H. G. Narahari
nodes.summary: H. G. Narahari was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he held posts at the Adyar Library and Research Centre and the University of Madras.

nodes.label: Charles Philip Brown
nodes.summary: Charles Philip Brown (1798–1884) studied at East India Company College and with traditional teachers. An Indologist and linguist, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and as Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1879).

nodes.label: Baliram Shukla
nodes.summary: Baliram Shukla works in philosophy and Indology. He has held appointments at Savitribai Phule Pune University, including Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.image: Shunryu Suzuki at Zen Mountain Center (cropped).png
nodes.summary: Shunryu Suzuki (1904-1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Eihei-ji, and under several teachers. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

nodes.label: Richard Baker
variants: ゼンテツ・リチャード・ベーカー
nodes.summary: Richard Baker (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley, and trained under Shunryu Suzuki. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center (1962), serving as its abbot from 1971 to 1984, and founded Dharma Sangha.

nodes.label: Huston Smith
nodes.summary: Huston Smith was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1940–1945). He held professorships at MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse University (1973–1983), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1990–2012).

nodes.label: Tassajara Zen Mountain Center
variants: タサハラ禅マウンテンセンター（禅心寺）

nodes.label: San Francisco Zen Center
variants: サンフランシスコ禅センター

nodes.label: Medawachchiye Dhammajothi
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies and Indology scholar Medawachchiye Dhammajothi studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing University. He became a senior lecturer at the University of Colombo around 2000.

nodes.id: I:Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka
nodes.label: Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka
variants: Buddhist and Pāli University in Sri Lanka
Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka

nodes.label: Nanjing University
variants: 南京大学中華文化研究院

nodes.label: Srisa Chandra Vasu
nodes.description: Indian judge, writer, and scholar in Sanskrit
nodes.summary: Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Government College University, Lahore, worked as a vakil at Allahabad High Court, became a fellow at the University of Allahabad, and founded the Panini Office in 1891.

nodes.label: Johanna Narten
nodes.description: Professor of Indo-European and Indo-Iranian Linguistics (1930-2019)
nodes.summary: Johanna Narten specialized in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied at Saarland under Ernst Zinn (1951) and at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (PhD 1955–1961, Habilitation ~1961–1971), later serving as an assistant there (1973–1977).

nodes.label: Jadunath Sarkar
nodes.summary: Jadunath Sarkar was an Indian historian and archaeologist who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (M.A. ~1892). He held posts at Patna College (1899–1926) and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).

nodes.label: Denis Sinor
nodes.summary: Denis Sinor (1916–2011) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at Cambridge, subsequently teaching at Cambridge (1948–1962) and directing at Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

nodes.label: Griffith University
variants: グリフィス大学現代アジア研究所

nodes.label: Herbert Franke
nodes.summary: Herbert Franke (1914–2011) was a sinologist who studied under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer at Cologne, Bonn, and Berlin. He held posts at the University of Cologne, University of Munich, and served as President of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Kazu Uehara
nodes.summary: Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1992). He held academic positions at the University of Miyazaki (~1957–1968) and Seijo University (~1968–1995).

nodes.label: Yasuro Abe
nodes.summary: Yasuro Abe is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Wako and Otani universities. He held posts at Osaka, Otemae, and Nagoya universities, later joining Ryukoku University in 2019.

nodes.label: Masahiro Asada
nodes.summary: Masahiro Asada (b. 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1973), where he later served as an assistant professor (~1985–1991).

nodes.label: Otemae University
variants: 大手前女子大学文学部

nodes.id: I:The Society for the History of Buddhism
nodes.label: The Society for the History of Buddhism
Jacqueline I. Stone
nodes.summary: Jacqueline I. Stone specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at SFSU and UCLA under William R. LaFleur, and served as professor at Princeton (1990–2019) with an affiliation at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kuroda Institute
variants: Kuroda Institute for the Study of Buddhism and Human Values

nodes.label: Nanjing Normal University
variants: Nanjing Normal University, Research Center for the Nanjing Massacre

nodes.label: Qingzhi Zhu
nodes.summary: Qingzhi Zhu works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He has held posts as a professor at Peking University (attested 2004) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Jinchuan Wan
nodes.summary: Jinchuan Wan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who has held professorships at National Central University (attested 2010) and Fo Guang University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Christoph Harbsmeier
nodes.description: German professor of Chinese linguistics and syntax
nodes.summary: Christoph Harbsmeier is a scholar of Sinology and linguistics educated at Merton College, Oxford, and the University of Copenhagen. He taught at Universiti Sains Malaysia and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980, later holding advisory professorships in China.

nodes.label: Shu-fen Chen
nodes.summary: Shu-fen Chen is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at National Tsing Hua University, where she later held a professorship attested in 2010. She studied under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock.

nodes.label: Ryan Richard Overbey
nodes.summary: Ryan Richard Overbey is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Brown and Harvard universities and has held positions at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley, and Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Todd Thornton Lewis
nodes.summary: Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Theodore Riccardi Jr., Alex Wayman, and others, and served as Murray Distinguished Professor of Arts and Humanities at the College of the Holy Cross.

nodes.label: Lothar Ledderose
nodes.summary: Sinologist and art historian Lothar Ledderose studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne. His main appointments included positions at Princeton, Harvard, the National Palace Museum, and a long tenure as professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010).

nodes.label: Graduate Theological Union
variants: Graduate Theological Union in Berkeley, California

nodes.label: Wai-lun Tam
nodes.summary: Wai-lun Tam is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He became a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

nodes.label: David Faure
nodes.summary: David Faure is a historian and sinologist who earned a sociology PhD at Princeton (~1970–1976). He lectured in Modern Chinese History at St Antony's College from 1990 and served as director at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2006).

nodes.label: Michel Strickmann
nodes.summary: Michel Strickmann was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden, the EPHE, and Paris Diderot (PhD ~1972–1979). He held positions at the University of Bordeaux (~1977–1978) and UC Berkeley (1978).

nodes.label: Dodrupchen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught pupils including Ronald M. Davidson and Tulku Thondup.

nodes.label: Qinni Liu
nodes.summary: Qinni Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

nodes.label: Kirill Solonin
nodes.summary: Kirill Solonin (born 1969) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Fo Guang University (~2005–2013) and at Renmin University of China (~2013).

nodes.label: Alf Sommerfelt
nodes.summary: Alf Sommerfelt was a scholar in linguistics. He founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924 and served as a professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

nodes.label: Olivier Lacombe
nodes.summary: Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris, where he later held a post (~1959–1970) before teaching at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

nodes.label: Institut Français Frankfurt
variants: French Insitute at Frankfurt am Main

nodes.label: Tu Weiming
nodes.summary: Tu Weiming (born 1940) specializes in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Tunghai University and Harvard, taught at Princeton, UC Berkeley, and Harvard, and later directed Peking University's Institute for Advanced Humanistic Studies.

nodes.label: Harvard-Yenching Institute
variants: ハーバード燕京研究所

nodes.label: Richard DeMartino
nodes.description: American psychoanalyst and religious studies scholar (1922-2013)

nodes.label: András Róna-Tas
nodes.image: András Róna-Tas is rector at the Univrsity of Szeged, 14.02.1991..JPG
nodes.summary: András Róna-Tas (born 1931) works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and held posts at Szeged (1968–2002), Vienna, SCAS, and the IATS.

nodes.label: Anam Thubten Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Anam Thubten Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and has served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

City University of Hong Kong Center for East Asian and Comparative Philosophy

nodes.label: Carl Olson
nodes.summary: Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Mentored by John Y. Fenton, he served as Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

nodes.label: Tai-shing Wut
nodes.summary: Tai-shing Wut is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Sangharakshita
nodes.description: Founder of the Friends of the Western Buddhist Order (1925–2018)
nodes.summary: Sangharakshita was a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Chien Ming Chen, and Dhardo Rinpoche. He founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

nodes.label: Triratna Buddhist Community
variants: Friends of the Western Buddhist Order

nodes.label: Wilt L. Idema
nodes.summary: Wilt L. Idema (born 1944) is a Sinologist. He earned degrees from Leiden University, where he studied under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, and served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976–1999) and Harvard University (2000–2013).

nodes.label: David Schaberg
nodes.summary: David Schaberg is a Sinologist who studied at Stanford and Harvard University. Joining the University of California, Los Angeles in 1996, he has served there as professor and dean of Humanities (2012).

nodes.label: Edward Kamens
nodes.summary: Edward Kamens is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University from ~1970 to 1982 and joined its faculty around 1986, becoming the Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

nodes.label: Shuming Liang
nodes.summary: Shuming Liang (1893–1988) was a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Shuntian Middle School. He joined the philosophy department at Peking University in 1917 and founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and China Democratic League.

nodes.label: Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h
nodes.summary: Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier (1988) and later served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1993–2008).

nodes.label: Kannika Wimonkasem
nodes.native: กรรณิการ์ วิมลเกษม

nodes.label: Thich Thien Nghiem
nodes.summary: Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Delhi, attested in 2012, under the supervision of Shalini Singhal.

nodes.label: David Ownby
nodes.summary: David Ownby is a historian and sinologist who studied at Vanderbilt and earned his Ph.D. from Harvard. He held posts at Southern Methodist University and the Université de Montréal (1994–2023), later joining the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology.

nodes.label: Vincent Goossaert
nodes.summary: Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1993–1997). He held posts at the CNRS (~1998–2012), CUHK (2007), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2012).

nodes.label: Zhe Ji
nodes.summary: Zhe Ji works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned a PhD in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007 and was an associate professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).

nodes.label: Benjamin A. Elman
variants: ベンジャミン・エルマン
ベンジャミン・A・エルマン
nodes.image: Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) at the lecture 'The Role of Shanghai in Building Modern Science in China in the 19th Century'.png
nodes.jawiki: ベンジャミン・エルマン
nodes.summary: Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) is a sinologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held major appointments at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University (2002).

nodes.label: Friederike Assandri
nodes.summary: Friederike Assandri is a sinologist and scholar of religious studies who studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer and pursued doctoral studies at Heidelberg University, where she also held an attested post in 2013.

nodes.label: Tufts University
variants: Tufts University School of Veterinary Medicine

nodes.label: Karen Nelson Villanueva
nodes.summary: Karen Nelson Villanueva is a scholar in religious studies and related fields. She earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.

nodes.label: Marta Sernesi
nodes.summary: Marta Sernesi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Turin (-2007) and held an appointment as Gastprofessorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shayne Clarke
nodes.summary: Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, and UCLA under Gregory Schopen. His posts include Associate Professor at McMaster University and Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Sonya S. Lee
nodes.summary: Sonya S. Lee specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu, taught at Swarthmore College (2003–2004), and held posts at Stanford University and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Hung Wu
nodes.summary: Hung Wu is an art historian and Sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard University (~1980–1987). He taught at Harvard before becoming the Harrie A. Vanderstappen Distinguished Service Professor of Art History at the University of Chicago in 1994.

nodes.label: Jerome Silbergeld
nodes.summary: Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Stanford and the University of Oregon. He held professorships and administrative posts at the University of Washington (~1975-2001) and Princeton University (~2001-2016).

nodes.id: I:University of North Carolina at Charlotte
nodes.label: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
variants: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

nodes.label: Richard A. Hutch
nodes.summary: Richard A. Hutch (born 1945) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).

nodes.label: Southern Illinois University Carbondale
variants: Morris Library, Southern Illinois University at Carbondale

nodes.label: William R. LaFleur
variants: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.summary: William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago, and taught at Princeton (~1971–1976), UCLA (~1978–1989), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

nodes.label: Sibaraj Chetry
nodes.summary: Sibaraj Chetry specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He was supervised for his doctorate by Sibnath Sarma, studied under several other teachers, and served as a Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College as attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Huiwen Zhuang
nodes.summary: Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under supervisor Kirill Solonin, and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Aaron P. Proffitt
nodes.summary: Aaron P. Proffitt studied at CU Boulder, the Inter-University Center, and the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback and others. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology, he became assistant professor of Japanese Studies at University at Albany, SUNY (~2015).

nodes.label: Valdo H. Viglielmo
variants: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.jawiki: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.summary: Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy who studied at Pennsylvania, Harvard, Tokyo, and Gakushuin. He taught at Harvard, Princeton, and other Japanese universities before serving as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–2002).

nodes.label: Dan Smyer Yü
nodes.summary: Dan Smyer Yü is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of California, Davis. He served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

nodes.label: David L. McMahan
nodes.summary: David L. McMahan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, and has served as a professor of religious studies at Franklin & Marshall College.

nodes.label: Hugh Gray
nodes.summary: Hugh Gray was an Indology scholar who attended Battersea Grammar School. He later served as a lecturer at SOAS, University of London, from around 1964 to 1970.

nodes.label: Drolma
nodes.summary: Drolma is a scholar of Tibetology who completed an M. Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Hanna Havnevik
variants: ハンナ・ハヴネヴィク
nodes.summary: Hanna Havnevik works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Oslo, serving as professor (attested 2006–2008) and later as professor emerita (attested 2026).

nodes.label: J. Thomas Rimer
nodes.summary: J. Thomas Rimer (born 1933) is a Japanologist educated at Princeton and Columbia. He held faculty posts at Washington University in St. Louis, UCLA, the University of Maryland, College Park, and the University of Pittsburgh.

nodes.label: Tomoko Masuzawa
nodes.summary: Tomoko Masuzawa, working in religious studies and history/archaeology, studied at International Christian University, Yale University, and UC Santa Barbara (PhD 1985). She held faculty posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1987–2001) and University of Michigan (1999, ~2001–2021).

nodes.label: James Robson
nodes.image: James Robson (academic) on Filled with Meaning.png
nodes.summary: James Robson (born 1965) specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at UC Santa Barbara (~1983–1987) and Stanford (PhD ~1996–2002), he taught at Williams College, Michigan (2004–2008), and Harvard, becoming Harvard-Yenching Institute director in 2024.

nodes.label: Lori Meeks
nodes.summary: Lori Meeks (born 1976) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Princeton (~1999–2003) under Jacqueline I. Stone and joined the University of Southern California as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies (~2004).

nodes.label: Masayuki Taira
nodes.summary: Masayuki Taira studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1979). Specializing in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology, he held posts at Kansai University (~1981–1995), Osaka University (~1995–2016), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2016).

nodes.label: Shunsho Manabe
nodes.summary: Shunsho Manabe (1939-2021) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1958-1962), taught at Hosen Gakuen College (~2004-2010), and was a professor at Shikoku University as attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Shenpen Hookham
nodes.summary: Shenpen Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido, as well as under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Tsewang Gyurme
nodes.summary: Tsewang Gyurme is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He served as President of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Lama Kunga Rinpoche
nodes.description: Buddhist Lama of the Sakya school
nodes.summary: Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959.

nodes.label: Brian Cutillo
nodes.summary: Brian Cutillo (1945–2006) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and under Geshe Wangyal.

nodes.label: Supree Kanjanapisarn
nodes.summary: Supree Kanjanapisarn is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at Assumption University under the supervision of Veerachart Nimanong, attested in 2011.

nodes.label: Veerachart Nimanong
nodes.native: วีรชาติ นิมะนงค์

nodes.label: Fabio Rambelli
variants: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.jawiki: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.summary: Fabio Rambelli specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari University, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Naples, holding posts at Sapporo University and later as Distinguished Professor and Shinto Studies Chair at UCSB.

nodes.label: Gregory P. A. Levine
nodes.summary: Gregory P. A. Levine (born 1963) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. Educated at Oberlin College and Princeton University, he became an associate professor in the Department of History of Art at UC Berkeley around 2005.

nodes.label: Lin Heng
nodes.summary: Lin Heng is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Steve Odin
nodes.summary: Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Stony Brook University under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey, and became a Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʱi at Mānoa in 1982.

nodes.label: Graham Parkes
nodes.summary: Graham Parkes (born 1949) specializes in philosophy and Japanology, earning a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. He served at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1979–2008; Emeritus ~2008) and University College Cork (~2008–2013) as professor of philosophy.

nodes.label: Jason M. Wirth
nodes.image: Jason Martin Wirth (born 1963) in the video 'Everybody's Climate 2025 – Jason Wirth on Humanity in the Anthropocene'.png
nodes.summary: Jason M. Wirth works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki and became professor of philosophy at Seattle University circa 2007.

nodes.label: Graham Priest
variants: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.jawiki: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.summary: Graham Priest (born 1948) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and the LSE under John Lane Bell, he held posts at Melbourne (Emeritus ~2000), Arche at St Andrews (~2007), and CUNY Graduate Center (Distinguished Professor ~2009).

nodes.label: Lili Zheng
nodes.summary: Lili Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University (attested 2011) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.

nodes.label: Uma Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Carmel College, Banaras Hindu University, University Law College, and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti. She taught at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

nodes.label: D. Devahuti
nodes.description: D. Devahuti, 1929-1988; taught at universities of Malaya, Queensland, and Delhi

nodes.label: Ron Garry
nodes.summary: Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ron Garry studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Usha Nilsson
nodes.summary: Usha Nilsson was an Indologist and linguist. She served as a faculty member and later Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Berthe Jansen
nodes.description: Assistant Professor of Tibetan Studies at Leiden University
nodes.summary: Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and Oxford, completing her doctorate under Jonathan A. Silk in 2010. She held posts at Heidelberg University (~2015–2016) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

nodes.label: Vincent Breugem
nodes.summary: Vincent Breugem specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Lucia Dolce, attended Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono Universities, and completed his MA (1996) and PhD (2012) at Leiden University, where he was a research fellow in 2012.

nodes.label: Tulku Thondup
nodes.summary: Tulku Thondup (1939–2023) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

nodes.label: David E. Cooper
nodes.summary: David E. Cooper is a philosopher who studied at St Edmund Hall from around 1961 to 1965. He lectured at the University of Oxford in 1967 and served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University from 1986 to 2008.

nodes.label: Simon P. James
nodes.summary: Simon P. James works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University, serving as a tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

nodes.label: University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point
variants: University of Wisconsin at Stevens Point

nodes.label: Latika Lahiri
nodes.summary: Latika Lahiri is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji as an Indian Government scholar in 1958 and later held a post at the University of Delhi.

nodes.label: Tan Chung
nodes.summary: Tan Chung earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University, specializing in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He served at the University of Delhi (1964–1978), Jawaharlal Nehru University (1978–1994), Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (1994), and the Institute of Chinese Studies.

nodes.label: Michael Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

nodes.label: Sonam Chhoki
nodes.summary: Sonam Chhoki works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. at SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

nodes.label: Thierry Mathou
nodes.summary: Thierry Mathou is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, and served as an associated political scientist at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique around 1993.

nodes.label: Ronald E. Purser
nodes.summary: Ronald E. Purser is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and other fields who studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985. He served at Loyola University Chicago (~1991–1997) and became Professor für Management at San Francisco State University (~1997).

nodes.label: San Francisco State University
variants: School of Business der San Francisco State University
サンフランシスコ州立大学

nodes.label: Pamela D. Winfield
nodes.summary: Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Paula Arai
nodes.summary: Paula Arai works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Kalamazoo College, Waseda, and Harvard under Nagatomi and Smith. She has held posts at Vanderbilt, LSU, Carleton College, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

nodes.label: Patricia Fister
variants: パトリシア・フィスター
nodes.jawiki: パトリシア・フィスター
nodes.summary: Patricia Fister specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Kansas (~1976–1983) and held posts at the University of Kansas (1984), Hakuho Women's College (1998), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1991–2019).

nodes.label: Michaela Mross
nodes.summary: Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and earned her PhD from the University of Munich in 2014. She held positions at UC Berkeley and Stanford University, where she is Assistant Professor of Japanese Buddhism (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Diane E. Riggs
nodes.summary: Diane E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at UCLA (2010) under William M. Bodiford and held posts at Pepperdine University, Kenyon College (attested 2010), and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Daniel Timothy Aitken
nodes.summary: Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania. He studied under Parimal G. Patil, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.

nodes.label: University of Tasmania
variants: Centre for Applied Philosophy and Ethics

nodes.label: Chanju Mun
nodes.summary: Chanju Mun (1964–) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002), supervised by Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda, and taught by John D. Dunne.

nodes.label: Valerie Hansen
nodes.summary: Valerie Hansen (born 1958) is a historian and sinologist who studied at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. She held a post at East China Normal University and served as an associate professor and professor at Yale University.

nodes.label: Yifa
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist nun, scholar and writer
nodes.summary: Yifa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Yale University. She founded the Woodenfish Foundation and served as department head and dean at the University of the West (~1996–2002).

nodes.label: Reginald A. Ray
nodes.summary: Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Mircea Eliade, Chögyam Trungpa, and others. He taught at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002) and served as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).

nodes.label: Dainin Katagiri
nodes.summary: Dainin Katagiri (1928–1990) was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar. He studied at Eihei-ji and Komazawa University, served as priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission, became interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Shodo Harada
nodes.summary: Shodo Harada is a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He studied at Shofuku-ji under Mumon Yamada from 1962 to 1982, became abbot at Sōgen-ji in 1982, and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

nodes.label: John Daido Loori
nodes.image: Daido Roshi in the Buddha Hall.jpeg
nodes.summary: John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Rutgers and trained under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi, whom he succeeded. He taught at Naropa University (1974) and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery (~1980–2009).

nodes.label: Richard Sorabji
nodes.summary: Richard Sorabji is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Pembroke College, Oxford. He held academic posts at Cornell University (circa 1962–1970), King's College London (circa 1970–2000), and Gresham College (circa 2000–2006).

nodes.label: Dagfinn Føllesdal
variants: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
ダグフィン・フォレスダール
nodes.jawiki: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
nodes.summary: Dagfinn Føllesdal (1932–2026) was a philosopher and linguist. He earned degrees at the University of Oslo and Harvard, where he completed his Ph.D. under Willard Van Orman Quine. He taught at Harvard, Stanford, and the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: Jiang Wu
nodes.summary: Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Nankai University and Harvard University, supervised by Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, and Zhichao Chen, and later served as Professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).

nodes.label: Yonsei University
variants: Institute of East and West Studies at Yonsei University

nodes.label: Gregory Adam Scott
nodes.summary: Gregory Adam Scott works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, and was educated at Columbia University. As of 2026, he is attested at the University of Edinburgh and as Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester.

nodes.label: Thierry Meynard
nodes.summary: Thierry Meynard is a sinologist and philosopher who earned his Ph.D. at Peking University under Yulie Lou. He served as professor of philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (around 2006) and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

nodes.id: I:The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
nodes.label: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
variants: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies

nodes.label: Scott Pacey
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, Scott Pacey earned his doctorate from the Australian National University (2011). He held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, the Australian National University, and the University of Manchester (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Ken McLeod
nodes.summary: Ken McLeod works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an M.Sc. at the University of British Columbia, studied with Kalu Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa, served as resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling, and founded Unfettered Mind.

nodes.label: Stephen H. Phillips
nodes.summary: Stephen H. Phillips is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor of philosophy (attested 1999) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026) at the University of Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Tomy Augustine
nodes.summary: Tomy Augustine is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Madras under C. S. Sundaram and Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal (PhD). He held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: T. S. Devadoss
nodes.summary: T. S. Devadoss is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held academic posts at the University of Madras, including serving as Professor (attested 1994, 2008).

nodes.label: Michela Clemente
nodes.summary: Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and conducted postdoctoral research under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015). She held a post as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny
nodes.description: Polish bibliologist, paper historian, conservator of monuments.
nodes.summary: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw (~1996–2001) and earned a PhD from Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~2002–2007). She held posts at Cornell University (attested 2009) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

nodes.label: Field Museum of Natural History
variants: フィールド自然史博物館

nodes.label: Thomas Cleary
nodes.summary: Thomas Cleary worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earned a PhD from Harvard University, and obtained a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Jonathan Christopher Cleary
nodes.summary: Jonathan Christopher Cleary (1947–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his doctoral studies at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and held an instructional post at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Kazuaki Tanahashi
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Tanahashi (born 1933) is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Soichi Nakamura (~1950–1960). He was a scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and a fellow at the World Academy of Art and Science.

nodes.label: Mary Clabaugh Wright
nodes.summary: Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) was a sinologist and historian. Educated at Vassar College and Radcliffe College (PhD ~1939–1951), she curated Stanford's China collection (1947) before becoming associate professor (1959) and full professor (1964) at Yale University.

nodes.label: Torkel Brekke
nodes.summary: Torkel Brekke works in religious studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Oslo and Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later holding posts at Oslo, PRIO (2016–2020), Oslo Metropolitan University (2019–2023), and MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society (2023).

nodes.label: Kenryu Tsuji
nodes.summary: Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He pursued his education at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Gerd J. R. Mevissen
nodes.summary: Gerd J. R. Mevissen specializes in Indology and archaeology/history. His career includes posts at the Free University of Berlin, where he was attested as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter.

nodes.id: I:National Museum Institute of the History of Art, Conservation and Museology
nodes.label: National Museum Institute of the History of Art, Conservation and Museology
Alka Patel
nodes.summary: Alka Patel works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and Harvard University, and served as Associate Professor at the University of California, Irvine.

nodes.label: Edward S. Casey
nodes.summary: Edward S. Casey is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, Yale (~1968–1978), and Stony Brook University (~1978), later serving as American Philosophical Association president (2009–2010).

nodes.label: Rebecca Redwood French
nodes.summary: Rebecca Redwood French is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Washington and Yale University. She held law faculty posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 1996–2003) and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Rafal Stepien
nodes.summary: Rafal Stepien works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure, and held appointments at Wadham College (2012–2013) and Harvard University (2015).

nodes.label: Chün-fang Yü
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, Chün-fang Yü studied at Columbia University (~1965–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001; Sheng Yen Professor Emerita attested 2026).

nodes.label: École Normale Supérieure
variants: Husserl Archives at the École normale supérieure (ENS/CNRS)

nodes.label: Philippe Turenne
nodes.summary: Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

nodes.label: Yaroslav Komarovski
nodes.summary: Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes and the University of Virginia, later holding a Mellon postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (attested 2011–2015).

nodes.label: Peter Schwieger
nodes.summary: Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He held a chair in Tibetology at Bonn (2001) and a visiting professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin (2001).

nodes.label: Dieter Schuh
nodes.summary: Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, where he earned his PhD and Habilitation. He served as außerplanmäßiger Professor at Bonn (1978–2007) and directed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Christian Wittern
nodes.summary: Christian Wittern works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields. He studied under Seizan Yanagida and held posts at Hanazono University (attested 2011) and Kyoto University, including as professor (attested 1993, 2008).

nodes.label: Eliot Deutsch
nodes.summary: Eliot Deutsch was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his PhD from Columbia University (1956–1960). He held posts at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006), and edited Philosophy East and West.

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Thittila
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Thittila was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University (~1934–1937). He served as a librarian at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1937–1938) and taught Buddhist philosophy at the University of Rangoon (1952).

nodes.label: Reiho Masunaga
nodes.summary: Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya. He served as a teacher at Komazawa University (attested 1956).

nodes.label: Kamala Tiyavanich
nodes.summary: Kamala Tiyavanich specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

nodes.label: David K. Wyatt
variants: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.jawiki: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.summary: David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University. He held academic posts at SOAS, the University of Michigan, and Cornell University (1969–2002), and served as president of the Association for Asian Studies in 1993.

nodes.label: Richard Polenberg
nodes.summary: Richard Polenberg was a historian of America who studied at Brooklyn College (BA) and Columbia University (PhD). He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and as a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University.

nodes.label: Trung Huynh
nodes.summary: Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Huynh earned a PhD at the University of the West under the supervision of Darui Long, attested in 2016.

nodes.label: Gendun Chopel
nodes.summary: Gendun Chopel (1903–1951) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Drisha, Labrang (1920), Kumbum (circa 1920–1927), and Drepung (1927) monasteries, and under Sherab Gyatso (1927) and Gendun Tendzin Gyatso.

nodes.label: Frances Wood
nodes.summary: Frances Wood is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Newnham College and Peking University before serving at the British Library from circa 1977 to 2013.

nodes.label: Joseph Margolis
variants: ジョセフ・ザルマン・マーゴリス
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・マーゴリス
nodes.summary: Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who completed his MA at Columbia University. He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University beginning in 1991.

nodes.label: Sandra A. Wawrytko
nodes.summary: Sandra A. Wawrytko works in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held positions at San Diego State University, where she is attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.

nodes.label: Megan Bryson
nodes.summary: Megan Bryson, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Rachelle M. Scott
nodes.summary: Rachelle M. Scott works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).

Oriental Collection, Hungarian Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Géza Bethlenfalvy
nodes.summary: Géza Bethlenfalvy worked in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Lajos Ligeti and held posts at the University of Delhi (1970), ELTE, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

nodes.label: Zsóka Gelle
nodes.description: Hungarian Tibetologist, translator, writer, filmmaker and guide
nodes.summary: Zsóka Gelle (born 1967) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Vienna, Gelle held fellowships at ELTE and the Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016).

nodes.label: Tsutomu Horio
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Horio is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1990).

nodes.label: Benjamin Bogin
nodes.summary: Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also studied with Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: John J. Holder
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, John J. Holder studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford and posts at St. Norbert College (attested 2006 and 2018).

nodes.label: Eric Huntington
nodes.summary: Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Gary A. Tubb.

nodes.label: Dina Bangdel
nodes.summary: Dina Bangdel was a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held academic appointments at Ohio State University (~1999–2002) and Virginia Commonwealth University (~2002–2017).

nodes.label: Andy Rotman
nodes.summary: Andy Rotman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at CIHTS and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, among others. He has held posts at Smith College (attested 2013–2026) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo
variants: ジャムヤン・キェンツェ・ワンポ
nodes.summary: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a master in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Rigdzin Zangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught figures such as Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

nodes.label: Peter Alan Roberts
nodes.summary: Peter Alan Roberts works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied with traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed doctoral research under Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

nodes.label: Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche
nodes.image: Thrangu Rinpoche on 24 May 2016 face detail, from- 17th Karmapa performs Long Life Offering to Kenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (1933–2023) studied under Khenpo Gangshar and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He served as abbot at Rumtek Monastery (~1976), Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981), and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).

nodes.label: Somphong Santacitto
nodes.summary: Somphong Santacitto works in the field of Buddhist studies. He earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Phra Suthithammanuwat
nodes.native: พระสุทธิธรรมนิเทศ

nodes.label: Watchara Ngamchitcharoen
nodes.native: วัชระ งามจิตรเจริญ

nodes.label: Brian D. Ruppert
nodes.summary: Brian D. Ruppert (born 1962) specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Willis Stoesz. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) and Bates College (~2018).

nodes.label: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani
nodes.summary: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of Perry Link.

nodes.label: Perry Link
nodes.summary: Perry Link (born 1944) is a Sinologist who completed his B.A. at Harvard (~1962–1966). He held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

nodes.label: James Ishmael Ford
nodes.summary: James Ishmael Ford (born 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sonoma State University, Pacific School of Religion, and under Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant, later founding Boundless Way Zen and the Empty Moon Zen Network.

nodes.label: Jiyu-Kennett
nodes.summary: Jiyu-Kennett was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Durham, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji under several teachers. She served as head priest at Unpukuji (~1968–1969) and founded and led Shasta Abbey (~1970–1996).

nodes.label: Jonathan C. Gold
nodes.summary: Jonathan C. Gold works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

nodes.label: Michael Eido Luetchford
nodes.summary: Michael Eido Luetchford (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned an engineering degree from the University of Bradford, studied under traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima (~1977–2007), and founded Windbell Publications.

nodes.label: Gudo Wafu Nishijima
nodes.summary: Gudo Wafu Nishijima studied law at the University of Tokyo and trained under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. A Buddhist studies scholar, he lectured at the University of Tokyo and the Eastern Institute, and founded Dogen Sangha International in 2007.

nodes.label: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche is a scholar and teacher in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

nodes.label: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson
nodes.summary: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins, and also studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.

nodes.label: Alexander Macmillan
nodes.summary: Alexander Macmillan is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the SIT Graduate Institute under advisor Elizabeth Morrison, attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Morrison
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her doctoral studies under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, and held academic posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Chögyam Trungpa
variants: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
チョギャム トゥルンパ
チューギャム・ドゥンパ
nodes.image: Trungpa from Khenpo gangshar2 cropped image.jpg
nodes.jawiki: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
nodes.summary: Chögyam Trungpa was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure who studied at Oxford and under teachers including Khenpo Gangshar. He served as spiritual advisor at Young Lamas Home School and founded Samye Ling, Naropa University, and Shambhala International.

nodes.label: Aruna Haldar
nodes.summary: Aruna Haldar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose. She held a teaching post at Patna University.

nodes.label: Girindrasekhar Bose
nodes.summary: Girindrasekhar Bose studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and as president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

nodes.label: Joachim Gentz
nodes.summary: Joachim Gentz works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held a post as Junior Professor at the University of Göttingen and posts as Reader (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026) at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Perry Schmidt-Leukel
nodes.summary: Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

nodes.label: Adam Yuet Chau
nodes.summary: Adam Yuet Chau is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Williams College and completed his PhD at Stanford University (2001), later serving as university lecturer (attested 2011–2015) and Professor of the Anthropology of China (attested 2026) at Cambridge.

nodes.label: Philip Clart
nodes.description: German Sinologist, Professor of Chinese Studies at Leipzig University, Germany
nodes.summary: Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from ~1990 to 1997. In ~2008, he became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig.

nodes.label: Michael Stanley-Baker
nodes.summary: Michael Stanley-Baker specializes in Sinology and religious studies, earning an MA at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2006). He held posts at Nanyang Technological University, University of Leipzig, Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and University of Pittsburgh.

nodes.label: Harold Stewart
nodes.summary: Harold Stewart was an Australian scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

variants: Editorial Committee of the BDK English Tripitaka

nodes.label: David Tracy
nodes.summary: David Tracy is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He taught at Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago (1969–2006).

nodes.label: Douglas L. Berger
nodes.summary: Douglas L. Berger is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Indology. He taught at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (attested 2007–2014) and holds posts at Leiden University as professor and Centre for Intercultural Philosophy director (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Akimichi Eda
nodes.summary: Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.

nodes.label: Lita Peipina
nodes.summary: Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under supervisor Jens Braarvig, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

nodes.label: Stephen Prothero
nodes.summary: Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar. He studied at Yale and Harvard University, completing his Ph.D. under William R. Hutchison (1986–1990). In ~1996 he joined Boston University, becoming Professor Emeritus of Religion in America.

nodes.label: Duncan Ryūken Williams
nodes.summary: Duncan Ryūken Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. His career includes posts at Harvard, UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Kosho Uchiyama
nodes.summary: Kosho Uchiyama (1912–1998) studied Western philosophy at Waseda University (~1934–1937) and studied under Kodo Sawaki from 1941. In Buddhist studies and philosophy, he taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (~1937–1939) and was abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).

nodes.label: Kodo Sawaki
nodes.summary: Kodo Sawaki (1880–1965) studied at Senju-ji, Shinshu Takada-ha Senmon Gakko, and Horyuji Kangakuin, studying under several teachers. In Buddhist studies and philosophy, he served as a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).

nodes.label: Sotan Oka
nodes.summary: Sotan Oka (1860–1921) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He served as a professor, dean, and president at Komazawa University and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

nodes.label: Ian Kishizawa
nodes.summary: Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka. He later taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

nodes.label: See Mui Yian
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, See Mui Yian pursued a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Warren Lee Todd
nodes.summary: Warren Lee Todd is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche, and Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Alison Denton Jones
nodes.summary: Alison Denton Jones works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Martin King Whyte as her doctoral supervisor, as well as under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

nodes.label: Martin King Whyte
nodes.summary: Martin King Whyte is a Sinologist and sociologist educated at Cornell and Harvard (PhD 1971). He held faculty posts at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University, and Harvard University, where he became professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Allan H. Barr
nodes.summary: Allan H. Barr is a Sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford in 1983. He held a post as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College.

nodes.label: Margaret H. Dornish
nodes.summary: Margaret H. Dornish is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Daniela Berti
nodes.summary: Daniela Berti is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Siena. She was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya in 2004.

nodes.label: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya
variants: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya, Paris

nodes.label: Gilles Tarabout
nodes.summary: Gilles Tarabout works in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Madeleine Biardeau. Attested in 2004, he served as a senior fellow at the CNRS, a member of EHESS, and exchange program director at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.

nodes.id: I:Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme
nodes.label: Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme
variants: Maison des Sciences de l'Homme, Paris

nodes.label: Cortland Dahl
nodes.summary: Cortland Dahl works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and received mentorship from Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

nodes.label: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under numerous teachers, including Rasvir Das and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He held teaching posts at Men-Tsee-Khang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1959–1967).

nodes.label: Myosei Tatsuguchi
nodes.summary: Myosei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested in 1987) and later became professor emeritus there (attested in 2015).

nodes.label: Robert Charles Zaehner
nodes.image: Internationaal Theologisch Congres toekomst van de religie, religie van de toeko, Bestanddeelnr 925-4729.jpg
nodes.description: British spy and academic on Eastern religions (1913–1974)
nodes.summary: Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, he was Oxford's Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and an All Souls fellow from 1952.

nodes.label: Stephen Harris
nodes.summary: Stephen Harris specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of New Mexico in 2014 and serves as a University Lecturer in Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kyoko Tokuno
nodes.summary: Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who taught Douglas Ober. She held academic posts at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington (attested 2017 as professor).

nodes.label: Dudjom Rinpoche
nodes.image: Dudjom Rinpoche with Prince Paljor Namgyal and Maharani Kunzang Dechen Tshomo Namgyal.jpg
nodes.summary: Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mindrolling and Dorje Drak monasteries. He founded the International Nyingma Society and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Matthew T. Kapstein, and Alexander Berzin.

nodes.label: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley
nodes.summary: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under F. E. L. Priestley and doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held an attested post at the University of Toronto in 1991.

nodes.label: Julia Ching
nodes.summary: Julia Ching was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned her doctorate from Australian National University. After teaching at Columbia and Yale, she became Professor of Religion, Philosophy, and East Asian Studies at the University of Toronto in 1978.

nodes.label: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby
nodes.summary: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby worked in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. He held posts at McGill (1960–1964), Yale (1966–1971), and Trinity College and the University of Toronto (~1971–1999).

nodes.label: Jacob Holubeck
nodes.summary: Jacob Holubeck specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Eric Stephen Goodell
nodes.summary: Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner.

nodes.label: Kristin Johnston Largen
nodes.summary: Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she held posts as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

nodes.label: Brandon Dotson
nodes.summary: Brandon Dotson (born 1978) works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at Oxford under Charles Ramble and a habilitation at the University of Munich, holding posts at SOAS (~2005–2009) and the University of Munich (~2010–2018).

nodes.label: Jongmyung Kim
nodes.summary: Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist and religious studies and history. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

nodes.label: Central Academy of Fine Arts
variants: Central Academy of Fine Arts in Beijing
国立北平芸術専科学校

nodes.label: Kristofer Schipper
nodes.summary: Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a Sinologist and religious studies scholar. Educated in Paris and Taiwan, he held posts at EFEO, EPHE (1972–2002), CNRS, Collège de France, Leiden University, and in China at Fuzhou and Minnan Normal universities.

nodes.label: Helen Baroni
nodes.summary: Helen Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, and joined the faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa around 1993.

nodes.label: Shou-chien Shih
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Sinology, Shih was a professor at National Taiwan University (~1990–2007) and served as director of the National Palace Museum (~2004–2006).

nodes.label: Alice Y. Tseng
nodes.summary: Alice Y. Tseng specializes in Japanology and history and archaeology. She was a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang and is attested as a professor at Boston University in 2013.

nodes.label: Brian J. Nichols
nodes.summary: Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under Anne Carolyn Klein and also studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies.

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Program for Chinese language studies at Tsinghua University
Inter-University Board of Chinese Language Studies

nodes.label: Tansen Sen
nodes.summary: Tansen Sen works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding a post at Baruch College attested in 2003.

nodes.label: Takeshi Umehara
nodes.summary: Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku, Ritsumeikan, and Kyoto City University of Arts, and served as director of the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1987–1995).

variants: sDe dge dbon stod slob grwa at sDe dge dgon chen Monastery
