variants: sDe dge Ku se gSer ljongs bshad grwa

nodes.label: Sarah Aoife Richardson
nodes.summary: Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD in 2016 at the University of Toronto under the supervision of Jenny Purtle.

nodes.label: Julia F. Andrews
nodes.summary: Julia F. Andrews is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Brown University, the University of California, Berkeley, and Harvard University, and she joined the faculty of Ohio State University circa 1987.

nodes.label: Frank J. Hoffman
nodes.summary: Frank J. Hoffman works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and completed his doctorate under Stewart Sutherland, having also studied under Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, and others.

nodes.label: Trent Walker
nodes.summary: Trent Walker works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where his doctoral supervisor was Alexander von Rospatt.

nodes.label: Tina Rasmussen
nodes.summary: Tina Rasmussen is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. She completed her MA under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw.

nodes.label: Pa-Auk Sayadaw
nodes.native: ဖားအောက်ဆရာတော်

nodes.label: Jan Chozen Bays
variants: ジャン・澄禅・ベイズ
nodes.summary: Jan Chozen Bays (b. 1945) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Swarthmore College and UC San Diego, trained under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada, and served as abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery around 2002.

nodes.label: Taizan Maezumi
nodes.summary: Taizan Maezumi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, SFSU, and under Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission (1956) and founded ZCLA.

nodes.label: Neal Donner
nodes.summary: Neal Donner is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Wenjie Qin
nodes.summary: Wenjie Qin is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu.

nodes.label: Wei-ming Tu
nodes.summary: Wei-ming Tu is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University. He held positions at Princeton, UC Berkeley, East-West Center, Harvard University, and Harvard-Yenching Institute, along with several visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Bing Chen
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Bing Chen held posts as Professor at Sichuan University (circa 1987) and at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Lhakpa Tsering
nodes.summary: Lhakpa Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He has served as a professor at Tibet University and as Assistant Professor of Tibetan Language and Literature at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Stephanie Roemer
nodes.summary: Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

nodes.label: Eberhard Sandschneider
nodes.summary: Eberhard Sandschneider studied at Saarland University (~1975–1986, PhD). In sinology and international relations, he served at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

nodes.label: German Council on Foreign Relations
variants: Forschungsinstitut der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Auswärtige Politik

nodes.label: Naoki Nabeshima
nodes.summary: Naoki Nabeshima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who founded Ryukoku University and served there as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).

nodes.label: David Matsumoto
nodes.summary: David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as Director of the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as President Emeritus of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

nodes.label: Jing-shen Tao
nodes.summary: Jing-shen Tao is a historian and Sinologist. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and Indiana University Bloomington (Ph.D. ~1963–1967), later serving as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).

nodes.label: Christian Coseru
nodes.description: American philosopher and scholar of Buddhist philosophy
nodes.summary: Christian Coseru studied at the University of Bucharest and Australian National University. A specialist in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he held posts at the College of Charleston (~2006) and UC Berkeley (~2018), alongside research affiliations in India.

nodes.label: C. W. Huntington, Jr.
nodes.summary: C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980-1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as professor at Hartwick College (~1992-2020).

nodes.label: Kevin Buckelew
nodes.summary: Kevin Buckelew works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College and was doctoral supervised by Bernard Faure, Chün-fang Yü, and Zhaohua Yang, alongside studying under Chao-heng Liao, Courtney Bender, Fumiko Nazikian, and Yan Ling.

nodes.label: Chao-heng Liao
nodes.summary: Chao-heng Liao specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held positions at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Valeria Gazizova
nodes.summary: Valeria Gazizova is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her master's degree at the University of Oslo, where she studied under Hanna Havnevik and MA supervisor Per Kværne.

nodes.label: Loden Sherab Dagyab
nodes.summary: Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Drepung Monastery and under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, he was director of Tibet House New Delhi (1964–1966) and Tibetologist at the University of Bonn (1966).

nodes.label: Martin Brauen
nodes.summary: Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at the Universities of Delhi and Zurich. He held curatorial and leadership posts at the University of Zurich's Ethnographic Museum (1975) and the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

nodes.label: Michael J. Sweet
nodes.summary: Michael J. Sweet specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and later served there as a clinical assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry (attested 1996, 2006).

nodes.label: John Ross Carter
nodes.summary: John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard (doctoral work under Wilfred Cantwell Smith, circa 1967–1972), he served as a professor at Colgate University (circa 1972–2006).

nodes.label: Amita Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Amita Chatterjee is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.

nodes.label: John M. Koller
nodes.summary: John M. Koller worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studying at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles Alexander Moore, and George T. Artola. He served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

nodes.label: Daya Krishna
nodes.summary: Daya Krishna (1924–2007) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Ex-Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (circa 1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Shigenori Nagatomo
nodes.summary: Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Shigenori Nagatomo taught Kin Cheung and Tao Jiang. He held posts at Temple University, where he is attested as a professor of religious studies in 1999 and attested in 2017.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Philosophy, Russian Academy of Sciences
nodes.label: Institute of Philosophy, Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Institute of Philosophy, Academy of Sciences USSR

nodes.label: Diego Loukota
nodes.summary: Diego Loukota is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed an MA at Peking University and earned his PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2019.

nodes.label: Susan Andrews
nodes.summary: Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (attested 2013), where her doctoral supervisor was Chün-fang Yü, and studied under Bernard Faure, David Max Moerman, Michael I. Como, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Michael I. Como
nodes.summary: Michael I. Como is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Sinology who studied under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He serves as Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Gendun Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Gendun Rinpoche (1918–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He served as abbot and retreat master at Dhagpo Kagyu Ling from circa 1977 to 1997, and founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, Dhagpo Kundreul Ling, Dhagpo Dargye Ling, and Dhagpo Dedrol Ling.

nodes.label: Bokar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Bokar Rinpoche studied under traditional teacher Kalu Rinpoche from circa 1960 to 1989. A figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held a post at Bokar Monastery from circa 1984 until 2004.

nodes.label: Michael M. Broido
nodes.summary: Michael M. Broido worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held an academic post at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Geshe Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: Geshe Tashi Tsering works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1970–1990) and Gyuto Monastery, later holding teaching positions at Kopan Monastery (~1992–1994) and Jamyang Buddhist Centre from 1994.

nodes.label: Qiwen Xiao
nodes.summary: Qiwen Xiao specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at Fo Guang University, where she earned a Master of Arts under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda
nodes.summary: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011) and as a Senior Fellow at the ICHR.

nodes.id: I:Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
variants: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute for Asian Studies

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Saksena
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy and Indology, Saksena held professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Malhotra
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Malhotra is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the East-West Center (c. 1964–1969) and founded the Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality.

nodes.label: Gregory Forgues
nodes.summary: Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie from the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, and studied under Birgit Kellner as well as several traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Chanmyay Sayadaw U Janakabhivamsa
nodes.native: ဦးဇနကာဘိဝံသ

nodes.label: Pema Bhum
nodes.summary: Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who previously served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, and as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

nodes.label: Morton Klass
nodes.summary: Morton Klass was an anthropologist who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, completing his doctorate in 1959. He held faculty posts at Bennington College (1959), Barnard College (1965), and Columbia University (1982–1985).

nodes.label: Margaret Mead
variants: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.jawiki: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.summary: Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at DePauw, Barnard (BA), and Columbia (MA, PhD under Franz Boas). She held posts at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969), Columbia (1954–1978), Fordham (1968–1970), and Rhode Island (1970).

nodes.label: Jan Jakob Maria de Groot
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ヤーコプ・マリア・デ・ホロート
nodes.summary: Jan Jakob Maria de Groot (1854–1921) specialized in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz, later serving as professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).

nodes.label: Xiaoting Wei
nodes.summary: Xiaoting Wei is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng Mei Ku, attested in 2004.

nodes.label: Jinshi Fan
nodes.summary: Jinshi Fan is a historian and archaeologist in Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University (~1958–1963) under Su Bai and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy from 1984 to 2014.

nodes.label: Luangpor Teean Jittasubho
nodes.native: หลวงพ่อเทียน จิตฺตสุโภ

nodes.label: Andrew Quintman
nodes.summary: Andrew Quintman works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

nodes.label: Masaharu Imai
nodes.summary: Masaharu Imai (b. 1942), a specialist in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology, earned his doctorate at Tokyo University of Education in 1977. He taught at Ibaraki University (1977) and became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba in 2006.

nodes.id: P:Bstan 'dzin zla grags chos kyi rgyal mtshan
nodes.label: Bstan 'dzin zla grags chos kyi rgyal mtshan
Lobsang Yongdan
nodes.summary: Lobsang Yongdan is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (-2014). He held postdoctoral posts at the University of Bonn and MPIWG.

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
variants: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, Berlin

nodes.label: Fernando Jose Benetti
nodes.summary: Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University under the doctoral supervision of Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

nodes.label: William H. Nienhauser, Jr.
nodes.summary: William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a sinologist who studied at Indiana University Bloomington and Bonn. He held visiting positions at several universities before serving as full professor and Halls-Bascom Professor of Classical Chinese Literature at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1983.

nodes.label: Kristina Myrvold
nodes.summary: Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She was a redaktör and doctoral candidate at Lund University (attested 2005, 2008) and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Gurinder Singh Mann
nodes.summary: Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Baring Union Christian College, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia, he taught at Columbia (1988–1999) and held the Sikh Studies Chair at UC Santa Barbara (1999–2015).

nodes.label: Hew McLeod
nodes.summary: Hew McLeod specialized in Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Nelson College, the University of Otago, and SOAS University of London, and later held a post at the University of Otago (~1971–1997).

nodes.label: Anne Hardgrove
nodes.summary: Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College and the University of Michigan before joining the University of Texas at San Antonio, where she held a post in 2000.

nodes.id: I:University of Texas at San Antonio
nodes.label: University of Texas at San Antonio
variants: University of Texas at San Antonio

nodes.label: Paul Copp
nodes.summary: Paul Copp specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at UMass Amherst and Princeton (Ph.D. attested 2005 under Stephen F. Teiser), and has held posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago (attested 2014–2026).

nodes.label: Ch'ing-mao Cheng
nodes.summary: Ch'ing-mao Cheng is a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who studied at National Taiwan University and Princeton University. He held positions at UC Berkeley, UMass Amherst, and served as Founding Chair at National Dong Hwa University.

nodes.label: Donald E. Gjertson
nodes.summary: Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Ching-yu Wang and held a faculty post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst from around 1976 to 2007.

nodes.label: Mohan Wijayaratna
nodes.description: Sinhalese anthropologist and translator specializing in Buddhism

nodes.label: Royall Tyler
nodes.summary: Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at Harvard and Columbia, earning his doctorate under Donald Keene (~1967–1977). He taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, and Oslo, before serving as head of the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000).

nodes.label: Huai-Chin Nan
nodes.summary: Huai-Chin Nan studied at the Republic of China Military Academy, University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology, he taught at the Military Academy, Chinese Culture University, National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

nodes.label: Chinese Culture University
variants: College of Chinese Culture Graduate School in Taipei
Institute of Chinese Culture in Taipei
中国文化大学印度研究所

nodes.label: Huynh Kim Lan
nodes.summary: Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under thesis advisers Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.

nodes.label: Gareth Fisher
nodes.summary: Gareth Fisher works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. After earning a PhD in socio-cultural anthropology at the University of Virginia in 2006, he served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

nodes.label: Nirupam Chakma
nodes.summary: Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Tilak Kariyawasam
nodes.summary: Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and as Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Fa Qing
nodes.summary: Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his dissertation at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, and Xiaojie Yang.

nodes.label: Wei Wu
nodes.summary: Wei Wu is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the International Buddhist College. Attested in 2026, Wu is an Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

nodes.label: Ki-yong Rhi
nodes.summary: Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held positions at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and was attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

nodes.label: Martin Willson
nodes.summary: Martin Willson (d. 2005) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

nodes.label: Michael Weiers
nodes.summary: Michael Weiers was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. After completing his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965), he served there as a professor from 1972 to 2003 and became an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University (~1989).

nodes.label: Geshe Jampa Tegchok
nodes.summary: Geshe Jampa Tegchok worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sera Monastery and held posts as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery and resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha.

nodes.label: Daniel L. Overmyer
nodes.description: Scholar of the history of Chinese popular religions
nodes.summary: Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia from around 1973 to 2001.

nodes.label: Dieter B. Kapp
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Dieter B. Kapp completed his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger. He held positions at Heidelberg (1971–1987) and served as director of the Institut für Indologie und Tamilistik at the University of Cologne (1990–2006).

nodes.label: Peter James Gilks
nodes.summary: Peter James Gilks is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, under teachers including John Powers and several Geshes, and earned a PhD from the Australian National University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués
nodes.summary: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs (2016) and has held posts at the Shan State Buddhist University, SUTD, and the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Di Luo
nodes.summary: Di Luo specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016), supervised by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge, after completing an MA supervised by James Steele.

nodes.label: Bettine Birge
nodes.summary: Bettine Birge is a sinologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University, studying under Wm. Theodore de Bary, Wing-tsit Chan, and Masaaki Sugiyama. She was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

nodes.label: Richard von Glahn
nodes.summary: Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles circa 1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.

nodes.label: Jeff Watt
nodes.summary: Jeff Watt is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology who studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima. He held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Justin Shimeld
nodes.summary: Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Jeff Malpas
nodes.summary: Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. He led the philosophy programme at Murdoch University and served as professor and emeritus distinguished professor at the University of Tasmania.

nodes.label: Sonam Thakchoe
nodes.summary: Sonam Thakchoe specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, and held a post there around 2003.

nodes.label: Barry Kerzin
nodes.image: Barry Kerzin, American Professor of Medicine and Buddhist monk.gif
nodes.summary: Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, the University of Southern California, and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He held posts at the University of Washington, CIHTS, and the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Shili Xiong
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology, Shili Xiong studied at the China Institute of Inner Learning under Jian Ouyang (1920). He held posts at Boone University, Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1947–1948).

nodes.label: Zongsan Mou
nodes.summary: Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Peking University and under Shili Xiong. He held professorships at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1968–1974) and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1974–1995).

nodes.label: Philip Whalen
nodes.summary: Philip Whalen was active in Buddhist and religious studies. After earning a BA at Reed College (~1946–1951), he studied under Richard Baker (1972) and held posts at Dharma Sangha (1984), South Ridge Zendo (~1984–1987), and Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

nodes.label: Noboru Miyata
nodes.summary: Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and folklore history. He studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, later serving as Professor of Folklore at Tsukuba (~1978–1997) and at Kanagawa University (~1997–2000).

nodes.label: Oleg Grabar
nodes.summary: Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton (PhD ~1955), he held posts at ASOR, the University of Michigan, Harvard, and IAS.

nodes.label: Jörg Heimbel
nodes.summary: Jörg Heimbel specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from the University of Hamburg in 2014 under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Hamburg, the University of Munich, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Elizabeth English
nodes.summary: Elizabeth English works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford in 1999 under the doctoral supervision of Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: Sung-Bae Park
nodes.summary: Sung-Bae Park is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD under Lewis Lancaster. He was an assistant professor at Dongguk University (~1968–1972) and later became Professor Emeritus at Stony Brook University.

nodes.label: Alfred Bloom
variants: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.summary: Alfred Bloom worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He completed a Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held posts at the University of Oregon (1961–1970), the Institute of Buddhist Studies (Dean, 1986–1994), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1970–2017).

nodes.label: University at Albany, SUNY
variants: State University of New York at Albany
University at Albany (State University of New York)
University at Albany, State University of New York
State University of New York, Albany

nodes.label: Ruben L. F. Habito
nodes.summary: Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila University, the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, and Sophia University. He held positions at Sophia, Ryukoku University, and Southern Methodist University (1989).

nodes.label: Yutai Ikeda
nodes.summary: Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he was attested as Emeritus Professor in 2006.

nodes.label: Kenshi Kusano
nodes.summary: Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and served as a professor there (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Shunsho Terakawa
nodes.summary: Shunsho Terakawa (1928-2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950-1953). He served as an emeritus professor at Otani University (~1963-2000).

nodes.label: Daniel W. Kent
nodes.summary: Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia. He held instructor posts at the University of Virginia (attested 2010) and Mary Baldwin University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Brian Daizen Victoria
variants: ブライアン・アンドレー・ヴィクトリア
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ヴィクトリア
nodes.summary: Brian Daizen Victoria (born 1939) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned degrees from Komazawa University and Temple University and held posts at the University of Auckland, Antioch University, Adelaide, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Nebraska Wesleyan University
variants: ネブラスカ・ウェズリアン大学

nodes.label: Xue Yu
nodes.summary: Xue Yu is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Posts include assistant professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010), Visiting Professor of Buddhism at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), and professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Baruch College
variants: Baruch College, City University of New York

nodes.label: Navina Lamminger
nodes.summary: Navina Lamminger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Munich under the doctoral supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Stacey Van Vleet
nodes.summary: Stacey Van Vleet is a Tibetology, sinology, and history scholar. She studied under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed a PhD and held an academic post at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Geoffrey Barstow
nodes.summary: Barstow works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia (PhD), training also under Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, and became assistant professor of religious studies at Oregon State University (~2013).

nodes.label: Takao Moriyasu
nodes.summary: Takao Moriyasu was a scholar of Central Asian history who studied at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University. He served as associate professor at Kanazawa University and Osaka University, and as professor at Osaka University from 1994 to 2012.

nodes.label: Tokio Takata
nodes.summary: Tokio Takata is a Sinology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, and served as professor at Kyoto University (1997–2014) and Fudan University (2016–2022).

nodes.label: Yutaka Yoshida
nodes.summary: Yutaka Yoshida (born 1954) specializes in history/archaeology, Japanology, and linguistics. Educated at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and University of Tokyo, he held posts at Hitotsubashi (1983–2018), Kyoto University (~2006–2020), Research Center for Peace and Reconciliation (2008), and Center of the Tokyo Raids (2019).

nodes.label: James Burnell Robinson
nodes.summary: James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundup Sopa. Around 1975, he became an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa.

nodes.label: Cuong T. Mai
nodes.summary: Cuong T. Mai is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under John R. McRae, later becoming an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: Reiko Ohnuma
nodes.summary: Reiko Ohnuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at UC Berkeley and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. She held posts at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Gereon Kopf
nodes.summary: Gereon Kopf focuses on philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University and under Yasuo Yuasa, holding posts at Luther College and the University of Hong Kong, alongside research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan universities.

nodes.label: John C. Maraldo
nodes.summary: John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He spent his academic career at the University of North Florida, where he eventually became distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy.

nodes.label: Seijun Ishii
nodes.summary: Seijun Ishii studied at Komazawa University from around 1977 to 1987. Working in the field of Buddhist studies, he became a professor at Komazawa University around 2003.

nodes.label: Tairyu Tsunoda
nodes.summary: Tairyu Tsunoda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Ruth W. Dunnell
nodes.summary: Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi, and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.

variants: Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich (ETHZ)
Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zürich
Swiss Federal Institute of Technology at Zurich

nodes.label: Purchase College, State University of New York
variants: Purchase College, State University of New York

nodes.label: Stephen G. Covell
nodes.description: professor of world religions and cultures
nodes.summary: Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone (~1995–2001) and held a post at Western Michigan University (~2003).

nodes.label: Wendi L. Adamek
nodes.summary: Wendi L. Adamek, a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, earned a PhD from Stanford in 1998. She held a post at Barnard College and became Professor and Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Sadajiro Sugiura
nodes.summary: Sadajiro Sugiura worked in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania (PhD), and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University, where he became professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Bo Jiang
nodes.summary: Bo Jiang works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

nodes.label: Soochow University
variants: School of Foreign Languages, Soochow University

nodes.label: Mary Evelyn Tucker
nodes.summary: Mary Evelyn Tucker (b. 1949) is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Japanology who earned her PhD at Columbia University. She served as Professor of Religion at Bucknell University (~1989–2006) and became a professor at Yale University (~2006).

nodes.label: Donald Harper
nodes.summary: Donald Harper is a sinologist who held posts at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and the University of Chicago, where he served as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryoshun Okubo
nodes.summary: Ryoshun Okubo specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Waseda University, he became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism there around 1993, while also holding posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Phanindra Nath Bose
nodes.description: Bengali historian, writer and professor at Santiniketan

nodes.label: Shashibhusan Dasgupta
nodes.description: Scholar in philosophy, languages and literature, particularly Bengali literature, literary critic, author, theologian
nodes.summary: Shashibhusan Dasgupta worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, where he earned his MA and PhD, and later served as a lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

nodes.label: Dung Ngoc Duong
nodes.summary: Dung Ngoc Duong specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Boston University by 2001 under doctoral supervisor Malcolm David Eckel.

nodes.label: Diego Cosmelli
nodes.summary: Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at École Polytechnique, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela.

nodes.label: Antoine Lutz
nodes.summary: Antoine Lutz completed a PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the supervision of Francisco Varela.

nodes.label: Christine Mollier
nodes.summary: Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She served as a researcher and Director of Research at CNRS and as Numata Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Jacques Giès
nodes.summary: Jacques Giès specialized in sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon, and taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and École du Louvre (1998–2008), later serving as president of the Guimet Museum (2008–2011).

nodes.label: Koun Yamada
variants: Yamada Koun Zenshin (山田 耕雲, Yamada Kōun)
nodes.summary: Koun Yamada (1907–1989) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at First Higher School, he studied under Konan Sokan, Sogen Asahina, Kanzui Hanamoto, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, whom he succeeded from 1961 to 1989 after founding Kamakura Haku-un-kai in 1953.

nodes.label: Dzongsar Institute
variants: Dzongsar Institute for Advanced Studies of Buddhist Philosophy and Research in Bir, India
Dzongsar Institute of Advanced Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Kumbum Monastery
variants: クンブム・チャンパーリン寺

nodes.label: Dhivan Thomas Jones
nodes.summary: Dhivan Thomas Jones specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He served as an associate lecturer at Open University (~2007) and held a post at the University of Chester in 2019.

nodes.label: Shan Shan Zhao
nodes.summary: Shan Shan Zhao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Mark Rowe
nodes.summary: Mark Rowe is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He has held a faculty post at McMaster University, serving as Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2015, 2026).

nodes.label: St Edmund's College
variants: St. Edmunds College, University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Margaret Gouin
nodes.summary: Margaret Gouin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.

nodes.label: Thinh Canh Quang
nodes.summary: Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. at the University of the West, attested in 2007, under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya and teachers Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

nodes.label: Patricia Buckley Ebrey
nodes.summary: Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist. She earned degrees from the University of Chicago and Columbia University, later holding faculty posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

nodes.label: Kate Wharton
nodes.summary: Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Peter Fenner
nodes.summary: Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy and held a post at Deakin University. He studied under advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, as well as traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Lindsay G. McCune
nodes.summary: Lindsay G. McCune specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. McCune studied under MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas as well as Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.

nodes.label: Nancy G. Lin
nodes.summary: Nancy G. Lin specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Columbia University and earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. In 2026, she is attested as faculty at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

nodes.label: Hermann Kulke
nodes.summary: Hermann Kulke worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Hermann Goetz, at the University of Madras, University of Freiburg, and Heidelberg University. His main appointments included Heidelberg University (1967–1988) and Kiel University (1988–2003).

nodes.label: Emanuel Sarkisyanz
nodes.summary: Emanuel Sarkisyanz (1923–2015) was a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tehran and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1948–1952). In 1967, he became a department head at Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Werner Sundermann
nodes.summary: Werner Sundermann was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967–1970), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1992), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).

Deutsche Akademie der Wissenschaften in Berlin
Institut für Orientforschung der Deutschen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin

nodes.label: Yanling Chen
nodes.summary: Yanling Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under Yongdong Shi and studied under the traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Agehananda Bharati
nodes.summary: Agehananda Bharati was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Akademisches Gymnasium and the University of Vienna (~1946–1948). He taught at Delhi, Banaras Hindu, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, Tokyo, and Kyoto, before serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

nodes.label: Ron Leifer
nodes.summary: Ron Leifer, active in Buddhist studies and other fields, studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) studied at Thrangu Monastery and under 8th Traleg Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught at Rumtek Monastery (1967) and became abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra (1978).

nodes.label: Krishnanath Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indology scholar who studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

nodes.label: Ramaranjan Mukherji
nodes.summary: Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist who completed his degrees at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Sanskrit department head at Jadavpur, vice chancellor at the University of Burdwan (1970-1984) and Rabindra Bharati University, and chancellor of National Sanskrit University.

nodes.id: I:University of Pennsylvania Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology
nodes.label: University of Pennsylvania Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology
variants: University of Pennsylvania Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology

nodes.label: J. P. Mallory
nodes.summary: J. P. Mallory (born 1945) is a scholar of archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Occidental College and UCLA, he served as Professor of Prehistoric Archaeology at Queen's University Belfast from circa 1997 to 2011.

nodes.label: James Matthew Baskind
nodes.summary: James Matthew Baskind is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Stanley Weinstein at Yale University, where he earned a PhD (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University from around 1964 to 1969 and served as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Tsuneki Nishiwaki
nodes.summary: Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1971) and held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1976–1995) and Kyoto University (~1995–2007).

nodes.label: Tom De Rauw
nodes.summary: Tom De Rauw specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Ann Heirman and holds an AAP post at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Anthony Cerulli
nodes.summary: Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies, having completed his studies at the University of Chicago. Around 2014, he served as Director of Graduate Studies and Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: C. Pierce Salguero
nodes.description: professor of Asian history and religious studies
nodes.summary: C. Pierce Salguero studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (PhD 2010). A specialist in Buddhist studies and history, he joined Pennsylvania State University as professor in 2010 and became editor-in-chief of Asian Medicine in 2016.

nodes.label: Christoph Kleine
nodes.description: German japanologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Christoph Kleine is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Marburg. He held posts at the University of Munich, the University of Leipzig, and the Hobogirin Institute.

nodes.label: Mervin Viggo Hanson
nodes.summary: Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, having also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.

nodes.label: Kendall Marchman
nodes.summary: Kendall Marchman specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Mario Poceski and earned his PhD at the University of Florida in 2015.

nodes.label: Si Ti La
nodes.summary: Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under doctoral supervisor J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014), following studies with multiple traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Osvald Sirén
nodes.summary: Osvald Sirén, a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology, completed his doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki. He held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923), Harvard and Yale (1916–1917), the Guimet Museum (1924–1925), and Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

nodes.label: Erik-Jan Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian and linguist who completed his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012), and became a professor at Leiden University in 1997.

nodes.label: City College of New York
variants: College of the City of New York
City College in New York City

nodes.label: A. H. Armstrong
nodes.summary: A philosopher educated at Jesus College, Cambridge, he held posts at Swansea, University of Malta, Beaumont College, and Cardiff. He served as Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972) and founded Dionysius in 1977.

nodes.label: Joseph Loizzo
nodes.summary: Joseph Loizzo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at Amherst, Harvard, and under Robert A. F. Thurman. He served as a Visiting Scholar of Religion at Columbia University and founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science.

nodes.label: Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science
variants: Nalanda Institute for Meditation and Healing

nodes.label: Kennard Lipman
nodes.summary: Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther and worked as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Gaton Ngawang Lekpa
nodes.summary: Gaton Ngawang Lekpa (1864–1941) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and later taught Shenphen Nangwa and Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima.

nodes.label: Culadasa
nodes.summary: Culadasa (1944–2021) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu, served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011), and taught Matthew Immergut.

nodes.label: Matthew Immergut
nodes.summary: Matthew Immergut studied under Culadasa (attested 2011) and works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He is attested in 2011 as Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

nodes.label: Namgyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Namgyal Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary, the University of Michigan, and under traditional teachers including Mahasi Sayadaw and the 16th Karmapa, later founding Kagyu Samye Ling and the Dharma Centre of Canada.

nodes.label: Sun-Ah Choi
nodes.summary: Sun-Ah Choi works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Choi earned a PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi, having also studied under Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

nodes.label: Robert S. Nelson
nodes.summary: Robert S. Nelson is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University and New York University. He held professorships at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and Yale University (~2005–2021).

nodes.label: Jaś Elsner
nodes.summary: Jaś Elsner works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge (BA, PhD), Harvard, and the Courtauld Institute, later holding posts at the Courtauld, Corpus Christi College, and the University of Oxford as professor from 2014.

nodes.label: Aden Kumler
nodes.summary: Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at Chicago, Toronto, Harvard (PhD ~1999–2007), and the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies. She served as assistant professor at the University of Chicago (2007) and became professor at the University of Basel (2020).

nodes.label: Carl Gustav Jung
nodes.jawiki: カール・グスタフ・ユング
nodes.summary: Carl Gustav Jung worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Wilhelmsgymnasium, Pädagogium Basel, and earned a medical degree at the University of Basel (1895–1900). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905–1913), ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and Basel (1944).

nodes.label: Erwin Rousselle
nodes.summary: Erwin Rousselle studied at Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, and Darmstadt, training under F. E. A. Krause, Max Walleser, and Alexander von Staël-Holstein. He taught at Peking, Tsinghua, and Frankfurt universities, and directed the Sino-Indian Institute and China-Institut Frankfurt.

nodes.label: Richard Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tübingen. He served as a guest professor at Peking University (1923) and held the chair for Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924, which he founded in 1925.

nodes.label: David L. Gosling
nodes.summary: David L. Gosling is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and was affiliated with the University of Cambridge, attested in 2001.

variants: St Stephen's College, University of Delhi
St. Stephen’s College der University of Delhi

variants: Académie des Sciences Sociales de Shanghai
Academy of Social Science of Shanghai

nodes.label: Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences
variants: Académie des Sciences Sociales de Chengdu

nodes.label: Ramin Etesami
nodes.summary: Ramin Etesami is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Richard J. Davidson
nodes.image: Rajesh Kasturirangan at Mind and Life.jpg
nodes.summary: Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University (~1968–1972) and Harvard University (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as a psychology professor from 2001 to 2017.

nodes.label: Benjamin Brose
nodes.description: American cultural historian of religion in China
nodes.summary: Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Stanford (~2003–2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. He was an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2009–2016).

nodes.label: Erik J. Hammerstrom
nodes.summary: Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as an assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Randy J. LaPolla
nodes.summary: Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He served as professor at City University of Hong Kong (~1996–2006) and held a post at Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai (2021).

nodes.label: Tak Pui Sze
nodes.summary: Tak Pui Sze is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh
nodes.summary: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Brigitte Marschall
nodes.summary: Brigitte Marschall (born 1957) earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna, where she later served as an associate professor (außerordentliche Universitätsprofessorin, ~2000) and taught Mungunchimeg Batmunkh.

nodes.label: Guo Jun
nodes.summary: Guo Jun works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Monash University, the University of Sydney, and Fuyan Buddhist Institute, he studied under Song Nian, Sheng Yen, and Qinyin, and served as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery (attested 2013).

nodes.label: George Lakoff
nodes.native: ジョージ・P・レイコフ
variants: ジョージ・P・レイコフ
nodes.summary: A linguist and philosopher, Lakoff studied at MIT (~1959–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1963–1966). He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969) and served as Professor of Linguistics at the University of California, Berkeley (1972–2016).

nodes.label: Mark Johnson
nodes.jawiki: マーク・ジョンソン (哲学者)

nodes.label: Glenn Wallis
nodes.summary: Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter, and taught Sonam Kachru.

nodes.label: Alexander Berzin
nodes.summary: Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and with traditional teachers including Geshe Wangyal. He co-founded the translation bureau at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

nodes.label: Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1914–1983) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Geshe Lharampa degree at Ganden Monastery, held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and Alexander Berzin.

International Organizing Committee for the UN Day of Vesak

nodes.label: Kamal K. Sridhar
nodes.summary: Kamal K. Sridhar is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She served at Stony Brook University as director, attested in 2007, and as Professor Emerita, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Shikaripur N. Sridhar
nodes.summary: Working in linguistics and indology, Shikaripur N. Sridhar served as Chair (attested 2007) and Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2026) at Stony Brook University.

nodes.label: Akira Takeda
nodes.summary: Akira Takeda (1930–2021) specialized in Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1949–1959) under Takeshiro Kuraishi, and later held posts at the University of Tokyo (1961–1991), Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1977–1988), and Meikai University (~1988–2001).

nodes.label: Charles Taliaferro
nodes.summary: Charles Taliaferro (b. 1952) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, Harvard Divinity School, the University of Rhode Island, and Brown University, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).

nodes.label: Charlene Makley
nodes.summary: Charlene Makley works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Roy Rappaport and completed her PhD under Norma Diamond at the University of Michigan by 1999, later becoming an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

nodes.label: Roy Rappaport
nodes.summary: Roy Rappaport worked in religious studies and anthropology, completing his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as Chair of the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and was president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

nodes.label: Marco Walther
nodes.summary: Marco Walther is a Tibetologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Jamie Hubbard
nodes.summary: Jamie Hubbard is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University and under Minoru Kiyota at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD), later holding professorships at Smith College (attested 2016, 2026).

variants: Becket Institute, St Hugh's College, Oxford
