nodes.description: Indian epigraphist, archaeologist and art historian

nodes.label: Eishoji Zen Center
variants: Eishoji Zen training and practice facility

nodes.label: Bingtao Ma
nodes.summary: Bingtao Ma, working in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned an MA from Peking University (by 2008) and a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Cécile Ducher
nodes.summary: Cécile Ducher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein, later serving as a research fellow there.

nodes.label: Charles Taylor
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・マーグレイヴ・テイラー
nodes.summary: Charles Taylor (b. 1931) studied at McGill University and Balliol College, Oxford. A philosopher, he held faculty posts at the Université de Montréal (~1961–1966), McGill University (~1961–1998 as Professor of Political Science), and Northwestern University (~2002–2012).

nodes.label: Zhiru Ng
nodes.summary: Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Ng earned an MA under Luis Oscar Gómez at the University of Michigan and a PhD under Robert M. Gimello at the University of Arizona.

nodes.label: Michel Clasquin-Johnson
nodes.description: Professor of Religious Studies at the University of South Africa
nodes.summary: Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at the University of South Africa from ~1989 through his doctoral thesis completion (~1994–1999), and joined the faculty there in 1990.

nodes.label: Bryan W. Van Norden
nodes.summary: Bryan W. Van Norden specializes in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Stanford University from around 1985 to 1991 and served as a professor in the Philosophy and Chinese & Japanese departments at Vassar College from around 1996 to 2020.

nodes.label: Chi-wah Chan
nodes.summary: Chi-wah Chan works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and was a teaching assistant at CUHK.

nodes.label: Patrice Ladwig
nodes.summary: Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Bristol and at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
variants: Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
Max Planck Institute of Social Anthropology

nodes.label: Ingmar Heise
nodes.summary: Ingmar Heise works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University in 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

nodes.label: Christopher Ives
nodes.summary: Christopher Ives is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound from 1987 to 1995 and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College around 2001.

nodes.label: Sharon J. Roe
nodes.summary: Sharon J. Roe works in religious studies and philosophy. Roe completed a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under the doctoral supervision of Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Yoshinaga
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies and Buddhist studies, Shin'ichi Yoshinaga studied at Kyoto University. He founded the Kindai Pyramido Kyokai and held a professorship at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested 2015).

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College
nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College
variants: 舞鶴工業高等専門学校人文科学部門

nodes.label: Yozo Taniyama
nodes.summary: Yozo Taniyama is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University from 1991 to 2002. He held posts at Tohoku University, Shitennoji University, St. Thomas University, Japan, and Sophia University.

nodes.label: Dickwela Piyananda
nodes.summary: Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).

nodes.label: Christian Bernert
nodes.summary: Christian Bernert works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, where he completed a Magister der Philosophie under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Karin Preisendanz, Gerald Hödl, and Junjie Chu.

nodes.label: Hugh J. Silverman
nodes.summary: Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who earned his doctorate from Stanford University (~1969–1973). He became a professor at Stony Brook University in 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1976–2013).

nodes.label: Heeraman Tiwari
nodes.summary: Heeraman Tiwari is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned degrees from Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Heidelberg University, and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Lang Chen
nodes.summary: Lang Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at Yale University, where she studied under Janet Gyatso, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Sogyal Rinpoche
variants: ソギャル・リンポチェ
nodes.description: Tibetan Dzogchen lama of the Nyingma tradition
nodes.summary: Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, studying at the University of Delhi, the University of Cambridge, and under several traditional masters. He founded Rigpa in 1975.

nodes.label: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje
variants: ドゥジョム・ジグドラル・イェシェ・ドルジェ
nodes.summary: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught Keith Dowman, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam
nodes.summary: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Erica Baffelli
nodes.summary: Erica Baffelli is a Japanology and religious studies scholar who studied under Massimo Raveri. She has held posts at the University of Otago and the University of Manchester, where she is attested as professor in Japanese studies in 2026.

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for Human Development
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for Human Development
variants: Max Planck Institute for Human Development

nodes.label: Lara Braitstein
nodes.summary: Lara Braitstein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and serves there as Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Markus Viehbeck
nodes.summary: Markus Viehbeck is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard (-2012), worked as a Heidelberg University project researcher, and joined Vienna's faculty (attested 2026).

nodes.label: David R. Kinsley
nodes.summary: David R. Kinsley worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, learning under Om Prakash Sharma and Virendra Singh, and was on the faculty at McMaster University (1969–2000).

nodes.label: Bihani Sarkar
nodes.summary: Bihani Sarkar works in Indology and religious studies. She held a post at the University of Hamburg and is attested in 2026 as Senior Lecturer in Comparative Non-Western Thought at Lancaster University.

nodes.label: Liang Cai
nodes.summary: Liang Cai is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied under Daniel Boucher. She held a post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Kenneth Doo Young Lee
nodes.summary: Kenneth Doo Young Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University.

nodes.label: David Phillip Stanley
nodes.summary: David Phillip Stanley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He has held posts at Naropa University and the Nitartha Institute.

nodes.label: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He directed Nitartha Institute (~1996) and served as director at Kamalashila Institute (attested 2013).

nodes.label: W. F. Jayasuriya
nodes.summary: W. F. Jayasuriya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

nodes.label: Beata Grant
nodes.summary: Beata Grant is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at Stanford University. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and a faculty post at Washington University in St. Louis.

nodes.label: Weiru Guan
nodes.summary: Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Sīlānanda
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sayadaw U Sīlānanda studied at University College, Colombo, and under U Paññāvanta and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at the University of Mandalay (~1960–1969), founded Dhammānanda Vihara, and served as Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (1999).

nodes.label: Mahasi Sayadaw
nodes.native: မဟာစည်ဆရာတော်
nodes.summary: Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies and religious figure who studied under teachers including Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada. He served as abbot at Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung (1941) and resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (1947).

nodes.label: Shwegu Taik Monastery
variants: Atithokdāyone Pali University in Shwegu Taik Monastery

nodes.label: Vishwanathan Venkatachalam
nodes.summary: Vishwanathan Venkatachalam was an Indologist educated at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram universities. He held posts at Vikram University, headed the Scindia Oriental Institute (~1972–1985), and served as vice-chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Joanna Cook
nodes.summary: Joanna Cook works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied under James Laidlaw and held a post at Christ's College, Cambridge.

nodes.label: Edo Shonin
nodes.summary: Working in religious and Buddhist studies, Edo Shonin is attested in 2015 as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

nodes.label: William Van Gordon
nodes.summary: William Van Gordon is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Nirbhay N. Singh
nodes.summary: Nirbhay N. Singh works in religious studies and psychiatry. He has held positions at Virginia Commonwealth University, the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, and Augusta University.

nodes.id: I:Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research
nodes.label: Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research
variants: Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research

nodes.label: Mark D. Griffiths
nodes.summary: Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Bradford and earned his PhD from the University of Exeter (1988–1990). He lectured at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) and became Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

nodes.label: Charles Gabriel Seligman
nodes.summary: Charles Gabriel Seligman (1873–1940) studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School (~1892–1896). Working in history and archaeology, he held the chair of Ethnology at the University of London and the London School of Economics (1913–1934).

nodes.label: Francis Harold Cook
nodes.summary: Francis Harold Cook, a specialist in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at the University of California, Riverside, and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 1999.

nodes.label: Anna Sawerthal
nodes.summary: Anna Sawerthal is a scholar of Tibetology. She earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and a PhD at Heidelberg University, having also studied under Johanna Buß, Dawa Tsering, and Norbu Tashi.

nodes.label: Lauran R. Hartley
nodes.summary: Lauran R. Hartley specializes in Tibetology. She held positions at Indiana University Bloomington, Rutgers University (attested 2003), and Latse Library (attested 2003), and serves as Adjunct Assistant Professor and Director of the Modern Tibetan Studies Program at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ann Appleby Hazlewood
nodes.summary: Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned an MA at the Australian National University (attested 1983), studying under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.

nodes.label: Nika Jovic
nodes.summary: Nika Jovic is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her master's degree at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, having also studied under Géza Bethlenfalvy.

nodes.label: Conor Roddy
nodes.summary: Conor Roddy specializes in philosophy and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Texas at Austin, attested in 2011, under the supervision of Kathleen Higgins.

nodes.label: Kathleen Higgins
nodes.summary: Kathleen Higgins is a philosopher whose appointments include resident scholar at the Bellagio Center (1993), visiting fellow at Australian National University and Canberra School of Music (1997), and professor of philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2012).

nodes.label: John W. Pettit
nodes.summary: John W. Pettit works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, earned his doctorate under Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

nodes.label: Haverford College
variants: Margaret Gest Center for the Cross-Cultural Study of Religion at Haverford

nodes.label: Lal Mani Joshi
nodes.summary: Lal Mani Joshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities, he held faculty posts at Gorakhpur (1961–1967), Punjabi University (1971–1981), and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1984).

nodes.label: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and later taught John W. Pettit.

nodes.label: New College of Florida
variants: New College of the University of South Florida

nodes.label: Rongdao Lai
nodes.summary: Rongdao Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned her Ph.D. at McGill University (attested 2013) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates. She later served as Assistant Professor at McGill (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Robin D. S. Yates
nodes.summary: Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~1993).

nodes.label: Zhenhua
nodes.summary: Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist College in 1947 and under Yinshun in 1952. He managed the Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992) and taught Chien Y. Hsu.

nodes.label: Robert Baker Aitken
nodes.summary: Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a scholar and teacher of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and UC Berkeley, and held posts at Besant Hill School, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the East-West Center.

nodes.label: Bruno Dagens
nodes.summary: Bruno Dagens was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO, KU Leuven, the French Institute of Pondicherry, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University.

nodes.label: Constance Powell Chin
nodes.summary: Constance Powell Chin specializes in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree at San Jose State University in 2012.

nodes.label: Michael G. Morony
nodes.summary: Michael G. Morony (born 1939) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and UCLA, becoming a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1974.

nodes.label: Benjamin Wood
nodes.summary: Benjamin Wood is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett. He also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thubten Champa.

nodes.label: Donald Keene
nodes.summary: Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University, Harvard University, and under Wm. Theodore de Bary. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (1955).

nodes.label: Kathleen M. Erndl
nodes.summary: Kathleen M. Erndl worked in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (~1988–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017) as Associate Professor of Religion.

nodes.label: Allan G. Grapard
nodes.summary: Allan G. Grapard worked in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from INALCO and held posts at the University of California, including ISF Professor of Shinto Studies and Professor Emeritus at UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: D. Dennis Hudson
nodes.summary: D. Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who taught in the Department of Religion and served as Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College (~1970–2004).

nodes.label: Dominique-Sila Khan
nodes.summary: Dominique-Sila Khan (1949–2016) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and served as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).

nodes.label: June McDaniel
nodes.summary: June McDaniel is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served on the faculty at the College of Charleston, attested between 2000 and 2015.

nodes.label: Yu-Chen Tsui
nodes.summary: Yu-Chen Tsui specializes in Buddhist studies. Tsui completed a master's at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü, pursued doctoral studies supervised by Natasha Heller (attested 2018), and also studied under the traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

nodes.label: Dermott Walsh
nodes.summary: Dermott Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his BA at Trinity College Dublin (2003), MA at Leiden University (2009), and completed his PhD at UCLA (2018) under the supervision of William M. Bodiford.

nodes.label: C. D. Sebastian
nodes.summary: C. D. Sebastian is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, had postdoctoral mentorship under Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and serves as Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Gavin D'Costa
nodes.summary: Gavin D'Costa (b. 1958) studied at Cambridge (circa 1980–1982) and Birmingham (circa 1982–1985). Working in religious studies and philosophy, he taught at West London Institute (circa 1985–1993) and held a post at the University of Bristol beginning in 1993.

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his degrees at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti, later heading philosophy departments at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and Banaras Hindu University (1963–1985).

nodes.label: Hiroko Kawanami
nodes.summary: Hiroko Kawanami works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott, and served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016), where she taught Kan Boonyakanchana and Jianchengshi.

nodes.label: Alfred Gell
nodes.summary: Alfred Gell worked in other fields, earning degrees at Cambridge and LSE, where he studied under Edmund Leach. He held posts at the University of Sussex, Australian National University, London School of Economics, and was a British Academy Fellow.

nodes.label: John Okell
nodes.summary: John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford (circa 1953–1957) and trained under Hla Pe (circa 1959–1963), Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS (1959–1999).

nodes.label: Sunhee Kim
nodes.summary: Sunhee Kim earned a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice from the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nancy McCagney
nodes.summary: Nancy McCagney works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under scholars including Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, and Gerald James Larson, and held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Jeong-Eun Kim
nodes.summary: Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (-2011) under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak.

nodes.label: Giovanni Verardi
nodes.summary: Giovanni Verardi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who studied at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities. His career includes positions at Ca' Foscari, the University of Bologna, and a professorship at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Aoyagi
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Aoyagi (born 1957) works in linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from International Christian University (~1984–1986) and a PhD from the University of Southern California (~1992–1998), becoming a professor at Nanzan University around 2007.

nodes.label: Antonio Terrone
nodes.summary: Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and has served as a scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
