variants: A lags gzan dkar rin po che thub bstan nyi ma

nodes.label: Sarah H. Jacoby
nodes.summary: Sarah H. Jacoby specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Yale University (~1993–1997) and the University of Virginia (~2000–2007), and later held posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (2009).

nodes.label: Royal University of Bhutan
variants: Institute of Language and Cultural Studies, Royal University of Bhutan
Institute of Language and Cultural Studies, Semtokha
College of Language and Culture Studies (CLCS), Royal University of Bhutan

nodes.label: Nicolas Sihlé
nodes.summary: Nicolas Sihlé works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010; attested former 2026) and taught Jay Holt Valentine.

nodes.label: Somboon Watana
nodes.native: สมบูรณ์ วัฒนะ
nodes.summary: Somboon Watana is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who received a PhD from Panjab University in 1999 under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma. He serves as an Assistant Professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tulku Sherdor
nodes.summary: Tulku Sherdor (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia under Ted Norton and Jeffrey Hopkins, and trained traditionally under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Sharon Salzberg
nodes.summary: Sharon Salzberg works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University at Buffalo and under traditional teachers including Anagarika Munindra, Dipa Ma, and Sayadaw U Pandita, co-founding the Insight Meditation Society and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Yuko Matsuda
nodes.summary: Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Matsuda studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held an affiliation at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Natalie Gummer
nodes.summary: Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held an affiliation at Harvard University (attested 2001) and was appointed professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

nodes.id: I:Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture
nodes.label: Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture
variants: Thomas Burke Memorial Washington State Museum, University of Washington

nodes.id: I:Centre for the Study of Developing Societies
nodes.label: Centre for the Study of Developing Societies
variants: Centre for the Study of Developing Societies

nodes.label: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt
nodes.summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Marburg, and held posts as guest professor at the University of Vienna (~2004) and Privatdozentin at the University of Marburg (2009).

nodes.label: Huidi Zeng
nodes.summary: Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, where Yi-hsun Huang served as MA supervisor.

nodes.label: Yi-hsun Huang
nodes.summary: Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner (attested 2001) and has taught Huidi Zeng.

nodes.label: Alexander Kabanoff
nodes.summary: Alexander Kabanoff worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Prayoon Mererk
nodes.native: พระพรหมบัณฑิต
nodes.summary: Prayoon Mererk is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi in 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

nodes.label: David Azzopardi
nodes.summary: David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

nodes.label: János Szerb
nodes.summary: János Szerb was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1974–1980) and held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1986).

nodes.label: Kurt Tropper
nodes.summary: Kurt Tropper specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Vienna in 2001 under Ernst Steinkellner, Michael Torsten Much, and Tashi Geisler, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Ñāṇavīra Thera
nodes.summary: Ñāṇavīra Thera, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge, and with traditional teachers Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Pelene Siri Vajiragnana. He served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

nodes.label: Pelene Siri Vajiragnana
variants: Pälänē Siri Vajirañāņa Mahā Nāyaka Thera

nodes.label: Heng Sure
nodes.summary: Heng Sure is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD under Ronald Y. Nakasone), alongside Hsuan Hua. He has held professorial posts at Dharma Realm Buddhist University, GTU, and Bond University.

nodes.label: Edmond Yee
nodes.summary: Working in religious studies and sinology, Edmond Yee held faculty posts attested in 2003 at Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union.

nodes.label: Phramaha Niras Ruangsan
nodes.summary: Phramaha Niras Ruangsan specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (attested 2015) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

nodes.label: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle
nodes.summary: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: Chien-hsing Ho
nodes.summary: Chien-hsing Ho specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. His academic posts include Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and a position at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Charles B. Jones
nodes.summary: Charles B. Jones works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner by 1996 and served as an associate professor and associate dean at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).

nodes.label: Technical University of Berlin
variants: ベルリンのシャルロッテンブルク工科大学

nodes.id: I:Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
nodes.label: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
variants: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Michael Wenger
nodes.summary: Michael Wenger is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned an M.A. at The New School and trained under Mel Weitsman (~1972–2021). He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1984–2012) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Ralph Abraham
nodes.summary: Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Princeton, before serving as an associate professor (1968) and professor (1980) at the University of California, Santa Cruz.

nodes.label: Sisir Roy
nodes.summary: Sisir Roy works in philosophy, having studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He has served as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and held a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).

nodes.label: National Institute of Advanced Studies
variants: National Institute of Advanced Studies, Bangalore

nodes.label: Ajahn Brahm
nodes.summary: Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1969–1972) and under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah (1974). He has served as abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery since ~1995.

nodes.label: Terese Tse Bartholomew
nodes.summary: Terese Tse Bartholomew is a specialist in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. She earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum (attested 1985–2003).

nodes.label: Ryan Anningson
nodes.summary: Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis.

nodes.id: I:Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
nodes.label: Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
variants: Royal Dutch Academy of Arts and Sciences
Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences

nodes.label: Amy Heller
nodes.summary: Amy Heller, a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist, earned degrees from Barnard College, INALCO, and the EPHE under Ariane Macdonald. She has held posts at Yale, CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, Sichuan University, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

nodes.label: Mireille Helffer
nodes.summary: Mireille Helffer was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She was a Chargé de Recherche at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (~1961–1993) and held a post at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

nodes.label: Dawa Norbu
nodes.summary: Dawa Norbu was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Delhi, St. Stephen's, and UC Berkeley. He taught at several institutions in California and served as Professor of Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2004).

nodes.label: Nawang Tsering Shakspo
nodes.summary: Nawang Tsering Shakspo works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies under Lal Mani Joshi and served as a Lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).

nodes.label: Hsuan Hua
nodes.summary: Hsuan Hua worked in Buddhist studies, having studied under Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, where he served as abbot (~1976–1995), as well as the Buddhist Text Translation Society and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

nodes.label: Drepung Gomang Dratsang
variants: Gomang College of the Gelugpa Drepung monastic university
Gomang College of Drepung Monastic University

nodes.label: Chien Y. Hsu
nodes.summary: Chien Y. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies. Hsu studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura and James B. Apple, as well as under traditional teacher Zhenhua.

nodes.label: Joseph D. Markowski
nodes.summary: Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed his Master of Arts at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Peter Francis Kornicki
nodes.summary: Peter Francis Kornicki is a scholar of Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Oxford, Tokyo University of Education, and under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida. He taught at Tasmania, Kyoto University, Robinson College, and Cambridge (Emeritus Professor ~2017).

nodes.label: Rosemary Radford Ruether
nodes.summary: Rosemary Radford Ruether was a religious studies scholar who studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1958–1965). She held a post at Howard University (~1965–1975).

nodes.label: E. W. Adikaram
nodes.summary: E. W. Adikaram was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he served as principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

nodes.label: Arthur Philip McKeown
nodes.summary: Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), studying under Diana L. Eck, Parimal G. Patil, and Pari Sangye.

nodes.label: Polly Young-Eisendrath
nodes.summary: Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who was educated at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis. In 1994, she became a clinical associate professor in psychiatry at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: Yasuo Deguchi
nodes.summary: Yasuo Deguchi is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Nagoya Institute of Technology before returning to Kyoto University, where he became a professor and dean, later visiting ZEN University in 2025.

nodes.label: Constance E. Kassor
nodes.summary: Constance E. Kassor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a BA at Smith College and a PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later joining the Smith College faculty (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Karin Meyers
nodes.summary: Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served as an assistant professor and MA program director at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Eyal Aviv
nodes.summary: Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

nodes.label: Annette Baier
nodes.summary: Annette Baier was a philosopher who completed degrees at the University of Otago and Somerville College. She held faculty appointments at Carnegie Mellon University from roughly 1968 to 1973 and at the University of Pittsburgh from 1973 to 1995.

nodes.label: Wilfrid Sellars
variants: ウィルフリド・ストーカー・セラーズ
nodes.jawiki: ウィルフリド・セラーズ
nodes.summary: Philosopher Wilfrid Sellars studied at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the universities of Iowa (~1938–1946), Minnesota (~1947–1958), and Yale (~1958–1963), before serving as a professor at the University of Pittsburgh from 1963 to 1989.

nodes.label: Zuicho Tachibana
nodes.summary: Zuicho Tachibana (1890–1968) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kozui Otani (~1907) and Edward Denison Ross (~1908).

nodes.label: Ines Konczak-Nagel
nodes.summary: Ines Konczak-Nagel specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She was a postdoctoral fellow at Berlin State Museums, a visiting fellow at Ryukoku University (2012), and joined the Kuča-Projekt at Leipzig University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Angela Falco Howard
nodes.summary: Angela Falco Howard specializes in art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and Yoshito S. Hakeda. She held a professorship at Rutgers University (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Vignato
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under teachers including Su Bai, Shichang Ma, Chongfeng Li, and Angela Falco Howard, and held a post there (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Shichang Ma
nodes.summary: Shichang Ma (1934–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He worked as a Buddhist archaeology researcher at the Dunhuang Academy from 1963 to 1978 and joined the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982.

nodes.label: Max Oidtmann
nodes.summary: Historian, Sinologist, and Tibetologist Max Oidtmann earned degrees from Carleton College, Indiana University Bloomington, and Harvard University, studying under Mark Elliott. He held posts at Georgetown University in Qatar from 2013 to 2021 and became a professor at the University of Munich around 2021.

nodes.label: Jotika Khur-Yearn
nodes.summary: Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Rangama Chandawimala
nodes.summary: Rangama Chandawimala, a Buddhist studies scholar, earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, and studied under Attaragama Gnanawimala. He is an associate professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gregory Price Grieve
nodes.summary: Gregory Price Grieve (born 1964) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned degrees at San Francisco State and Chicago. He held lecturer posts at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and department head at UNC Greensboro.

nodes.label: Michael S. Drummond
nodes.summary: Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

nodes.id: I:Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry
nodes.label: Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry
variants: Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry
Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry

nodes.label: Owen Flanagan
nodes.summary: Owen Flanagan is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fordham University (~1966–1970) and Boston University (~1973–1977), and held a post as Professor of Philosophy at Duke University (~1996).

nodes.label: Andrew Olendzki
nodes.summary: Andrew Olendzki works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held posts at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Insight Meditation Society
variants: Insight Meditation Society in Barre, Massachusetts

nodes.label: University of Warwick
variants: Centre for Translation & Comparative Cultural Studies, University of Warwick

nodes.label: Fazun
nodes.summary: Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and institutes in China under Taixu and Amdo Geshe, among others. He directed the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and led the Buddhist Academy of China.

nodes.label: Tzungkuen Wen
nodes.summary: Tzungkuen Wen specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Queensland and held posts at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005 and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, attested for 2026.

nodes.label: Robert Anthony Orsi
nodes.summary: Robert Anthony Orsi is a religious studies scholar and historian. He studied at Trinity College and Yale University. He held academic posts at Fordham (1981–1988), Indiana University (1988–2001), Harvard (2001–2007), and Northwestern University from ~2007.

nodes.label: Clara Sue Kidwell
nodes.description: Native American academic scholar, historian, feminist
nodes.summary: Clara Sue Kidwell worked in history and archaeology, earning her master's and Ph.D. at the University of Oklahoma (~1963–1970). Her career included positions at UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian (~1993–1995), and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

nodes.label: Karen McCarthy Brown
nodes.summary: Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. She served as a professor of anthropology at Drew University from circa 1976 to 2009.

nodes.label: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri
nodes.summary: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College, London, Pennsylvania, and Toronto. He founded and served as president of the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, and held posts at Toronto and Ontario Tech University.

nodes.label: Christopher Hatchell
nodes.summary: Christopher Hatchell is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Virginia under the academic mentorship of David Germano.

nodes.label: Jason Matthew McCombs
nodes.summary: Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan and completed his PhD under Gregory Schopen at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he also served as a lecturer.

nodes.label: Lobsang Tenpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

nodes.label: Jigmeth Junu
nodes.summary: Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fo Guang University for an MA (attested 2013) under supervisor Yongdong Shi, and also studied under Hui Xian.

nodes.label: Martin Heidegger
variants: マルティン・ハイデッガー
nodes.jawiki: マルティン・ハイデッガー
nodes.summary: Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl (~1909–1923). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (1915–1923, 1936–1940) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

nodes.label: Christian Haskett
nodes.summary: Christian Haskett specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, among others, holding a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Linda Jean LaMacchia
nodes.summary: Linda Jean LaMacchia works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the doctoral supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).

nodes.label: China Institute of Inner Learning
variants: China Institute of Inner Learning (支那內學院)
China Inner Academy of Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Michael Sheehy
nodes.summary: Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019–2026).

nodes.label: Qingying Chen
nodes.summary: Qingying Chen (1942–2022) worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. He taught at Qinghai Nationalities University and Minzu University before serving at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Anagarika Govinda
nodes.image: Lama Govinda in an internment camp during World War II.jpg
nodes.summary: Anagarika Govinda worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Freiburg, Naples, and Cagliari, he studied under Nyanatiloka and Tomo Geshe Rinpoche, taught at Indian universities including Visva-Bharati and Patna, and led the Arya Maitreya Mandala.

nodes.label: Adeu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Zen Mountain Monastery
variants: Zen Mountain Monastery at Mt. Tremper

nodes.label: Hegoda Khemananda
nodes.summary: Hegoda Khemananda is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

nodes.label: Dewei Zhang
nodes.summary: Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Paul Crowe
nodes.summary: Paul Crowe works in Sinology and religious studies. He completed graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and served as a professor at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: King Pong Chiu
nodes.summary: King Pong Chiu works in Indology and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under the supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Thomé H. Fang
nodes.summary: Thomé H. Fang worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking, with John Dewey, and earned an MA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He held posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

nodes.label: Ilkka Pyysiäinen
nodes.description: Finnish cognitive science of religion scholar
nodes.summary: Ilkka Pyysiäinen works in religious studies. He studied under René Gothóni around 1985 to 1993, served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki in 1984, and held a post as a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: ISEAS–Yusof Ishak Institute
variants: Institute of Southeast Asian Studies, Singapore

nodes.label: Andrew B. Irvine
nodes.summary: Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Boston University and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Brooke Schedneck
nodes.summary: Brooke Schedneck is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Juliane Schober.

nodes.label: Jacques Leider
nodes.summary: Jacques Leider works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne, INALCO under Denise Bernot, and Luxembourg, and held teaching posts at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2001).

nodes.label: William Edward Soothill
nodes.summary: William Edward Soothill was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of London, he served as President of Shanxi University in 1911 and became Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford in 1920.

nodes.label: Lewis Hodous
nodes.summary: Lewis Hodous was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Case Western Reserve University, Hartford Seminary, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He served as president of Fukien Union Theological Seminary and later taught at Hartford Seminary (1917–1945).

nodes.label: Adrian Zenz
nodes.summary: Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He earned a master's degree at the University of Auckland (~1999–2001) and a Ph.D. under Hildegard Diemberger at the University of Cambridge (~2007–2011). He held posts at the European School of Culture and Theology, Columbia International University Korntal (~2006–2019), and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation (2019).

nodes.label: Xiuzhi Zeng
nodes.summary: Xiuzhi Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a master's degree at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen, attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Ramon Prats
nodes.summary: Ramon Prats is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Pompeu Fabra University
variants: Department of Humanities of the University Pompeu Fabra

nodes.label: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy
nodes.summary: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy works in Tibetology. She studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Harvard University, Tibet University, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts at Laval University in ~2004 and 2007.

nodes.label: Tibetan Arts Research Bureau
variants: Tibetan Arts Research Bureau (Bod ljongs sgyu rtsal zhib 'jug khang)

nodes.label: James Whitehill
nodes.summary: James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He founded the Columbia Zen Center and served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

nodes.label: David Bubna-Litic
nodes.summary: David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and related fields. He earned his PhD at Western Sydney University and served as a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney, attested in 2000.

nodes.label: University of Technology Sydney
variants: School of Management in the University of Technology, Sydney

nodes.label: Susan Naquin
nodes.summary: Susan Naquin is a historian and sinologist. After earning a BA at Stanford (~1962–1966) and an MA and PhD at Yale (~1966–1974), she taught history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and served as professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

nodes.label: Jiyu Ren
nodes.summary: Jiyu Ren worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He, he taught there (1942–1964) and directed the Institute of World Religions at CASS (1964–1986).

nodes.label: Xiaoling Wu
nodes.summary: Xiaoling Wu was a sinologist and Indologist who held posts at Peking University, Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and served as a professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).

nodes.label: Marion L. Matics
nodes.summary: Marion L. Matics is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as under teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

nodes.label: Horace L. Friess
nodes.summary: Horace L. Friess worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University and Heidelberg University, later serving on Columbia University's faculty from 1919 and as Joseph L. Buttenwieser Professor (1962-1966), alongside a post at Johns Hopkins.

nodes.label: Soto Zen Buddhism International Center
variants: Soto Zen Education Center of North America

nodes.label: Susan L. Beningson
nodes.summary: Susan L. Beningson works in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr.

nodes.label: Robert E. Harrist, Jr.
nodes.summary: Robert E. Harrist, Jr. works in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Columbia University, attested in 2009 and later attested in 2026 as Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Wayne Bass
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Wayne Bass specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA (PhD attested 2013) under Gregory Schopen. He held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego (both attested 2013).

nodes.label: William P. Chu
nodes.summary: William P. Chu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his M.A. at the University of California, Los Angeles, by 2006, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.id: I:International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
variants: International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
IITB GmbH (International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies GmbH)

nodes.label: Dhirendra Sharma
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology. He studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

nodes.label: John R. B. Campbell
nodes.summary: John R. B. Campbell is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, alongside training with traditional teachers and other scholars.

nodes.label: H. V. Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Geshe Karma Sonam
nodes.summary: Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Gyume Tantric College and Sera Monastery.

nodes.label: Lang Eun Ra
nodes.summary: Lang Eun Ra is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Temple University, where she was supervised by Charles Wei-hsun Fu and studied under Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

nodes.label: Norbert M. Samuelson
nodes.summary: Norbert M. Samuelson worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Northwestern University, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He held faculty positions at Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Leonard Swidler
nodes.summary: Leonard Swidler was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from St. Norbert College, Marquette, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later serving as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).

nodes.label: Alan Gerard Wagner
nodes.summary: Alan Gerard Wagner specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, having also studied with Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

nodes.label: Iselin Frydenlund
nodes.summary: Iselin Frydenlund works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. In 2016, she was attested as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and as a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: Bruce M. Knauft
nodes.summary: Bruce M. Knauft is an anthropologist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1976–1983) and held a professorship at Emory University beginning around 1985.

nodes.label: Richard Taupier
nodes.summary: Richard Taupier works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate and MS at UMass Amherst, where he became Associate Director of Research Development, and was a visiting lecturer at Smith College.

nodes.label: Martin Lehnert
nodes.summary: Martin Lehnert is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg and served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich (attested 2016).

nodes.label: James Mark Shields
nodes.summary: James Mark Shields (born 1971) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was Associate Professor at Bucknell University and an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

nodes.label: Foundation for Buddhist Studies
variants: Foundation for Buddhist Studies in Hamburg

nodes.label: Kim Gutschow
nodes.summary: Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD from Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Geshe Ngawang Nyima
nodes.summary: Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Leiden University, Drepung Monastery, and Drepung Gomang Dratsang, and served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

nodes.label: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Brown University from around 1968 to 1970, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Jenkuan Shih
nodes.summary: Jenkuan Shih specializes in Buddhist studies. Shih earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, having studied under MA supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa and doctoral supervisors Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.

nodes.label: David A. Dilworth
nodes.summary: David A. Dilworth is a scholar in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968).

nodes.label: Giuliana Martini
nodes.summary: Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic appointments in 2010 at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

nodes.label: Keith Dowman
nodes.description: Dzogchen teacher, translator of Tibetan Buddhist texts
nodes.summary: Keith Dowman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Anagarika Munindra. In 1973, he held a post at Sonoma State University.

nodes.label: David Ralph Quinter
nodes.summary: David Ralph Quinter specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at UC Boulder, Stanford (PhD under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure), and the University of Tokyo, later serving as associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta.

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies in Yokohama
Inter-University Center for Advanced Language Study
Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies

nodes.label: Kenji Matsuo
nodes.summary: Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1973 to 1982 and held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1988 to 2020.

nodes.label: Sonja Arntzen
nodes.summary: Sonja Arntzen (b. 1945) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1967–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

nodes.label: Shuichi Kato
nodes.summary: Shuichi Kato (1919–2008) worked in Japanology, history, and philosophy after medical studies at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Sophia University, Free University of Berlin, and UBC, and later directed the Kyoto Museum for World Peace at Ritsumeikan University.

nodes.label: Qichao Liang
nodes.summary: Qichao Liang (1873–1929) was a scholar in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Youwei Kang (~1890–1898). He held posts at the Current Affairs Academy, the Translation Bureau, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and the National Library of China.

nodes.label: Youwei Kang
nodes.summary: Youwei Kang (1858–1927) was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He founded the Wanmu Caotang academy in 1890 and held a post there from around 1891 to 1898.

nodes.label: Cameron Bailey
nodes.summary: Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Bailey studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and Wolfson College, Oxford, completing doctoral work at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.

nodes.label: Lucia Galli
nodes.summary: Lucia Galli is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

nodes.label: Rory Brendan Lindsay
nodes.summary: Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Amanda K. Goodman
nodes.summary: Amanda K. Goodman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

nodes.id: I:Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
nodes.label: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
variants: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Hong Kong University of Science & Technology

nodes.label: Mamoru Tonami
nodes.summary: Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki. He held assistant, associate, and full professor posts at Kyoto University (1965–2001) and taught at Otani University.

nodes.label: Jeffery D. Long
nodes.summary: Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Notre Dame and the University of Chicago, and became an associate professor of religion and Asian studies at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

nodes.label: Angela Sumegi
nodes.summary: Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa, studying under Nalini Devdas, and held a post as assistant professor at Carleton University (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Lucia Dolce
nodes.summary: Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She has held posts at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015), and is attested at Minobusan University in 2026.

nodes.label: Grace S. Fong
nodes.summary: Grace S. Fong is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1978–1984). She served as a professor at Smith College (~1984–1986) and became associate professor and department chair at McGill around 1989.

nodes.label: Ching-mei Shyu
nodes.summary: Ching-mei Shyu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed an MA under Jan Nattier at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and earned a PhD from Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

nodes.label: Jane-Marie Law
nodes.summary: Jane-Marie Law is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. She has held posts at Cornell University, serving as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ellison Banks Findly
nodes.summary: Ellison Banks Findly works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Fred Pfeil and held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Kazuo Okabe
nodes.summary: Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at the Institute for Zen Studies and Komazawa University (1973–2006).

nodes.label: Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara
nodes.native: สมเด็จพระญาณสังวร
variants: Somdet Phra Sangharaja Chao Krommaluang Vajirañāṇasaṃvara
nodes.jawiki: ワシラガーナサンバラ
nodes.summary: Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara and under Swami Satyananda Puri and Vajirayanavangsa. He was abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013) and director at Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961).

nodes.label: Hanung Kim
nodes.summary: Hanung Kim is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Kim earned a master's degree at Columbia University and a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Ruth Gamble
nodes.summary: Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the Australian National University under John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman. She has held research posts at the Australian National University and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Petra Maurer
nodes.summary: Petra Maurer works in Tibetology and Indology, having studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held posts at the University of Munich, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Cuilan Liu
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology, Cuilan Liu served as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and held an attested post at the University of Munich in 2018.

nodes.label: Emanuela Garatti
nodes.summary: Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who has held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Phramonchai Saitanaporn
nodes.summary: Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, and also studied under Phrathepyanmahamuni.

nodes.label: Jeff Wilson
nodes.summary: Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under Taitetsu Unno and Myosei Tatsuguchi.

nodes.label: Phrathepyanmahamuni
nodes.native: พระราชภาวนาวิสุทธิ์

nodes.label: Shuman Chen
nodes.summary: Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Northwestern University under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn, and also studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

nodes.label: Brook Ziporyn
nodes.summary: Brook Ziporyn works in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and the University of Michigan, he held faculty posts at Northwestern University, the National University of Singapore, and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Anne Ruth Hansen
nodes.summary: Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history, having studied under Charles Hallisey. She was affiliated with the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee and has held associate professor and professor posts at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

nodes.label: Thomas Nathan Patton
nodes.summary: Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held an attested post at the City University of Hong Kong in 2018.

nodes.label: Anne M. Blackburn
nodes.summary: Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who was a graduate student at the University of Chicago in 1991. She held posts at Cornell University, Harvard University, and the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Hoseok Leigh
nodes.summary: Hoseok Leigh works in philosophy and religious studies. Leigh studied under Ha-u Kim and Cheonghwa, completing a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Catherine Bell
nodes.summary: Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa (~1976–1983) and served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

nodes.label: Hsiang-Kuang Chou
nodes.summary: Working in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Chou studied under Sivananda Saraswati (attested 1960). He held posts at the University of Delhi, University of Allahabad, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).

nodes.id: I:Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration
nodes.label: Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration
Kin Cheung
nodes.summary: Kin Cheung works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).

nodes.label: James Blumenthal
nodes.summary: James Blumenthal was a Buddhist studies scholar and tibetologist who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He taught at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

nodes.label: Kōsen Imakita
nodes.summary: Kōsen Imakita was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Togai Fujisawa, Kyokuso Hirose, Daisetsu Jōen, and Gisan Zenkai. He served as abbot of Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892), and at the Ministry of Religion (~1872–1877).

nodes.label: Beatrice Erskine Lane
variants: ベアトリス・アースキン・レイン・スズキ
nodes.jawiki: ベアトリス・レイン・スズキ
nodes.summary: Beatrice Erskine Lane was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Radcliffe College and Columbia University under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana. In 1921, she held a professorship at Otani University.

nodes.label: Josiah Royce
nodes.summary: Josiah Royce was a philosopher who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, Johns Hopkins University, and the University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze. He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and served on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 to 1916.

nodes.label: George Santayana
variants: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.summary: Philosopher George Santayana was educated at Boston Latin School, Harvard College, Humboldt University of Berlin, and King's College, Cambridge, completing his PhD at Harvard under William James. He served on the Harvard University philosophical faculty from 1907 to 1912.

nodes.label: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche
variants: ティンレー・ノルブ・リンポチェ
nodes.image: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche wearing a white shirt, red zen, pink curtain in background.jpg
nodes.summary: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (Dudjom Rinpoche). He also founded the White Lotus School.

nodes.label: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under numerous teachers, including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Thubten Chodron
nodes.summary: Thubten Chodron works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, Dorje Pamo Monastery, and under several teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama. She held posts at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Sravasti Abbey.

nodes.label: Daniel R. Tuzzeo
nodes.summary: Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

nodes.label: George A. Keyworth
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Keyworth studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned his PhD at UCLA (2001) under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held a professorship at the University of Colorado Boulder (2001) and served as associate professor at the University of Saskatchewan.

nodes.label: Ronald Egan
nodes.summary: Ronald Egan is a sinologist who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1971–1977). He held posts at Harvard (~1977–1986), Wellesley College (~1986–1988), UC Santa Barbara (~1993–2012; emeritus ~2012), and Stanford University (~2012–2021).

nodes.label: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen
nodes.summary: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Leiden University in 1991, where he was also attested as a Research-Fellow in 1996.

nodes.label: Namio Egami
nodes.summary: Namio Egami was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), later teaching there (~1949–1967) and serving as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).

nodes.label: Nalini Devdas
nodes.summary: Nalini Devdas specialized in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, earning a PhD from Concordia University (attested 2004) under Leslie Orr. She also studied under several teachers, including Paul David Devanandan, and held a post at Carleton University.

nodes.label: Paul David Devanandan
nodes.summary: Paul David Devanandan was a religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Yale (~1927–1931). He taught at Jaffna College, served as professor at United Theological College, Bangalore (1932–1949), and directed the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society (1956).

nodes.label: Tsultrim Gyatso
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Hozen Seki
nodes.summary: Hozen Seki was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy. He also served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Susan Meinheit
nodes.summary: Susan Meinheit is a Tibetologist who held posts at the Library of Congress (attested 1998 and 2007).

nodes.label: Bhuwan Lal Joshi
nodes.summary: Bhuwan Lal Joshi was a scholar of Indology who studied at Patna University from around 1948 to 1952. He later held posts at the University of California, Berkeley, and the University of California, Santa Cruz.

nodes.label: Andrei Vostrikov
nodes.summary: Andrei Vostrikov (1904–1937) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky) and later taught Bidia Dandaron.

nodes.label: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov
nodes.summary: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1921–1925) and worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences from ~1926 to 1938.

nodes.label: Jørn Borup
nodes.summary: Jørn Borup worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Aarhus University around 1999–2002 under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served as an associate professor there from circa 2008 to 2023.

nodes.label: Ian Reader
nodes.summary: Ian Reader is a religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Leeds. He held posts at Kansai Gaidai, Stirling, Lancaster, and Manchester, where he was Emeritus Professor (~2006–2015).

nodes.label: Michaela Haas
nodes.summary: Michaela Haas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2008), where she was supervised by Peter Schwieger, and also studied under Rechungpa and traditional teacher Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

nodes.label: Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul
nodes.native: 'jigs med rnam rgyal 'dzi sgar kong sprul
variants: ‘Jigs med rNam rgyal ‘Dzi sgar Kong sprul

nodes.label: Rudolf Kaschewsky
nodes.summary: Rudolf Kaschewsky worked in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, he taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt and held an academic post at the University of Bonn (1974–2004).

nodes.label: Andreas Doctor
nodes.summary: Andreas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, studied under traditional teachers including Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Phakchok Rinpoche
nodes.description: Vajra Master of Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling monastery
nodes.summary: Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at the Dzongsar Institute (~1995–2003) and under several traditional teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.

nodes.label: Ngodup Tsering
nodes.image: Ngodup Tsering, Geshe Lhakdor and Geshe Lobsang Monlam.jpg

nodes.label: Susan Niditch
nodes.summary: Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who served as a faculty member in the religion department at Amherst College from approximately 1978 to 2020.

nodes.label: Will Sweetman
nodes.description: professor of religion in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge (~1996–1999) and held a post at the University of Otago (~2005).

nodes.label: Dongchu
nodes.summary: Dongchu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy and abbot at Dinghui Monastery.

nodes.label: Craig Preston
nodes.summary: Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia, where he was taught by Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson.

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Paul
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Paul is a scholar of Tibetology, archaeology, and Indology who completed doctoral studies under Gudrun Bühnemann, also studying with Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

nodes.label: Philadelphia Museum of Art
variants: フィラデルフィア美術館

nodes.label: David Jones
nodes.summary: David Jones is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. Attested in 2007, he directed the Center for the Development of Asian Studies and taught within the University System of Georgia.

nodes.id: I:Center for the Development of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Center for the Development of Asian Studies
variants: Center for the Development of Asian Studies

nodes.id: I:East-West Connections: Review of Asian Studies
nodes.label: East-West Connections: Review of Asian Studies
variants: East-West Connections: Review of Asian Studies

nodes.label: Max Kaltenmark
nodes.summary: Max Kaltenmark specialized in Sinology and religious studies. He directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques (1946) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953), and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris.

nodes.label: Léon Vandermeersch
nodes.summary: Sinologist and philosopher Léon Vandermeersch (1928–2021) studied at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot. He held posts at Paris Diderot (1973–1979), EPHE (1979–1993), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1981–1984), and directed the EFEO (1989–1993).

nodes.label: Wen-ling Jane
nodes.summary: Wen-ling Jane is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2009), also studying under Lobsang Jamspal.

nodes.label: Kammie Takahashi
nodes.description: academic, college faculty, Associate Professor of Religion Studies
nodes.summary: Kammie Takahashi is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama. She held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.

nodes.label: Sabine Löhr
nodes.summary: An Indologist and philosopher, Sabine Löhr studied at the University of Freiburg and earned an M.A. at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Lambert Schmithausen. She also worked as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Graham Lock
nodes.summary: Graham Lock is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

nodes.label: Robert Barnett
nodes.summary: Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1976). He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1999–2018), SOAS University of London (~2018), and King's College London (~2018).

nodes.label: Arthur F. Buehler
nodes.summary: Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held a post at Victoria University of Wellington.

nodes.label: Halle O'Neal
nodes.summary: Halle O'Neal works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler (attested 2011) and holds a co-director post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

nodes.label: David W. Tien
nodes.summary: David W. Tien is a scholar in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, working under teachers including Julia Ching, Robert H. Sharf, and doctoral supervisor James Robson.

nodes.label: Jim Rheingans
nodes.summary: Jim Rheingans works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hamburg and a PhD from Bath Spa University and the University of the West of England, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.

nodes.id: I:University of the West of England
nodes.label: University of the West of England
variants: University of the West of England, Bristol
University of the West of England

nodes.label: Stephen Suen
nodes.summary: Stephen Suen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Mark T. Unno
nodes.summary: Mark T. Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College and Stanford University, holding academic positions at Brown University and the University of Oregon (~2000).

Buryat-Mongolian Research Institute of Culture in Ulan-Ude

nodes.label: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir
nodes.summary: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MPhil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008), and also studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.

nodes.label: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska
nodes.summary: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and has held posts at the University of Warsaw (attested 2008 and 2026).

nodes.label: Moscow State University
variants: Moscow State University's Institute of Asian and African Studies
Institute of Asian and African Studies

nodes.label: Cameron Foltz
nodes.summary: Cameron Foltz works in religious studies and Japanology. After earning an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas, Foltz was a postdoctoral fellow at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yu Yan Pang
nodes.summary: Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, as well as teacher Eric Kvan.

nodes.label: Miranda Shaw
nodes.summary: Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, teacher Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

nodes.label: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza
nodes.summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (from 1988), and founded the SBL.

nodes.label: Ngawang Jorden
nodes.summary: Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Sulak Sivaraksa
nodes.native: สุลักษณ์ ศิวรักษ์
nodes.summary: Sulak Sivaraksa is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Lampeter, Assumption College, and SSRC. Sivaraksa held visiting posts at Berkeley, Harvard, Toronto, and Cornell, and was an honorary fellow at Lampeter.

nodes.label: Subhadradis Diskul
nodes.native: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล
variants: モムチャオ＝スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.image: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล.jpg
nodes.jawiki: スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.summary: Diskul studied at Chulalongkorn, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and UCL. A specialist in history and archaeology, he served as curator at Bangkok's National Museum (~1953–1964) and professor, dean, and rector (1976–1986) at Silpakorn University.

nodes.label: David Kerman Tomlinson
nodes.summary: David Kerman Tomlinson is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold, also studying under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman. He has held a post at Smith College.

nodes.label: Sven Wittemann
nodes.summary: Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Juichiro Tanabe
nodes.summary: Juichiro Tanabe works in philosophy. Tanabe was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford from 2000 to 2001 and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

nodes.label: Bong Seok Joo
nodes.summary: Bong Seok Joo completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser. His academic fields are Buddhist studies and sinology.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Stout
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brown University (~1968-1972) and Princeton University (~1972-1976, PhD), and served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

nodes.label: Jann Ronis
nodes.summary: Jann Ronis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Sonam Tenpa, and held an attested post there in 2007.

nodes.label: Faren
nodes.summary: Faren is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong, attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Wenbiao Mai
nodes.summary: Wenbiao Mai is an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned a PhD at Peking University and studied at Kyoto and Hamburg. Mai served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Zhonghui Cui
nodes.summary: Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where Cui served as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Christopher D. Emms
nodes.summary: Christopher D. Emms is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, where he has studied under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.

nodes.label: Gin Ling Liu
nodes.summary: Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2008) under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin, having also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Kim Knott
nodes.summary: Kim Knott (born 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. She held positions at the University of Leeds (~1980–2011) and Lancaster University (~2012).

nodes.label: Eleanor Nesbitt
nodes.summary: Eleanor Nesbitt is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the University of Oxford. She served as professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989–2012).

nodes.label: John H. Berthrong
nodes.summary: John H. Berthrong, working in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies, completed graduate study under Alfonso Verdu. He held a post at Boston University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Elizabeth J. Harris
nodes.summary: Elizabeth J. Harris specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate under Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, holding posts at Westminster College (~1993–1996) and Birmingham (~2018).

nodes.label: Michael Harack
nodes.summary: Michael Harack specializes in religious studies and Sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Defense Language Institute
variants: アメリカ陸軍の語学学校

nodes.label: Robert J. Topmiller
nodes.summary: Robert J. Topmiller specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Kentucky under the supervision of George C. Herring.

nodes.label: George C. Herring
nodes.image: Dr. George Herring, Alumni Professor of History Emeritus at the University of Kentucky 2015 (cropped).jpg

nodes.label: Jang-Kil Chun
nodes.summary: Jang-Kil Chun works in the fields of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Frances Wilson.

nodes.label: Alexander Rödel
nodes.summary: Alexander Rödel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied for a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh under supervisors Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw, attested in 2008.

nodes.label: University of Rhode Island
variants: ロードアイランド大学

nodes.label: Christian Matthias Boehm
nodes.summary: Christian Matthias Boehm specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2005) and studied under Toshifumi Konno.

nodes.label: UNESCO
variants: International Commission for a History of the Scientific and Cultural Development of Mankind
International Board of Editors for the history of Civilizations in Central Asia at UNESCO

nodes.label: Hsueh-li Cheng
nodes.summary: Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held academic posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1975–2005).

nodes.label: Troy Organ
nodes.summary: Troy Organ (1912–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1937–1941). He held positions at Parsons College (~1944–1946), the University of Akron (~1946–1954), Ohio University (1954), and Chatham University.

nodes.label: Surya Das
nodes.summary: Surya Das is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the University at Buffalo from 1967 to 1971 and under traditional teacher Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche from ~1984 to 1999.

nodes.label: Aristotle C. Dy
nodes.summary: Aristotle C. Dy is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).
