variants: University of Miami School of Medicine

nodes.label: University of Tehran
variants: Faculty of Political and Social Sciences in Tehran

nodes.label: Kristin Scheible
nodes.summary: Kristin Scheible is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned a BA from Colby College and an MTS from Harvard University, studying under Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey, later teaching at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College.

nodes.label: Bruce Chilton
nodes.summary: Bruce Chilton works in religious studies. He studied at St John's College (~1974–1977) and later held posts at Yale University (~1985–1987) and Bard College (~1987).

nodes.label: Matthew Steven Mitchell
nodes.summary: Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Osaka City University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and Duke University (PhD attested 2015) under Richard M. Jaffe, Helen Baroni, Michel Mohr, and Amy L. Allocco.

nodes.label: Richard M. Jaffe
nodes.summary: Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1992–1999) and Duke University, where he became Professor of Religious Studies (~1999).

nodes.label: Chong Go
nodes.summary: Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under traditional teacher Daehaeng (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Bongkil Chung
nodes.summary: Bongkil Chung earned his PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner. Specializing in philosophy and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Florida International University in 1991–1992 and as professor of philosophy, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Woosung Huh
nodes.summary: Woosung Huh is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He was attested in 2012 as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University.

nodes.label: Patrick R. Uhlmann
nodes.summary: Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who was a Ph.D. candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Woncheol Yun
nodes.summary: Woncheol Yun is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Stony Brook University. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Jin Y. Park
nodes.summary: Jin Y. Park specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Park served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and has been a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Pema Chödrön
nodes.summary: Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa and others, serving as director and abbess of Gampo Abbey beginning in 1984.

nodes.label: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen, and served as a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University in 1990.

nodes.label: Geo Widengren
variants: ゲオ・ヴィデングレン
nodes.summary: Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, Widengren studied at Stockholm University and Uppsala University, earning a doctorate under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He was a professor at Uppsala (1940-1973) and served as president of the IAHR (~1960-1970).

nodes.label: Benoît Vermander
nodes.summary: Benoît Vermander (born 1960) is a sinologist and religious studies scholar educated at Sciences Po, Yale, Fu Jen, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) before joining Fudan University in 2009.

nodes.label: Taipei Ricci Institute
variants: Taipei Ricci Institute for Chinese Studies

nodes.label: Chiko Corona
nodes.summary: Chiko Corona is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued traditional training under Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.

nodes.label: Mikaël Bauer
nodes.summary: Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD at Harvard University under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010). He is Associate Professor at McGill University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hyon Gak Sunim
nodes.summary: Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar born in 1964. He studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), and Harvard University (~1989–1992), and trained under Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

nodes.label: Walther Heissig
nodes.native: ワルター・ハイシッヒ
variants: ワルター・ハイシッヒ
nodes.jawiki: ワルター・ハイシッヒ
nodes.summary: Walther Heissig was a scholar of Central Asian and religious studies. He studied at the University of Vienna, Humboldt University of Berlin, Göttingen, and Bonn, later holding posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Heidi Fjeld
nodes.summary: Heidi Fjeld is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Oxford and the University of Oslo under Signe Howell, later serving as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Oslo from around 2006 to 2010.

nodes.label: Ben Jiao
nodes.summary: Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University by 2001 under doctoral supervisor Melvyn C. Goldstein. He later served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Alexander O. Hsu
nodes.description: researcher of Global Affairs and religious studies scholar (field of Buddhism)
nodes.summary: Alexander O. Hsu specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer (~2011–2018), and held a teaching post at North Dakota State University (~2019–2020).

nodes.label: Anthony C. Yu
nodes.description: American scholar of literature and religion (1938-2015)
nodes.summary: Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of Chicago from around 1968 until 2005.

nodes.label: Joan Jiko Halifax
nodes.image: Joan Halifax and the Dalai Lama.jpg
nodes.description: American Zen Buddhist roshi, anthropologist, ecologist, and civil rights activist
nodes.summary: Joan Jiko Halifax studied at Newcomb College, Union Institute & University, and University of Miami. She held posts at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Harvard, and founded the Ojai Foundation and Upaya Zen Center.

nodes.label: Ajahn Sucitto
nodes.summary: Ajahn Sucitto works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971) and trained under Ajahn Sumedho starting in 1977. He served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

nodes.label: Franz Aubrey Metcalf
nodes.summary: Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. He is attested as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles, from 2002 to 2006.

nodes.label: California State University, Los Angeles
variants: California State University at Los Angeles

nodes.label: Paul David Numrich
nodes.summary: Paul David Numrich is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan (1992) and held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ann Gleig
nodes.summary: Ann Gleig is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Geshe Losang Chödar
nodes.summary: Geshe Losang Chödar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Everding
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He has held positions at Hamburg and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Sharma
nodes.summary: A scholar in Indology and linguistics, Sharma was the founder of the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

nodes.label: John B. Cobb Jr.
nodes.summary: John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University and co-founded the Center for Process Studies.

nodes.label: Joseph Prabhu
nodes.summary: Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under Bernard Williams, Alasdair MacIntyre, and doctoral supervisor John N. Findlay. He served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and held several visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Ecumenical Institute of Bossey
variants: Ecumenical Institute of the World Council of Churches

nodes.label: Sushanta Sen
nodes.summary: Sushanta Sen worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Visva-Bharati University, he served there as a lecturer in 1986 and was also Lecturer in Indian Religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

nodes.label: Sakyong Mipham
variants: サキョン・ミパム・リンポチェ
サワン・ウーセル・ランジュン・ムクポ
nodes.summary: Sakyong Mipham works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, whom he succeeded. He served on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

nodes.label: Shinobu Arai Apple
nodes.summary: Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Her studies were conducted under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003), academic adviser Robert Bickner, and teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi (2000).

nodes.label: Robert Warren Clark
nodes.summary: Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Karen Christina Lang and studied under adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Daniel Aaron Getz
nodes.summary: Daniel Aaron Getz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He was attested as an associate professor at Bradley University in 2019.

nodes.label: Kelsey Alise Seymour
nodes.summary: Kelsey Alise Seymour specializes in Sinology and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair and was a Visiting Predoctoral Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science from 2017 to 2018.

nodes.label: Tsukasa Mizushima
nodes.summary: Tsukasa Mizushima works in indology and history and archaeology. After earning his undergraduate and graduate degrees at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

nodes.label: Ankur Barua
nodes.summary: Ankur Barua works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong, he studied under supervisor Dorothy C. Wong and held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Dorothy C. Wong
nodes.summary: Dorothy C. Wong is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She has held posts at the University of Hong Kong as a visiting professor of Buddhist art and at the University of Virginia as affiliate faculty.

nodes.label: Randall Studstill
nodes.summary: Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under teachers Steven D. Goodman and Richard Payne, who served as his doctoral supervisor.

nodes.label: Chisan Kohō
nodes.summary: Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966 and served in leadership roles at Saijō-ji, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Sōji-ji (~1957–1967).

nodes.label: Maurine Stuart
nodes.summary: Maurine Stuart worked in Buddhist studies, having studied at the University of Manitoba and under teachers including Eido Shimano, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

nodes.label: Prabhasa Dharma
nodes.summary: Prabhasa Dharma (1931–1999) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies practitioner and scholar who completed traditional training under Joshu Sasaki beginning in 1967 and under Seikaku Hirata.

nodes.label: Joshu Sasaki
nodes.summary: Joshu Sasaki worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Zuiryo-ji and under Joten Soko Miura, later serving as abbot at Yotoku-in (1948–1953), Shojuan (1953), and Mount Baldy Zen Center until 2012.

nodes.label: Yong Hua
nodes.summary: Yong Hua specializes in Buddhist studies. Hua earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Hyoung Seok Ham
nodes.summary: Hyoung Seok Ham is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Virginia (2010). He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Madhav M. Deshpande (attested 2016).

nodes.label: 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Kalu Rinpoche, Beru Khyentse Rinpoche I, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. Over his career, he taught many students, including Reginald A. Ray and Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche.

nodes.id: I:American Baptist Seminary of the West
nodes.label: American Baptist Seminary of the West
variants: American Baptist Seminary of the West

nodes.label: Yoshihiro Hayashi
nodes.summary: Yoshihiro Hayashi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 2009, Hayashi was attested as a part-time lecturer at both Ritsumeikan University and Shitennoji University.

nodes.label: Ritsumeikan University
variants: 立命館大学総合心理学部
立命館大学国際関係学部

nodes.label: Anagarika Munindra
nodes.summary: Anagarika Munindra was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. He served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957 and studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka.

nodes.label: Philip Novak
nodes.summary: Philip Novak works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Notre Dame (~1968–1972) and Syracuse University (~1975–1981), and taught at Dominican University of California from ~1980 to 2017.

nodes.label: Zuigan Goto
nodes.summary: Zuigan Goto (1879–1965) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Tokyo (1903–1906) and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1901–1914). He served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

nodes.label: Dominic Sur
nodes.summary: Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Virginia, completing his doctoral studies under David Germano, and held a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Prasarn Lao-areun
nodes.summary: Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied under Viroj Inthanon and completed a PhD attested in 2014 at the University of Mysore.

nodes.label: Shrivatsa Goswami
nodes.summary: A scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, Goswami studied at Banaras Hindu University, where he also taught. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University, founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana, and was affiliated with Vrindaban Research Institute.

nodes.label: Sylvie Hureau
nodes.summary: Sylvie Hureau works in sinology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts as maître de conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Trevor Leggett
nodes.summary: Trevor Leggett (1914–2000) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Arthur Waley, Hari Prasad Shastri, and Yukio Tani. He served as Head of the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970).

nodes.label: John Riley Perks
nodes.summary: John Riley Perks is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

nodes.label: Tibetan Children's Village
variants: Central Tibetan Children's Village (TCV) school in Dharamsala

nodes.label: Jack Laughlin
nodes.summary: Jack Laughlin works in indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999 and held an academic post at the University of Sudbury.

nodes.label: Singhathon Narāsabho
nodes.summary: Singhathon Narāsabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the doctoral supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

nodes.label: Takeo Hibino
nodes.summary: Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held posts at Kyoto University and its Institute for Research in Humanities (1936–1977), Otemon Gakuin University (1977), and Otemae University (1980).

nodes.label: Abigail I. MacBain
nodes.summary: Abigail I. MacBain earned an MA at McMaster University, studying under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, and others. Specializing in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, she is attested at the University of Edinburgh in 2026.

nodes.label: Farzand Ali Durrani
nodes.summary: Farzand Ali Durrani was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Peshawar, the University of the Punjab, and the University of London. He served as a professor at the University of Peshawar from around 1970 to 1993.

nodes.label: Yu-min Lee
nodes.summary: Yu-min Lee is a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington. Lee later served as Professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002) and taught Pei-jung Wu.

nodes.label: Yaping Dou
nodes.summary: Yaping Dou is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Steffen Döll
nodes.summary: Steffen Döll specializes in Buddhist studies and japanology. He studied at the University of Munich and Kyoto University. His appointments include positions at Munich, Seikei University, and the University of Hamburg, where he became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism in 2015.

nodes.label: Stefania Travagnin
nodes.image: Stefania Travagnin in the video 'Accomplished women Female leadership and reproductive health in the Bhikṣuņī-Vinaya'.png
nodes.summary: Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She served as an assistant professor at the University of Groningen from circa 2012 to 2020 and held a post at SOAS University of London starting in 2020.

nodes.label: Koen Wellens
nodes.summary: Koen Wellens works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Per Kværne.

nodes.label: Yuguang Liu
nodes.summary: Yuguang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).

nodes.label: James H. Austin
nodes.summary: James H. Austin (born 1925) is an academic neurologist active in Buddhist studies. He studied under Katsujo Terayama and Nanrei Sohaku Kobori, holding posts at the University of Oregon/OHSU, the University of Colorado, and the University of Idaho.

nodes.label: Carmen Blacker
variants: カーメン・ブラッカー
nodes.jawiki: カーメン・ブラッカー
nodes.summary: Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, Somerville College, and Keio University under Shigeru Gorai. She served as a lecturer at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and was president of the Folklore Society (1982–1984).

nodes.label: Shigeru Gorai
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, Shigeru Gorai studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. His appointments included Kyoto Normal School, Koyasan University (~1957–1967), Otani University (1955–1978), and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore (~1964–1993).

nodes.label: Vladimir Tikhonov
nodes.image: Prof. Vladimir Tikhonov (Pak Noja) San-Peterbur Khanon-214.jpg
nodes.summary: Vladimir Tikhonov is a historian and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, Korea University, and Moscow State University. He lectured at Kyung Hee University before joining the University of Oslo in 2000.

nodes.label: Dharma Drum Mountain
variants: International Affairs Office of Dharma Drum Mountain
International Cultural and Educational Foundation of Dharma Drum Mountain

nodes.label: Hyejeong Choi
nodes.summary: Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and was attested in 2015 as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture.

nodes.label: Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture
variants: Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture

nodes.label: Karl Brunnhölzl
nodes.summary: Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under several traditional teachers, including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

nodes.label: Tenga Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tenga Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Benchen Monastery. He served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1981) and later founded Benchen Monastery in 1976.

nodes.label: Ringu Tulku
nodes.summary: Ringu Tulku is a Buddhist studies scholar and Tibetologist who studied at Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru. He founded Bodhicharya.

variants: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
Max-Planck-Institut zur Erforschung multireligiöser und multiethnischer Gesellschaften

nodes.label: Peter van der Veer
nodes.summary: Peter van der Veer worked in religious studies, Indology, and Sinology, studying at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University. His posts include the University of Amsterdam (1992) and director of the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity (~2008–2021).

nodes.label: Polish Academy of Sciences
variants: Committee on Oriental Studies of the Polish Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: John M. Rosenfield
variants: ジョン・マックス・ローゼンフィールド3世
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・マックス・ローゼンフィールド
nodes.summary: Rosenfield, who worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earned degrees from several universities, completing his PhD at Harvard under Benjamin Rowland. He held posts at Iowa, UCLA, Harvard University (1965–1991), Harvard Art Museums, and the Fogg Museum.

nodes.label: Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā
nodes.summary: Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā works in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007), studying under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe, as well as Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and N. A. Jayawickrama.

nodes.label: Toshiichi Endo
nodes.summary: Toshiichi Endo works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under supervisors including Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake, as well as Hajime Nakamura.

nodes.label: Ross Bolleter
nodes.summary: Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia under David Tunley (~1964–1967) and studied under John Tarrant and Robert Baker Aitken. He served as a Zen Buddhist teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1989–2023).

nodes.label: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit
nodes.summary: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp (~1959–1963) and Gustav Mensching (~1963–1965), and became Direktor at the University of Bonn in 1972.

nodes.label: Tara Doyle
nodes.summary: Tara Doyle specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She held posts at Emory University, where she is attested in 2003 as a lecturer and director of the Tibetan Studies Program, and in 2026 as Professor Emerita.

nodes.label: Jared Rhoton
nodes.summary: Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teacher Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his doctoral dissertation at Columbia University under Alex Wayman in 1985.

nodes.label: Seiichi Mizuno
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Seiichi Mizuno earned his doctorate and studied under Kosaku Hamada at Kyoto University. He held posts at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities and was a university professor (1949–1968).

nodes.label: Toshio Nagahiro
nodes.summary: Toshio Nagahiro worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at Kyoto University. He served at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (1929, 1950–1969), Kyoto University (~1957–1969), and Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).

nodes.label: Lucy Annette Jones
nodes.summary: Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

nodes.label: Edith Wyschogrod
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy and religious studies, Edith Wyschogrod studied at Hunter College (~1947–1951) and Columbia University (~1964–1970). She served as the J. Newton Rayzor Professor at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.

nodes.label: Helena Michie
nodes.summary: Helena Michie is an academic who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Rice University beginning around 1989.

nodes.label: John Vincent Bellezza
nodes.summary: John Vincent Bellezza is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology who studied under tutor Yungdrung Tenzin and teacher Tshering Choephel. He held an attested post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.

nodes.label: Konchok Gyatso
nodes.summary: Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Smithsonian Institution
variants: Bureau of Ethnicity of the Smithsonian Institution

nodes.label: Zayn Kassam
nodes.summary: Zayn Kassam is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. At Pomona College, she was appointed department chair, Associate Dean, and Professor in 1995; she also served at the Institute of Ismaili Studies and directed the Pacific Basin Institute.

nodes.label: Paul W. Kroll
nodes.summary: Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1976) and served as Associate Professor of Chinese and chairman of Oriental Languages and Literatures at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1980).

nodes.label: Anna M. Shields
nodes.image: Anna M. Shields (born 1966) at the Center for Chinese Studies Annual Lim Lecture.png
nodes.summary: Anna M. Shields is a Sinologist. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).

nodes.label: Douglas Allen
nodes.summary: Douglas Allen (b. 1941) works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu, and Vanderbilt universities. He taught at Southern Illinois and Central Connecticut State, and was a long-time professor at the University of Maine from 1974.

variants: ラウィー・パーウィライ
nodes.summary: Rawi Bhavilai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and Australian National University. He was a physics professor (1945–1986) and director at Chulalongkorn University, and a fellow of the Royal Institute of Thailand.

nodes.label: Gary Snyder
variants: ゲイリー・スナイダー
ゲーリー・スナイダー
nodes.jawiki: ゲーリー・スナイダー
nodes.summary: Gary Snyder is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley under Chiura Obata and Shih-Hsiang Chen, later serving as professor at UC Davis (1986–2002) and UC Irvine (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Enamul Haque
nodes.summary: Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was a Bangladeshi scholar of history and Indology who studied at Dhaka and Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991) and held leadership roles at the International Centre for Bengal Art.

nodes.label: Matthew W. King
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Matthew W. King earned his Ph.D. from the University of Toronto under doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett, having also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thubten Champa.

nodes.label: Natalie Rothman
nodes.summary: Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan (1999–2006) and took up a post at the University of Toronto in 2006.

nodes.label: Marylin Martin Rhie
nodes.summary: Marylin Martin Rhie specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Mentored by Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, she served as a professor at Smith College.

nodes.label: Pramod Chandra
nodes.summary: Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) was an art historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Mumbai. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago and later as Bickford Professor at Harvard University from 1980 to 2004.

nodes.label: Richard Foltz
nodes.jawiki: リチャード・フォルツ
nodes.summary: Richard Foltz works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and history. He studied at the University of Utah (~1982–1988) and Harvard (~1991–1996), later serving as Founding Director of the Centre for Iranian Studies at Concordia University (~2006–2026).

nodes.label: Louise Child
nodes.summary: Louise Child works in religious studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Leeds, where she completed her PhD under Linda Hogan and also studied under Ringu Tulku; she subsequently held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

nodes.label: Linda Hogan
nodes.summary: Linda Hogan (born 1964) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Maynooth University and Trinity College Dublin. She held posts at Chester, Leeds, and Trinity College Dublin, including Vice-Provost and Chief Academic Officer (2011–2016).

nodes.label: Tyler Dewar
nodes.summary: Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and under traditional teachers Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and Tashi Wangchuk.

nodes.label: Mettanando Bhikkhu
nodes.summary: Mettanando Bhikkhu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under the doctoral supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

nodes.label: Franz Xaver Erhard
nodes.summary: Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who earned master's degrees from the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and his Ph.D. from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Noa Gal
nodes.summary: Noa Gal is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

nodes.label: T. Y. Lee
nodes.summary: T. Y. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

nodes.label: Julian Schott
nodes.summary: Julian Schott is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Schott is attested in 2026 as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg and as a faculty member at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Lama Jabb
nodes.summary: Lama Jabb is a Tibetologist who has served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Andrew P. Tuck
nodes.summary: Andrew P. Tuck works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University, with teachers including Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.

nodes.label: Huaiyu Chen
nodes.summary: Huaiyu Chen studied at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and later under Stephen F. Teiser. Working in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology, Chen served as assistant professor of Chinese religions at Arizona State University (~2007–2013).

nodes.label: Sally McAra
nodes.summary: Sally McAra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), where she studied under supervisors Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

nodes.label: Karen Nero
nodes.description: professor of education in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Karen Nero is an academic who held posts at the University of Canterbury around 2004 and at the University of Otago.

nodes.label: Tsui Lan Liza Cheung
nodes.summary: Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), studying under supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and under Toshiichi Endo.

nodes.label: Nikolai Solmsdorf
nodes.summary: Nikolai Solmsdorf works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard, having also studied under Alexander von Rospatt, and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Martin Lowenthal
nodes.summary: Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Signe Howell
nodes.summary: Signe Howell was a scholar of religious studies who studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford. She became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

nodes.label: René Gothóni
nodes.summary: René Gothóni (born 1950) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1971–1977) and later served on its faculty (~1979–2014), teaching Ilkka Pyysiäinen.

nodes.label: Michael Pye
nodes.summary: Michael Pye is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds, he held posts at Leeds (~1974–1978), Marburg (1982–2004), Lancaster (1991–1994), and Otani University (~2004–2007).

nodes.label: Hung-Yi Yang
nodes.summary: Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon.

nodes.label: Roy Tzohar
nodes.summary: Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1998–2004) under Shlomo Biderman and earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2004–2011) under Gary A. Tubb. He joined the faculty of Tel Aviv University in ~2011.

nodes.label: Penghao Sun
nodes.summary: Penghao Sun is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He completed doctoral studies under Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under teachers including Mark Elliott, Peter K. Bol, Weirong Shen, and Qingying Chen (2009–2011).

nodes.label: Alva Noë
nodes.summary: Alva Noë works in philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1986–1988) and Harvard University (~1988–1995), later holding posts at CUNY (~1995–1996), UC Santa Cruz (~1996–2003), and UC Berkeley (~2003).

nodes.label: Donald Wiebe
nodes.summary: Donald Wiebe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He held a post at Trinity College, Toronto, from approximately 1980 to 2013 and served as general editor for Toronto Studies in Religion.

nodes.label: Kuntala Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Kuntala Bhattacharya earned her PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, having also studied under Prabal Kumar Sen. She held an attested post at Rabindra Bharati University in 2009.

nodes.label: Prabal Kumar Sen
nodes.summary: Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as a professor in 2009.

nodes.label: Yoshinori Takeuchi
nodes.description: Japanese historian of religion and philosopher (1913-2002)
nodes.summary: Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) studied philosophy and religious and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe. He served as an assistant professor and professor at Kyoto University, professor at Aichi Gakuin University, and member of the Japan Academy.

nodes.label: Shu-chen Chen
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Chen earned a PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang, and served there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

nodes.label: Willy Vande Walle
nodes.jawiki: ウィリー・ヴァンドゥワラ

nodes.label: Feng Youlan
nodes.summary: Feng Youlan worked in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Central China Normal University, Peking University, Tsinghua University, and Columbia University. He held posts at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952), the University of Pennsylvania (1946–1947), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1946–1947).

nodes.label: Soorakkulame Pemaratana
nodes.summary: Soorakkulame Pemaratana specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore and serves as a visiting professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Joy Brennan

nodes.label: Hank Glassman
nodes.summary: Hank Glassman is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held a faculty post at Haverford College (attested 2009 and 2019).

nodes.label: Ryan Matthew Jacobson
nodes.summary: Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University. He studied under teachers including Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, and Sarah Harding, alongside several traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Amelia Hall
nodes.summary: Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate from the University of Oxford in 2012 and held posts at Naropa University and Central Michigan University (both attested 2019).

nodes.label: Elijah Sacvan Ary
nodes.summary: Elijah Sacvan Ary is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (~2001–2007), completing his PhD under Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: St Bartholomew's Hospital Medical College
variants: St Bartholomew's Medical School, London University

nodes.label: Katharina Sabernig
nodes.summary: Katharina Sabernig is a Tibetologist who earned her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Medical University of Vienna
variants: Center for Public Health, Medical University of Vienna

nodes.id: I:DNKL Tibetan Buddhist Center for Universal Peace
nodes.label: DNKL Tibetan Buddhist Center for Universal Peace
variants: DNKL Tibetan Buddhist Center for Universal Peace (Redding, CT)

nodes.id: I:Namgyal Monastery Institute of Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: Namgyal Monastery Institute of Buddhist Studies
variants: Namgyal Monastery Institute of Buddhist Studies (Ithaca, NY)

nodes.label: Claudia Weber
nodes.summary: Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

nodes.label: Gregor Ahn
nodes.summary: Gregor Ahn (born 1958) is a religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Bonn and Copenhagen. He held posts at Münster (1992–1994) and Tartu (1995), before becoming professor at Heidelberg University in 1996.

nodes.label: Fa Yao
nodes.summary: Fa Yao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He is attested as a Visiting Lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago for 2026.

nodes.label: Michael Hookham
nodes.summary: Michael Hookham is a practitioner and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa beginning in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

nodes.label: Fred Pfeil
nodes.summary: Fred Pfeil was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at Amherst College and Stanford University. He taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford.

nodes.label: Gary Goh Wee Kian
nodes.summary: Gary Goh Wee Kian works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under supervisor Hui-Chieh Loy, foster supervisor Jay L. Garfield, and teachers Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

nodes.label: Amber D. Carpenter
nodes.summary: Amber D. Carpenter works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated by teachers including M. M. McCabe and Verity Harte, she has held posts at the University of York, University of St Andrews, and Yale-NUS College.

nodes.label: Rachael Wiseman
nodes.summary: Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York. She served as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool around 2016.

nodes.label: Bronwyn Finnigan
nodes.summary: Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Universities of Sydney, Melbourne, and Auckland (studying under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop), she held posts at Auckland, Marquette University, and the Australian National University.

nodes.label: Christopher Kelley
nodes.summary: Christopher Kelley is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at Columbia University. He taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College, and founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy.

nodes.label: Trine Brox
nodes.summary: Trine Brox specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Christian K. Wedemeyer and was attested as an Associate Professor at the University of Copenhagen in 2026.

nodes.label: Heidi I. Koppl
nodes.summary: Heidi I. Koppl is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed an MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and studied under the traditional teacher Sherab Zangpo.

nodes.label: Eugen Pander
nodes.summary: Eugen Pander (1854–1894) studied at Polytechnikum Riga and worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. In 1881, he was appointed professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.

nodes.label: Qiang Ning
nodes.summary: Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Supervised by Hung Wu and Irene Winter, he worked as a researcher at the Dunhuang Academy and taught at San Diego State University, Yale University, and the University of Michigan (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Shuhong Chang
nodes.summary: Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. After studying in Lyon and Paris, he taught at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and served as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy.

nodes.label: Ives Waldo
nodes.summary: Ives Waldo works in philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa from 1970 to 1988.

nodes.id: I:Starr King School for the Ministry
nodes.label: Starr King School for the Ministry
variants: Starr King School for the Ministry

nodes.label: Wing-tsit Chan
nodes.summary: Wing-tsit Chan (1901–1994) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard University (~1924–1929) and held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1936–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

nodes.label: Masaaki Sugiyama
nodes.summary: Masaaki Sugiyama (1952–2019) worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978) and held a post at Kyoto Women's University (~1983–1992).

nodes.label: Brandon J. Harwood
nodes.summary: Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015) under the supervision of Patrick Pranke.

nodes.label: Patrick Pranke
nodes.summary: Patrick Pranke is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.

nodes.label: Andree Dominique Messent
nodes.summary: Andree Dominique Messent specializes in Buddhist studies. Messent earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams, also studying under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

nodes.label: Tan Poh Beng
nodes.summary: Tan Poh Beng is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, supervised by Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, and also studied under Sumanasiri and Shengshou.

nodes.label: Ayya Khema
nodes.summary: Ayya Khema was a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner and scholar who studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Mahathera, and Matara Sri Ñāṇārāma. She served as a teacher at Buddha-Haus from 1989.

nodes.label: Chatsumarn Kabilsingh
nodes.native: ฉัตรสุมาลย์ กบิลสิงห์
nodes.summary: Chatsumarn Kabilsingh worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh Universities. She taught in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University from circa 1973 to 2000.

nodes.label: Thích Thiện Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Thiện Châu was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed his education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1967–1971) and completing his doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1967–1977).

nodes.id: I:Tulana Research Centre for Encounter and Dialogue
nodes.label: Tulana Research Centre for Encounter and Dialogue
variants: Tulana-Forschungszentrum (Tulana Research Center for Encounter and Dialogue)
Tulana Research Centre for Encounter and Dialogue

nodes.label: Hla Pe
nodes.summary: Hla Pe was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon and earned a doctorate from SOAS University of London. He taught Burmese language and culture at SOAS starting in 1948 and became Professor of Burmese (1966–1980).

nodes.label: Magdalene College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学のモードリン・カレッジ

nodes.label: Gisela Emma Full
nodes.summary: Gisela Emma Full, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she held research fellow appointments at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

nodes.label: European University Viadrina
variants: フランクフルト（オーダー）大学

nodes.label: Samueli Institute
variants: Samueli-Institute of Brain, Mind and Healing

nodes.label: Mingyu Fu
nodes.summary: Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

nodes.id: I:Buddhist Association of the United States
nodes.label: Buddhist Association of the United States
variants: Buddhist Association of the United States

nodes.label: Joey Hung
nodes.summary: Joey Hung (born 1991) works in computational fields and Buddhist studies. After attending the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, he held a post at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (~2014) and later at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Vidya Dehejia
nodes.summary: Vidya Dehejia is an art historian and Indologist who studied at St. Xavier's, Newnham, and the University of Cambridge (PhD). She held posts at Sydney, Hong Kong, SPA New Delhi, the Smithsonian Institution, and Columbia University, where she was appointed professor in 2002.

nodes.label: American Museum of Natural History
variants: アメリカ自然史博物館

nodes.label: James Miller
nodes.summary: James Miller (born 1968) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA from Cambridge (by 1997) and a PhD from Boston University (by 2000), later serving as Professor at Queen's University Belfast (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Emily T. Yeh
nodes.summary: Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who earned degrees from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She joined the faculty of the University of Colorado Boulder around 2003.

nodes.label: Surendra Man Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

nodes.label: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya works in Buddhist studies. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre, and he taught Surendra Man Bajracharya.

nodes.label: Yungfen Ma
nodes.summary: Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ma earned a PhD at Columbia University (attested 2011), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü.

nodes.label: Paul Debes
nodes.summary: Paul Debes was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), the journal Wissen und Wandel (1955), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955).

nodes.label: Hari Shankar Prasad
nodes.summary: Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, under Ramakant Tripathi, and under doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Mark A. Nathan
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and history, Mark A. Nathan earned his PhD from UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held positions at UCLA, Kangwon National University, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Leopold Pospisil
nodes.summary: Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University, Willamette University, the University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale from 1956 and as an anthropology curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (circa 1956–1993).

nodes.label: Harold C. Conklin
nodes.summary: Harold C. Conklin was a linguist and anthropologist. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley and Yale University. He taught at Columbia University and served as a professor at Yale (1962–1996) and curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (1974–1996).

nodes.label: Mirjan Damaška
nodes.summary: Mirjan Damaška studied law at Zagreb, the Hague Academy, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Ljubljana (PhD 1960). He held posts at the University of Zagreb, University of Pennsylvania, and Yale University (beginning 1975–1976).

nodes.label: Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ユリウス・ローデウェイク・ドイフェンダック
nodes.summary: Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889–1954) was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University, the Sorbonne, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held visiting professorships at Columbia, Princeton, and Oxford, and served as Professor of Chinese at Leiden University (1930–1954).

nodes.label: Fu-shih Lin
nodes.summary: Fu-shih Lin was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser (ca. 1988–1994), later working at Academia Sinica (ca. 1994–2021).

nodes.label: Hwansoo Kim
nodes.summary: Hwansoo Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held posts as a professor at Duke University and as a professor of religious studies at Yale University.

nodes.label: Helena Blankleder
nodes.summary: Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, as attested in 1999.

nodes.label: Marek Zemánek
nodes.summary: Marek Zemánek is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under the supervision of Radek Chlup.

nodes.label: Thich Nhat Tu
nodes.image: TT. Thích Nhật Từ phát biểu trong lễ bế mạc Đại lễ Vesak 2014.JPG

nodes.label: Tan Yun-shan
nodes.summary: Tan Yun-shan was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at Wenjiang Shuyuan, Mijiang Shuyuan, Chuanshan Academy, and Hunan Normal University, he founded the Sino-Indian Cultural Society and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (1937–1968).

nodes.label: Kshitimohan Sen
variants: クシティモハン・セン
nodes.jawiki: クシティモハン・セン
nodes.summary: Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed an MA in Sanskrit at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, worked in the Chamba State Education Department (1902–1908), and served as Adhyaksha at Visva-Bharati University (1953–1954).

nodes.label: Paul Kingsbury
nodes.summary: Paul Kingsbury worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).

nodes.label: John Stevens
nodes.description: Buddhist priest, teacher of Buddhist studies and aikido teacher

nodes.label: Piotr Klafkowski
nodes.summary: Piotr Klafkowski (1953–2002) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski, having also studied under Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Jerzy Bańczerowski
nodes.summary: Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956-1961). He spent his career there as department head (1969) and professor (1977-1991), and was a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences (~1989).

nodes.label: Ruixuan Chen
nodes.summary: Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen completed an MA under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, earned a PhD at Leiden University under Paul Harrison (attested 2018), and is affiliated with Peking University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Adelheid Mette
nodes.summary: Adelheid Mette was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg (1953–1958, Habilitation by 1972). She held professorships at the University of Munich (1978, 1980) and served as chair of Indology at the University of Münster (1988–2000).

nodes.label: Olav Hackstein
nodes.summary: Olav Hackstein (born 1962) specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UPenn and the University of Freiburg, later holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg, UPenn, EPHE, and a chair at the University of Munich (2008).

nodes.label: Linda Learman
nodes.summary: Linda Learman is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She was supervised by doctoral advisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory (both attested 2005).

nodes.label: University of Nebraska at Omaha
variants: ネブラスカ大学オマハ校

nodes.label: David W. Chappell
nodes.summary: David W. Chappell worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale, he was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1972–2002) and later taught at Soka University of America (~2002–2004).

nodes.label: Hajime Tanabe
nodes.summary: Hajime Tanabe (1885–1962) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, as well as in Germany under Heidegger, Rickert, and Husserl. Influenced by Kitaro Nishida, he taught at Kyoto University from 1919 to 1945.

nodes.label: Cuma Ozkan
nodes.summary: Cuma Ozkan is a scholar in religious studies and Sinology who earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Stephan Marcus Salzberg
nodes.summary: Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia, where his teachers included Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

nodes.id: I:Institute for the Study of American Religion
nodes.label: Institute for the Study of American Religion
variants: Institute for the Study of American Religion

nodes.label: Edmund Leach
nodes.summary: Edmund Leach studied at Cambridge and the London School of Economics (PhD). Working in religious studies and related fields, he held posts at the LSE (~1947–1953), Cambridge (1953–1978), King's College, Cambridge (1966–1979), and the Royal Anthropological Institute (1971–1975).

nodes.label: Carolyn Woodford Schmidt
nodes.summary: Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and held posts at Ohio State University and Denison University.

nodes.label: Yanfei Zhou
nodes.summary: Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and sinology. Zhou earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.

nodes.label: Yiliang Zhou
nodes.summary: Yiliang Zhou was a historian, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University, and Harvard University. A student of Yinke Chen (~1935–1939), he was a professor at Peking University (~1953–2001).

nodes.label: Université libre de Bruxelles
variants: Center for Study of South and Southeast Asia at the University of Brussels

nodes.label: Chack-fan Lee
nodes.summary: Chack-fan Lee, active in Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1968) and the University of Western Ontario (~1969–1972). He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.

nodes.label: Sze-bong Tso
nodes.summary: Sze-bong Tso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

nodes.label: Loukram Ibempishak Devi
nodes.summary: Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University (attested 1999) under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma, having also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Yamamoto is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Silpakorn University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.

nodes.label: Samniang Leurmsai
nodes.native: สำเนียง เลื่อมใส

nodes.label: Chirapat Prapandvidya
nodes.native: จิรพัฒน์ ประพันธ์วิทยา
nodes.summary: Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University and served as its director in 1996.

nodes.id: I:Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism
nodes.label: Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism
variants: Dawn Mountain Community Center & Research Institute

nodes.label: Phra Sigambhirayan
nodes.native: พระศรีคัมภีรญาณ
nodes.summary: Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Riika J. Virtanen
nodes.summary: Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who conducted her doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and studied under teacher Sangye Tandar Naga.

nodes.label: Sandra Hochwarter
nodes.summary: Sandra Hochwarter works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Anne MacDonald.

nodes.label: August Johan Bernet Kempers
nodes.image: Installatie nieuwe directeur van het Rijksmuseum voor Volkenkunde Het Nederland, Bestanddeelnr 909-2587.jpg
nodes.summary: August Johan Bernet Kempers was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Leiden University. He directed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1936–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and University of Amsterdam.

nodes.label: Theodoor van Erp
nodes.image: Portret van Dr Th. van Erp, luitenant der genie en restaurator van de Borobudur, RP-F-2013-61-1.jpg

nodes.label: Madhu Khanna
nodes.summary: Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (both attested 2012).

nodes.label: Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche (born 1946) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Suk Fun Ng
nodes.summary: Suk Fun Ng is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014). She studied under teachers including K. L. Dhammajoti, Jing Yin, and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa.

nodes.label: Sarat Sarma
nodes.summary: Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Manipur University under the supervision of S. Shyamkishore Singh (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Jan Dolensky
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jan Dolensky earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Ming Mei
nodes.summary: Ming Mei is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MPhil from the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan. She also studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

nodes.label: Andrey Terentyev
nodes.summary: Andrey Terentyev (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University's Faculty of Philosophy (~1970–1975), taught Ming Mei, and held a post at the Museum of history of religion (~1978–1992).

nodes.label: Wulstan Fletcher
nodes.summary: Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1999, he studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Pei-jung Wu
nodes.summary: Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. She studied at National Taiwan University and completed her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles under Donald F. McCallum.

nodes.label: Ng-Fung Yuen
nodes.summary: Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of the West under the doctoral supervision of Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Tsoknyi Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Adeu Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, holding a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

nodes.label: Ling Ji
nodes.summary: Ling Ji is a sinologist who earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the doctoral supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Notto R. Thelle
nodes.summary: Notto R. Thelle works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served as associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo from 1986 to 2006.

nodes.id: I:NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
nodes.label: NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
variants: National Christian Council (NCC) Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in Kyōto

nodes.label: Kiattisak Ponampon
nodes.summary: Kiattisak Ponampon specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and was taught in 2013 by Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others.

nodes.label: Somchai Thanavuddho
nodes.native: สมชาย ฐานวุฑฺโฒ

nodes.label: Ann Grodzins Gold
nodes.summary: Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD in anthropology at the University of Chicago (~1970–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993).

nodes.label: Mumon Yamada
variants: Mumon Yamada (山田 無文, Yamada Mumon)
nodes.summary: Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Shofuku-ji (~1949–1978), president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies.

nodes.label: Gianpaolo Vetturini
nodes.summary: Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

nodes.label: Keir Strickland
nodes.summary: Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Durham University (~2007–2011) under Robin Coningham. He held academic posts at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University (2016).

nodes.label: Zeng Yang
nodes.summary: Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Tsering Shakya
nodes.summary: Tsering Shakya works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD from SOAS University of London, later serving there as a research fellow (1999–2002), teaching at Oxford, and joining the University of British Columbia (~2005).

nodes.label: Kang-nam Oh
nodes.summary: Kang-nam Oh is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and earned his doctorate under Yün-hua Jan. He held an attested post at the University of Regina from 1990 to 1998.

nodes.label: Hsu-feng Lee
nodes.summary: Hsu-feng Lee studied at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and earned a PhD from the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017). Lee works in Buddhist studies.

nodes.label: Douglas Q. Adams
nodes.summary: Douglas Q. Adams works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1968 to 1972 and held a post at the University of Idaho around 1972.

nodes.label: Filippo Marsili
nodes.summary: Filippo Marsili is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, Arcangela Santoro, and Paolo Daffinà. He has held a post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Jane Bunnag
nodes.summary: Jane Bunnag is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London in 1969, where she was supervised by E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

nodes.label: E. Michael Mendelson
nodes.description: American poet, essayist, anthropologist, and translator (1928–2024)
nodes.summary: E. Michael Mendelson was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He was educated at the University of Cambridge (King's College) (~1948–1952), the University of Paris (~1952–1956), and the University of Chicago (~1956–1963).

nodes.label: Barbara E. Ward
nodes.summary: Barbara E. Ward was a sinologist who studied at Newnham College, the University of London, and the London School of Economics. She held posts at the University of London, Cambridge, Cornell, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: David M. DiValerio
nodes.summary: David M. DiValerio works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute and the University of Virginia, where he earned his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee.

nodes.label: Hubert Decleer
nodes.summary: Decleer studied at Hoger Technisch Instituut Oostende and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at SIT Graduate Institute, Alliance Française, Middlebury College, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Lloyd W. Pflueger
nodes.summary: Lloyd W. Pflueger works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate from the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kshanika Saha
nodes.summary: Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and earned her PhD from the University of Calcutta (attested 1966).

nodes.label: Michael Baxandall
variants: マイケル・バクサンドール
nodes.jawiki: マイケル・バクサンドール
nodes.summary: Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) was an art historian educated at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, Oxford, the Courtauld Institute, UC Berkeley, and Cornell University.

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Drège
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at INALCO, the University of Burgundy, and under Yves Hervouet. He served as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from around 1998 to 2004.

nodes.label: Mohammad Ashraf Dar
nodes.summary: Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indologist and historian who earned an MPhil from Vikram University, where he was attested as a research scholar in 2014.

nodes.label: Nyingcha Duoji
nodes.summary: Nyingcha Duoji works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Boston University and completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under Mark Elliott.

nodes.label: Chih-fu Li
nodes.summary: Chih-fu Li specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He served as Director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007), later becoming its honorary director upon retiring in December 2006.

nodes.label: Stephen Fuchs
nodes.summary: Stephen Fuchs worked in Indology and religious studies, earning his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt. He founded the Anthropos Institute and Institute of Indian Culture, and taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950–1954) and University of San Carlos.

nodes.label: Ronald Neufeldt
nodes.summary: Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Calgary (~1977–2006), serving as Associate Professor in Religious Studies (~1982–1990) and becoming Professor Emeritus in ~2006.

nodes.label: Fumio Tamamuro
nodes.summary: Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1953–1957) and later held a post there from ~1968 to 2006.

nodes.label: Yuan Ren
nodes.summary: Yuan Ren works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ren earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Doris Unterthurner
nodes.summary: Doris Unterthurner works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her master's degree at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Manfred Taube
nodes.summary: Manfred Taube was a Tibetologist and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller. In 1991, he became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at Leipzig.

nodes.label: Diane L. Howard
nodes.summary: Diane L. Howard specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She was a graduate student at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Lama Yeshe Gyamtso
nodes.summary: Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

nodes.label: Douglas Ober
nodes.summary: Douglas Ober works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under supervisor Harjot Oberoi (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Harjot Oberoi
nodes.summary: Harjot Oberoi works in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University before holding the Chair of Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia from around 1987.

nodes.label: Ter Ellingson
nodes.description: American ethnomusicologist and professor of music
nodes.summary: Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he served as a music professor at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

nodes.label: Alnis Dickson
nodes.summary: Alnis Dickson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at McGill University, where he studied under supervisor Lara Braitstein and teacher G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

nodes.label: Ösel Tendzin
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies practitioner, Ösel Tendzin studied at Fordham University and under Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He served as executive vice president of Vajradhatu beginning in 1973, later succeeding Trungpa in 1987.

nodes.label: Chamnong Adivadhanasit
nodes.summary: Chamnong Adivadhanasit is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. He served as a Professor at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University (both attested 2012).

nodes.label: Lê Mạnh Thát
nodes.summary: Lê Mạnh Thát (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history. He earned a BA at Saigon University (c. 1962–1965) and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (c. 1967–1974), later holding a post at Vạn Hạnh University (c. 1974–1975).

nodes.label: Pataraporn Sirikanchana
nodes.summary: Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania and held a professorship at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Nobumi Iyanaga
nodes.summary: Nobumi Iyanaga (1948–) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1968–1969). He held a research contract at the EFEO Tokyo Centre (2008–2014) and lectured at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Phillip Bloom
nodes.summary: Phillip Bloom is a scholar of archaeology and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

nodes.label: John Corrigan
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar John Corrigan earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1975–1982). His career includes positions at the University of Virginia (~1982–1987), Arizona State University (~1987–2001), and Florida State University, where he chaired the Religion Department (~2001).

nodes.label: Françoise Robin
nodes.summary: Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who earned her DEA at INALCO and completed her doctorate under Heather Stoddard. She directed the Tibetan department and Southeast Asia/Pacific department at INALCO, served as director at Collège de France, and founded SFEMT.

nodes.label: Maurice Wiles
nodes.summary: Maurice Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tonbridge School (~1937–1941) and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1945–1950).

nodes.label: Iso Kern
nodes.summary: Iso Kern is a philosopher and scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at KU Leuven, Freiburg, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University, he held posts at KU Leuven (1962–1971), Heidelberg (~1973–1979), Bern (1985), Zurich, and Fribourg.

nodes.label: David Fiordalis
nodes.summary: David Fiordalis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and served as associate professor and chair of religious studies at Linfield University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Burton Watson
nodes.summary: Burton Watson was a scholar of sinology and Japanology who studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University. He taught at Doshisha University, Kyoto University, Columbia University, and Stanford University.

nodes.label: Victor Forte
nodes.summary: Victor Forte is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at Temple University in 2004. He held an assistant professorship in religious studies at Albright College, attested in 2007.

nodes.label: Robert Magliola
nodes.summary: Robert Magliola is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Princeton (~1965–1970). He held faculty posts at Purdue (1969), Tamkang, Assumption University, and National Taiwan University (1987–1998).

nodes.label: Yingshan Chen
nodes.summary: Yingshan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996) and is attested as an honorary research fellow there in 2026, having retired in 2023.

nodes.label: Rinzin Thargyal
nodes.summary: Rinzin Thargyal is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

nodes.label: Fredrik Barth
nodes.summary: Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He founded and held a professorship at the University of Bergen, later holding chairs and teaching posts at Oslo, the Museum of Cultural History, Emory, Harvard, and Boston University.

nodes.label: John Buescher
