nodes.summary: John Buescher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America.

nodes.label: Marshall Sahlins
nodes.jawiki: マーシャル・サーリンズ
nodes.summary: Marshall Sahlins was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1947–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954), held a post at Michigan (~1957–1973), and joined the University of Chicago faculty in 1973.

nodes.label: Jinping Liao
nodes.summary: Jinping Liao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

nodes.label: Gary D. DeAngelis
nodes.summary: Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

nodes.label: George Rupp
nodes.summary: George Rupp is a religious studies scholar who studied at Princeton, Yale, Yale Divinity School, Harvard, and Harvard Divinity School. He held academic posts at Rice University from 1985 to 1993 and at Columbia University from around 1993 to 2002.

nodes.label: Thomas Borchert
nodes.summary: Thomas Borchert works in Buddhist and religious studies. A former PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005), he held an appointment as Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Anna Brown
nodes.summary: Anna Brown is a scholar of religious studies and a Zen student under Robert Kennedy (attested 2017). Attested in 2017, she served as chair of the political science department and director of the social justice program at Saint Peter's University.

nodes.label: Robert Kennedy
nodes.description: American Jesuit priest, psychoanalyst and Zen rōshi

nodes.label: Hsiao-Lan Hu
nodes.summary: Hsiao-Lan Hu earned a PhD from Temple University in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Hu served as an associate professor at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Richard Sylvan
nodes.summary: Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington and Princeton University. He held positions at the University of Sydney (circa 1963–1964) and the Australian National University (from 1971).

nodes.label: Mei Ching Hsuan
nodes.summary: A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Mei Ching Hsuan earned a PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh, and was attested as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2026.

nodes.label: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche (b. 1966) is an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under his spiritual teacher, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and founded the organization Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

nodes.label: Matthieu Ricard
nodes.summary: Matthieu Ricard works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob and under traditional teachers Kangyur Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, later serving as a board member of the Mind and Life Institute.

nodes.label: Karolinska Institute
variants: Department of Histology at the Karolinska Institute

nodes.id: I:National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
nodes.label: National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
variants: National Hospital for the Paralysed and Epileptic

nodes.id: I:Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels
nodes.label: Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels
variants: Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels

nodes.id: I:National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
nodes.label: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
variants: National Institute of Neurology and Psychiatry

nodes.label: Levi McLaughlin
nodes.summary: Levi McLaughlin specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Princeton University and the University of Tokyo under Susumu Shimazono, and has served as an associate professor at North Carolina State University since 2012.

nodes.label: Takashi Nakao
nodes.summary: Takashi Nakao was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education. He was an associate professor at Bunkyo University Women's College and later professor emeritus at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Axel Klein
nodes.summary: Axel Klein is a scholar of Japanology who studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994). He held posts at Bonn, the German Institute for Japanese Studies, and became a professor at the University of Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

nodes.label: Michael J. Tetreault
nodes.summary: Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned a Master of Arts at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko, attested in 2011.

nodes.label: Natasha Reichle
nodes.summary: Natasha Reichle is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, under Joanna Gottfried Williams, Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.

nodes.label: Amin Sweeney
nodes.summary: Amin Sweeney was a linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of London (~1967–1970). He taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and UC Berkeley (1986–1991), becoming emeritus professor in 1998.

nodes.label: Luboš Bělka
nodes.summary: Luboš Bělka specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from ~1977 to 1982 and held a post there beginning around 1993.

nodes.label: Masaryk University
variants: Institute for the Study of Religions at Masaryk University of Brno

nodes.label: Diana Lange
nodes.summary: Diana Lange works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, and EPHE, she worked at TU Berlin, Humboldt, Leipzig, Hamburg, and was appointed Professor of Central Asian History and Cultures at Humboldt in 2025.

nodes.label: Solomon George FitzHerbert
nodes.summary: Solomon George FitzHerbert is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He served as Departmental Lecturer at Oxford and as a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Kathleen McDonald
nodes.summary: Kathleen McDonald is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Adam Pearcey
nodes.summary: Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, and studied with numerous traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama.

nodes.label: Trulshik Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trulshik Rinpoche (1924–2011) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and others, and taught prominent students including the 14th Dalai Lama, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Daijaku Judith Kinst
nodes.summary: Daijaku Judith Kinst specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She held a faculty post at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and is attested as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 2026.

nodes.label: Raimon Panikkar
nodes.summary: Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) specialized in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Barcelona, Bonn, Mysore, Banaras Hindu, Complutense (under Juan Zaragüeta), and Lateran universities, later teaching at Complutense, Harvard, and UC Santa Barbara (1971–1978; emeritus circa 1987–2010).

nodes.label: Zenkei Blanche Hartman
nodes.summary: Zenkei Blanche Hartman was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the University of California (~1943–1947), she trained under Jōshin Kasai, Richard Baker, and Mel Weitsman, later serving as co-abbess at the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).

nodes.label: Victor B. Lieberman
nodes.summary: Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned a BA from Yale University and a PhD from SOAS University of London. In 1984, he was appointed Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Christopher Jon Jensen
nodes.summary: Christopher Jon Jensen is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University, earning his PhD in 2018 under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn.

nodes.label: Kathrin Holz
nodes.summary: Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation with the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Eva K. Neumaier
nodes.summary: Eva K. Neumaier works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. By 2006, she was Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary, as well as Professor Emeritus and former Chair of East Asian Studies at the University of Alberta.

nodes.label: Hammalawa Saddhatissa
nodes.image: Most Venerable Hammalawa Saddhatissa Maha Thera (1914–1990).jpg
nodes.summary: Hammalawa Saddhatissa (1914–1990) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Sastrodaya and Vidyodaya Pirivenas, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Edinburgh. He taught at BHU and Toronto, and headed the London Buddhist Vihara (~1957–1990).

nodes.label: Shenghai Li
nodes.summary: Shenghai Li works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Li completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., having also studied with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Ram Shankar Tripathi, among others.

nodes.label: Jean Petitot
nodes.summary: Jean Petitot is a philosopher and linguist who studied at the École Polytechnique from circa 1964 to 1966 and later served as its director from circa 1992 to 1999.

nodes.label: Bradley L. Herling
nodes.summary: Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies and philosophy. He served as Assistant Director at Boston University and held a post at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Sumi Lee
nodes.summary: Sumi Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Lee completed an MA under Alexander L. Mayer at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and a PhD under Robert E. Buswell Jr. at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Christmas Humphreys
nodes.summary: Christmas Humphreys was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as President of the Buddhist Society from circa 1924 to 1983.

nodes.label: Michael von Brück
nodes.description: German Protestant theologian and pastor, religious scientist and author, and Zen and yoga teacher
nodes.summary: Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his promotion at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and studied at the University of Madras (~1980–1985). He held chairs at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and University of Munich (~1991–2014).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Mehlman
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy. He held positions at Cornell University (~1971-1974), Yale University, Johns Hopkins University (~1974-1980), and Boston University (~1984), alongside visiting professorships at Harvard, UC Berkeley, CUNY Graduate Center, Washington University, and MIT.

nodes.label: Stephanie Kaza
nodes.summary: Stephanie Kaza works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Oberlin College, Stanford University, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry, studying under Thich Nhat Hanh and Joanna Macy. She was a professor at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: George Quasha
nodes.summary: George Quasha worked in religious studies and Tibetology and founded Station Hill Press. He held teaching posts at Stony Brook University, Bard College, The New School, and Naropa University.

nodes.label: Nguyen Thi Xinh
nodes.summary: Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Kathleen D. Morrison
nodes.summary: Kathleen D. Morrison is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Notre Dame, the University of New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She held positions at Northwestern University and the University of Pennsylvania.

nodes.label: Khenpo Dazer
nodes.summary: Khenpo Dazer was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima. He held teaching posts at Śrī Siṃha Shedra and the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

nodes.label: Hisao Kanaseki
nodes.summary: Hisao Kanaseki, active in Buddhist studies and other fields, studied at Doshisha University (c. 1937–1941). He was a professor at Kobe University (c. 1950–1963) and Komazawa University (c. 1982–1989), and honorary professor at Tokyo Metropolitan University (c. 1963–1982).

nodes.label: King Chung Lo
nodes.summary: King Chung Lo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of Leipzig, supervised by Eli Franco in 2009.

nodes.label: Jinling He
nodes.summary: Jinling He is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.

nodes.label: Natalie Depraz
nodes.summary: Philosopher Natalie Depraz studied at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre. She held posts at the Collège International de Philosophie, Paris-Sorbonne, Galatasaray, and the University of Rouen Normandy, where she founded the Rouen School of Phenomenology.

nodes.label: Limei Chi
nodes.summary: Limei Chi works in Buddhist studies and sinology and studied under Jinhua Chen. Chi held posts as faculty at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and Professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Karma Sonam Palmo
nodes.summary: Karma Sonam Palmo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Yui Suzuki
nodes.summary: Yui Suzuki specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. Suzuki studied at UCLA under doctoral supervisors William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Davis Schoening
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Davis Schoening specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), studying under doctoral supervisor Collett Cox and advisor Sanghasen Singh.

nodes.label: Chönyi Drolma
nodes.summary: Chönyi Drolma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).

nodes.label: Tsering Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Mark Owen
nodes.summary: Mark Owen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Stuart
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality and served as Direktorin at the University of Winchester in 2021.

nodes.label: Jürgen Renn
nodes.description: German physicist, historian of science and university professor
nodes.summary: Jürgen Renn works in history/archaeology and philosophy, earning a PhD from TU Berlin in 1987. He taught at Boston University and was named director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994) and Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (2022).

nodes.label: Yulian Zeng
nodes.summary: Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Zeng studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Graham E. Clarke
nodes.summary: Graham E. Clarke (d. 1998) worked in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was attested as a Senior Member in 1998.

nodes.label: Gelek
nodes.summary: Gelek is a Tibetology scholar who served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998). He has also held appointments as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Nancy E. Levine
nodes.summary: Nancy E. Levine is a scholar of Tibetology and anthropology. She held positions in anthropology at the University of California, Los Angeles, attested as Associate Professor in 1998 and Professor in 2026.

nodes.label: Angela Manderscheid
nodes.summary: Angela Manderscheid works in Tibetology and related fields. She has held posts at the Free University of Berlin and at the University of Oulu, where she was attested as a researcher in 1998.

nodes.label: Ronald D. Schwartz
nodes.summary: Working in Tibetology and sociology, Ronald D. Schwartz held positions as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Klaus-Josef Notz
nodes.summary: Klaus-Josef Notz (1942–2013) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied theology at Philosophisch-Theologische Hochschule Benediktbeuern (1966–1971) and the University of Munich (1978–1984), where he later served as a Lehrbeauftragter in 1996.

nodes.id: I:Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München
nodes.label: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München
variants: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München

nodes.label: Holmes Welch
nodes.summary: Holmes Welch was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his B.A. and M.A. at Harvard University (~1940-1957) and served as a lecturer at both Harvard and Yale University.

nodes.label: Chüan-ying Yen
nodes.summary: Chüan-ying Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and sinology. She completed her PhD at Harvard University, studying under Chu-tsing Li, John Hay, and John M. Rosenfield.

nodes.label: Chu-tsing Li
nodes.summary: Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking (1943–1947), art history at Iowa (circa 1956–1966), and served on the University of Kansas faculty (1966).

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Saunders
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara circa 1908–1912. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at Pacific School of Religion and Lecturer at the University of California (~1921–1935).

nodes.label: Takamaro Shigaraki
nodes.summary: Takamaro Shigaraki was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University. He served as professor and president of Ryukoku University (1989–1995) and chairman of Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (1995–2008; ~2010–2014), and founded Kōmyōji.

nodes.label: Ontario Tech University
variants: University of Ontario Institute of Technology

nodes.id: I:Vienna University of Economics and Business
nodes.label: Vienna University of Economics and Business
variants: Institut für Wirtschafts- und Sozialgeschichte, Wirtschaftsuniversität Wien

nodes.label: Monika Nowakowska
nodes.summary: Monika Nowakowska is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who has held posts at the University of Warsaw, attested in 2010 and 2026.

nodes.label: Kuno Lorenz
nodes.summary: Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, Kiel (PhD), and Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg in 1970 and served as a professor at Saarland University from 1974 to 1998.

nodes.label: Claus Oetke
nodes.summary: Claus Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, completing his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1969–1983). He taught at Hamburg (~1974–1987) and led the Indology department at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

nodes.id: I:Internationales Kolleg für Geisteswissenschaftliche Forschung, Erlangen
nodes.label: Internationales Kolleg für Geisteswissenschaftliche Forschung, Erlangen
Rolf Scheuermann
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Rolf Scheuermann completed a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under supervisor Helmut Tauscher (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Edward H. Schafer
nodes.summary: Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Harvard. He was a faculty member in the Department of Oriental Languages at UC Berkeley from ~1947 to 1984.

nodes.label: Thomas B. Ellis
nodes.summary: Thomas B. Ellis is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Appalachian State University as Assistant Professor of Religion (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Jos Gommans
nodes.summary: Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist who studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University, where he completed his doctoral studies under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. He was appointed associate professor at Leiden University in 1993.

nodes.label: Dirk H. A. Kolff
nodes.summary: Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who completed his MA and doctorate at Leiden University. He served at Leiden University as a lecturer in 1967 and held the Chair of Indian History from 1971 to 2003.

nodes.label: Delhi School of Economics
variants: Delhi School of Economics, University of Delhi

nodes.label: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph
nodes.summary: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph studied at Sarah Lawrence, Harvard (MA, PhD), and Radcliffe. After teaching political science at Harvard (~1955–1963), she was a professor at the University of Chicago (from 1964) and president of the American Political Science Association (2003–2004).

nodes.id: I:Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
nodes.label: Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
variants: Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
Fine Arts Institute, Academy of Sciences, Uzbekistan

nodes.label: Eiki Hoshino
nodes.summary: Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1962–1972). He later served there as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director (~1985–2014).

nodes.label: Phanit Jetjiravat
nodes.summary: Phanit Jetjiravat specializes in Buddhist studies and earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where they were advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

nodes.label: Prayoon Dhammacitto
nodes.native: พระธรรมโกศาจารย์

nodes.label: Paetpong Worapongpichet
nodes.native: แปดพงศ์ วรพงศ์พิเชษฐ

nodes.label: Yuri Parfionovich
nodes.summary: Yuri Parfionovich (1921–1990) worked in tibetology. He studied under George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.

nodes.label: Francis N. J.
nodes.summary: Francis N. J. works in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned a master's at the University of Calicut and completed doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier, attested in 2002.

nodes.label: M. R. Raghava Varier
nodes.summary: M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is an Indologist, historian, and linguist. He earned degrees from the University of Calicut, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and studied at the Archaeological Survey of India, later serving as Professor at the University of Calicut (c. 1976–1996).

nodes.label: Rajan Gurukkal
nodes.summary: Rajan Gurukkal (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he held posts at JNU, Mahatma Gandhi University (Director, 1988), and the Indian Institute of Science (2012–2016).

nodes.label: Harold Scheub
nodes.summary: Harold Scheub earned degrees from the University of Michigan and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, also studying at UCLA. After teaching at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he served as a professor of humanities at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1970–2013).

nodes.label: Thomas James Mazanec
nodes.summary: Thomas James Mazanec specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University, earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder, and received his PhD from Princeton University under supervisors Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser.

nodes.label: Jeff Dolven
nodes.summary: Jeff Dolven studied at Yale University and the University of Oxford. He served as a fellow at Harvard University and Trinity College, Cambridge, before becoming a professor of English at Princeton University around 2001.

nodes.label: Joshua Timothy Katz
nodes.summary: Joshua Timothy Katz is a linguist who studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He was Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (~2022).

nodes.label: Christopher Braider
nodes.description: American French and Italian language professor

nodes.label: Nalini Bhushan
nodes.description: Andrew W. Mellon Professor in the Humanities at Smith College

nodes.label: Wilburn Hansen
nodes.summary: Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Colorado Boulder and Stanford University, studying under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

nodes.label: Yu-kwan Ng
nodes.summary: Yu-kwan Ng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Ng studied under Zongsan Mou at CUHK (~1968–1974) and earned a Ph.D. at McMaster University (~1980–1985) under Yün-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara, later holding posts at HKBU (1988) and NCU (~1999–2011).

nodes.label: Bruce Charles Williams
nodes.summary: Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.

nodes.label: Sodo Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar. He studied at Antai-ji (1949–1957) under Kodo Sawaki, as well as under Ekō Hashimoto, and taught Joko Shibata.

nodes.label: Elena France Hanson
nodes.summary: Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Narraway
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

nodes.label: Cheryl A. Crowley
nodes.summary: Cheryl A. Crowley specializes in Japanology. She studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

nodes.label: Dawa Tsering
nodes.summary: Dawa Tsering is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He held an academic post at Tibet University.

nodes.label: Wolfram Eberhard
nodes.summary: Wolfram Eberhard worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied under Ferdinand Lessing at Humboldt University and the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen. He taught in China, curated at the Grassi Museum, was professor at Ankara University, and later sociology professor at UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Dörte Kamarid
nodes.summary: Dörte Kamarid is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, with Helmut Tauscher supervising her MA.

nodes.label: Bhikkhu U Dhammissara
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under supervisor Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Asen Balikci
nodes.summary: Asen Balikci was an anthropologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University (1956). He held positions at the National Museum of Canada (c. 1957–1964) and the Université de Montréal (1963–1993).

nodes.label: Bo-Kwang Han
nodes.summary: Bo-Kwang Han is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Dongguk University, where his post is attested in 2004 and 2015.

nodes.id: I:Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology
nodes.label: Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology
variants: Norwegian Institute for Palaeography and Historical Philology

nodes.label: Hoger Technisch Instituut Oostende
variants: Regent Hotel and Technical School in Ostend

nodes.label: Anne Nishimura Morse
nodes.summary: Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied under John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata, and held visiting posts at Smith College, Tokyo National Research Institute, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.

nodes.label: Taka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Taka Yanagisawa was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Japan Women's University. She served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

nodes.label: Yutaka Hirata
nodes.summary: Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who earned a doctorate from Kyushu University (-1996). He held posts at Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1961–1971), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995).

nodes.label: Bunsaku Kurata
nodes.description: born:1918|died:1983|; 倉田, 文作, 1918-1983; Kurata, Bunsaku, 1918-....; 倉田, 文作; Kurata, Bunsaku
nodes.summary: Bunsaku Kurata specialized in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology, studying at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University. He held posts with the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, Tokyo National Museum, Agency for Cultural Affairs, and was Director of Nara National Museum.

nodes.label: Seiji Nemoto
nodes.summary: Seiji Nemoto studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and worked in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba from around 2003 to 2015.

nodes.label: Martin T. Adam
nodes.summary: Martin T. Adam works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and studied under teachers including Leslie S. Kawamura, Tom Tillemans, and Shoryu Katsura, later instructing at McGill.

nodes.label: Michael P. Berman
nodes.summary: Michael P. Berman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Brock University and managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Bela Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Bela Bhattacharya (born 1950) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She served as Professor of the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and later as Professor at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Bernard Williams
nodes.jawiki: バーナード・ウィリアムズ (哲学者)
nodes.summary: Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He later held posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).

nodes.label: Alasdair MacIntyre
nodes.jawiki: アラスデア・マッキンタイア
nodes.summary: Alasdair MacIntyre was a philosopher who studied at Queen Mary University of London and the University of Manchester. His academic posts included positions at the University of Essex, Brandeis University, Duke University, and the University of Notre Dame.

nodes.label: Bruno Galasek
nodes.summary: Bruno Galasek is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Palmo Kyi
nodes.summary: Palmo Kyi is a Tibetology scholar. She studied under teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal, as well as supervisor Per Kværne (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Hiroo Sato
nodes.summary: Hiroo Sato (born 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1972–1982) and held posts at Morioka College (~1989–1993) and as professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).

nodes.label: Hsiu-hui Ji
nodes.summary: Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

nodes.label: David Patt
nodes.summary: David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa as well as Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

nodes.label: Ngan-che Chan
nodes.summary: Ngan-che Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Chan earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Geshe Lhakdor
nodes.summary: Geshe Lhakdor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery, later serving at Tibet House and as Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

nodes.label: Meiping Li
nodes.summary: Meiping Li, working in Buddhist studies, earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Tao Jin
nodes.summary: Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Augsburg and the University of Munich, he held posts at Munich, the Munich School of Politics and Public Policy, and as professor at the Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

nodes.id: I:Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt
nodes.label: Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt

nodes.id: I:Munich School of Politics and Public Policy
nodes.label: Munich School of Politics and Public Policy
Carlo Jamelle Harris
nodes.summary: Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA in philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, and also studied under Sonam Germano, William A. Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

nodes.label: Richard P. Boyle
nodes.summary: Richard P. Boyle completed graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held a post at the University of New Mexico (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Tenshin Tanouye
nodes.summary: Tenshin Tanouye was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied under Sogen Omori. He founded Chozen-ji and succeeded Sogen Omori.

nodes.label: Sogen Omori
nodes.summary: Sogen Omori (1904–1994) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Nihon University. He became abbot of Koho-in in 1947, was appointed professor at Hanazono University in 1970, and served as its president from 1978 to 1982.

nodes.label: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach
nodes.summary: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

nodes.label: Johannes Beltz
nodes.summary: Johannes Beltz works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Johannes Bronkhorst and Marie-Louise Reiniche at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, finishing by 1999.

nodes.label: Esben Andreasen
nodes.summary: Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen and served as a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

nodes.label: Daniel Borengasser
nodes.summary: Daniel Borengasser works in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

nodes.label: Akiko Walley
nodes.summary: Akiko Walley works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), later holding a post at the University of Oregon (2009–2016).

nodes.label: Sonam Tsering
nodes.summary: Sonam Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Supervised for his doctorate by Gray Tuttle and taught by several prominent scholars, he serves as Senior Lecturer and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Günter Blamberger
nodes.description: German specialist in literature, university teacher and writer
nodes.summary: Günter Blamberger held a post at the University of Kassel (1993–1995) and served as Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne from around 1995 to 2020.

nodes.label: Sudhir Kakar
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Kakar studied at Gujarat University, the University of Mannheim, the University of Vienna, and Sigmund-Freud-Institut. He held posts at Harvard (~1967–1971), IIM Ahmedabad (~1971–1977), and IIT Delhi (1976–1977).

nodes.label: Naman P. Ahuja
nodes.summary: Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate from SOAS University of London and has served as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Jens Schlieter
nodes.summary: Jens Schlieter works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Bonn (~1993-1999) under Josef Simon. He held posts at Urania Berlin, Bonn, Munich, Bayreuth, and the University of Bern (~2009).

nodes.label: Yeshi Dhonden
nodes.summary: Yeshi Dhonden was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. He founded Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961, serving as its director from 1961 to 1966, and taught students including Eliot Tokar.

nodes.label: Chi Chen Ho
nodes.summary: Chi Chen Ho works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ho earned a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., studied under Hsuan Hua, and served as a teaching assistant at UCLA.

nodes.label: K. Venkata Ramanan
nodes.summary: K. Venkata Ramanan specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Supervised by Yongtong Tang, Sentian Wang, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, he studied at Peking University, the Harvard-Yenching Institute, and Visva-Bharati University, where he taught.

nodes.label: Satyendra Nath Bose
variants: サティエンドラ・ナート・ボース
nodes.jawiki: サティエンドラ・ボース
nodes.summary: Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974) studied at Presidency University and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka, and served as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

nodes.label: Walter Liebenthal
nodes.summary: Walter Liebenthal was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Dr. phil from the University of Breslau, studying under Johannes Nobel, Max Walleser, and Otto Strauss. His posts included Peking University and the University of Tübingen.

nodes.label: Norman Fischer
nodes.description: American Soto Zen roshi, poet and Buddhist author practicing in the lineage of Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.summary: Norman Fischer works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Colgate University, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, trained under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker, and founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.

nodes.label: Kichinosuke Ito
nodes.summary: Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosophy scholar educated at the First Higher School, University of Tokyo (~1906–1909), and University of Freiburg (1920). He served as a professor at Tokyo (1923–1945), dean at Hokkaido University, and professor at Chuo University (1951–1958).

nodes.label: Huynh Thi Ha Vy
nodes.summary: Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.

nodes.label: David Gonsalez
nodes.summary: David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His training includes traditional study under Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra
nodes.summary: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, and taught numerous students including Ngulchu Yangchen Drubpai Dorje.

variants: Dharma Drum Foundation for Research in the Humanities and Social Sciences

nodes.label: Warrin Ratanamalai
nodes.summary: Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007). The degree was supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, alongside studies under Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

nodes.label: Hae-ju Sunim
nodes.summary: Hae-ju Sunim is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She was a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and an Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Dietmar Rothermund
nodes.summary: Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Munich, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD). He spent his career at Heidelberg University, serving as Wissenschaftlicher Assistent in 1963 and holding the Chair of South Asian History (1968–2001).

nodes.label: Lama Palden Drolma
nodes.summary: Lama Palden Drolma is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who studied under traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Alan Watts
nodes.image: Alan Watts UVM 15 June 1958 Hon. D.D (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Alan Watts was a philosopher of religion. He studied at Bexley Seabury Seminary, held an Episcopal chaplaincy at Northwestern University (1944–1950), and taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies and the Esalen Institute.

nodes.label: Alasdair Urquhart
nodes.summary: Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who completed degrees at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Pittsburgh. He held posts at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and the University of Toronto (emeritus professor 1986).

nodes.label: Tianshu Zhu
nodes.summary: Tianshu Zhu works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at Northwest University and a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, later holding posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Ohio State, and Korea University.

nodes.label: Paul Tillich
nodes.summary: Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau, holding professorships at Dresden, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (1955–1962), and Chicago (1962–1965).

nodes.label: Jacob N. Kinnard
nodes.summary: Jacob N. Kinnard works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and indology. He has held academic posts at the College of William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion and at the Iliff School of Theology.

nodes.label: Bryce Ryan
nodes.summary: Bryce Ryan was a scholar active in Indology and other fields. Over his career, he held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Nguyen Van Thuong
nodes.summary: Nguyen Van Thuong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi, where his MA was supervised by Karam Tej Singh Sarao.

nodes.label: Xinru Liu
nodes.summary: Xinru Liu is a historian and Indologist who earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. Liu served as a professor at CASS's Institute of World History and became Professor Emeritus at The College of New Jersey.

nodes.label: Janet R. Goodwin
nodes.summary: Janet R. Goodwin is a scholar of Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and held posts at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.

nodes.label: Lawrence William Nelson
nodes.summary: Lawrence William Nelson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies, and studied at Butler, Indiana, New York, and Northwestern Universities, among other institutions.

nodes.label: Santa Fe University of Art and Design
Andrew Watsky
nodes.summary: Andrew Watsky (born 1957) works in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1987–1994), taught Bryan D. Lowe, and held a post at Vassar College (~1994–2008).

nodes.label: Towao Sakaehara
nodes.summary: Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his degrees at Kyoto University (~1965–1993). He held academic posts at Otemon Gakuin University and Osaka City University (1981–2010), later directing the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).

nodes.label: Ben Joffe
nodes.summary: Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

nodes.id: I:Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies
nodes.label: Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies
variants: Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies

nodes.label: Saba Mahmood
nodes.description: American anthropologist, Professor, University of California, Berkeley
nodes.summary: A scholar of religious studies and anthropology, Saba Mahmood studied at the University of Washington and completed her PhD at Stanford University (~1992–1998). She held posts at the University of Chicago (~1999–2004) and as Professor of sociocultural anthropology at UC Berkeley (2004–2018).

nodes.label: Martin Riesebrodt
nodes.summary: Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (PhD), and Munich (Habilitation). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (1990–2011) and at the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).

nodes.label: Mark I. Wallace
nodes.description: author, minister, and theologian who teaches in the department of religion at Swarthmore College
nodes.summary: Mark I. Wallace works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul Ricœur (~1982–1986) and held posts at Georgia State University (~1987–1989) and Swarthmore College (~1989).

nodes.label: Joanne Punzo Waghorne
nodes.summary: Joanne Punzo Waghorne specializes in religious studies and Indology. After studying at the University of Chicago, she held positions at the University of Massachusetts Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University (from 2002; attested 2014).

nodes.label: Takahiko Kameyama
nodes.summary: Takahiko Kameyama is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2015, he was attested as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Courtney Bruntz
nodes.summary: Courtney Bruntz works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a professorship at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and serves as professor of East Asian Buddhism at the Numata Center (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Wes Borton
nodes.summary: Wes Borton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Derek F. Maher, attended East Carolina University, and studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer

nodes.label: Hogen Bays
nodes.summary: Hogen Bays is a figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada. He has served as co-abbot at Great Vow Zen Monastery.

nodes.label: Mikio Otsuki
nodes.summary: Mikio Otsuki specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. In 2007, he is attested as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and a professor at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: M. M. McCabe
nodes.summary: Philosopher M. M. McCabe (born 1948) studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She was a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990), Professor at King's College London (1990–2014), and held posts at UCL and Newnham College.

nodes.label: Verity Harte

nodes.label: Raimond Gaita

He held professorships at King's College London (1977–2011) and Australian Catholic University (1993–2011), later becoming an Honorary Professorial Fellow at Melbourne (2019).

nodes.label: Jonathan Lear
nodes.summary: Jonathan Lear (1948–2025) was a philosopher educated at Yale, Cambridge, Rockefeller University, and the Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis. He held academic posts at Cambridge, Clare College, Yale University, and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Susan Neiman
nodes.description: American philosopher, essayist and cultural commentator (born 1955)
nodes.summary: Susan Neiman is a philosopher educated at Harvard (PhD ~1977–1986) and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum (2000–2026).

nodes.label: Jonathan Glover

nodes.summary: Shunji Hosaka (born 1956) is a religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Waseda University. He taught at Reitaku University (~1990–2001) and Chuo University (~2001–2021), and held lecturing posts attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Iwao Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Iwao Ishikawa specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held appointments as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Yasuko Kojima
nodes.summary: Yasuko Kojima is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She has held lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shoko Miyata
nodes.summary: Shoko Miyata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata holds lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryuken Nawa
nodes.summary: Ryuken Nawa works in Indology and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he was attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Ryushin Sudo
nodes.description: Japanese bhikkhu, historian and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Ryushin Sudo (1929–2018) studied at Taisho University around 1948–1953, specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Masataka Suzuki
nodes.summary: Masataka Suzuki studied at Keio University (~1968–1978) and held a post there (~1984–2015). A specialist in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology, he has served as lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Masayuki Tsukimoto
nodes.summary: Masayuki Tsukimoto is a scholar of Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.

nodes.label: Flavio Geisshuesler
nodes.summary: Flavio Geisshuesler works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Bern, Lausanne, and the University of Virginia under David Germano, holding posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019) and the University of Sydney (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shuichi Nara
nodes.summary: Shuichi Nara (born 1961) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University. His posts include researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and lecturer at Chuo University, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Jifu Lan
nodes.summary: Jifu Lan works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Tunghai University (~1965–1969) and held a research post at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, retiring in 2019.

nodes.label: Zack Beer
nodes.summary: Zack Beer specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research and the University of California, Berkeley, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger
nodes.summary: Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Goshen College (1970–1974) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1978–1984), and she became Professor Emerita at Emory University, where she held a post from circa 1990.

nodes.label: Maanasa Visweswaran
nodes.summary: Maanasa Visweswaran works in Indology and computational fields. She studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Roland Ferenczi
nodes.summary: Historian, archaeologist, and Indologist Roland Ferenczi is attested in 2026 as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University and a project researcher at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Chuichi Kimura
nodes.summary: Chuichi Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held academic posts at Minobusan University, serving as an associate professor (attested 2015) and former professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryoji Kishino
nodes.summary: Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Yuki Sasaki
nodes.summary: Yuki Sasaki works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Sasaki held part-time lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Yoshimi Nozawa
nodes.summary: Yoshimi Nozawa works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. As of 2026, Nozawa has served as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Vinay Lal
nodes.summary: Vinay Lal is a historian and Indologist who studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1984–1986). Around 1993, he became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Saloni Mathur
nodes.summary: Saloni Mathur is a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. She serves at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she was an associate professor of art history and later professor and chair of the Department of Art History.

nodes.label: Monica L. Smith
nodes.summary: Monica L. Smith is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Michigan (ca. 1991–1997). She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2002 as a professor.

nodes.label: Daniel M. Neuman
nodes.summary: Daniel M. Neuman is an Indologist who studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Dartmouth College (1971–1980), the University of Washington (1980–1995), and the University of California, Los Angeles (~1994–2018).

nodes.label: Edgar Polomé
nodes.summary: Edgar Polomé studied at Université catholique de Louvain (~1945–1949). In linguistics and Indology, he served as Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1993–2000).

nodes.label: Mirella Lingorska
nodes.summary: Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Rebecca Hufen
nodes.summary: Rebecca Hufen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she studied at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk and served there as a lector for Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Andrew Ollett
nodes.summary: Andrew Ollett (born 1986) works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford (~2006–2008) and Columbia University (~2009–2016), and became an associate professor at the University of Chicago (~2020).

nodes.label: Uta Reinöhl
nodes.description: researcher in the field of digital humanities
nodes.summary: Uta Reinöhl is a linguist and Indologist. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and serves as Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg.

nodes.label: Sarah Merkle-Schneider
nodes.summary: Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Tübingen, where she also held an M.A. post (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Klaus Butzenberger
nodes.summary: Klaus Butzenberger is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Friedrich Wilhelm at the University of Munich. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin and served as chairholder at the University of Tübingen from 1999 to 2017.

nodes.label: Mahiro Ito
nodes.summary: Mahiro Ito (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026), having succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021.

nodes.label: Hironobu Minami
nodes.summary: Hironobu Minami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryushin Saito
nodes.summary: Ryushin Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was attested as a professor at Bukkyo University in 2015 and as a faculty member at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

nodes.label: Danuta Stasik
nodes.summary: Danuta Stasik is an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1975–1980) under Maria Byrski (~1980–1989). She later held posts at the University of Warsaw, beginning in 1980 and 1986.

nodes.label: Eiju Fukushima
nodes.summary: Eiju Fukushima works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. As attested in 2026, he held faculty posts at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

nodes.label: Norihiro Matsuura
nodes.summary: Norihiro Matsuura works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Matsuura is attested in 2026 as a faculty member at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

nodes.label: Y. B. Damle
nodes.summary: Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and served as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Vinayaka P. Bhatta
nodes.summary: Vinayaka P. Bhatta is an Indologist and linguist who has served as head and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: Ali S. Asani
nodes.description: Chair:Near Eastern Languages/Civilizations Department/Director:Prince Alwaleed bin Talal Islamic Studies Program/Harvard University
nodes.summary: Ali S. Asani works in religious studies and Indology. After completing his studies at Harvard College and Harvard University, he served as a professor of Middle Eastern Studies and Indo-Muslim and Islamic Religion and Cultures at Harvard.

nodes.label: Amartya Sen
nodes.summary: Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist educated at the University of Calcutta and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1953–1959). He held appointments at Jadavpur, Delhi, the London School of Economics (~1971–1982), and Harvard University (~2004).

nodes.label: Uranchimeg Tsultem
nodes.summary: Uranchimeg Tsultem is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history who completed her PhD at UC Berkeley. She has held teaching and research roles at UC Berkeley, the National University of Mongolia, and IUPUI's Herron School of Art and Design.

nodes.label: Remeen Firoz
nodes.summary: Remeen Firoz is an Indologist who is attested in 2026 as a PhD student at the Australian National University studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Ranu Kunwar
nodes.summary: Ranu Kunwar is a PhD student attested at the Australian National University in 2026, studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Giti Dutt
nodes.summary: Giti Dutt is an archaeology and interdisciplinary scholar who is attested in 2026 as a PhD student at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Muhamad Saputra
nodes.summary: Muhamad Saputra is an academic who studied as a PhD student under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron at the Australian National University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Azizah Nur
nodes.summary: Azizah Nur is a doctoral student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under supervisor Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Sabine Klein-Schwind
nodes.summary: A scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, Sabine Klein-Schwind studied under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson and is attested as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg in 2026.

nodes.label: Leo Rishi Nelson Jones
nodes.summary: Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and held a post there as Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: William Chittick
nodes.summary: William Chittick works in religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Tehran, he held posts at Sharif University of Technology, University at Albany, SUNY, and Stony Brook University from circa 1983.

nodes.label: Lakshmi Swaminathan
nodes.description: officer in the Indian National Army (INA) and former presidential candidate of India
nodes.summary: Lakshmi Swaminathan was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Queen Mary's College (~1930–1932) and Madras Medical College (~1932–1938). She served as a lecturer at Stony Brook University.

nodes.label: Sara Frumento
nodes.summary: Sara Frumento is an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied for a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sondra L. Hausner
nodes.summary: Sondra L. Hausner specializes in religious studies and Indology. She serves as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mallica Kumbera Landrus
nodes.summary: Mallica Kumbera Landrus specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. As of 2026, she is attested as Keeper of Eastern Art and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.

nodes.label: Gyokusen Hosaka
nodes.summary: Gyokusen Hosaka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College from approximately 1950 to 1963.

nodes.label: Reirin Yamada
nodes.summary: Reirin Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as president of Komazawa Junior College.

nodes.label: Arti Dhand
nodes.summary: Arti Dhand is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who was educated at the University of Calgary (c. 1989–1993) and McGill University (c. 1993–2000). Around 2002, she became an Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti
nodes.description: Indologist, scholar of Onomastics & Vedic Studies, Author & Editor. Emeritus Fellow, UGC.
nodes.summary: Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti specializes in Indology and religious studies. He has held posts at the University of Calcutta and at The Asiatic Society, where he is attested in 2026 as Professor (Special Invitee).

nodes.label: Kumkum Bandyopadhyay
nodes.summary: Kumkum Bandyopadhyay specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay and has held a post as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sampan Chakrabarty
nodes.summary: Sampan Chakrabarty works in Indology and completed doctoral studies under Pallab Sengupta. In 2026, Chakrabarty is attested as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Tista Biswas
nodes.summary: Tista Biswas is an Indology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Subuddhi Charan Goswami and holds the post of Sir William Jones Research Fellow in Sanskritic Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Smita Halder
nodes.summary: Smita Halder is an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar. As of 2026, she is attested as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Susmita Basu Majumdar
nodes.summary: Susmita Basu Majumdar is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, and later held a post at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Priyanku Chakraborty
nodes.summary: Priyanku Chakraborty specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Aishwarya Biswas, he served as Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellow in Buddhist Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Praggnaparamita Biswas
nodes.summary: Praggnaparamita Biswas is an Indology researcher who studied under doctoral supervisor Ratna Basu. She is attested as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Imran Philip
nodes.summary: Imran Philip works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Manasi Dilip Nadkarni
nodes.summary: Manasi Dilip Nadkarni is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. Attested in 2026, she studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Biswajit Biswas
nodes.summary: Biswajit Biswas, working in religious studies and Indology, studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and was attested as a Research Scholar or Fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Moumita Hossain
nodes.summary: Moumita Hossain works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and was a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society as attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Poulami Ray
nodes.summary: Poulami Ray is a history and archaeology researcher who studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen. She is attested as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Sulagna Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Sulagna Bhattacharya is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Pratap Bandyopadhyay. Bhattacharya held an H P Shastri Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Tanaya Afroz
nodes.summary: Tanaya Afroz works in linguistics, having studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya. Afroz is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar and Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Sunanda Mukhopadhyay
nodes.summary: Sunanda Mukhopadhyay is an Indologist and linguist who studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya. Mukhopadhyay was attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Minakshi Banerjee
nodes.summary: Minakshi Banerjee is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar. In 2026, she held a James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Ankita Chakraborty
nodes.summary: Ankita Chakraborty is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Bijoya Goswami (attested 2026). She held an appointment as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Neelima Mundayar
nodes.summary: Neelima Mundayar is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She is a PhD student at the University of Edinburgh under the doctoral supervision of Wilfried Swenden (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jiaqi Wang
nodes.summary: Jiaqi Wang worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied under Gongga Rinpoche as a disciple and is attested as a PhD student at Columbia University in 2026.

nodes.label: Sravani Kanamarlapudi
nodes.summary: Sravani Kanamarlapudi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied under Richard G. Salomon, attended the University of Washington, and pursued PhD studies at the University of Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Christophe Jaffrelot
nodes.summary: Christophe Jaffrelot is an Indologist who studied at Sciences Po under Jean Leca. He joined Sciences Po and the CNRS around 1991 and became Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London circa 2012.

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Chevillard
nodes.summary: Jean-Luc Chevillard is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli. He held posts as a researcher at the CNRS from around 1990 and as a lecturer at the University of Hamburg around 2008.

nodes.label: Koichi Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Koichi Hiraoka (born 1961) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1984) and is attested as a visiting professor at Shuchiin University in 2026.

nodes.label: Alastair Gornall
nodes.summary: Alastair Gornall specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. After completing his PhD at the University of Cambridge, he held posts at the Singapore University of Technology and Design, SOAS, and the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Tom Ginsburg
nodes.summary: Tom Ginsburg is a scholar of Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1985–1999). He held positions at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) and the University of Chicago (~2008).

nodes.label: Aritri Dutta
nodes.summary: Aritri Dutta works in Tibetology and religious studies. As an external PhD student attested in 2026, she studied at Leiden University under the supervision of Henk Blezer.

nodes.label: S. N. Krishna
nodes.summary: An Indologist, S. N. Krishna is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, studying under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva.

nodes.label: R. Gayathri
nodes.summary: R. Gayathri works in Indology. She has been a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

nodes.label: V. R. Srinivasan
nodes.summary: V. R. Srinivasan is an Indology and religious studies scholar who pursued doctoral research at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

nodes.label: P. S. Chandrasekharan
nodes.summary: P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Vijayalakshmi Mani
nodes.summary: Vijayalakshmi Mani is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who pursued Ph.D. studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Lavanya V. Eswar
nodes.summary: Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She was attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar studying at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

nodes.label: Yukihiko Asayama
nodes.summary: Yukihiko Asayama specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Asayama held posts as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as a researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Ernst Gombrich
variants: エルンスト・ゴンブリッチ
nodes.summary: Ernst Gombrich was an art historian who studied at the University of Vienna. He held positions at the Warburg Institute as a research assistant (1936) and director (1959–1976), and worked at the University of London (1956–1959).

nodes.label: Katsuji Fujioka
nodes.summary: Katsuji Fujioka was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Leipzig. He later served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.

nodes.label: Leonard Bloomfield
variants: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.jawiki: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Leonard Bloomfield (1887–1949) was a linguist educated at Harvard, Wisconsin, and Chicago under Francis Asbury Wood. He held professorships at Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago (1927–1940), and served as Sterling Professor of Linguistics at Yale (1940–1949).

nodes.label: Kaigen Noritake
nodes.summary: Kaigen Noritake specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo and served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Daito Shimaji
nodes.summary: Daito Shimaji (1875–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku and Otani universities, he taught at Komazawa, Rissho, and Toyo universities, as well as Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1923.

nodes.label: Amalia Pezzali
nodes.summary: Amalia Pezzali is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed doctoral studies under T. R. V. Murti and also studied under Michel Hulin.

nodes.label: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff
nodes.summary: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated in Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he studied under Friedrich Leo and Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He held professorships in Greek at Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht (1917–1946).

nodes.label: Fumio Masutani
nodes.summary: Fumio Masutani was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1952–1966) and Taisho University (~1966–1973), and served as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

nodes.label: Hoseong Kim

nodes.label: Hartmut Scharfe
nodes.summary: Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.summary: Daijō Tokiwa (1870–1945) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, later holding professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, among other institutional roles.

nodes.label: Yuishin Ito
nodes.summary: Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, earning a doctorate from Bukkyo University, where he taught from 1961 to 1997. He later served as president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College and Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, and held posts at Shōjōke-in and Chion-in.

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (1770–1774). He served as professor of Oriental languages at Jena (1775) and professor of philosophy at Göttingen (1788).

nodes.label: Keiki Yabuki
nodes.summary: Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Tohoku Gakuin, Taisho, and the University of Tokyo, he founded Miwa Gakuin and held teaching posts at Taisho University, Shukyo University, and the University of Tokyo.
