nodes.summary: Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded Juze-kai, Kairitsu Gakko, and Juuzen Hokutsu.

nodes.label: Kozen Shaku
nodes.summary: Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Senmyō. He served as abbot at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded Shakuson Shofukai in 1893.

nodes.label: Friedrich August Rosen
nodes.summary: Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig and under Franz Bopp in Berlin. He served as professor of Oriental languages and Sanskrit at the University of London (UCL) and held secretary roles in London scholarly societies.

nodes.label: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
variants: ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・ヘーゲル
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・ヘーゲル
nodes.summary: The philosopher Hegel studied at the Tübinger Stift, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Jena under Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling. He held positions at Jena (~1801-1807), Heidelberg University (~1816-1818), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818-1831).

nodes.label: Victoria University of Manchester
variants: マンチェスターのヴィクトリア大学

nodes.label: Claude Lévi-Strauss
variants: クロード・レヴィ＝ストロース
nodes.jawiki: クロード・レヴィ＝ストロース
nodes.summary: A scholar in philosophy and other fields, Claude Lévi-Strauss studied under Marcel Mauss (~1930–1935). He held appointments at the University of São Paulo (~1935–1939), EPHE (~1950–1974), EHESS (~1948–1982), and the Collège de France (1959–1982).

nodes.label: Antoine Meillet
variants: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.summary: Antoine Meillet was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Paris, the Sorbonne, and EPHE under Darmesteter, Lévi, and de Saussure. He held professorships at EPHE, INALCO, and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

nodes.label: Theodore Dwight Woolsey
nodes.description: American jurist; president of Yale University (1801–1889)
nodes.summary: Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics and other fields. After studying at Hopkins School, Yale College, and Princeton University, he served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and president of the American Oriental Society from 1853 to 1863.

nodes.label: Toru Takahashi
nodes.summary: Toru Takahashi was a Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1898–1902). He held posts including professor at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

nodes.id: I:Academic Association of Koreanology in Japan
nodes.label: Academic Association of Koreanology in Japan
Seok-hyeong Kim
nodes.summary: Seok-hyeong Kim worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Taisho University, he served as a professor at Dongguk University and as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University.

nodes.label: Tsutomu Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Kubo was a philosophy scholar. He studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1912) and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University, holding posts at Tokyo, Tohoku University (1929–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

nodes.label: Ernest Renan
variants: ジョゼフ・エルネスト・ルナン
nodes.summary: Ernest Renan was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and served as professor of Hebrew (1861) and administrator (1883) at the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Tendai Daigakurin
variants: 天台宗西部大学専修院

nodes.label: Jean Deloche
nodes.summary: Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He taught at the Suryavarman II School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras (1962–1966), and held research posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

nodes.label: Anna Seidel
nodes.summary: Anna Seidel was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied in Munich, Hamburg, and under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. She held posts at the EFEO (1969), Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1970–1991), and visited UH Mānoa and UCSB.

nodes.label: Götz von Selle
nodes.summary: Götz von Selle worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen. He held library and professorial posts at Göttingen, the Royal Library of Berlin, and the University of Königsberg (ca. 1928–1945).

nodes.label: John Borthwick Gilchrist
variants: ジョン・ボースウィック・ギルクリスト
nodes.image: John Borthwick Gilchrist, cropped from UCL portrait by Blanconi.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・ギルクリスト
nodes.summary: John Borthwick Gilchrist was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the East India Company, became principal of Fort William College, and was University College London's first Professor of Hindustani.

nodes.label: Claudius Buchanan
nodes.summary: Claudius Buchanan was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Glasgow and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795). In 1801, he was appointed Vice-Provost of Fort William College.

nodes.label: Bruno Petzold
variants: ブルーノ・ペツォルト
nodes.jawiki: ブルーノ・ペツォルト
nodes.summary: Bruno Petzold was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Leipzig and Berlin, and by Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji, he taught at the First Higher School, Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.

nodes.label: Seiichiro Ono
nodes.summary: Seiichiro Ono studied at the University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino, earning a doctorate in 1933. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1922–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977), publishing in law, Buddhist studies, and philosophy.

nodes.label: Haya Akegarasu
nodes.summary: Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) studied Buddhist and religious studies under Manshi Kiyozawa, Kyoshi Takahama, and Shimei Futabatei at Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He held leadership posts at Shinshu Otani-ha and Higashi Hongan-ji.

nodes.label: Siddharth College
variants: シッダールタ女子大学

nodes.label: Poerbatjaraka
nodes.summary: Poerbatjaraka (1884–1964) was an Indonesian scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. After earning his doctorate at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom, he served as a professor at Gadjah Mada University, the University of Indonesia, and Udayana University.

nodes.label: Herman Kellgren
nodes.summary: Herman Kellgren worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. From around 1849 to 1856, he held a post at the University of Helsinki.

nodes.label: William Kirkpatrick
variants: ウィリアム・カークパトリック
nodes.description: British army officer in the East India Company and diplomat (1754 or 1756-1812)

nodes.id: I:Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde
nodes.label: Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde
variants: Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde

nodes.label: Albert Thumb
nodes.image: Professor Albert Thumb 18.05.1865 bis 14.08.1915 Sohn von Ida Schanzenbach und Albert Alois Thump.jpg
nodes.summary: Albert Thumb was a linguist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing his habilitation at the University of Freiburg (~1888–1891). He held posts at Freiburg (1891–1895), Marburg (~1901–1909), and Strasbourg (1909).

nodes.label: Genro
nodes.summary: Genro (1717–1789) was a Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the post of first seat (第一座) at Myoshin-ji.

nodes.label: Hakuin Ekaku
nodes.summary: Hakuin Ekaku (1686–1769) was active in Buddhist studies. He studied under Dōkyō Etan around 1708 and under Hakuyūshi around 1710–1711, and he taught Suiō Genro.

nodes.label: Julius Klaproth
nodes.jawiki: ユリウス・ハインリヒ・クラプロート

nodes.label: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland
nodes.summary: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) was an Indology scholar. He studied at the East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and served as a professor of law at Presidency University.

nodes.id: I:Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
nodes.label: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
variants: ノルウェー科学文学アカデミー

nodes.label: Benkyo Shiio
nodes.summary: Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Taisho University (1926) and head of both Sanko Library and Sanko Research Institute (~1948–1971).

nodes.label: Sanko Library
variants: 三康文化研究所附属三康図書館

nodes.label: Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland
variants: Dutch Oriental Society (Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland)

nodes.label: Louis H. Gray
nodes.summary: Louis H. Gray was a scholar in linguistics, indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton (~1892–1896) and Columbia (~1896–1900), and held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1921).

nodes.label: Phuntsok Tashi
nodes.summary: Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and has held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

nodes.label: George van Driem
variants: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.summary: Linguist and Tibetologist George van Driem studied at the University of Virginia and Leiden University. He held professorships at Leiden University and served as Professor of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern from 2010 to 2022.

nodes.label: Lungten Dubgyur
nodes.summary: Lungten Dubgyur is a Tibetology scholar who completed degrees at Sherubtse College, Government Law College in Mumbai (LL.B), and the University of Edinburgh (LL.M).

nodes.label: Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji
nodes.summary: Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, later serving on its General Council from 1964 to 1965.

nodes.label: Georg von der Gabelentz
variants: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
ハンス・ゲオルク・コーノン・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.summary: Specializing in Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology, he studied at the University of Jena, TU Dresden, and the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889), joining the Prussian Academy of Sciences in 1889.

nodes.label: Robert Hyde Colebrooke
nodes.description: British infantry officer and surveyor in India (1762–1808)

nodes.label: John Herbert Harington
nodes.description: British administrator in India and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: John Herbert Harington worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society, and as an honorary professor at Fort William College from circa 1801 to 1823.

nodes.label: Amaranatha Jha
nodes.summary: Amaranatha Jha studied at Muir Central College, where he became Professor of English in 1917. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1947) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).

nodes.label: Charles Elliott
nodes.summary: Charles Elliott (1776–1856) was an Indologist who worked for the East India Company (~1795–1827). He later served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1836–1856).

nodes.label: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder
nodes.summary: Indologist Edmund Nathaniel Snyder graduated from Harvard University in 1886 and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

nodes.label: British School at Athens
variants: British School of Archaeology in Athens

nodes.label: James Irving Manatt
nodes.summary: James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell College and Yale University under William Dwight Whitney, holding posts at Denison College, Marietta College, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and Brown University.

nodes.label: Royal Holloway, University of London
variants: Royal Holloway College der University of London

nodes.label: Gordon Johnson
nodes.summary: Gordon Johnson is an Indologist and historian who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1961–1967). He served as a fellow of Trinity and Selwyn Colleges, president of Wolfson College (1993–2010), Cambridge's Deputy Vice-Chancellor (1974–2010), and president of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

nodes.label: Kurfürst-Ruprecht-Gymnasium Neustadt
variants: Gymnasium at Neustadt an der Haardt

nodes.label: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe
nodes.summary: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe (1865–1937) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Richmond College, Galle, and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. He was epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1929) and taught at the University of London (~1918–1930).

nodes.label: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner
nodes.summary: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at King's College London and Heidelberg. He held posts at King's College, was principal of Government College University, Lahore (1864), and was registrar of the University of the Punjab.

nodes.label: George Uglow Pope
nodes.summary: George Uglow Pope was an Indologist and linguist who led Breeks Memorial School and Bishop Cotton Boys' School. He later served as a lecturer at Balliol College, Oxford, and as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Rewata Dhamma
nodes.summary: Rewata Dhamma (1929–2004) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, and completed a doctorate at Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

nodes.label: Oliver Codrington
nodes.summary: Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He served as Secretary at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society (attested 1892).

nodes.label: José Gerson da Cunha
nodes.description: Indo-Portuguese physician, orientalist, historian, linguist, and numismatist

nodes.label: Dermot Killingley
nodes.summary: Dermot Killingley is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS, he held positions at the University of Malaya (1961–1968), Newcastle University (~1970–2005), and a visiting professorship at the University of Vienna in 2008.

nodes.label: Institute of Economic Growth
variants: Institute of Economic Growth (University of Delhi)

nodes.label: Sumathi Ramaswamy
nodes.summary: Sumathi Ramaswamy is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania. Her career includes posts at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Declan Quigley
nodes.summary: Declan Quigley is a scholar in Indology and other fields. He has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

nodes.label: Gauri Viswanathan
nodes.summary: Gauri Viswanathan (b. 1950) studied at the University of Delhi (circa 1968–1973) and Columbia University (circa 1980–1985). She taught English at Delhi (circa 1973–1978) and became Professor in the Humanities and South Asia Institute Director at Columbia (circa 1989).

nodes.label: Henry Herbert Dodwell
nodes.summary: Henry Herbert Dodwell (1879–1946) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture of the British Dominions in Asia at SOAS.

nodes.label: Madan Mohan Malaviya
nodes.summary: Madan Mohan Malaviya (1861–1946) worked in Indology. He studied at Muir Central College, the University of Calcutta (B.A.), and the University of Allahabad (LL.B.), founded Banaras Hindu University in 1916, and served as its Vice Chancellor from 1919 to 1938.

nodes.label: S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar
nodes.summary: An Indologist and historian, S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar earned his history degree and M.A. at the University of Madras. He lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909), held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929), and edited the Journal of Indian History (~1921–1934).

nodes.label: Suzanne Karpelès
nodes.summary: Suzanne Karpelès was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Lévi, Foucher, and Finot. She held posts at the EFEO, the National Library of Cambodia, and the Buddhist Institute.

nodes.label: Ian James Coghlan
nodes.summary: Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University by 2004 and was a research fellow at the Monash Asia Institute, Monash University, attested in 2005.

nodes.label: Holly Gayley
nodes.summary: Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2001-2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

nodes.label: Heinz Mode
nodes.description: German art historian, orientalist and indologist (1913-1992)
nodes.summary: Heinz Mode was a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Berlin and Basel, learning from G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer. He was a professor of Oriental archaeology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1948–1978).

nodes.label: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen
variants: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR

nodes.label: Otto Fischer
nodes.description: German art historian, director of Kunstmuseum Basel (1886–1948)
nodes.summary: Otto Fischer was a scholar of sinology, Japanology, and history/archaeology who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He served as director of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920) and Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and taught at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

nodes.label: Willem Bollée
nodes.summary: Willem Bollée was an Indologist. He studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1956) and the University of Hamburg (~1965–1975). He served as an assistant professor at Münster (1971–1978) and as a lecturer and professor at Heidelberg University (~1977–1993).

nodes.label: William Frederic Sinclair
nodes.summary: William Frederic Sinclair was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the Royal School, Armagh, and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

nodes.id: I:Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・フォン・ハンマー・プルグスタル
nodes.summary: Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).

nodes.label: William Rainey Harper
nodes.summary: William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and served as professor at Yale (1886) and president of the University of Chicago (1891–1906) and Bradley University (~1897–1899).

nodes.label: Daniel Coit Gilman
nodes.summary: Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as president of the University of California, founding president of Johns Hopkins University, and president of both the Carnegie Institution and the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh
nodes.summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles. In 1998, she was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University.

nodes.label: John Jorgensen
nodes.summary: John Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He has held positions as a researcher at Australian National University, taught Japanese Studies at Griffith University, and served as Senior Research Associate at La Trobe University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Thomas Jülch
nodes.summary: Thomas Jülch is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies educated at Goethe University Frankfurt, Hull, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich (PhD ~2006–2011). He was a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University from 2013 to 2019.

nodes.id: I:Singapore University of Technology and Design
nodes.label: Singapore University of Technology and Design
variants: Singapore University of Technology and Design

nodes.label: Thomas Roebuck
nodes.summary: Thomas Roebuck was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal High School. He served as assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George in 1811 and was a member of The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Lionel Obadia
nodes.summary: Lionel Obadia (born 1968) works in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Lille (1997). He held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University (attested 2002), and Lyon 2 (attested 2010–2014).

nodes.label: Lille 3 University - Charles de Gaulle
variants: Charles-de-Gaulle University of Arts and Social Sciences

nodes.label: Richard Hughes Seager
nodes.summary: Richard Hughes Seager is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1982–1987), and was an Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994).

nodes.label: Michelle Spuler
nodes.summary: Michelle Spuler (born 1971) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2000). She taught in the Department of Religious Studies at Victoria University of Wellington and also taught at Colorado College.

nodes.label: Robert Maclagan
nodes.description: British Army officer and military engineer (1820–94)
nodes.summary: Robert Maclagan worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and Royal School of Military Engineering, and served as principal of IIT Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

nodes.label: Erberto Lo Bue
nodes.description: Italian indologist, tibetologist, translator and university teacher
nodes.summary: Erberto Lo Bue was a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London. He was a lecturer in Tibetan language and literature at the University of Milan (around 1983–2004) and later worked at the University of Bologna.

nodes.label: Nathaniel Wallich
nodes.jawiki: ナサニエル・ウォーリッチ
nodes.description: surgeon and botanist of Danish origin who worked in India (1786-1854)
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Wallich studied at the University of Copenhagen. He served as Superintendent at the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden from approximately 1817 to 1846.

nodes.label: David Brown
nodes.summary: David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied as a sizar at Magdalene College, Cambridge in 1782 and served as Provost at Fort William College from circa 1800 to 1807.

nodes.label: Theodorus Willem Juynboll
nodes.summary: Theodorus Willem Juynboll was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University between approximately 1885 and 1893. In 1916, he held a post at Utrecht University.

nodes.label: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton
nodes.jawiki: フランシス・ブキャナン＝ハミルトン
nodes.summary: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton was an Edinburgh-educated physician and naturalist who studied under John Hope. He served in the Bengal Medical Service (1794–1815) and as director of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

nodes.label: Mona Schrempf
nodes.summary: Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin in 2001. In 2006, she was a research fellow at Humboldt University and taught at Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Jogindra Nath Samaddar
nodes.summary: Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) was an Indologist and historian educated at Bangabasi College and Presidency University. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College (~1908–1917), Patna College (1912), and Patna University (1923).

nodes.label: Winfred Robert Martin
nodes.summary: Winfred Robert Martin (died 1915) worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and later as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

nodes.label: Daniel John Gogerly
nodes.summary: Daniel John Gogerly was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He headed the Wesleyan Mission Press, chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society, and served as secretary, vice-president, and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka.

nodes.label: James Mackintosh
nodes.image: Sir James Mackintosh by Sir Thomas Lawrence.jpg
nodes.summary: James Mackintosh (1765–1832) was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and the University of Edinburgh, and he founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, serving as its president from ~1804 to 1811.

nodes.label: John Leyden
nodes.summary: John Leyden worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Henry Thomas Colebrooke from circa 1805 to 1810. He served as assistant secretary and secretary of The Asiatic Society between circa 1809 and 1811.

nodes.label: J. M. E. McTaggart
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・マクタガート
nodes.summary: J. M. E. McTaggart (1866–1925) was a philosopher who was educated at Clifton College. He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from roughly 1891 to 1923.

nodes.label: Parul Dave-Mukherji
nodes.summary: Parul Dave-Mukherji is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Kazuaki Komine
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees at Waseda University. He taught at Waseda Jitsugyo High School, Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

nodes.label: Hermann Sauppe
nodes.summary: Hermann Sauppe worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He earned his doctorate under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig. He held posts at Zurich (1833), Zentralbibliothek Zürich (1837), Weimar (1845), and the University of Göttingen (1855).

nodes.label: Addiscombe Military Seminary
variants: Hon. East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
Honourable East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
アディスコム軍事神学校

nodes.label: Henry George Keene
nodes.description: English employee of the East India Company and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: Henry George Keene (1781–1864) worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, he served with the East India Company and as Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College.

nodes.label: William Price
nodes.summary: William Price (1780–1830) was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College (~1813–1830).

nodes.label: David Ruddell
nodes.summary: David Ruddell was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Laval University. He served as Secretary at Fort William College.

nodes.label: John Shakespear
nodes.summary: John Shakespear was an Indologist and linguist who studied under John Richardson. He held an orientalist professorship at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809) and was Professor of Oriental Languages at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).

nodes.label: David Shea
nodes.summary: David Shea was an Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology scholar. He studied at Trinity College Dublin in 1793 and served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at East India Company College until 1836.

nodes.label: Emil Rödiger
variants: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.jawiki: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.summary: Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a German scholar of linguistics and religious studies. Educated at Halle-Wittenberg (Dr. phil. 1826), he became full professor there (1835–1860) before serving as professor of Oriental languages at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1860.

nodes.label: Alfred Master
nodes.description: Master, Alfred (1883-1978) Lecturer in Indian Philology

nodes.label: William Erskine
nodes.summary: William Erskine was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1787 to 1792.

nodes.label: James Atkinson
nodes.description: English surgeon, artist and Persian scholar (1780–1852)
nodes.summary: James Atkinson, a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, was educated at the University of Edinburgh. He served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818 and held posts at the India Government Mint, Kolkata.

nodes.label: Dayong
nodes.summary: Dayong (1893–1929) was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, later teaching there in 1923. He also studied under Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Bai Puren, and Dorje Geshe.

nodes.label: Buddhist Academy of China
variants: Institute of Buddhist Studies of Beijing

nodes.label: Eberhard Schrader
nodes.summary: Linguist Eberhard Schrader studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Göttingen (~1854–1858). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1863–1870), University of Giessen (~1870–1873), University of Jena (~1873–1875), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

nodes.label: John Thompson Platts
variants: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.summary: John Thompson Platts was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford, he taught at institutions in India and served as Teacher of Persian at Oxford in 1880.

nodes.id: P:Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John
nodes.label: Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John
nodes.enwiki: Richard Fleming St Andrew St John

nodes.label: Andrea R. Jain
nodes.summary: Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2010). She has taught at IUPUI and advanced from assistant to full professor at Indiana University Bloomington (2010–2021).

nodes.label: Hidehiko Kurita
nodes.summary: Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University, attested in 2020.

nodes.label: Kwangsoo Park
nodes.summary: Kwangsoo Park, a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, completed an MA at the University of Iowa and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Samani Pratibha Pragya
nodes.summary: Samani Pratibha Pragya works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she was attested as a research assistant in 2020.

nodes.label: Edward Clive Bayley
nodes.summary: Edward Clive Bayley was an Indology and history/archaeology specialist who studied at East India Company College (~1840–1842) and Haileybury and Imperial Service College. He joined the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

nodes.label: Henry Miers Elliot
nodes.summary: Henry Miers Elliot (1808–1853) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Winchester College and served as a civil servant with the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.

nodes.label: Justus Olshausen
variants: ユストゥス・オルスハウゼン
nodes.summary: Justus Olshausen was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, and held positions at Kiel University, the University of Königsberg, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and the Prussian ministry.

nodes.label: Étienne Marc Quatremère
nodes.image: Portret van de oriëntalist Étienne Marc Quatremère Quatremère, Etienne-Marc (titel op object) Leden van het Institut Royal de France (serietitel) Iconographie de l'Institut royal de France (serietitel op object), RP-P-1911-978.jpg
nodes.summary: Quatremère specialized in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1800–1807) and held a post at the Collège de France from 1819 to 1857.

nodes.label: Christopher Andreas Holmboe
nodes.image: Portrett av professor Christopher Andreas Holmboe (1796-1882).jpg
nodes.summary: Christopher Andreas Holmboe was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal Frederick University and in Paris under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval
nodes.summary: Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval was a linguist and scholar. He was appointed professor of modern Arabic at INALCO in 1821 and professor of Arabic at the Collège de France in 1833, joining the Académie des Inscriptions in 1849.

nodes.label: Carl Paul Caspari
nodes.summary: Carl Paul Caspari was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig (1834–1842) under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1838–1840). He served at the University of Oslo from 1847, becoming professor in 1857.

北海道教育大学函館分校

nodes.label: Asahikawa University Junior College
variants: 旭川大学女子短期大学部

nodes.label: Doranne Jacobson
nodes.summary: Doranne Jacobson is an Indology scholar who earned a doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

nodes.label: McKim Marriott
variants: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.jawiki: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and religious studies, McKim Marriott studied at Harvard University under Clyde Kluckhohn and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, where he served as professor of anthropology and social sciences from 1953 to 1998.

nodes.label: Gore Ouseley
nodes.summary: Gore Ouseley worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held a post at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (~1810–1814) and served as vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1844).

nodes.label: George Ritso Jervis
nodes.description: George Ritso Jervis (1794-1851) 1841 Lieut-Col George Ritso Jervis of the Engineers, Bombay Company

nodes.label: S. Sankaranarayanan
nodes.summary: An Indologist and historian, S. Sankaranarayanan was an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre from around 1986 to 1999, and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

nodes.label: Chinmaya International Foundation
variants: Adi Sankara Nilayam, Chinmaya International Foundation

nodes.label: R. Thangaswami Sarma
nodes.summary: R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. He held positions at Presidency College, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).

nodes.id: I:Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre
nodes.label: Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre
variants: Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre

nodes.label: Geoffrey Goble
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, Goble earned his MA at the University of Virginia and his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington. He served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).

nodes.label: August Boeckh
nodes.summary: August Boeckh (1785–1867), a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics, studied under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher at Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811–1861).

nodes.label: Max Leopold Margolis
nodes.summary: Linguist and religious studies scholar Max Leopold Margolis received his Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1891. He held faculty posts at Hebrew Union College, the University of California, and Dropsie College, where he chaired biblical philology from 1909 to 1932.

nodes.label: Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Research Institute
variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派総合研究所

variants: 和歌山赤十字看護専門学校

nodes.label: Yuka Otani
nodes.summary: Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who held part-time lecturer positions at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (both attested 2015).

nodes.id: I:Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
nodes.label: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
variants: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies
George Cœdès
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology, Cœdès studied at the EPHE and Humboldt University of Berlin. He directed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1929–1947), later teaching at INALCO, the Sorbonne, and other Parisian institutions.

nodes.label: Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi
variants: Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi

Sri Lanka branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Arthur Christensen
nodes.summary: Arthur Christensen was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1903) and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding Copenhagen's first chair in Oriental studies (1919–1945).

nodes.label: Friedrich Carl Andreas
nodes.jawiki: フリードリッヒ・カール・アンドレアス
nodes.summary: Friedrich Carl Andreas was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist who studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen.

nodes.label: Henrik Samuel Nyberg
variants: エンリコ・サムエリ・ニーベリ
nodes.summary: Henrik Samuel Nyberg (1889–1974) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Uppsala University in 1908, taught at Fjellstedt School (c. 1916–1919), and served as lecturer and professor at Uppsala University (c. 1919–1956).

nodes.label: Otto Höfler
nodes.summary: Linguist and religious studies scholar Otto Höfler studied at the University of Vienna under Rudolf Much, as well as at Lund and Kiel. He held professorships at Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945, 1954), and Vienna (1957–1971).

nodes.label: George Shirt
nodes.summary: George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Cambridge, earning a B.A. by 1864, and subsequently attended the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, from around 1864 to 1866.

nodes.label: Jean Humbert
nodes.description: academic (1792 - 1851), member of the Accademia delle Scienze di Torino since 1832

nodes.label: Syed Ali Bilgrami
nodes.summary: Syed Ali Bilgrami was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Patna College, Lucknow, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and London. He served the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and was Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (1901).

nodes.label: Sukumari Bhattacharji
nodes.summary: Sukumari Bhattacharji was an Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. She was a professor of English at Lady Brabourne College in 1945 and taught at Jadavpur University from 1957 to 1986.

nodes.label: Johann Tobias Beck
nodes.summary: Johann Tobias Beck was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1822–1826). He held posts at the University of Basel (~1836–1843) and the University of Tübingen (~1843–1878).

nodes.label: Gerardus van der Leeuw
variants: ヘラルドゥス・ファン・デル・レーウ
nodes.jawiki: ゲラルダス・ファン・デル・レーウ
nodes.description: Dutch religious studies scholar and politician (1890–1950)
nodes.summary: Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1908 to 1916 and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 until 1950.

nodes.label: Edward Albert Gait
nodes.summary: Edward Albert Gait was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at University College London (~1880–1882). He founded the Bihar and Orissa Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

nodes.label: Frederick James Furnivall
nodes.summary: Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist who studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He co-founded the Philological Society, serving as its secretary, founded the Working Men's College and multiple literary societies, and edited the Oxford English Dictionary.

nodes.label: Royal Masonic School for Boys
variants: Royal Masonic School for Boys at Wood Green

nodes.label: Tanzan Hara
nodes.summary: Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He taught at the University of Tokyo starting in 1879, joined the Japan Academy in 1885, and became superintendent of Komazawa University in 1891.

nodes.id: P:Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo
nodes.label: Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo
13th Dalai Lama
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, the 13th Dalai Lama studied under Agvan Dorzhiev, Pa Ri Rabsal, Tertön Sogyal, and others. He taught numerous prominent figures, including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and the 9th Panchen Lama.

nodes.label: Kumja Paik Kim
nodes.summary: Kumja Paik Kim (born 1934) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate from Stanford University and became curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum in 1989.

nodes.label: Leedom Lefferts
nodes.summary: Leedom Lefferts specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2011, he served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus, at Drew University and as a Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

nodes.label: Louise Allison Cort
nodes.summary: Louise Allison Cort is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College (~1967–1969) and served as a ceramics curator at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries (~1981–2020).

nodes.label: Kavita Singh
nodes.summary: Kavita Singh (1964–2023) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MS University of Baroda, and Panjab University/University of the Punjab, and held posts at Marg Publications, College of Art, Delhi, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

nodes.label: Jules Michelet
nodes.description: French historian; popularized the historical concept of the Renaissance
nodes.summary: Jules Michelet was a historian who studied at Lycée Charlemagne. He held teaching posts at the École Normale Supérieure, served as a section head at the Archives Nationales (1830–1851), and was Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

nodes.label: Raghu Ananthanarayanan
nodes.summary: Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and philosophy and religious studies under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. He taught at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and was a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, the University of Mysore, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari, later teaching at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1953–1958).

nodes.label: T. K. V. Desikachar
nodes.summary: T. K. V. Desikachar (1938–2016) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1961 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

nodes.label: Catherine Cornille
nodes.summary: Catherine Cornille works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, later serving as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College (attested ~2005).

nodes.label: Manshi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Manshi Kiyozawa (1863–1903) was a Japanese scholar of Buddhism and philosophy. He studied at Otani University, Toyo University, and the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He later served as Otani University's founding president (1901–1902).

nodes.label: Ernest Fenollosa
variants: アーネスト・フランシスコ・フェノロサ
nodes.jawiki: アーネスト・フェノロサ
nodes.summary: Ernest Fenollosa was a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and history who studied at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1878), Tokyo National Museum (1888), and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1890–1896).

nodes.label: Kyoto Ordinary Middle School
variants: Jinjō Middle School 尋常中学校

nodes.label: The Eastern Buddhist
variants: イースタン・ブディスト

nodes.label: Khenpo Gangshar
nodes.summary: Khenpo Gangshar (1925–1980) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shechen Monastery under Khyentse Ozer, Shechen Kongtrul, and Karsé Kongtrul, later serving as senior teacher there (~1950–1957) and founding dean at Surmang Monastery (~1957–1959).

nodes.label: Gembo Dorji
nodes.summary: Gembo Dorji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, receiving instruction from traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

nodes.label: Ngawang Nyima
nodes.summary: Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Dagpo Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Shechen Gyaltsab
nodes.summary: Shechen Gyaltsab (1871–1926) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught figures including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

nodes.label: Karuna Kusalasaya
nodes.native: กรุณา กุศลาสัย
nodes.summary: Karuna Kusalasaya was an Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Fafang
nodes.summary: Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He held a post as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Satiranjan Sen
nodes.summary: Satiranjan Sen worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Peking University, he was a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

nodes.label: Rongtha Damchö Gyatso
variants: Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho

nodes.label: Yuexia
nodes.summary: Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served there as a teacher.

nodes.label: Dixian
nodes.summary: Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Mingzu. He served as abbot at Guanzong Temple from around 1913 to 1932.

nodes.label: Nicholas Roerich
variants: ニコライ・コンスタンティノヴィチ・リョーリフ
nodes.jawiki: ニコライ・リョーリフ
nodes.description: Russian painter, writer, archaeologist and philosopher (1874–1947)
nodes.summary: Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) was a scholar and artist in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts, founded the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute, and directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts.

nodes.label: Drakgyab Lodrö
variants: mKhan Rinpoche Brag gyab Blos gros

nodes.label: New Asia College
variants: 香港中文大学新亜書院

nodes.label: School of the Tibetan Language
variants: School of the Tibetan Language (Xi fan xue zong guan)

nodes.id: P:Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
nodes.label: Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
John Lockwood Kipling
nodes.image: John Lockwood Kipling és Rudyard Kipling.jpg
nodes.summary: Kipling worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, having studied at Woodhouse Grove School. He taught at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (circa 1865–1875) and served as Principal of the National College of Arts and Curator of Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

nodes.label: Lorna Dewaraja
nodes.summary: Lorna Dewaraja worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon (~1949–1952) and the University of London (~1966–1969). Her career included posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Colombo (~1969–1989), and St Anne's College.

nodes.label: Senarat Wijayasundara
nodes.summary: Senarat Wijayasundara worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

nodes.label: Dorje Geshe
variants: Duojie gexi zunzhe 多傑格西尊者

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wundt
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ヴント
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ヴント
nodes.description: German physician, physiologist, philosopher and professor (1832–1920)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wundt worked in philosophy. He studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg (~1852–1856), and Berlin. He held positions at the University of Zurich (1857), the University of Leipzig (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).

nodes.label: Edvard Westermarck
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・ウェスターマーク
nodes.summary: Edvard Westermarck worked in philosophy and religious studies, having studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881–1889). He held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1904–1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918–1932).

nodes.label: Dedong Wei
nodes.summary: Dedong Wei (born 1968) specializes in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from Renmin University of China (circa 1995–1998) and became an associate professor of religious studies there around 2002.

nodes.label: Amy Paris Langenberg
nodes.image: Amy Paris Langenberg in the video 'Accomplished women Female leadership and reproductive health in the Bhikṣuņī-Vinaya'.png
nodes.summary: Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University around 2001–2008 and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College around 2014.

nodes.label: Tenzin Namdak
nodes.summary: Tenzin Namdak was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan and earned a lha rams pa degree at Menri Monastery (1950–1953). He later founded Triten Norbutse Monastery in 1986.

nodes.id: P:sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan
nodes.label: sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan
variants: sGangs ru tshul khrims rgyal mtshan

nodes.label: Marsha Weidner
nodes.summary: Marsha Weidner is a scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, she served at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and as Professor of the History of Art at the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Damdin Badaraev
nodes.summary: Damdin Badaraev specialized in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

nodes.label: Filippo De Filippi
nodes.jawiki: フィリッポ・デ・フィリッピ
nodes.summary: Filippo De Filippi was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.

nodes.label: Adhémard Leclère
nodes.summary: Adhémard Leclère worked in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Résident de France at Kratie in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and was vice-president of the Société Ethnologique de Paris, which he founded.

nodes.label: Douglas J. Penick
nodes.summary: Douglas J. Penick (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University from circa 1962 to 1966 and trained under the traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.

nodes.label: Giovanni Gentile
variants: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.jawiki: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.description: Italian philosopher, educator, fascist theoretician and politician (1875-1944)
nodes.summary: Philosopher Giovanni Gentile studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the universities of Florence and Pisa. He held professorships at Palermo, Pisa, and Rome (1917–1944), and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

nodes.id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
nodes.label: Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
nodes.summary: Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro (1952–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).

nodes.label: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje
nodes.summary: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught numerous students such as Chögyam Trungpa and Pema Chödrön.

nodes.label: First Zen Institute of America
variants: Kyoto branch of the First Institute of America
First Zen Institute of America in Japan
First Zen Institute of America in Kyoto

nodes.label: Emmanuel College, Toronto
variants: Emmanuel College of Victoria University in the University of Toronto

nodes.label: Tao Pan
nodes.summary: Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned a BA from Fudan University by 2010 and completed a Magister Artium degree at the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Nicholas Witkowski
nodes.summary: Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from Stanford University in 2015 and served as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Yuanxing Guo
nodes.summary: Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Gongga Rinpoche. Guo held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and served as a researcher at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism.

nodes.label: Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism
variants: Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism (Zhongguo Fojiao Wenhua Yanjiusuo 中國佛教文化研究所)

nodes.label: Nianzu Huang
nodes.summary: Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied Buddhist studies, attending Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and studying under several teachers including Lianju Xia and Hsu Yun. He headed the Central People's Broadcasting Station and was a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (~1953–1980).

nodes.label: Voice of America
variants: Tibetan Broadcast Service for Voice of America

nodes.label: René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz
nodes.summary: René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz (1923–1959) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Vienna, SOAS, Berlin, and LSE, he studied under Wilhelm Koppers, Giuseppe Tucci, and others. In 1958, he was a wissenschaftlicher Beamter at the Weltmuseum Wien.

nodes.label: Pieter Hendrik Pott
nodes.summary: Pieter Hendrik Pott (1918–1989) worked in Tibetology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as curator at Museum Volkenkunde (c. 1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

nodes.label: Lajos Ligeti
nodes.summary: Lajos Ligeti worked in Inner Asian, Sinological, and Tibetan studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University, Eötvös József Collegium, and the University of Paris, he held posts at Eötvös Loránd University from 1931, including chair of Inner Asian Studies from 1940.

nodes.label: Chogye Shabdrung
nodes.summary: Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

nodes.id: P:Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro
nodes.label: Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro
variants: Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drimé Lekpé Lodrö
シェチェン・コントゥル

nodes.label: Krisztina Teleki
nodes.description: (1978–) Hungarian literary translator, linguist, orientalist, tibetologist and mongolist
nodes.summary: Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Eötvös Loránd University (1997–2009), where she also served as a research fellow around 2010.

nodes.label: August Conrady
variants: アウグスト・コンラーディ
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・コンラーディ (中国学者)
nodes.summary: August Conrady (1864–1925) was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Würzburg and Leipzig, he held posts at Peking University (1903–1904) and the University of Leipzig, where he became a professor in 1920.

nodes.label: Berthold Laufer
variants: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.image: Annual report of the Director to the Board of Trustees for the year .. (1933) (17811378703).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.summary: Berthold Laufer worked in sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, completing his PhD at Leipzig under August Conrady. He held positions at the American Museum of Natural History (1901, 1904–1906), Columbia University (1905–1907), and the Field Museum (1907).

nodes.label: Bruno Schindler
variants: ブルーノ・シンドラー
nodes.summary: Bruno Schindler was a scholar in sinology who studied under doctoral supervisor August Conrady around 1913 to 1919. He founded Asia Major in 1923 and worked as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries from around 1939 to 1964.

nodes.label: Johannes Schubert
nodes.summary: Johannes Schubert worked in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at the University of Leipzig under Conrady, Francke, Franke, Schmitt, and Weller. He held posts at Leipzig University Library, Ahnenerbe, and the University of Leipzig, including a chair in Tibetology.

nodes.label: Stanisław Schayer
nodes.summary: Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He became a professor at the University of Warsaw in 1922 and was a member of the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences and Warsaw Scientific Society.

nodes.label: Jan Jaworski
nodes.summary: Jan Jaworski (1903–1945) was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1921–1927) and trained under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

nodes.label: Ludwik Skurzak
nodes.summary: Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He later served as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

nodes.label: Maryla Falk
nodes.description: Polish indologist and historian of religions
nodes.summary: Maryla Falk (1906–1980) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1937–1939) and was a member of the Polish Oriental Society and the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz
nodes.summary: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (1901–1981) was a Polish linguist and Indologist. After studying at the University of Lviv (~1919–1924), he held positions at Lviv (~1928–1939), Nicolaus Copernicus University (~1945–1953), and the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

nodes.label: Paul Ekman
nodes.summary: Paul Ekman studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held an academic post at the University of California, San Francisco, from approximately 1960 to 2004.

nodes.label: Somchai Kusalacitto
nodes.summary: Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Stephen Addiss
nodes.summary: Stephen Addiss was a scholar of japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan, and held professorships at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (1992–2013).

nodes.label: Laurence Austine Waddell
nodes.summary: Laurence Austine Waddell was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who earned a medical degree from the University of Glasgow. He served in the Indian Medical Service and Indian Army, and was Professor of Tibetan at University College London (1906–1908).

nodes.label: Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok
nodes.summary: Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (1933–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His teachers included Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima, Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel, Yonten Gonpo, and Khenchen Dazer, among others.

nodes.label: Yuanying
nodes.summary: Yuanying (1878–1953) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under teachers including Zeng Xi, Miaolian, Yekai, and Bazhi Toutuo. He served as abbot at Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples and held leadership posts in the Buddhist Association of China.

nodes.label: Marian Ury
nodes.summary: Marian Ury (1932–1995) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis from 1969 to 1995.

nodes.label: Seán McLoughlin
nodes.summary: Seán McLoughlin is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. After completing a Ph.D. at the University of Manchester, he served as Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Eric J. Sharpe
nodes.summary: Eric J. Sharpe was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Manchester and Uppsala University. He held posts at Lancaster, Uppsala, and the University of Sydney, where he was the first chair of religious studies.

nodes.label: Phra Rajavaramuni
nodes.native: พระราชวรมุนี
nodes.summary: Phra Rajavaramuni is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Liqian Liu
nodes.summary: Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1944–1949), the State Council translation administration department, and the Ethnic Publishing House.

nodes.label: West China Union University
variants: Border Area Institute of Research of the West China University

nodes.id: I:State Council of the People's Republic of China
nodes.label: State Council of the People's Republic of China
Genzao
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Genzao studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche in 1948 and Kalu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Dzogchen Monastery
variants: monastische Kolleg Shri Singha des Dzogchen-Klosters
Shri Singha Shedra at Dzogchen Monastery

nodes.id: I:Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
nodes.label: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
variants: Beijing Institute of Post and Telecommunications

nodes.label: Charles Alfred Bell
nodes.summary: Charles Alfred Bell (1870–1945) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his education at Winchester College (~1884–1889) and New College (~1889–1891).

nodes.label: Augustus William Heyde
nodes.description: German missionary to Tibetans in Northern India; b. Wilhelm Heide, Feb. 16, 1825; later changed surname to Heyde; d. Aug. 27, 1907

nodes.label: John Claude White
nodes.description: British engineer, civil servant and photographer in India (1853–1918)
nodes.summary: Active in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, John Claude White studied at Rugby School (1868) and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876). In 1876, he served as an Assistant Engineer for the Bengal Public Works Department.

nodes.label: Edward Sapir
nodes.summary: Linguist Edward Sapir studied at Columbia University (~1901–1909) under Franz Boas and Wilhelm Wundt. He served as Chief of Anthropology at the Victoria Museum (~1910–1925) and held professorships at the University of Chicago (~1925–1931) and Yale University (~1931–1939).

nodes.label: Edmund Husserl
variants: エトムント・フッサール
nodes.jawiki: エトムント・フッサール
nodes.description: German philosopher, known as the father of phenomenology (*1859 – †1938)
nodes.summary: Philosopher Edmund Husserl studied under Wilhelm Wundt at Leipzig, as well as at Berlin, Vienna, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1887–1901), University of Göttingen (1901–1916), and University of Freiburg (1916–1928).

nodes.label: Friedrich Schleiermacher
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュライアマハー
nodes.description: German theologian, philosopher, and biblical scholar (1768-1834)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Schleiermacher (1768–1834) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1789), where he later held a post (~1804–1807), followed by a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1834).

nodes.label: Józef Szczepan Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Józef Szczepan Kowalewski worked in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vilnius and Kazan, later serving as professor and rector at Kazan Imperial University (1833–1860) and professor and dean at the University of Warsaw.

nodes.label: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk
nodes.summary: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk (1938–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.

nodes.label: Longlian
nodes.summary: Longlian (1909–2006) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Fazun in 1939 and under traditional teacher Nenghai Shi from approximately 1941 to 1967.

nodes.label: Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies
variants: Institut d'études du bouddhisme sino-tibétain (Hanzang jiaoli yuan)
Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (Hanzang Jiaoliyuan 漢藏教理院)

nodes.label: Guankong
nodes.summary: Guankong worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a teacher at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and became a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

nodes.label: D. Neil Schmid
nodes.summary: D. Neil Schmid is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Pennsylvania, completing his doctorate under Victor H. Mair.

nodes.label: Rachel H. Pang
nodes.summary: Rachel H. Pang is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia and was Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Sangseraima Ujeed
nodes.summary: Sangseraima Ujeed specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford (circa 2013–2017) and held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara (around 2018–2020).

nodes.label: Seikaku Hirata
nodes.summary: Seikaku Hirata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1946–1949) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, as well as under Bokuo Seki. He held a post at Hanazono University from around 1969 to 2000.

nodes.label: Sokatsu Shaku
nodes.summary: Sokatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kōsen Imakita and Soyen Shaku. He founded Ryobokai (1901), the Ryobokai Dojo of North America (1906), and Ningen Zen, and taught Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki.

nodes.label: Peter Connolly
nodes.summary: Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and became a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

nodes.label: Lynn Thomas
nodes.summary: Lynn Thomas works in Indology and religious studies. She earned degrees from Lancaster University and a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford (until 1987), later serving as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Erik Erikson
nodes.jawiki: エリク・H・エリクソン
nodes.summary: Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. His academic career included positions at Harvard University (circa 1934–1970), the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1939–1950), and the University of Pittsburgh (circa 1951–1960).

nodes.label: Eiichi Makino
nodes.summary: Eiichi Makino was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903). He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938) and later held posts at Chuo University (~1938–1946) and Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (~1953–1968).

nodes.label: Shigemitsu Dando
nodes.summary: Shigemitsu Dando studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (~1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University (~1974), and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz (ca. 1889–1893) and Karl Foy.

nodes.label: Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal
nodes.summary: Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812–1894) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and later held a post at Heidelberg University from circa 1836 to 1842.

nodes.label: Shenphen Nangwa
nodes.summary: Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Önpo Tenzin Norbu, among others. He taught at Dzogchen Monastery and became the first khenpo of the new shedra at Dzongsar Monastery.

nodes.label: Patrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Patrul Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1830–1842), Do Khyentse Yeshe Dorje (~1832), and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Minyak Kunzang Sonam.

nodes.label: Denise Bernot
nodes.summary: Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a scholar in linguistics. She studied at the École des chartes and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and later held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from circa 1960 to 1989.

nodes.label: Georg Ruppelt
nodes.image: Georg Ruppelt Direktor der Gottfried-Wilhelm-Leibniz Bibliothek anläßlich der Buchvorstellung Alles über Wikipedia im Werner Kraft Vortragssaal.jpg

nodes.label: Sven Hedin
nodes.description: Swedish geographer, topographer, explorer, photographer, travel writer and illustrator (1865-1952)
nodes.summary: Sven Hedin was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and history scholar. He studied at Stockholm University (~1886–1888), Uppsala University (1888), the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1889–1890), and the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1892).

nodes.label: Staatsgalerie Stuttgart
variants: Württembergische Museum der Bildenden Künste in Stuttgart

nodes.label: Eileen Power
nodes.summary: Eileen Power was a historian who studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1907–1910) and the University of Paris (~1910–1911). She held posts at the London School of Economics and the University of London (~1921–1940).

nodes.label: James Darmesteter
nodes.jawiki: ジャーム・ダルメステテール
nodes.summary: James Darmesteter (1849–1894) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault and Michel Bréal, later holding posts there and at the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Marcel Cohen
nodes.summary: Marcel Cohen (1884–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1954) and the University of Paris (~1926–1954).

nodes.label: Lucien Tesnière
nodes.jawiki: ルシアン・テニエール
nodes.summary: Lucien Tesnière was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and attended the University of Paris, University of Leipzig, and ENLOV. He held academic posts at the universities of Ljubljana (c. 1920–1924), Strasbourg (1924–1937), and Montpellier (1937).

nodes.label: Pierre Chantraine
nodes.summary: Pierre Chantraine (1899–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes. He held a post at the University of Paris from circa 1938 to 1969.

nodes.label: Michel Lejeune
nodes.summary: Michel Lejeune was a French linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) and under Antoine Meillet (~1927–1932). He held academic posts at the University of Poitiers (~1937–1946), the University of Paris (~1947–1977), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1977).

nodes.label: Jerzy Kuryłowicz
variants: イェジ・クリウォヴィチ
nodes.jawiki: イェジ・クリウォヴィチ
nodes.summary: Jerzy Kuryłowicz was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Lviv (~1920–1923) and under Antoine Meillet (~1923–1925), later holding posts at the University of Lviv (~1926–1946) and Jagiellonian University (~1948–1965).

nodes.label: André Martinet
nodes.jawiki: アンドレ・マルティネ
nodes.summary: André Martinet (1908–1999) was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne and Humboldt University of Berlin under mentor Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1938–1947), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1977).

nodes.label: Joseph Vendryes
nodes.image: Réunion des doyens des facultés dans le bureau du recteur, décembre 1940. M. Bruhat M. Gidel M. Baudouin M. Carcopino M. Maurain M. Vendryès M. Damiens (cropped).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョゼフ・ヴァンドリエス
nodes.summary: Joseph Vendryes was a linguist who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, and under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the University of Paris (~1907–1946), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1907–1944), and École Normale Supérieure (~1907–1925).

nodes.label: Alfred Ernout
nodes.summary: Alfred Ernout was a scholar in linguistics. He held academic positions at the University of Lille (1913–1924), the University of Paris (c. 1927–1949), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1927–1949), and the Collège de France (1941–1951).

nodes.label: Kyoto Prefectural Rakuhoku High School
variants: Kyōto Prefectural Ordinary Junior High School

nodes.label: Jacques André
nodes.summary: Jacques André worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1930–1948), he held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

nodes.label: Raphael Kühner
nodes.summary: Raphael Kühner was a linguist who studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (~1821–1825). He later taught Georg Bühler.

nodes.label: Peter K. Austin
nodes.summary: Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He held a post at SOAS University of London from ~2002 to 2018.

nodes.label: Matthias Alexander Castrén
nodes.jawiki: マティアス・カストラン
nodes.summary: Matthias Alexander Castrén specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki and Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836), later holding posts at both institutions from around 1851 to 1852.

nodes.label: Yasodhara
variants: Yasodhara: The Newsletter on International Buddhist Women's Activities

nodes.id: I:École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer
nodes.label: École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer
variants: École nationale de la France d’Outre-Mer
École nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer
フランス海外領国立学校

nodes.label: Robert Göbl
nodes.summary: Robert Göbl was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna from 1947 to 1950 and held a post there from around 1955 to 1989.

nodes.label: Karl Lachmann
nodes.summary: Karl Lachmann was a scholar in linguistics who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815). He held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1851.

nodes.label: Newcomb College
variants: H. Sophie Newcomb Memorial College der Tulane University
Harriet Sophie Newcomb College at Tulane University

nodes.label: Alan Lomax
nodes.jawiki: アラン・ローマックス
nodes.summary: Alan Lomax was an ethnomusicologist. He attended Choate Rosemary Hall, St. Mark's School of Texas, Harvard University (c. 1933–1934), the University of Texas at Austin (c. 1934–1936), and Columbia University (c. 1939–1940).

nodes.label: Stanislav Grof
nodes.image: Крістіна і Станіслав Грофи (Christina and Stanislav Grof) (cropped).JPG
nodes.jawiki: スタニスラフ・グロフ
nodes.summary: Stanislav Grof studied at Charles University. He held positions at psychiatric institutions in Czechoslovakia, Johns Hopkins University, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Esalen Institute, and the California Institute of Integral Studies.

nodes.label: University for Continuing Education Krems
variants: Zentrum Religion und Globalisierung der Donau-Universität Krems
Fachbereich Interkulturelle Studien der Donau-Universität Krems
