variants: Churchill College der University of Cambridge

nodes.id: I:Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
nodes.label: Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
variants: Institut für Archäologie der Chinesischen Akademie der Sozialwissenschaften in Peking
中国社会科学院考古研究所

nodes.label: Karl Müllenhoff
nodes.summary: Karl Müllenhoff specialized in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel University, the University of Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at Kiel University (1842) and Frederick William University Berlin (1858).

nodes.label: American Academy in Rome
variants: American School of Classical Studies in Rome
School of Classical Studies in the American Academy in Rome

nodes.label: Alfred Körte
nodes.summary: Alfred Körte worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, having studied at the University of Bonn. His academic career included posts at Greifswald, Bonn, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig.

nodes.label: Friedrich Leo
nodes.summary: Friedrich Leo (1851–1914) worked in linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Bonn, the latter under Hermann Usener. He held posts at Bonn, Kiel, Rostock, Strasbourg, and Göttingen (1889–1914).

nodes.label: Walter Porzig
nodes.summary: Walter Porzig was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Jena and under Wilhelm Streitberg. He held academic posts at Leipzig, Bern, Jena, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

nodes.id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
nodes.label: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
variants: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
nodes.image: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark by Boucas.jpg
nodes.enwiki: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
nodes.jawiki: ペトロス・ティス・エラザス
nodes.description: anthropologist, specialising in Tibetan beliefs and customs
nodes.summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark was a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics (~1935–1939), and served in the Office of Strategic Services (~1943–1945).

nodes.label: Rudolf Thurneysen
nodes.summary: Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1877–1879) and under Heinrich Zimmer (~1881–1882). He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), the University of Freiburg (~1887–1913), and the University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

nodes.label: Bedřich Hrozný
nodes.jawiki: ベドジフ・フロズニー
nodes.summary: Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Vienna (~1905–1919) and Charles University (~1919–1952).

nodes.id: I:Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis
nodes.label: Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis
variants: Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis

nodes.label: Friedrich Nietzsche
variants: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
nodes.summary: Friedrich Nietzsche (1844–1900) worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Bonn and Leipzig, studying under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and held a faculty post at the University of Basel from 1869 to 1878.

nodes.label: Friedrich Delitzsch
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・デーリッチュ
nodes.summary: Friedrich Delitzsch (1850–1922) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Brockhaus, Curtius, Windisch, Fleischer, and Dillmann. He held posts at Breslau (~1893–1899) and Berlin (~1899–1920).

nodes.label: Gustav Mensching
nodes.summary: Gustav Mensching worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin, Marburg (under Rudolf Otto), and Göttingen, later holding posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

nodes.label: Rudolf Otto
nodes.description: German theologian, philosopher, and comparative religionist (1869–1937)
nodes.summary: Rudolf Otto was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1888–1891) and under Richard von Garbe, later holding posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).

nodes.label: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer
nodes.summary: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1968) and the University of Munich (~1968–1973), later holding positions at the University of Munich (~1979–1993) and the University of Göttingen (~1993–2015).

nodes.label: Shimin Geng
nodes.summary: Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, Shimin Geng studied at Minzu University of China (~1949–1952) and later held a post there (~1953).

nodes.label: Philip Boas Yampolsky
nodes.summary: Philip Boas Yampolsky worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University and under Yoshitaka Iriya, later serving as an adjunct associate professor and East Asian Library librarian at Columbia (1968–1996) and chair at the Numata Center (1991–1996).

nodes.label: Franz Boas
nodes.summary: Franz Boas was a scholar in linguistics and anthropology who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held positions at Clark University, the Smithsonian Institution, the American Museum of Natural History (1896–1900), and Columbia University (around 1896–1936).

nodes.label: Otto Jahn
nodes.description: German classical philologist, archaeologist and musicologist (1813-1869)
